docs.text: cis ¤ This role provides support for Configuring IBM Cloud Internet Services. During CIS provisioning it performs four tasks in the given order: Provision CIS Instance in customer account Add customer domain to customer's CIS Instance Configure Domain settings in customer CIS Instance Add DNS Records of type NS for customer's Domain nameservers to Master CIS Account During CIS Instance deprovisioning the role will perform the following tasks: Delete DNS Record from Master Account Delete Domain from Customer Account Delete Customer CIS Instance Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cis_action No provision cis_plan No standard ibmcloud_region No us-east ibmcloud_apikey Yes None ibmcloud_resourcegroup No Default master_ibmcloud_api_key Yes None master_cis_resource_group No manager master_cis_resource_name No <mas_instance_id>-cis master_cis_base_domain Yes None mas_instance_id Yes None cluster_name Yes None mas_config_dir Yes None CIS Instance ¤ cis_action ¤ Action to perform on the Cloud Internet Services instance — provision creates the CIS instance, adds the domain, configures domain settings, and adds NS records to the master account; deprovision deletes the DNS records from the master account, removes the domain, and deletes the CIS instance. Optional Environment Variable: CIS_ACTION Default: provision Use provision (default) when setting up DNS and CDN services for a new MAS deployment, and deprovision when cleaning up CIS resources after MAS uninstallation. Provisioning creates a multi-account DNS delegation architecture and requires coordination between the customer and master IBM Cloud accounts; failed provisioning may require manual cleanup in the IBM Cloud console. Warning Deprovisioning permanently removes all CIS resources and DNS records that may still be in use (irreversible) — verify before proceeding, and always deprovision before removing the OpenShift cluster. cis_plan ¤ IBM Cloud Internet Services plan tier, which determines available features (WAF rules, rate limiting, page rules, load balancing), performance limits, SLA guarantees, and pricing — standard (basic CDN, DDoS protection, and DNS, sufficient for most development and test environments) or enterprise (advanced security, performance, and support features, recommended for production deployments with high traffic). Plan availability and features may vary by region. Optional Environment Variable: CIS_PLAN Default: standard Only applies when cis_action is provision . The plan cannot be changed after provisioning (it requires recreation), so review IBM Cloud CIS pricing before selecting a plan. ibmcloud_region ¤ IBM Cloud region targeted by the CIS operations. Optional Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_REGION Default: us-east Customer Account ¤ ibmcloud_apikey ¤ The IBM Cloud API key (44-character alphanumeric string) for the customer account where CIS will be provisioned. Must have Editor or Administrator role on the CIS service and access to the specified resource group. Required Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Always required for both provisioning and deprovisioning. Authenticates all operations in the customer's account, which owns the CIS instance and incurs charges. Store API keys securely using environment variables or secrets management, never commit them to version control, and consider using service IDs with restricted permissions. ibmcloud_resourcegroup ¤ The IBM Cloud resource group (case-sensitive, must exist before provisioning) in the customer account that will own the CIS instance — for example Default , Production , Development , or MAS-Resources . Optional Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Default The resource group determines billing and cost allocation and controls IAM access policies; it cannot be changed after CIS instance creation. Ensure ibmcloud_apikey has access to the specified resource group, and use consistent resource groups across all MAS-related services. Master Account ¤ master_ibmcloud_api_key ¤ The IBM Cloud API key for the master account that hosts the base domain. This is a separate key from ibmcloud_apikey , typically provided by the organization managing the master domain, and needs only DNS record management permissions in the master CIS instance (not full CIS access). Required Environment Variable: MASTER_IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Used to create the NS (nameserver) records in the master CIS instance that delegate the subdomain to the customer's CIS nameservers — without it the customer's domain will not be resolvable. Store it securely, since it has access to the master DNS infrastructure. master_cis_resource_group ¤ The resource group (case-sensitive) in the master account where the master CIS instance is located — must match the actual resource group in which master_cis_resource_name exists. Optional Environment Variable: MASTER_CIS_RESOURCE_GROUP Default: manager Used to locate the master CIS instance for NS record creation; an incorrect value causes DNS delegation to fail. The default manager is commonly used in IBM MAS deployments — verify the correct resource group with the master account administrator, and ensure master_ibmcloud_api_key has access to it. master_cis_resource_name ¤ The name of the master CIS instance in the master account that hosts the base domain and receives the NS records for subdomain delegation — must match an existing CIS instance (case-sensitive) in master_cis_resource_group . Optional Environment Variable: MASTER_CIS_RESOURCE_NAME Default: <mas_instance_id>-cis The instance must already exist in the master account; this role only uses it for NS record management, it does not create it. If the master CIS instance uses a different naming convention than the default, verify the correct instance name with the master account administrator. master_cis_base_domain ¤ The base domain hosted in the master CIS instance under which the customer's subdomain will be delegated — for example mas.ibm.com , maximo.example.com , or apps.company.com , without protocol (http/https) or trailing slashes. Required Environment Variable: MASTER_CIS_BASE_DOMAIN Default: None The domain must already exist and be active in the master CIS instance; verify DNS propagation of the base domain before provisioning. The full customer domain will be <cluster_name>.<mas_instance_id>.<master_cis_base_domain> — for example cluster1.prod.mas.ibm.com when the base domain is mas.ibm.com . Domain Naming and MAS Configuration ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ The MAS instance identifier used to generate the CIS service name and as part of the domain name structure — an alphanumeric string, typically 3-12 characters, lowercase recommended for DNS compatibility (for example prod , dev , test , or masinst1 ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Generates the default CIS instance name ( <mas_instance_id>-cis ) and forms the second part of the domain: <cluster_name>.<mas_instance_id>.<base_domain> . Use the same mas_instance_id across all MAS DevOps roles for consistency; it cannot be changed after provisioning without recreating resources. cluster_name ¤ The OpenShift cluster name used as the first component of the domain name — alphanumeric with hyphens, lowercase recommended for DNS compatibility (for example ocp-prod , rosa-cluster , roks-dev , or cluster1 ), and unique within the MAS instance. Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Multiple clusters can share the same mas_instance_id with different cluster_name values — for example cluster_name=rosa-prod , mas_instance_id=mas01 , base domain ibm.com yields rosa-prod.mas01.ibm.com . mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory where the role saves the CIS instance details as Kubernetes ConfigMap YAML files for use by other MAS components — for example ~/masconfig or /opt/mas/config . The directory is created if it doesn't exist and must be writable by the user running the playbook; an absolute path is recommended. Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None This directory is the central location for all MAS configuration artifacts and should be the same across all MAS DevOps roles. The ConfigMaps generated here are applied to the OpenShift cluster during MAS installation, so back the directory up. Example Playbook ¤ Create CIS Instance along with save Instance details in MAS_CONFIG_DIR path as ConfigMap - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cis_action: provision mas_instance_id: masinst1 mas_config_dir: ~/masconfig ibmcloud_apikey: "****" master_ibmcloud_api_key: "******" cluster_name: "test" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cis License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: cos ¤ This role provides support for: Provisioning and Configuring Cloud Object Storage in MAS. It currently supports two providers: In-cluster Ceph Object Storage leveraging OpenShift Container Storage IBM Cloud Object Storage Deprovision Cloud Object Store. It currently supports one provider: IBM Cloud Object Storage Currently this role only supports generating a system-scoped ObjectStorageCfg resource, but the generated file can be modified if you wish to use other scopes. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cos_type Yes None cos_action No provision custom_labels No None cos_instance_name No Object Storage for MAS cos_location_info No global cos_plan_type No standard cos_region No us-standard cos_url No https://s3.us.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud cos_resource_key_iam_role No Manager cos_use_hmac No true cos_apikey No Falls back to ibmcloud_apikey ibmcloud_apikey Conditional None cos_resourcegroup No Falls back to ibmcloud_resourcegroup ibmcloud_resourcegroup No Default ocp_ingress_tls_secret_name No router-certs-default include_cluster_ingress_cert_chain No False cos_include_isrg_root_cert No true mas_instance_id No None mas_config_dir No None Variables marked Conditional are required only when cos_type is ibm ( ibmcloud_apikey , unless cos_apikey is provided instead). Additionally, both mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir must be set for the role to generate an ObjectStorageCfg resource — if either is missing, the role only provisions the storage. COS Provider and Action ¤ cos_type ¤ The Cloud Object Storage provider to use for MAS — ibm (IBM Cloud Object Storage, a managed cloud service) or ocs (in-cluster Ceph object storage via OpenShift Container Storage / OpenShift Data Foundation). Required Environment Variable: COS_TYPE Default: None ibm provisions an IBM Cloud COS instance (requires an IBM Cloud account and API key, incurs cloud costs, provides unlimited scalability, and is recommended for production deployments requiring high availability and separation of storage from compute), while ocs creates a Ceph object store within the OpenShift cluster (requires the OCS/ODF operator and sufficient cluster storage capacity, with no external costs — suitable for on-premises or air-gapped deployments). The choice also affects the generated ObjectStorageCfg resource format; consider data residency and compliance requirements when choosing. cos_action ¤ The action to perform on the Cloud Object Storage instance — provision (create and configure the COS instance, generate credentials, and create the ObjectStorageCfg resource) or deprovision (delete the COS instance; IBM COS only, not supported for OCS). Optional Environment Variable: COS_ACTION Default: provision Warning Deprovisioning permanently deletes the IBM Cloud COS instance and all data — this is irreversible. Ensure all data is backed up first and verify no applications are using the instance before deprovisioning. IBM Cloud COS deprovisioning may fail if buckets contain data; for OCS, deprovisioning must be done manually through the OpenShift console. custom_labels ¤ Custom key=value labels to apply to provisioned resources, as a comma-separated list (e.g. environment=production,team=platform,cost-center=engineering ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels are metadata only and do not affect resource behavior; they are useful for cost tracking, resource organization, and automation-driven resource discovery (IBM Cloud supports label-based cost allocation and reporting). IBM Cloud Object Storage ¤ cos_instance_name ¤ The name for the IBM Cloud Object Storage instance — any string following IBM Cloud resource naming conventions (e.g. prod-mas-cos , dev-maximo-cos ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_INSTANCE_NAME Default: Object Storage for MAS , or Object Storage for MAS - <mas_instance_id> when mas_instance_id is set Used as the display name in the IBM Cloud console, to locate the instance during deprovisioning, and to identify the instance among other cloud resources; IBM Cloud allows renaming instances after creation. cos_location_info ¤ The geographic location where the IBM Cloud COS instance will be available — global (maximum flexibility and automatic failover), a specific region code ( us-south , us-east , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok , au-syd ), or a cross-region ( us , eu , ap ) for multi-region redundancy. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_LOCATION Default: global global is recommended for most deployments unless data residency is required; regional instances ensure data stays within specific geographic boundaries and may have lower latency for local access. Cannot be changed after instance creation, and cos_url should match the location for optimal performance. cos_plan_type ¤ The IBM Cloud COS service plan tier — standard (pay-as-you-go pricing with unlimited capacity; suitable for most MAS deployments) or lite (free tier with limited capacity, not suitable for production). Optional (IBM COS only, for provisioning) Environment Variable: COS_PLAN Default: standard Only used when cos_action is provision ; the plan cannot be changed after provisioning (it requires recreation). Pricing is based on storage capacity, requests, and data transfer. cos_region ¤ The IBM Cloud COS region identifier — e.g. us-south , eu-de , us-east . Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION Default: us-standard When set to a non-empty value, the region is included in the generated secret and ObjectStorageCfg resource; it is omitted when empty. cos_url ¤ The IBM Cloud COS regional endpoint URL for S3 API access — e.g. https://s3.us.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (US), https://s3.eu.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (EU), https://s3.ap.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (AP), or private/direct endpoints ( https://s3.private.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , https://s3.direct.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION_LOCATION_URL Default: https://s3.us.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud Used in the generated ObjectStorageCfg resource for MAS to connect to COS; it must be accessible from the OpenShift cluster. Private endpoints provide better security and lower costs for in-cloud access (recommended for OpenShift clusters running in IBM Cloud), and direct endpoints provide better performance for high-throughput workloads. cos_resource_key_iam_role ¤ The IAM role to assign to the COS service credentials — Manager (full access to buckets and objects; default), Writer (read and write access to objects with limited bucket operations), Reader (read-only access to objects), or Content Reader (read-only without listing capabilities). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_RESOURCE_KEY_IAM_ROLE Default: Manager Always use the Manager role for MAS deployments — lower privilege roles are not sufficient for MAS to create and manage buckets and will cause MAS functionality to fail. The role is assigned to the service credentials, not the instance itself. cos_use_hmac ¤ Controls whether to use HMAC-style credentials for COS access — true generates AWS S3-compatible access key ID and secret access key credentials; false uses IAM API key authentication (not compatible with MAS). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_USE_HMAC Default: true Important Always use true for MAS deployments — MAS requires HMAC credentials for S3 API compatibility, and setting this to false will cause MAS object storage configuration to fail. The credential format cannot be changed after credential creation (it requires new credentials). cos_apikey ¤ The IBM Cloud API key specifically for COS operations — a 44-character alphanumeric key with COS service management permissions. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_APIKEY Default: Falls back to ibmcloud_apikey if not set When set, this key is used instead of ibmcloud_apikey for COS operations, allowing a less privileged dedicated key for COS management following the principle of least privilege. ibmcloud_apikey ¤ The default IBM Cloud API key for all IBM Cloud operations — a 44-character alphanumeric key with Editor or Administrator role on the COS service and access to the specified resource group. Required when cos_type is ibm (unless cos_apikey is set) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Used for all IBM Cloud operations unless cos_apikey is specified; it determines which IBM Cloud account owns the COS instance (and is billed for usage). Store API keys securely and never commit them to version control. cos_resourcegroup ¤ The IBM Cloud resource group for the COS instance — any existing, case-sensitive resource group name (e.g. Default , Storage , MAS-Resources ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Falls back to ibmcloud_resourcegroup if not set Determines billing, cost allocation, and IAM access policies for the COS instance, and cannot be changed after instance creation; set it to organize COS separately from other IBM Cloud resources. The API key must have access to the specified resource group. ibmcloud_resourcegroup ¤ The default IBM Cloud resource group for all IBM Cloud resources — any existing, case-sensitive resource group name (e.g. Default , Production , Development ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Default Used as the default resource group for COS and other IBM Cloud resources across multiple roles in the collection; can be overridden by cos_resourcegroup for COS-specific placement. Ingress Certificate Chain ¤ ocp_ingress_tls_secret_name ¤ The name of the OpenShift cluster's default router certificate secret — must be a valid secret containing a TLS certificate and key in the openshift-ingress namespace. Optional (OCS only) Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_TLS_SECRET_NAME Default: router-certs-default Only relevant when cos_type is ocs : this secret is the source of the cluster's ingress certificate used in the ObjectStorageCfg. The default works for standard OpenShift installations — override only if you have customized your cluster's ingress certificates; an incorrect value will cause certificate validation failures when accessing OCS. include_cluster_ingress_cert_chain ¤ Controls whether to include the complete certificate chain from the cluster's ingress in the ObjectStorageCfg — True includes the full chain, False only the leaf certificate. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_CLUSTER_INGRESS_CERT_CHAIN Default: False Primarily relevant for OCS with custom certificates: enable when your cluster's ingress uses certificates signed by a trusted CA and you experience certificate validation issues in environments with intermediate CAs. Not typically needed for IBM Cloud COS. cos_include_isrg_root_cert ¤ Controls whether to append the ISRG Root X1 certificate (the default root certificate used by Let's Encrypt) to the ObjectStorageCfg certificate chain. Optional (OCS only) Environment Variable: COS_INCLUDE_ISRG_ROOT_CERT Default: true Only applied when OCS ingress certificates are present; mainly needed for IBM Cloud hosted services. MAS Configuration ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ The MAS instance ID that the ObjectStorageCfg will target — an alphanumeric string, typically 3-12 lowercase characters (e.g. prod , dev , test , masinst1 ), matching the MAS instance ID used throughout your deployment. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Required (together with mas_config_dir ) for the role to generate an ObjectStorageCfg resource — if either is missing, the role only provisions the storage. The ObjectStorageCfg is created in the mas-<instance-id>-core namespace. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory where the ObjectStorageCfg resource will be saved — any valid local filesystem path (e.g. ~/masconfig , /opt/mas/config ); the directory is created if it doesn't exist. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None Required (together with mas_instance_id ) for the role to generate an ObjectStorageCfg resource. The generated file can be applied manually with oc apply -f or used as input to the suite_config role for automated configuration. Example Playbook ¤ Create the Ceph Object store on the existing OCS cluster and prepare the objectstorageCfg yaml to mas_config_dir. - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cos_type: ocs mas_instance_id: masinst1 mas_config_dir: ~/masconfig roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cos Create the IBM Cloud Object storage Instance and prepare the objectstorageCfg yaml to mas_config_dir. - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cos_type: ibm ibmcloud_apikey: <Your IBM Cloud API Key> mas_instance_id: masinst1 mas_config_dir: ~/masconfig roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cos License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: This role provides support for: Provisioning and Configuring Cloud Object Storage in MAS. It currently supports two providers: In-cluster Ceph Object Storage leveraging OpenShift Container Storage IBM Cloud Object Storage Deprovision Cloud Object Store. It currently supports one provider: IBM Cloud Object Storage Currently this role only supports generating a system-scoped ObjectStorageCfg resource, but the generated file can be modified if you wish to use other scopes.

docs.text: The Cloud Object Storage provider to use for MAS — ibm (IBM Cloud Object Storage, a managed cloud service) or ocs (in-cluster Ceph object storage via OpenShift Container Storage / OpenShift Data Foundation). Required Environment Variable: COS_TYPE Default: None ibm provisions an IBM Cloud COS instance (requires an IBM Cloud account and API key, incurs cloud costs, provides unlimited scalability, and is recommended for production deployments requiring high availability and separation of storage from compute), while ocs creates a Ceph object store within the OpenShift cluster (requires the OCS/ODF operator and sufficient cluster storage capacity, with no external costs — suitable for on-premises or air-gapped deployments). The choice also affects the generated ObjectStorageCfg resource format; consider data residency and compliance requirements when choosing.
docs.title: cos_type

docs.text: The action to perform on the Cloud Object Storage instance — provision (create and configure the COS instance, generate credentials, and create the ObjectStorageCfg resource) or deprovision (delete the COS instance; IBM COS only, not supported for OCS). Optional Environment Variable: COS_ACTION Default: provision Warning Deprovisioning permanently deletes the IBM Cloud COS instance and all data — this is irreversible. Ensure all data is backed up first and verify no applications are using the instance before deprovisioning. IBM Cloud COS deprovisioning may fail if buckets contain data; for OCS, deprovisioning must be done manually through the OpenShift console.

docs.text: Custom key=value labels to apply to provisioned resources, as a comma-separated list (e.g. environment=production,team=platform,cost-center=engineering ). docs.text: The name for the IBM Cloud Object Storage instance — any string following IBM Cloud resource naming conventions (e.g. prod-mas-cos , dev-maximo-cos ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_INSTANCE_NAME Default: Object Storage for MAS , or Object Storage for MAS - <mas_instance_id> when mas_instance_id is set Used as the display name in the IBM Cloud console, to locate the instance during deprovisioning, and to identify the instance among other cloud resources; IBM Cloud allows renaming instances after creation.

docs.text: The geographic location where the IBM Cloud COS instance will be available — global (maximum flexibility and automatic failover), a specific region code ( us-south , us-east , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok , au-syd ), or a cross-region ( us , eu , ap ) for multi-region redundancy. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_LOCATION Default: global global is recommended for most deployments unless data residency is required; regional instances ensure data stays within specific geographic boundaries and may have lower latency for local access. Cannot be changed after instance creation, and cos_url should match the location for optimal performance.
docs.title: cos_location_info

docs.text: The IBM Cloud COS service plan tier — standard (pay-as-you-go pricing with unlimited capacity; suitable for most MAS deployments) or lite (free tier with limited capacity, not suitable for production). Optional (IBM COS only, for provisioning) Environment Variable: COS_PLAN Default: standard Only used when cos_action is provision ; the plan cannot be changed after provisioning (it requires recreation). Pricing is based on storage capacity, requests, and data transfer.
docs.title: cos_plan_type

docs.text: The IBM Cloud COS region identifier — e.g. us-south , eu-de , us-east . Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION Default: us-standard When set to a non-empty value, the region is included in the generated secret and ObjectStorageCfg resource; it is omitted when empty.
docs.title: cos_region

docs.text: The IBM Cloud COS regional endpoint URL for S3 API access — e.g. https://s3.us.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (US), https://s3.eu.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (EU), https://s3.ap.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (AP), or private/direct endpoints ( https://s3.private.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , https://s3.direct.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION_LOCATION_URL Default: https://s3.us.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud Used in the generated ObjectStorageCfg resource for MAS to connect to COS; it must be accessible from the OpenShift cluster. Private endpoints provide better security and lower costs for in-cloud access (recommended for OpenShift clusters running in IBM Cloud), and direct endpoints provide better performance for high-throughput workloads.

docs.text: The IAM role to assign to the COS service credentials — Manager (full access to buckets and objects; default), Writer (read and write access to objects with limited bucket operations), Reader (read-only access to objects), or Content Reader (read-only without listing capabilities). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_RESOURCE_KEY_IAM_ROLE Default: Manager Always use the Manager role for MAS deployments — lower privilege roles are not sufficient for MAS to create and manage buckets and will cause MAS functionality to fail. The role is assigned to the service credentials, not the instance itself.

docs.text: Controls whether to use HMAC-style credentials for COS access — true generates AWS S3-compatible access key ID and secret access key credentials; false uses IAM API key authentication (not compatible with MAS). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_USE_HMAC Default: true Important Always use true for MAS deployments — MAS requires HMAC credentials for S3 API compatibility, and setting this to false will cause MAS object storage configuration to fail. The credential format cannot be changed after credential creation (it requires new credentials).

docs.text: cos_bucket ¤ This role extends support to create or deprovision Cloud Object Storage buckets. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cos_type Yes None cos_bucket_action No create cos_bucket_name No <mas_instance_id>-<mas_workspace_id>-bucket cos_bucket_storage_class No smart cos_instance_name Conditional None cos_location_info No global cos_bucket_region_location_type No cross_region_location cos_bucket_region_location No Derived from ibmcloud_region ibmcloud_region No us-east cos_url No https://s3.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud cos_resource_key_iam_role No Manager ibmcloud_apikey Conditional None ibmcloud_resourcegroup No Default cos_bucket_versioning_flag No True cos_bucket_expire_rule_id No delete_files cos_bucket_expire_rule_enable_flag No True cos_bucket_expire_rule_days No 60 cos_service_credentials_name No {mas_instance_id}-{mas_workspace_id}-{cos_resource_key_iam_role lowercase}-key aws_bucket_name No <mas_instance_id>-<mas_workspace_id>-bucket aws_region No us-east-2 aws_url No https://s3.{aws_region}.amazonaws.com aws_bucket_versioning_flag No True aws_bucket_encryption No None aws_bucket_force_deletion_flag No True Variables marked Conditional are required only when cos_type is ibm ( cos_instance_name and ibmcloud_apikey ); when cos_type is aws , AWS credentials must be provided via environment variables or AWS CLI configuration. Bucket Provider and Action ¤ cos_type ¤ The Cloud Object Storage provider for bucket operations — ibm (IBM Cloud Object Storage) or aws (AWS S3). Required Environment Variable: COS_TYPE Default: None The provider determines which set of configuration variables is required: ibm requires ibmcloud_apikey , cos_instance_name , and the IBM COS bucket settings below, while aws requires AWS credentials (via environment variables or AWS CLI configuration) and aws_region . Bucket names must be globally unique within each provider; IBM COS buckets support the smart, vault, cold, and flex storage classes, and AWS S3 buckets support versioning and encryption configurations. cos_bucket_action ¤ The action to perform on the bucket — create (create a new bucket with the specified storage class, region, and lifecycle settings) or delete (delete an existing bucket). Optional Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_ACTION Default: create Warning Bucket deletion is irreversible — all data in the bucket will be lost. Back up data before deleting, and verify the bucket name to avoid removing the wrong bucket. IBM COS bucket deletion may fail if the bucket contains objects; for AWS, deletion behavior depends on aws_bucket_force_deletion_flag . IBM Cloud Object Storage Buckets ¤ cos_bucket_name ¤ The name for the IBM Cloud Object Storage bucket — 3-63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and periods only, starting and ending with a letter or number, and globally unique across all IBM Cloud COS (e.g. prod-mas-workspace1-bucket , dev-maximo-data-bucket ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_NAME Default: <mas_instance_id>-<mas_workspace_id>-bucket The default naming includes the MAS instance and workspace IDs for uniqueness. The name cannot be changed after creation (it requires recreation), appears in S3 API endpoints and URLs, and is globally visible — avoid including sensitive information. cos_bucket_storage_class ¤ The IBM Cloud COS storage class for the bucket — smart (automatically transitions data between hot and cool tiers based on access patterns; recommended and default), vault (data accessed less than once per month), cold (data accessed less than once per year), or flex (dynamic workloads with unpredictable access patterns). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_STORAGE_CLASS Default: smart The class determines storage pricing and data retrieval costs — lower-tier classes (vault, cold) have higher retrieval costs and latency. It cannot be changed after bucket creation, and availability varies by location type ( cos_bucket_region_location_type ). cos_instance_name ¤ The name of the IBM Cloud COS instance where the bucket will be created — must match an existing, case-sensitive COS instance name in your account (e.g. mas-cos-instance ). Required when cos_type is ibm Environment Variable: COS_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None The instance must exist in the specified resource group before running this role — use the cos role to provision it first. An incorrect name will cause bucket creation to fail. cos_location_info ¤ The geographic location of the IBM Cloud COS instance — global , a specific region code ( us-south , us-east , eu-gb , eu-de ), or a cross-region ( us , eu , ap ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: None Default: global Must match the location used when the COS instance was created; a mismatch will cause bucket operations to fail. The default global works for most deployments. cos_bucket_region_location_type ¤ The resiliency type for the IBM Cloud COS bucket — cross_region_location (data replicated across multiple regions; highest availability, ~99.99%; default), region_location (data stored in a single region; best performance, ~99.95%), or single_site_location (single data center; lowest cost and availability). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_REGION_LOCATION_TYPE Default: cross_region_location Determines which values are valid for cos_bucket_region_location and cannot be changed after bucket creation. cross_region_location is recommended for production MAS workloads; region_location suits performance-sensitive workloads. cos_bucket_region_location ¤ The specific region(s) for the IBM Cloud COS bucket — us , eu , or ap for cross_region_location ; us-south , us-east , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok , au-syd , ca-tor , jp-osa , or br-sao for region_location ; specific data center codes for single_site_location . Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_REGION_LOCATION Default: Derived from ibmcloud_region (e.g. us , eu , ap ) Determines the physical location of data storage, affecting data residency compliance (GDPR, data sovereignty) and network latency. Must be compatible with cos_bucket_region_location_type , cannot be changed after bucket creation, and should align with cos_url for optimal performance. ibmcloud_region ¤ The IBM Cloud region used to derive the default cross-region location — e.g. us-east , us-south , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok . Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_REGION Default: us-east Only used when cos_bucket_region_location_type is cross_region_location and cos_bucket_region_location is not explicitly set: us-* regions derive the us cross-region, eu-* derive eu , and jp-* / au-* derive ap . cos_url ¤ The IBM Cloud COS S3 API endpoint URL — regional endpoints such as https://s3.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , cross-region endpoints such as https://s3.us.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , or private/direct endpoints ( https://s3.private.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , https://s3.direct.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION_LOCATION_URL Default: https://s3.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (constructed from cos_bucket_region_location ) Should match the bucket's region location for best performance; private endpoints provide better security and lower costs for in-cloud access and are recommended for OpenShift clusters in IBM Cloud. Not applicable for AWS buckets (see aws_url ). cos_resource_key_iam_role ¤ The IAM role for COS service credentials created during bucket setup — Manager (full access to buckets and objects; default), Writer (read and write access to objects), or Reader (read-only access to objects). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_RESOURCE_KEY_IAM_ROLE Default: Manager Lower privilege roles may limit functionality — the Manager role is required for full bucket management. ibmcloud_apikey ¤ The IBM Cloud API key for bucket operations — a 44-character alphanumeric key with COS bucket management and resource group access permissions. Required when cos_type is ibm Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Authenticates all IBM Cloud COS operations and determines which account owns the bucket. It can alternatively be provided via the COS_APIKEY environment variable ( cos_apikey ), which falls back to this key when unset. Store API keys securely and never commit them to version control. ibmcloud_resourcegroup ¤ The IBM Cloud resource group containing the COS instance — any existing, case-sensitive resource group name in your account (e.g. Default , Production , MAS-Resources ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Default Must match the resource group used when creating the COS instance (the same one used in the cos role), and the API key must have access to it. It can alternatively be provided via the COS_RESOURCEGROUP environment variable ( cos_resourcegroup ), which falls back to this value when unset. cos_bucket_versioning_flag ¤ Controls whether to enable object versioning for the IBM Cloud COS bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_VERSIONING_FLAG Default: True cos_bucket_expire_rule_id ¤ Identifier for the rule that expires the current version of objects in the IBM Cloud COS bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_EXPIRE_RULE_ID Default: delete_files The expiry rule removes the current version of objects after cos_bucket_expire_rule_days days when cos_bucket_expire_rule_enable_flag is enabled — see the IBM Cloud COS expiry documentation . cos_bucket_expire_rule_enable_flag ¤ Whether to enable the object expiry rule for the IBM Cloud COS bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_EXPIRE_RULE_ENABLE_FLAG Default: True With the default value ( True ), objects in the bucket are deleted after cos_bucket_expire_rule_days days (60 by default). Setting this to False is the supported way to disable this behavior — the expiry rule is still created on the bucket, but it remains in a disabled state rather than being removed. cos_bucket_expire_rule_days ¤ Number of days after which the current version of objects in the IBM Cloud COS bucket expires. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_EXPIRE_RULE_DAYS Default: 60 cos_service_credentials_name ¤ The name of the COS service credentials created and retrieved for the bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_SERVICE_CREDENTIALS_NAME Default: {mas_instance_id}-{mas_workspace_id}-{cos_resource_key_iam_role lowercase}-key For IBM Cloud, the username in the generated service credentials corresponds to this credentials name. AWS S3 Buckets ¤ To run this role successfully for AWS s3 buckets, you must have already installed the AWS CLI . Also, you need to have AWS user credentials configured via aws configure command or simply export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables with your corresponding AWS username credentials prior running this role. aws_bucket_name ¤ The name for the AWS S3 bucket — 3-63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and periods only, starting and ending with a letter or number, globally unique across all AWS S3, without consecutive periods or underscores, and not formatted as an IP address (e.g. prod-mas-workspace1-bucket , dev-maximo-data-bucket ). Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_NAME Default: <mas_instance_id>-<mas_workspace_id>-bucket The default naming includes the MAS instance and workspace IDs for uniqueness. The name cannot be changed after creation (it requires recreation), appears in S3 API endpoints and URLs, and is globally visible — avoid including sensitive information. Not used for IBM COS buckets (see cos_bucket_name ). aws_region ¤ The AWS region where the S3 bucket will be created — e.g. us-east-1 , us-east-2 , us-west-2 , eu-west-1 , eu-central-1 , ap-southeast-1 . Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: AWS_REGION Default: us-east-2 Choose a region close to your OpenShift cluster and users for optimal performance, considering data residency compliance (GDPR, data sovereignty) — pricing varies by region, some regions may have capacity constraints, and the region cannot be changed after bucket creation. aws_url ¤ The AWS S3 API endpoint URL used for bucket operations. Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION_LOCATION_URL Default: https://s3.{aws_region}.amazonaws.com Should match the bucket's region. aws_bucket_versioning_flag ¤ Controls whether to enable versioning for the AWS S3 bucket. Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_VERSIONING_FLAG Default: True Versioning keeps multiple variants of each object in the bucket, providing rollback protection against accidental deletion or overwrite (recommended for production) at the cost of increased storage, since all versions consume space. Once enabled, versioning cannot be fully disabled (only suspended), and versioned buckets cannot be force-deleted (see aws_bucket_force_deletion_flag ). aws_bucket_encryption ¤ The default server-side encryption configuration for the AWS S3 bucket, as a JSON-formatted string — e.g. '{"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"}}]}' for S3-managed keys, or '{"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "aws:kms", "KMSMasterKeyID": "arn:aws:kms:region:account:key/key-id"}}]}' for KMS-managed keys. Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_ENCRYPTION Default: None When set, all objects uploaded to the bucket are automatically encrypted. AES256 is simpler and has no additional cost; aws:kms provides better key management and audit trails but incurs additional costs. Encryption can be changed after bucket creation. aws_bucket_force_deletion_flag ¤ Controls whether to force-delete bucket contents before deleting the AWS S3 bucket — True (default) automatically deletes all objects first; False fails if the bucket contains any objects (safer, requires manual cleanup). Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_FORCE_DELETION_FLAG Default: True Only takes effect when cos_bucket_action is delete , and only works if versioning is disabled — versioned buckets cannot be force-deleted ( aws_bucket_versioning_flag must be False ). Warning Force deletion permanently removes all data in the bucket and is irreversible. Back up data before force deletion. docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: The Cloud Object Storage provider for bucket operations — ibm (IBM Cloud Object Storage) or aws (AWS S3). Required Environment Variable: COS_TYPE Default: None The provider determines which set of configuration variables is required: ibm requires ibmcloud_apikey , cos_instance_name , and the IBM COS bucket settings below, while aws requires AWS credentials (via environment variables or AWS CLI configuration) and aws_region . Bucket names must be globally unique within each provider; IBM COS buckets support the smart, vault, cold, and flex storage classes, and AWS S3 buckets support versioning and encryption configurations.
docs.title: cos_type

docs.text: The action to perform on the bucket — create (create a new bucket with the specified storage class, region, and lifecycle settings) or delete (delete an existing bucket). Optional Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_ACTION Default: create Warning Bucket deletion is irreversible — all data in the bucket will be lost. Back up data before deleting, and verify the bucket name to avoid removing the wrong bucket. IBM COS bucket deletion may fail if the bucket contains objects; for AWS, deletion behavior depends on aws_bucket_force_deletion_flag .
docs.title: cos_bucket_action

docs.text: The name for the IBM Cloud Object Storage bucket — 3-63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and periods only, starting and ending with a letter or number, and globally unique across all IBM Cloud COS (e.g. prod-mas-workspace1-bucket , dev-maximo-data-bucket ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_NAME Default: <mas_instance_id>-<mas_workspace_id>-bucket The default naming includes the MAS instance and workspace IDs for uniqueness. The name cannot be changed after creation (it requires recreation), appears in S3 API endpoints and URLs, and is globally visible — avoid including sensitive information.
docs.title: cos_bucket_name

docs.text: The IBM Cloud COS storage class for the bucket — smart (automatically transitions data between hot and cool tiers based on access patterns; recommended and default), vault (data accessed less than once per month), cold (data accessed less than once per year), or flex (dynamic workloads with unpredictable access patterns). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_STORAGE_CLASS Default: smart The class determines storage pricing and data retrieval costs — lower-tier classes (vault, cold) have higher retrieval costs and latency. It cannot be changed after bucket creation, and availability varies by location type ( cos_bucket_region_location_type ).
docs.title: cos_bucket_storage_class

docs.text: The name of the IBM Cloud COS instance where the bucket will be created — must match an existing, case-sensitive COS instance name in your account (e.g. mas-cos-instance ). Required when cos_type is ibm Environment Variable: COS_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None The instance must exist in the specified resource group before running this role — use the cos role to provision it first. An incorrect name will cause bucket creation to fail.
docs.title: cos_instance_name

docs.text: The geographic location of the IBM Cloud COS instance — global , a specific region code ( us-south , us-east , eu-gb , eu-de ), or a cross-region ( us , eu , ap ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: None Default: global Must match the location used when the COS instance was created; a mismatch will cause bucket operations to fail. The default global works for most deployments.
docs.title: cos_location_info

docs.text: The resiliency type for the IBM Cloud COS bucket — cross_region_location (data replicated across multiple regions; highest availability, ~99.99%; default), region_location (data stored in a single region; best performance, ~99.95%), or single_site_location (single data center; lowest cost and availability). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_REGION_LOCATION_TYPE Default: cross_region_location Determines which values are valid for cos_bucket_region_location and cannot be changed after bucket creation. cross_region_location is recommended for production MAS workloads; region_location suits performance-sensitive workloads.
docs.title: cos_bucket_region_location_type

docs.text: The specific region(s) for the IBM Cloud COS bucket — us , eu , or ap for cross_region_location ; us-south , us-east , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok , au-syd , ca-tor , jp-osa , or br-sao for region_location ; specific data center codes for single_site_location . Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_REGION_LOCATION Default: Derived from ibmcloud_region (e.g. us , eu , ap ) Determines the physical location of data storage, affecting data residency compliance (GDPR, data sovereignty) and network latency. Must be compatible with cos_bucket_region_location_type , cannot be changed after bucket creation, and should align with cos_url for optimal performance.
docs.title: cos_bucket_region_location

docs.text: The IBM Cloud region used to derive the default cross-region location — e.g. us-east , us-south , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok . Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_REGION Default: us-east Only used when cos_bucket_region_location_type is cross_region_location and cos_bucket_region_location is not explicitly set: us-* regions derive the us cross-region, eu-* derive eu , and jp-* / au-* derive ap .
docs.title: ibmcloud_region

docs.text: The IBM Cloud COS S3 API endpoint URL — regional endpoints such as https://s3.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , cross-region endpoints such as https://s3.us.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , or private/direct endpoints ( https://s3.private.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , https://s3.direct.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION_LOCATION_URL Default: https://s3.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud (constructed from cos_bucket_region_location ) Should match the bucket's region location for best performance; private endpoints provide better security and lower costs for in-cloud access and are recommended for OpenShift clusters in IBM Cloud. Not applicable for AWS buckets (see aws_url ).
docs.title: cos_url

docs.text: The IAM role for COS service credentials created during bucket setup — Manager (full access to buckets and objects; default), Writer (read and write access to objects), or Reader (read-only access to objects). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_RESOURCE_KEY_IAM_ROLE Default: Manager Lower privilege roles may limit functionality — the Manager role is required for full bucket management.
docs.title: cos_resource_key_iam_role

docs.text: The IBM Cloud API key for bucket operations — a 44-character alphanumeric key with COS bucket management and resource group access permissions. Required when cos_type is ibm Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Authenticates all IBM Cloud COS operations and determines which account owns the bucket. It can alternatively be provided via the COS_APIKEY environment variable ( cos_apikey ), which falls back to this key when unset. Store API keys securely and never commit them to version control.
docs.title: ibmcloud_apikey

docs.text: The IBM Cloud resource group containing the COS instance — any existing, case-sensitive resource group name in your account (e.g. Default , Production , MAS-Resources ). Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Default Must match the resource group used when creating the COS instance (the same one used in the cos role), and the API key must have access to it. It can alternatively be provided via the COS_RESOURCEGROUP environment variable ( cos_resourcegroup ), which falls back to this value when unset.
docs.title: ibmcloud_resourcegroup

docs.text: Controls whether to enable object versioning for the IBM Cloud COS bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_VERSIONING_FLAG Default: True
docs.title: cos_bucket_versioning_flag

docs.text: Identifier for the rule that expires the current version of objects in the IBM Cloud COS bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_EXPIRE_RULE_ID Default: delete_files The expiry rule removes the current version of objects after cos_bucket_expire_rule_days days when cos_bucket_expire_rule_enable_flag is enabled — see the IBM Cloud COS expiry documentation .
docs.title: cos_bucket_expire_rule_id

docs.text: Whether to enable the object expiry rule for the IBM Cloud COS bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_EXPIRE_RULE_ENABLE_FLAG Default: True With the default value ( True ), objects in the bucket are deleted after cos_bucket_expire_rule_days days (60 by default). Setting this to False is the supported way to disable this behavior — the expiry rule is still created on the bucket, but it remains in a disabled state rather than being removed.
docs.title: cos_bucket_expire_rule_enable_flag

docs.text: Number of days after which the current version of objects in the IBM Cloud COS bucket expires. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_EXPIRE_RULE_DAYS Default: 60
docs.title: cos_bucket_expire_rule_days

docs.text: The name of the COS service credentials created and retrieved for the bucket. Optional (IBM COS only) Environment Variable: COS_SERVICE_CREDENTIALS_NAME Default: {mas_instance_id}-{mas_workspace_id}-{cos_resource_key_iam_role lowercase}-key For IBM Cloud, the username in the generated service credentials corresponds to this credentials name.
docs.title: cos_service_credentials_name

docs.text: To run this role successfully for AWS s3 buckets, you must have already installed the AWS CLI . Also, you need to have AWS user credentials configured via aws configure command or simply export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables with your corresponding AWS username credentials prior running this role.
docs.title: AWS S3 Buckets

docs.text: The name for the AWS S3 bucket — 3-63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and periods only, starting and ending with a letter or number, globally unique across all AWS S3, without consecutive periods or underscores, and not formatted as an IP address (e.g. prod-mas-workspace1-bucket , dev-maximo-data-bucket ). Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_NAME Default: <mas_instance_id>-<mas_workspace_id>-bucket The default naming includes the MAS instance and workspace IDs for uniqueness. The name cannot be changed after creation (it requires recreation), appears in S3 API endpoints and URLs, and is globally visible — avoid including sensitive information. Not used for IBM COS buckets (see cos_bucket_name ).
docs.title: aws_bucket_name

docs.text: The AWS region where the S3 bucket will be created — e.g. us-east-1 , us-east-2 , us-west-2 , eu-west-1 , eu-central-1 , ap-southeast-1 . Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: AWS_REGION Default: us-east-2 Choose a region close to your OpenShift cluster and users for optimal performance, considering data residency compliance (GDPR, data sovereignty) — pricing varies by region, some regions may have capacity constraints, and the region cannot be changed after bucket creation.
docs.title: aws_region

docs.text: The AWS S3 API endpoint URL used for bucket operations. Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_REGION_LOCATION_URL Default: https://s3.{aws_region}.amazonaws.com Should match the bucket's region.
docs.title: aws_url

docs.text: Controls whether to enable versioning for the AWS S3 bucket. Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_VERSIONING_FLAG Default: True Versioning keeps multiple variants of each object in the bucket, providing rollback protection against accidental deletion or overwrite (recommended for production) at the cost of increased storage, since all versions consume space. Once enabled, versioning cannot be fully disabled (only suspended), and versioned buckets cannot be force-deleted (see aws_bucket_force_deletion_flag ).
docs.title: aws_bucket_versioning_flag

docs.text: The default server-side encryption configuration for the AWS S3 bucket, as a JSON-formatted string — e.g. '{"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"}}]}' for S3-managed keys, or '{"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "aws:kms", "KMSMasterKeyID": "arn:aws:kms:region:account:key/key-id"}}]}' for KMS-managed keys. Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_ENCRYPTION Default: None When set, all objects uploaded to the bucket are automatically encrypted. AES256 is simpler and has no additional cost; aws:kms provides better key management and audit trails but incurs additional costs. Encryption can be changed after bucket creation.
docs.title: aws_bucket_encryption

docs.text: Controls whether to force-delete bucket contents before deleting the AWS S3 bucket — True (default) automatically deletes all objects first; False fails if the bucket contains any objects (safer, requires manual cleanup). Optional (AWS S3 only) Environment Variable: COS_BUCKET_FORCE_DELETION_FLAG Default: True Only takes effect when cos_bucket_action is delete , and only works if versioning is disabled — versioned buckets cannot be force-deleted ( aws_bucket_versioning_flag must be False ). Warning Force deletion permanently removes all data in the bucket and is irreversible. Back up data before force deletion.
docs.title: aws_bucket_force_deletion_flag

docs.text: cp4d ¤ This role installs or upgrades IBM Cloud Pak for Data Operator in the target cluster. It assumes that you have already installed the IBM Maximo Operator Catalog and configured Certificate Manager in the target cluster. These actions are performed by the ibm_catalogs cert_manager roles in this collection. Maximo tailored installation This role performs a Maximo tailored installation of Cloud Pak for Data that matches the configuration the Maximo team use internally. It does not support further post-install configuration beyond the configuration supported by the role, and it does not support every possible way to configure Cloud Pak for Data — it sets the platform up in a very specific way (namespaces, storage classes, Zen control plane sizing, licensing, and the set of CPD services supported by the cp4d_service role). Customers who need direct control over customizing their Cloud Pak for Data installation can choose to install and manage Cloud Pak for Data themselves; the MAS applications will work against any correctly configured CPD instance. When installing and managing CPD yourself, you are responsible for the CPD lifecycle (installation, upgrades, and any configuration you apply). Cloud Pak for Data will be configured as a specialized installation Info A specialized installation allows a user with project administrator permissions to install the software after a cluster administrator completes the initial cluster setup. A specialized installation also facilitates strict division between Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform projects (Kubernetes namespaces). In a specialized installation, the IBM Cloud Pak foundational services operators are installed in the ibm-common-services project and the Cloud Pak for Data operators are installed in a separate project (typically cpd-operators). Each project has a dedicated: Operator group, which specifies the OwnNamespace installation mode NamespaceScope Operator, which allows the operators in the project to manage operators and service workloads in specific projects In this way, you can specify different settings for the IBM Cloud Pak foundational services and for the Cloud Pak for Data operators. Currently supported Cloud Pak for Data release versions are: 5.2.0 (installed via OLM) 5.3.1 (platform installed via OLM, services installed via Helm) 5.4.0 (installed via Helm) Tip For more information about CPD versioning, see IBM Cloud Pak for data Operator and operand versions Cloud Pak for Data Version Mapping ¤ Users can choose to install a specific version of Cloud Pak for Data by setting CPD_PRODUCT_VERSION variable. However, by default, the version of Cloud Pak for Data will be determined by the version of the Maximo Operator Catalog that is installed in the cluster. If CPD_PRODUCT_VERSION variable is not defined, and the role is not able to find the Maximo Operator Catalog, then the role will default to installing the Cloud Pak for Data version supported by the latest released MAS catalog. Upgrade ¤ The role will automatically install or upgrade (if targeted to an existing CPD deployment) the corresponding Zen version associated to the chosen Cloud Pak for Data release, for example: Cloud Pak for Data release version 5.2.0 installs Zen/Control Plane version 6.2.0 Cloud Pak for Data release version 5.3.1 installs Zen/Control Plane version 6.4.0 Cloud Pak for Data release version 5.4.0 installs Zen/Control Plane version 6.10.0 Tip For more information about IBM Cloud Pak for Data upgrade process, refer to the Cloud Pak for Data official documentation . Cloud Pak for Data Deployment Details ¤ Cloud Pak for Data 5.x leverages Cloud Pak Foundational Services v4, which runs its deployments in isolated/dedicated scope model, that means that its dependencies will be grouped and installed within the Cloud Pak for Data related projects/namespaces. There are only two namespaces that will be used: CPD instance namespace (e.g ibm-cpd ) and CPD operators namespace (e.g ibm-cpd-operators ). In the ibm-cpd-operators namespace: oc -n ibm-cpd-operators get deployments NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE cpd-platform-operator-manager 1/1 1 1 17h ibm-common-service-operator 1/1 1 1 17h ibm-namespace-scope-operator 1/1 1 1 17h ibm-zen-operator 1/1 1 1 17h meta-api-deploy 1/1 1 1 17h operand-deployment-lifecycle-manager 1/1 1 1 17h postgresql-operator-controller-manager-1-18-7 1/1 1 1 17h In the ibm-cpd namespace: oc -n ibm-cpd get zenservice,ibmcpd,deployments,sts,pvc NAME VERSION STATUS AGE zenservice.zen.cpd.ibm.com/lite-cr 6.0.1 Completed 17h NAME AGE ibmcpd.cpd.ibm.com/ibmcpd-cr 17h NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE deployment.apps/ibm-mcs-hubwork 1/1 1 1 17h deployment.apps/ibm-mcs-placement 1/1 1 1 17h deployment.apps/ibm-mcs-storage 1/1 1 1 17h deployment.apps/ibm-nginx 3/3 3 3 16h deployment.apps/ibm-nginx-tester 1/1 1 1 16h deployment.apps/usermgmt 3/3 3 3 16h deployment.apps/zen-audit 2/2 2 2 16h deployment.apps/zen-core 3/3 3 3 16h deployment.apps/zen-core-api 3/3 3 3 16h deployment.apps/zen-watchdog 2/2 2 2 16h deployment.apps/zen-watcher 1/1 1 1 16h NAME READY AGE statefulset.apps/zen-minio 3/3 17h NAME STATUS VOLUME CAPACITY ACCESS MODES STORAGECLASS AGE persistentvolumeclaim/export-zen-minio-0 Bound pvc-b2a2a729-13c1-4e7f-b672-0b5efc6aa40a 20Gi RWO ibmc-block-gold 17h persistentvolumeclaim/export-zen-minio-1 Bound pvc-7e772a3a-8849-4291-8e14-501f49e79182 20Gi RWO ibmc-block-gold 17h persistentvolumeclaim/export-zen-minio-2 Bound pvc-e0dd1dc-916d-4b15-9d9c-351db0a2b47f 20Gi RWO ibmc-block-gold 17h persistentvolumeclaim/ibm-cs-postgres-backup Bound pvc-ef788b99-784f-4531-a1b3-12611f112551 20Gi RWO ibmc-block-gold 16h persistentvolumeclaim/ibm-zen-objectstore-backup-pvc Bound pvc-d5e61dcf-65a3-4930-9cbf-ab80d04dda00 20Gi RWO ibmc-block-gold 16h persistentvolumeclaim/zen-metastore-edb-1 Bound pvc-19d44f17-05ab-4dc0-bb5d-1b5f15ffd201 20Gi RWO ibmc-block-gold 17h persistentvolumeclaim/zen-metastore-edb-2 Bound pvc-741ea444-b6f0-44ff-a123-bb4615d97381 20Gi RWO ibmc-block-gold 17h Tip You can retrieve the Initial Cloud Pak for Data password from the admin-user-details secret: oc -n ibm-cpd get secret admin-user-details -o jsonpath="{.data.initial_admin_password}" | base64 -d . After installation the role automatically looks up the CPD admin username and password from the cluster secrets ( ibm-iam-bindinfo-platform-auth-idp-credentials for CPD 4.8+, admin-user-details for CPD 4.6) — they are resolved by the role rather than set through its variables. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cpd_product_version No Determined by installed MAS catalog version ibm_entitlement_key Yes None cpd_entitlement_key No Value of ibm_entitlement_key cpd_primary_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected cpd_metadata_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected cpd_operators_namespace No ibm-cpd-operators cpd_instance_namespace No ibm-cpd cpd_scale_config No medium The storage class variables are resolved in this order: explicit variable → storage classes already in use by an existing Ibmcpd CR in cpd_instance_namespace → cluster auto-detection. They are only required when no source yields a value; for production deployments we recommend always setting them explicitly. When updating or upgrading an existing CP4D instance the same storage classes are read back from the existing CR, so these variables do not need to be re-provided. Installation ¤ cpd_product_version ¤ Cloud Pak for Data release version to install — 5.2.0 (OLM), 5.3.1 (platform via OLM, services via Helm), or 5.4.0 (Helm). The version determines the Zen/Control Plane version and the features and compatibility requirements. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_PRODUCT_VERSION Default: Determined by installed MAS catalog version If not set, the version is determined by the installed Maximo Operator Catalog, or the CP4D version supported by the latest released MAS catalog when the catalog cannot be found. It also determines the compatible CPD service versions and the available cpd_scale_config options; see CP4D Operator and operand versions for version-specific details. ibm_entitlement_key ¤ IBM entitlement key for accessing container images — obtain from the IBM Container Library ; it must have valid entitlement for CP4D. Required Environment Variable: IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Provides authentication to IBM Container Registry for pulling CP4D container images; without a valid key, image pulls will fail and CP4D installation cannot proceed. Keep the key secure and do not commit it to source control — it can be overridden for CP4D-specific scenarios with cpd_entitlement_key . cpd_entitlement_key ¤ CP4D-specific entitlement key override (primarily for development). Optional Environment Variable: CPD_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: Value of ibm_entitlement_key When set, this key is used instead of ibm_entitlement_key for CP4D image pulls. Most deployments should use ibm_entitlement_key only; this override is primarily for development scenarios where different keys are needed for different components. Storage ¤ cpd_primary_storage_class ¤ Primary storage class for CP4D — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for shared file storage. Required when auto-detection does not find a known storage class Environment Variable: CPD_PRIMARY_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Read back from an existing Ibmcpd CR ( spec.storageClass , falling back to spec.fileStorageClass ), then auto-detected ( ibmc-file-gold-gid , ocs-storagecluster-cephfs , or azurefiles-premium ) CP4D uses this for shared file storage across pods; a storage class that does not support RWX will cause the deployment to fail. When an existing Ibmcpd CR is present (update/upgrade scenarios) the storage class already in use is preferred over cluster auto-detection, so the value does not need to be re-provided. See CP4D Storage Considerations for details. cpd_metadata_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the CP4D Zen metadata database — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode for block storage, which typically provides better performance for databases. Required when auto-detection does not find a known storage class Environment Variable: CPD_METADATA_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Read back from an existing Ibmcpd CR ( spec.zenCoreMetadbStorageClass , falling back to spec.blockStorageClass ), then auto-detected ( ibmc-block-gold , ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd , or managed-premium ) The Zen metadata database uses this for persistent storage; a storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. When an existing Ibmcpd CR is present (update/upgrade scenarios) the storage class already in use is preferred over cluster auto-detection, so the value does not need to be re-provided. Namespaces ¤ cpd_operators_namespace ¤ Namespace for the CP4D operators installation — any valid Kubernetes namespace name, and must be different from cpd_instance_namespace . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_OPERATORS_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-cpd-operators All CP4D operators (platform, zen, common services, etc.) are installed in this namespace. CP4D uses a specialized installation model with operators in one namespace and instance workloads in another, which provides better isolation and management. cpd_instance_namespace ¤ Namespace for the CP4D instance workloads (Zen, MinIO, PostgreSQL, services) — any valid Kubernetes namespace name, and must be different from cpd_operators_namespace . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-cpd Operators in cpd_operators_namespace watch and manage resources in this namespace. This separation provides better isolation and follows CP4D best practices. Sizing ¤ cpd_scale_config ¤ Resource scaling configuration for the CP4D instance — small (development/test environments), medium (standard production deployments, default), or large (high-capacity production environments). Optional Environment Variable: CPD_SCALE_CONFIG Default: medium Determines resource requests/limits and replica counts for CP4D components; larger scales require more cluster resources but provide better performance and capacity. Available scale options may vary by cpd_product_version — see Managing resources for detailed resource requirements per scale configuration, and ensure your cluster has sufficient resources. Example Playbook ¤ Install Cloud Pak for Data 5.2.0 ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cpd_product_version: 5.2.0 cpd_primary_storage_class: ibmc-file-gold-gid cpd_metadata_storage_class: ibmc-block-gold roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cp4d Run Role Playbook ¤ export CPD_PRODUCT_VERSION=5.2.0 export CPD_PRIMARY_STORAGE_CLASS=ibmc-file-gold-gid export CPD_METADATA_STORAGE_CLASS=ibmc-block-gold export IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY=xxxxx ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

Cloud Pak for Data will be configured as a specialized installation Info A specialized installation allows a user with project administrator permissions to install the software after a cluster administrator completes the initial cluster setup. A specialized installation also facilitates strict division between Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform projects (Kubernetes namespaces). In a specialized installation, the IBM Cloud Pak foundational services operators are installed in the ibm-common-services project and the Cloud Pak for Data operators are installed in a separate project (typically cpd-operators). Each project has a dedicated: Operator group, which specifies the OwnNamespace installation mode NamespaceScope Operator, which allows the operators in the project to manage operators and service workloads in specific projects In this way, you can specify different settings for the IBM Cloud Pak foundational services and for the Cloud Pak for Data operators. Currently supported Cloud Pak for Data release versions are: 5.2.0 (installed via OLM) 5.3.1 (platform installed via OLM, services installed via Helm) 5.4.0 (installed via Helm) Tip For more information about CPD versioning, see IBM Cloud Pak for data Operator and operand versions

docs.text: Users can choose to install a specific version of Cloud Pak for Data by setting CPD_PRODUCT_VERSION variable. However, by default, the version of Cloud Pak for Data will be determined by the version of the Maximo Operator Catalog that is installed in the cluster. docs.text: Variable Required Default cpd_product_version No Determined by installed MAS catalog version ibm_entitlement_key Yes None cpd_entitlement_key No Value of ibm_entitlement_key cpd_primary_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected cpd_metadata_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected cpd_operators_namespace No ibm-cpd-operators cpd_instance_namespace No ibm-cpd cpd_scale_config No medium The storage class variables are resolved in this order: explicit variable → storage classes already in use by an existing Ibmcpd CR in cpd_instance_namespace → cluster auto-detection. They are only required when no source yields a value; for production deployments we recommend always setting them explicitly. When updating or upgrading an existing CP4D instance the same storage classes are read back from the existing CR, so these variables do not need to be re-provided.
docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Cloud Pak for Data release version to install — 5.2.0 (OLM), 5.3.1 (platform via OLM, services via Helm), or 5.4.0 (Helm). The version determines the Zen/Control Plane version and the features and compatibility requirements. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_PRODUCT_VERSION Default: Determined by installed MAS catalog version If not set, the version is determined by the installed Maximo Operator Catalog, or the CP4D version supported by the latest released MAS catalog when the catalog cannot be found. It also determines the compatible CPD service versions and the available cpd_scale_config options; see CP4D Operator and operand versions for version-specific details.
docs.title: cpd_product_version

docs.text: IBM entitlement key for accessing container images — obtain from the IBM Container Library ; it must have valid entitlement for CP4D. Required Environment Variable: IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Provides authentication to IBM Container Registry for pulling CP4D container images; without a valid key, image pulls will fail and CP4D installation cannot proceed. Keep the key secure and do not commit it to source control — it can be overridden for CP4D-specific scenarios with cpd_entitlement_key .
docs.title: ibm_entitlement_key

docs.text: CP4D-specific entitlement key override (primarily for development). Optional Environment Variable: CPD_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: Value of ibm_entitlement_key When set, this key is used instead of ibm_entitlement_key for CP4D image pulls. Most deployments should use ibm_entitlement_key only; this override is primarily for development scenarios where different keys are needed for different components.
docs.title: cpd_entitlement_key

docs.text: Primary storage class for CP4D — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for shared file storage. Required when auto-detection does not find a known storage class Environment Variable: CPD_PRIMARY_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Read back from an existing Ibmcpd CR ( spec.storageClass , falling back to spec.fileStorageClass ), then auto-detected ( ibmc-file-gold-gid , ocs-storagecluster-cephfs , or azurefiles-premium ) CP4D uses this for shared file storage across pods; a storage class that does not support RWX will cause the deployment to fail. When an existing Ibmcpd CR is present (update/upgrade scenarios) the storage class already in use is preferred over cluster auto-detection, so the value does not need to be re-provided. See CP4D Storage Considerations for details.
docs.title: cpd_primary_storage_class

docs.text: Storage class for the CP4D Zen metadata database — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode for block storage, which typically provides better performance for databases. Required when auto-detection does not find a known storage class Environment Variable: CPD_METADATA_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Read back from an existing Ibmcpd CR ( spec.zenCoreMetadbStorageClass , falling back to spec.blockStorageClass ), then auto-detected ( ibmc-block-gold , ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd , or managed-premium ) The Zen metadata database uses this for persistent storage; a storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. When an existing Ibmcpd CR is present (update/upgrade scenarios) the storage class already in use is preferred over cluster auto-detection, so the value does not need to be re-provided.
docs.title: cpd_metadata_storage_class

docs.text: Namespace for the CP4D operators installation — any valid Kubernetes namespace name, and must be different from cpd_instance_namespace . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_OPERATORS_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-cpd-operators All CP4D operators (platform, zen, common services, etc.) are installed in this namespace. CP4D uses a specialized installation model with operators in one namespace and instance workloads in another, which provides better isolation and management.
docs.title: cpd_operators_namespace

docs.text: Namespace for the CP4D instance workloads (Zen, MinIO, PostgreSQL, services) — any valid Kubernetes namespace name, and must be different from cpd_operators_namespace . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-cpd Operators in cpd_operators_namespace watch and manage resources in this namespace. This separation provides better isolation and follows CP4D best practices.
docs.title: cpd_instance_namespace

docs.text: Resource scaling configuration for the CP4D instance — small (development/test environments), medium (standard production deployments, default), or large (high-capacity production environments). Optional Environment Variable: CPD_SCALE_CONFIG Default: medium Determines resource requests/limits and replica counts for CP4D components; larger scales require more cluster resources but provide better performance and capacity. Available scale options may vary by cpd_product_version — see Managing resources for detailed resource requirements per scale configuration, and ensure your cluster has sufficient resources.
docs.title: cpd_scale_config

docs.text: cp4d_service ¤ Install or upgrade a chosen Cloud Pak for Data service. Currently supported Cloud Pak for Data release versions are: 5.2.0 (services installed via OLM) 5.3.1 (services installed via Helm) 5.4.0 (services installed via Helm) The role automatically installs the CPD service operator channel and custom resource version associated with the chosen Cloud Pak for Data release version. For more information about the specific CPD service channels and versions associated with a particular Cloud Pak for Data release, refer to the olm-utils configuration . Maximo tailored installation This role only installs the CPD services that Maximo Application Suite depends on, configured in the specific way that the Maximo team use internally. It does not support further post-install configuration of these services beyond the configuration supported by the role, and it does not support installing or configuring CPD services in any other way. Customers who need CPD services or configuration that this role does not provide can choose to install and manage Cloud Pak for Data (including its services) themselves; the MAS applications will work against any correctly configured CPD instance. When installing and managing CPD yourself, you are responsible for the CPD lifecycle (installation, upgrades, and any configuration you apply). Services Supported ¤ These services can be deployed and configured using this role: Watson Studio required by Predict Watson Machine Learning required by Predict Analytics Services (Apache Spark) required by Predict Application Support For more information on how Predict and HP Utilities make use of Watson Studio, refer to the Predict/HP Utilities documentation . Upgrade ¤ This role also supports seamless CPD service minor version upgrades, as well as patch version upgrades. All you need to do is define cpd_product_version to the version you want to upgrade to, and run this role for the particular CPD service. It's important that before you upgrade CPD services, the CPD Control Plane/Zen is also upgraded to the same release version. For more information about the IBM Cloud Pak for Data upgrade process, refer to the CPD official documentation . Warning The reconcile of many CP4D resources will be marked as Failed multiple times during initial installation, these are misleading status updates , the install is just really slow and the operators can not properly handle this. For example, if you are watching the install of CCS you will see that each rabbitmq-ha pod takes 10-15 minutes to start up and it looks like there is a problem because the pod log will just stop at a certain point. If you see something like this as the last message in the pod log WAL: ra_log_wal init, open tbls: ra_log_open_mem_tables, closed tbls: ra_log_closed_mem_tables be assured that there's nothing wrong, it's just there's a long delay between that message and the next ( starting system coordination ) being logged.
