Service Installation ¤ cpd_service_name ¤ Name of the CPD service to install — valid values are wsl (Watson Studio), wml (Watson Machine Learning), and spark (Analytics Engine powered by Apache Spark). Required Environment Variable: CPD_SERVICE_NAME Default: None cpd_product_version ¤ The Cloud Pak for Data release version (also known as the operand version) of the service to install — valid values are 5.2.0 , 5.3.1 , and 5.4.0 . Required Environment Variable: CPD_PRODUCT_VERSION Default: Defined by the installed MAS catalog version The role automatically selects the operator channel and custom resource version associated with this release version. When upgrading, the CPD Control Plane/Zen must already be upgraded to the same release version. cpd_service_storage_class ¤ Storage class used to set spec.storageClass in all CPD services that use file storage (read-write-many, RWX). Required when the cluster does not provide a detectable default storage class Environment Variable: CPD_SERVICE_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Read back from the existing service CR ( spec.storageClass , falling back to spec.fileStorageClass ), then the existing platform Ibmcpd CR, then auto-detected from the cluster's default storage classes — for example ibmc-file on IBM Cloud or efs on AWS cpd_service_block_storage_class ¤ Storage class used to set spec.blockStorageClass in all CPD services that use block storage (read-write-once, RWO). Required when the cluster does not provide a detectable default storage class Environment Variable: CPD_SERVICE_BLOCK_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Read back from the existing service CR ( spec.blockStorageClass ), then the existing platform Ibmcpd CR, then auto-detected from the cluster's default storage classes — for example ibmc-block on IBM Cloud or gp2 on AWS cpd_instance_namespace ¤ Namespace where the CP4D instance is deployed. For more information, refer to Managing resources in the IBM Cloud Pak for Data documentation. docs.text: cp4d_uninstall ¤ Uninstall IBM Cloud Pak for Data and all its services from an OpenShift cluster. This role provides a clean removal process for CP4D, removing all services, platform components, prerequisites, and optionally namespaces and persistent data. The role supports uninstallation of all CP4D components including Watson Studio, Watson Machine Learning, Analytics Engine (Spark), and the CP4D platform itself. Destructive Operation This role performs destructive operations that cannot be undone. Always backup critical data before running this role. By default, PVCs are preserved, but this can be changed with the cpd_uninstall_delete_pvcs variable. Uninstall Process ¤ The role follows a specific order to ensure clean uninstallation: Services - Watson Studio, Watson Machine Learning, Spark, CCS, DataRefinery Platform - ZenService and Ibmcpd custom resources Prerequisites - CPFS, NamespaceScope, IBM Licensing ODLM Cleanup - OperandRequest, OperandConfig, and OperandRegistry resources in both instance and operators namespaces Subscriptions - All remaining operator subscriptions CSVs - All ClusterServiceVersions Catalog Sources - CP4D-specific catalog sources and ConfigMaps PVCs - Persistent Volume Claims (optional, disabled by default) Namespaces - All CP4D-related namespaces (optional, disabled by default) Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cpd_operators_namespace No ibm-cpd-operators cpd_instance_namespace No ibm-cpd cpd_cs_control_namespace No cs-control cpd_cpfs_namespace No ibm-common-services cpd_ibm_licensing_namespace No ibm-licensing cpd_platform_cr_name No ibmcpd-cr zen_cr_name No lite-cr cpd_uninstall_delete_pvcs No false cpd_uninstall_delete_namespaces No false cpd_uninstall_delete_catalog_sources No true cpd_uninstall_delete_helm_cluster_resources No true cpd_uninstall_wait_timeout No 1200 Namespaces ¤ cpd_operators_namespace ¤ Namespace where the CP4D operators are installed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name that must match the namespace used during CP4D installation. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_OPERATORS_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-cpd-operators The role removes operator subscriptions and related resources from this namespace. cpd_instance_namespace ¤ Namespace where the CP4D instance workloads are deployed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name that must match the namespace used during CP4D installation. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-cpd The role removes all CP4D custom resources and workloads from this namespace. cpd_cs_control_namespace ¤ Namespace for the Common Services control plane — a valid Kubernetes namespace name that must match the namespace used during CP4D installation. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_CS_CONTROL_NAMESPACE Default: cs-control The role removes Common Services CSVs and subscriptions from this namespace. cpd_cpfs_namespace ¤ Namespace for Cloud Pak Foundational Services — a valid Kubernetes namespace name that must match the namespace used during CP4D installation. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_CPFS_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-common-services The role removes CPFS resources (and PVCs, when cpd_uninstall_delete_pvcs is enabled) from this namespace. cpd_ibm_licensing_namespace ¤ Namespace for IBM Licensing — a valid Kubernetes namespace name that must match the namespace used during CP4D installation. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_IBM_LICENSING_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-licensing The role removes IBM Licensing resources from this namespace. Platform Custom Resources ¤ cpd_platform_cr_name ¤ Name of the Ibmcpd custom resource representing the CP4D platform installation — a valid Kubernetes resource name that must match the CR name used during installation. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_PLATFORM_CR_NAME Default: ibmcpd-cr The role deletes the Ibmcpd custom resource with this name during platform uninstallation. zen_cr_name ¤ Name of the ZenService custom resource that manages the CP4D control plane — a valid Kubernetes resource name that must match the CR name used during installation. Optional Environment Variable: ZEN_CR_NAME Default: lite-cr The role deletes the ZenService custom resource with this name during platform uninstallation. Uninstall Options ¤ cpd_uninstall_delete_pvcs ¤ Delete PersistentVolumeClaims during uninstall — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_UNINSTALL_DELETE_PVCS Default: false When false (default), PVCs are preserved so data remains available for potential reinstallation. Warning Setting this to true permanently deletes all CP4D data — PVCs in both cpd_instance_namespace and cpd_cpfs_namespace are removed and the data cannot be recovered. Always backup critical data before enabling this option. cpd_uninstall_delete_namespaces ¤ Delete the CP4D-related namespaces after all resources are uninstalled — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_UNINSTALL_DELETE_NAMESPACES Default: false Set to false to preserve namespaces for troubleshooting or reinstallation (they may contain residual resources). Namespace deletion can take several minutes due to finalizers; the role includes appropriate wait conditions. cpd_uninstall_delete_catalog_sources ¤ Delete the CP4D-specific catalog sources ( cpd-platform , opencloud-operators ) — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_UNINSTALL_DELETE_CATALOG_SOURCES Default: true Set to false if you plan to reinstall CP4D soon; catalog sources can be recreated during reinstallation if needed. cpd_uninstall_delete_helm_cluster_resources ¤ Delete the Helm cluster-scoped resources (CRDs, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding) installed by the CPD 5.3.1 Helm cluster-scoped charts — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: CPD_UNINSTALL_DELETE_HELM_CLUSTER_RESOURCES Default: true Safe to run on any CPD version — resources that do not exist are silently skipped. Set to false only if you want to preserve the CRDs for manual management. cpd_uninstall_wait_timeout ¤ Wait timeout for each resource deletion operation, in seconds — a positive integer. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_UNINSTALL_WAIT_TIMEOUT Default: 1200 (20 minutes) Increase for large CP4D deployments or slow storage; longer timeouts allow more time for resource cleanup but increase total uninstall time. Individual retry loops may have different retry counts and delays beyond this timeout. Example Playbook ¤ Basic Uninstall (Preserve PVCs) ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # Use default namespaces # PVCs will be preserved (default) # Namespaces will be preserved (default) roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cp4d_uninstall Complete Uninstall (Delete Everything) ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cpd_uninstall_delete_pvcs: true # WARNING: Deletes all data cpd_uninstall_delete_namespaces: true cpd_uninstall_delete_catalog_sources: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cp4d_uninstall Uninstall with Custom Namespaces ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cpd_operators_namespace: my-cpd-operators cpd_instance_namespace: my-cpd cpd_uninstall_delete_namespaces: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cp4d_uninstall Uninstall but Preserve Namespaces ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cpd_uninstall_delete_namespaces: false # Keep namespaces cpd_uninstall_delete_pvcs: false # Keep data roles: - ibm.mas_devops.cp4d_uninstall Run Role Playbook ¤ # Basic uninstall (preserve PVCs and namespaces) ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role # Complete uninstall (delete everything) export CPD_UNINSTALL_DELETE_PVCS=true export CPD_UNINSTALL_DELETE_NAMESPACES=true export CPD_UNINSTALL_DELETE_CATALOG_SOURCES=true ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role # Uninstall with custom namespaces export CPD_OPERATORS_NAMESPACE=my-cpd-operators export CPD_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE=my-cpd ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Important Notes ¤ Data Preservation ¤ By default, PVCs are NOT deleted - Your data is preserved Set cpd_uninstall_delete_pvcs: true to permanently delete all data Always backup critical data before uninstalling Idempotency ¤ The role is idempotent and safe to run multiple times If CP4D is not installed, the role will exit gracefully Missing resources are handled without errors Uninstall Time ¤ Complete uninstall typically takes 20-40 minutes Namespace deletion can take additional time due to finalizers The role includes appropriate wait conditions and retries What Gets Removed ¤ All CP4D service custom resources (Watson Studio, WML, Spark) CP4D platform custom resources (ZenService, Ibmcpd) CPFS, NamespaceScope, and IBM Licensing All operator subscriptions and CSVs Custom catalog sources (if enabled) PVCs (if enabled) Namespaces (if enabled) What Does NOT Get Removed ¤ IBM Operator Catalog (shared resource) Certificate Manager (shared resource) External databases or storage Backup data stored outside the cluster Troubleshooting ¤ If resources fail to delete due to finalizers: Check for stuck pods: oc get pods -A | grep -E 'cpd|zen|common-service' Check for stuck finalizers: oc get <resource> -o yaml | grep finalizers Manually remove finalizers if needed (advanced users only) Re-run the role - it's idempotent License ¤ EPL-2.0
docs.title: cp4d_uninstall

docs.text: db2 ¤ This role creates, upgrades, migrates, or manages Db2 instances using the Db2u Operator. When installing Db2, the Db2u operator will be installed into the same namespace as the Db2 instance. IMPORTANT: The Db2uCluster resource is deprecated (replaced by Db2uInstance). This Ansible collection will retain support for Db2uCluster until its eventual EOL. Use the db2u-migration action to migrate existing Db2uCluster deployments to Db2uInstance. If you already have the Db2 operator and Db2 instances running in separate namespaces, this role will migrate the Db2 operators (not the instances) from ibm-common-services to the namespace defined by the db2_namespace property (in case of a new role execution for a Db2 install or Db2 upgrade). A private root CA certificate is created and is used to secure the TLS connections to the database. A Db2 Warehouse cluster will be created along with a public TLS encrypted route to allow external access to the cluster (access is via the ssl-server nodeport port on the *-db2u-engn-svc service). Internal access is via the *-db2u-engn-svc service and port 50001. Both the external route and the internal service use the same server certificate. The private root CA certificate and the server certificate are available from the db2u-ca and db2u-certificate secrets in the Db2 namespace. The default user is db2inst1 and the password is available in the instancepassword secret in the same namespace. You can examine the deployed resources in the Db2 namespace. This example assumes the default namespace db2u : oc -n db2u get db2uinstance NAME STATE MAINTENANCESTATE AGE db2u-db01 Ready None 29m It typically takes 20-30 minutes from the Db2uCluster being created until it is ready. If the Db2uCluster is not ready after that period then check that all the PersistentVolumeClaims in the Db2 namespace are ready and that the pods in the namespace are not stuck in init state. If the c-<db2_instance_name>-db2u-0 pod is running then you can exec into the pod and check the /var/log/db2u.log for any issue. If the mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are provided then the role will generate the JdbcCfg yaml that can be used to configure MAS to connect to this database. It does not apply the yaml to the cluster but does provide you with the yaml files to apply if needed. When upgrading Db2, specify the existing namespace where the Db2uInstance instances exist. All the instances under that namespace will be upgraded to the Db2 version specified. The version of Db2 must match the channel of Db2 being used for the upgrade. db2_v12_upgrade (upgrading from v11 to v12), db2_ldap_password (when db2_ldap_username is set), db2_meta_storage_class and db2_data_storage_class (when the cluster has no default storage classes), mas_instance_id , mas_application_id , mas_backup_dir , and db2_backup_version (backup and restore operations), and the backup_s3_* variables (when backup_vendor is s3 ). Installation and Upgrade ¤ db2u_kind ¤ Db2 deployment type — db2ucluster (deprecated Db2uCluster CR, for maintaining existing deployments only) or db2uinstance (current Db2uInstance CR, recommended for all new deployments). Both types use the same underlying configuration variables. Optional Environment Variable: DB2U_KIND Default: db2ucluster The default of db2ucluster preserves backward compatibility with existing automation and scripts. Strict validation ensures DB2U_KIND matches the existing deployment type — the deployment type of an existing instance cannot be changed, and attempting to change it fails with a clear error message. Warning Db2uCluster is deprecated. Use db2uinstance for all new deployments; existing Db2uCluster deployments continue to work but cannot be automatically converted — use the db2u-migration action to migrate them (see Migrating from Db2uCluster to Db2uInstance ). ibm_common_services_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where IBM Common Services is installed — leave as the default for standard installations, and set only when Common Services is installed in a non-standard namespace. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_COMMON_SERVICES_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-common-services The role uses this namespace to locate the Common Services components shared by the Db2u operator; an incorrect namespace causes the role to fail when accessing them. Works with db2_namespace to manage operator and instance placement. db2_action ¤ Operation to perform on the Db2 database — one of install , upgrade , backup , backup-database , restore , restore-database , or db2u-migration (details below). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ACTION Default: install Valid actions: install (default) — creates a new Db2 operator and instance; when db2_backup_version is provided, installs from backup (instance + database) upgrade — upgrades ALL instances in db2_namespace to db2_version backup — backs up both the instance resources (secrets, certificates, Db2uCluster/Db2uInstance CR, ConfigMaps) and the database; enables full disaster recovery and install-from-backup, but is slower backup-database — backs up only the database data; faster, but restore requires an existing Db2 instance restore — creates a new Db2 operator and instance from the backup of the Db2 instance resources and restores the database data to the created instance restore-database — restores the database to an existing running Db2 instance (does not restore instance resources) db2u-migration — migrates an existing Db2uCluster to Db2uInstance using the db2u_migrate CLI tool (namespace-scoped, requires v12) Related variables by action: db2_version is required for upgrade (and must match the operator channel); db2_instance_name is required for db2u-migration (which Db2uCluster to migrate); db2_backup_version is required for restore / restore-database and optional for backup (defaults to YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS ); override_storageclass controls storage class handling during restore; mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir optionally update the MAS JdbcCfg during migration. Warning The upgrade action upgrades all Db2 instances in db2_namespace — plan accordingly. The db2u-migration action requires the Db2uCluster to be running v12.x; the original Db2uCluster CR is not automatically deleted after migration (see the migration guide for optional cleanup steps). db2_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the Db2u operator and Db2 instances will be deployed — use the default ( db2u ) for standard single-instance deployments, or a custom namespace (e.g. db2u , db2-prod , mas-db2 ) when organizing multiple Db2 deployments. Must match the existing namespace when upgrading Db2 instances. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_NAMESPACE Default: db2u All Db2 resources (operator, instances, secrets, services) are created in this namespace. If the Db2 operator and instances already run in separate namespaces, the role migrates the Db2 operators (not the instances) from ibm-common-services to this namespace during a new install or upgrade. When db2_action=upgrade , all instances in this namespace are upgraded together. db2_channel ¤ Subscription channel for the Db2 Universal Operator, determining which operator version stream you receive and which Db2 engine versions are available — e.g. v2.2 , v3.0 , v3.1 . Leave unset for new installations (the default channel is recommended); when upgrading, the channel must be compatible with db2_version . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CHANNEL Default: Operator package default channel (automatically selected) Channels typically correspond to major Db2 versions. Check the operator package for available channels and their supported versions; changing channels may require operator migration. db2_instance_name ¤ Unique name for the Db2 instance (the Db2uCluster/Db2uInstance resource) — a valid Kubernetes resource name, lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens (e.g. db01 , mas-db , manage-db ), unique within the namespace. Use a descriptive name indicating purpose (e.g. maximo-db , iot-db , manage-db ). Required Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None The name is embedded throughout the Db2 deployment — the CR name, service names (e.g. {instance_name}-db2u-engn-svc ), pod names (e.g. c-{instance_name}-db2u-0 ), and secret names — and is used in the generated JdbcCfg when mas_instance_id is provided. It cannot easily be changed after creation. Also required for the db2u-migration action, to specify which Db2uCluster to migrate. ibm_entitlement_key ¤ IBM Container Library entitlement key for pulling Db2 container images from the IBM Container Registry — obtain it from the IBM Container Library using your IBM ID. Required Environment Variable: IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Without a valid key, Db2 container images cannot be pulled and installation will fail; the key is stored in an image pull secret in the Db2 namespace. The same key is used across all IBM MAS components. Treat it as a credential — keep it secure and do not commit it to source control. db2_dbname ¤ Name of the database to create within the Db2 instance — a valid Db2 database name, uppercase alphanumeric up to 8 characters (e.g. BLUDB , MAXDB , MASDB ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DBNAME Default: BLUDB BLUDB is the standard database name for Db2 Warehouse and most MAS deployments; set a custom name only when organizational standards require it. The name is used in connection strings and the generated JdbcCfg — applications must use this exact name to connect. db2_version ¤ Db2 engine version to use for installation or upgrade — a valid Db2 engine version supported by the operator (e.g. 11.5.8.0 , 11.5.9.0 ). Required when using db2_action=upgrade (specifies the target version) Environment Variable: DB2_VERSION Default: Latest version supported by the installed Db2 operator (auto-detected from the db2u-release configmap) Leave unset for new installations to use the latest supported version. The version must be available in the operator's channel — when upgrading, ALL instances in db2_namespace are upgraded to this version. Supported versions are listed in the db2u-release configmap in the ibm-common-services namespace. db2_license_file ¤ Path to the Db2 Warehouse license file on the local filesystem — an absolute path to a valid license file in .lic format, e.g. /path/to/db2wh.lic . Required when upgrading from Db2 v11 to v12 (with db2_v12_upgrade=true ) Optional for new Db2 installations (Db2 v12 uses a 30-day trial license when not provided) Environment Variable: DB2_LICENSE_FILE Default: None IBM may refer to this file by different names — "Db2 Warehouse license", "Db2 activation key", db2wh.lic , or db2ese.lic ; see Upgrading Db2 from v11 to v12 for an example of the expected file format. Must be combined with db2_v12_upgrade=true and a v12 channel (e.g. v12.0.0-cn1 ). Warning Without a valid license, Db2 v12 operates under a 30-day trial license — when the trial expires the database becomes unavailable. This is especially critical for production systems. db2_v12_upgrade ¤ Explicit opt-in flag required to authorize a major version upgrade from Db2 v11 to v12 — a safety gate ( true / false ) preventing accidental major version upgrades, which are significant and irreversible operations requiring explicit user consent. Required when upgrading from Db2 v11 to v12 Environment Variable: DB2_V12_UPGRADE Default: false Must be combined with db2_license_file and a v12 db2_channel (e.g. v12.0.0-cn1 ). The upgrade fails if the license file is not provided — this is intentional, to prevent a silent downgrade from a full production license to a 30-day trial license. Instance Configuration ¤ db2_type ¤ Db2 instance type, optimized for specific workload patterns — db2wh (data warehouse/analytical queries, recommended for MAS Manage) or db2oltp (online transaction processing with high concurrency). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TYPE Default: db2wh Affects resource allocation and database tuning. Align with db2_workload and db2_table_org . db2_timezone ¤ Server timezone for the Db2 instance, used for timestamp operations and scheduling — a valid timezone code (e.g. GMT , EST , PST , CET , UTC ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TIMEZONE Default: None (the Db2 engine defaults to UTC) Set to the local timezone when all users are in the same timezone. Mismatched timezones between Db2 and applications can cause data inconsistencies. Important If using this Db2 instance with MAS Manage, you must also set MAS_APP_SETTINGS_SERVER_TIMEZONE to the same value to ensure consistent timestamp handling. db2_4k_device_support ¤ Controls support for storage devices with 4K sector sizes — ON (required for most modern storage systems, including OCS and Portworx) or OFF (legacy storage with 512-byte sectors only). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_4K_DEVICE_SUPPORT Default: ON Check your storage specifications if unsure; keep ON unless you have specific legacy storage requirements. Works with the storage class configuration to ensure compatibility. db2_workload ¤ Workload profile for Db2 instance optimization — ANALYTICS (balanced optimization for mixed analytical workloads, suitable for most MAS deployments) or PUREDATA_OLAP (pure data warehouse/OLAP query patterns). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_WORKLOAD Default: ANALYTICS Affects memory allocation, query optimization, and other performance parameters. Align with db2_type and db2_table_org ; change only if you have specific OLAP requirements. db2_table_org ¤ Default table organization for database tables — ROW (row-by-row storage, better for OLTP, updates, and mixed workloads; required by MAS Manage) or COLUMN (column-by-column storage, better for analytical queries and aggregations). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TABLE_ORG Default: ROW This sets the default — individual tables can override it. Align with db2_type and db2_workload ; use COLUMN only for dedicated analytical/reporting databases. LDAP User Management ¤ db2_ldap_username ¤ Custom LDAP username for Db2 authentication, configured in Db2's local LDAP registry and used in the generated MAS JdbcCfg — leave unset to use the default db2inst1 user. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LDAP_USERNAME Default: None (uses the default db2inst1 user) Set when you need a custom database user for MAS connections or when organizational policies require specific usernames. When set, the user is created in Db2's LDAP registry with the necessary database permissions, and db2_ldap_password must also be provided. db2_ldap_password ¤ Password for the LDAP user specified in db2_ldap_username — a strong password string meeting security requirements. Required when db2_ldap_username is set for initial user creation Environment Variable: DB2_LDAP_PASSWORD Default: None The password is stored in Db2's LDAP registry and included in the generated JdbcCfg for MAS. It is required at creation time because db2_rotate_password defaults to false and only works with existing users — it cannot create new users. Keep the password secure and do not commit it to source control. db2_rotate_password ¤ Rotate the password of an existing Db2 LDAP user ( true / false ) by generating a new strong random password and updating both Db2's LDAP registry and the MAS JdbcCfg. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LDAP_ROTATE_PASSWORD Default: False Warning This feature is only for existing users — it fails if the user does not already exist in Db2's LDAP registry, and cannot be used to create new users. Typical workflow — first deployment creates the user with a known password ( db2_ldap_username + db2_ldap_password , db2_rotate_password: false ); subsequent deployments set only db2_ldap_username and db2_rotate_password: true to rotate to an auto-generated password ( db2_ldap_password is not needed during rotation). The auto-generated password is stored securely in Kubernetes secrets and MAS configuration; mas_instance_id is required to update the MAS JDBC configuration. Storage Variables ¤ We recommend reviewing the Db2 documentation about the certified storage options for Db2 on Red Hat OpenShift. Please ensure your storage class meets the specified deployment requirements for Db2uInstance and for Db2uCluster . db2_meta_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the Db2 metadata persistent volume — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for shared access across Db2 pods; typically file-based storage (e.g. ibmc-file-gold , ocs-storagecluster-cephfs ). Required when the cluster has no default RWX storage class (auto-detection fails and the role exits with an error) Environment Variable: DB2_META_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWX storage class (auto-detected) Metadata storage (system catalogs, configuration files, and other operational data) is critical for Db2 operation — a storage class that does not support RWX will cause the deployment to fail. See Db2 certified storage options for supported storage. db2_meta_storage_size ¤ Size of the metadata persistent volume, in Kubernetes storage size format (e.g. 10Gi , 20Gi , 50Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_META_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 10Gi 10Gi is sufficient for most deployments; increase for large-scale deployments with many databases or complex configurations. Metadata storage requirements are typically much smaller than data storage — monitor usage and adjust if the metadata volume fills up. db2_meta_storage_accessmode ¤ Access mode for the metadata storage volume — ReadWriteMany (RWX), required so Db2 metadata is accessible from multiple pods. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_META_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteMany Do not change from the default: Db2 requires RWX access mode for metadata storage, and db2_meta_storage_class must support it. db2_data_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the Db2 user data persistent volume (database tables, indexes, and all user data) — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode; typically high-performance block storage (e.g. ibmc-block-gold , ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ). Required when the cluster has no default RWO storage class (auto-detection fails and the role exits with an error) Environment Variable: DB2_DATA_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected) Choose high-performance storage for production workloads — a storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. See Db2 certified storage options for supported storage. db2_data_storage_size ¤ Size of the user data persistent volume, in Kubernetes storage size format (e.g. 50Gi , 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DATA_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 50Gi 50Gi is suitable for development/test environments and small deployments only — production MAS Manage deployments typically require 500Gi or more. Insufficient data storage causes database operations to fail when the volume fills up; size for expected data volume plus growth, monitor usage, and expand as needed. db2_data_storage_accessmode ¤ Access mode for the user data storage volume — ReadWriteOnce (RWO), the correct mode for Db2 data storage which is accessed by a single pod at a time. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DATA_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce Do not change from the default: Db2 data storage is designed for RWO access mode, and db2_data_storage_class must support it. db2_backup_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the Db2 backup persistent volume — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for shared access during backup operations; typically file-based storage. Set to None to drop the backup storage from the Db2uCluster CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWX storage class (auto-detected) Warning Setting this to None disables backup capability — only do this for non-production environments. Production systems should always have backup storage configured. db2_backup_storage_size ¤ Size of the backup persistent volume, in Kubernetes storage size format (e.g. 50Gi , 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 50Gi The volume stores database backups for disaster recovery and point-in-time recovery. Insufficient backup storage causes backup operations to fail — a common practice is to size it at 2-3x the data storage size, to accommodate multiple full backups plus transaction logs per your retention policy. db2_backup_storage_accessmode ¤ Access mode for the backup storage volume — ReadWriteMany (RWX), required for Db2 backup operations to be accessible from multiple pods. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteMany Do not change from the default: Db2 backup operations require RWX access mode, and db2_backup_storage_class must support it. db2_logs_storage_class ¤ Storage class used for transaction logs — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Set to None to drop the logs storage from the Db2uCluster CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LOGS_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected) db2_logs_storage_size ¤ Size of the transaction logs persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LOGS_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 30Gi db2_logs_storage_accessmode ¤ The access mode for the transaction logs storage — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LOGS_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce db2_temp_storage_class ¤ Storage class used for temporary data — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Set to None to drop the temp storage from the Db2uCluster CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TEMP_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected) db2_temp_storage_size ¤ Size of the temporary persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TEMP_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 10Gi db2_temp_storage_accessmode ¤ The access mode for the temporary storage — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TEMP_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce db2_audit_logs_storage_class ¤ Storage class used for audit logs — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Set to None to drop the audit logs storage from the Db2uInstance CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AUDIT_LOGS_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected) db2_audit_logs_storage_size ¤ Size of the audit logs persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AUDIT_LOGS_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 30Gi db2_audit_logs_storage_accessmode ¤ The access mode for the audit logs storage — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AUDIT_LOGS_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce db2_archivelogs_storage_class ¤ Storage class used for archive logs — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for Db2uInstance and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode for Db2uCluster . Set to None to drop the archivelogs storage from the Db2uInstance CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ARCHIVELOGS_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default storage class (auto-detected; RWX for Db2uInstance , RWO for Db2uCluster ) db2_archivelogs_storage_size ¤ Size of the archive logs persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ARCHIVELOGS_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 30Gi db2_archivelogs_storage_accessmode ¤ The access mode for the storage — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for Db2uInstance and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode for Db2uCluster . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ARCHIVELOGS_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: Dynamically set according to the kind of Db2 ( Db2uInstance or Db2uCluster ) Resource Requests ¤ These variables allow you to customize the resources available to the Db2 pod in your cluster. In most circumstances you will want to set these properties because it is impossible for us to provide a default value that will be appropriate for all users. We have set defaults that are suitable for deploying Db2 onto a dedicated worker node with 4 CPU and 16GB memory. Tip Note that you must take into account the system overhead on any given node when setting these parameters, if you set the requests equal to the number of CPU or amount of memory on your node then the scheduler will not be able to schedule the Db2 pod because not 100% of the worker nodes' resource will be available to pod on that node, even if there's only a single pod on it. Db2 is sensitive to both CPU and memory issues, particularly memory, we recommend setting requests and limits to the same values, ensuring the scheduler always reserves the resources that Db2 expects to be available to it. db2_cpu_requests ¤ Define the Kubernetes CPU request for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CPU_REQUESTS Default: 4000m db2_cpu_limits ¤ Define the Kubernetes CPU limit for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CPU_LIMITS Default: 6000m db2_memory_requests ¤ Define the Kubernetes memory request for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_MEMORY_REQUESTS Default: 8Gi db2_memory_limits ¤ Define the Kubernetes memory limit for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_MEMORY_LIMITS Default: 16Gi Node Label Affinity ¤ Specify both db2_affinity_key and db2_affinity_value to configure requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity with appropriately labelled nodes. db2_affinity_key ¤ Specify the key of a node label to declare affinity with. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AFFINITY_KEY Default: None db2_affinity_value ¤ Specify the value of a node label to declare affinity with. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AFFINITY_VALUE Default: None Node Taint Toleration ¤ Specify db2_tolerate_key , db2_tolerate_value , and db2_tolerate_effect to configure a toleration policy to allow the Db2 instance to be scheduled on nodes with the specified taint. db2_tolerate_key ¤ Specify the key of the taint that is to be tolerated. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TOLERATE_KEY Default: None db2_tolerate_value ¤ Specify the value of the taint that is to be tolerated. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TOLERATE_VALUE Default: None db2_tolerate_effect ¤ Specify the type of taint effect that will be tolerated ( NoSchedule , PreferNoSchedule , or NoExecute ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TOLERATE_EFFECT Default: None Database Configuration Overrides ¤ The following variables overwrite the Db2uCluster default properties for the Db2 configuration sections: spec.environment.database.dbConfig spec.environment.instance.dbmConfig spec.environment.instance.registry db2_database_db_config ¤ Overwrites the Db2uCluster database configuration settings under the spec.environment.database.dbConfig section. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DATABASE_DB_CONFIG Default: Built-in defaults ( db2_default_config.dbConfig ) The built-in defaults set APPLHEAPSZ: 8192 AUTOMATIC and circular logging ( LOGARCHMETH1: OFF , LOGARCHMETH2: OFF ) — see the backup_type variable for how this affects online versus offline backups. db2_instance_dbm_config ¤ Overwrites the Db2uCluster instance database manager configuration settings under the spec.environment.instance.dbmConfig section. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_DBM_CONFIG Default: None (Db2u built-in defaults are used) Important Do not set instance_memory . The Db2 engine does not know Db2 is running inside a container, setting dbmConfig.INSTANCE_MEMORY: automatic will cause it to read the cgroups of the node and potentially go beyond the pod memory limit. Db2U has logic built in to use a normalized percentage that takes into account the memory limit and free memory of the node. db2_instance_registry ¤ Overwrites the Db2uCluster instance registry settings under the spec.environment.instance.registry section. You can define parameters to be included in this section using semicolon separated values. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_REGISTRY Default: Built-in defaults ( db2_default_config.registry ) The built-in defaults set DB2AUTH: OSAUTHDB,ALLOW_LOCAL_FALLBACK,PLUGIN_AUTO_RELOAD , DB2_FMP_RUN_AS_CONNECTED_USER: NO , and DB2_4K_DEVICE_SUPPORT / DB2_WORKLOAD (derived from the db2_4k_device_support and db2_workload variables). Db2 MPP Configuration ¤ Warning Do not use these variables if you intend to use the Db2 instance with IBM Maximo Application Suite; no MAS application supports Db2 MPP db2_mln_count ¤ The number of logical nodes (i.e. database partitions) to create. Note: ensure that the application using this Db2 can support Db2 MPP (which is created when DB2_MLN_COUNT is greater than 1). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_MLN_COUNT Default: 1 db2_num_pods ¤ The number of Db2 pods to create in the instance. Note that db2_num_pods must be less than or equal to db2_mln_count . A single db2u pod can contain multiple logical nodes, so avoid specifying a large number for db2_mln_count while specifying a small number for db2_num_pods ; if in doubt, make db2_mln_count = db2_num_pods . For more information refer to the Db2 documentation . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_NUM_PODS Default: 1 Db2 Add-ons ¤ db2_addons_audit_config ¤ Audit add-on configuration for the Db2 instance, provided as a YAML string. When set, the content is injected into the spec.addOns.audit section of the Db2uInstance custom resource, enabling configuration of the Db2 audit facility add-on. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ADDONS_AUDIT_CONFIG Default: "" MAS Configuration ¤ When both mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are provided the role generates the JdbcCfg YAML that can be used to configure MAS to connect to this database. It does not apply the YAML to the cluster but does provide you with the files to apply if needed. mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier (e.g. inst1 , masinst1 ) — providing this together with mas_config_dir instructs the role to generate a JdbcCfg template for configuring MAS to connect to this database. Optional for JdbcCfg generation; Required for backup and restore operations (identifies the MAS instance associated with the Db2 backup, used for organizing backups and ensuring restore operations target the correct instance) Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Also used by db2_rotate_password to update the MAS JDBC configuration, and optionally by the db2u-migration action to update the MAS JdbcCfg after migration. mas_config_dir ¤ Directory where the generated JdbcCfg YAML files are written — providing this together with mas_instance_id instructs the role to generate the JdbcCfg template for configuring MAS to connect to this database. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The role does not apply the generated YAML to the cluster; it provides the files for you to apply if needed. mas_config_scope ¤ Scope for the generated MAS configuration — supported values are system , ws , app , or wsapp . This is only used when both mas_config_dir and mas_instance_id are set. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_SCOPE Default: system mas_workspace_id ¤ Workspace identifier — only used when both mas_config_dir and mas_instance_id are set, and mas_config_scope is set to either ws or wsapp . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None mas_application_id ¤ MAS application identifier (e.g. manage , iot , monitor ) — used when mas_config_scope is set to either app or wsapp , and required for backup and restore operations (identifies the MAS application that uses this Db2 database, used for organizing backups and database-specific operations). Optional for JdbcCfg generation; Required for backup and restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None Backup and Restore Variables ¤ mas_instance_id and mas_application_id (see MAS Configuration ) are also required for backup and restore operations. mas_backup_dir ¤ Local directory path where backups will be stored or restored from (e.g. /tmp/mas_backups , /backup/db2 ) — must be accessible from the system running the Ansible playbook and have sufficient disk space for database backups. Required for backup and restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None This directory serves as the staging area for all backup and restore operations. Backup files and metadata are stored in subdirectories structured <mas_backup_dir>/backup-<version>-db2u-<app>/ . When backup_vendor is s3 , database backups go to S3 but instance resources still use this directory. db2_backup_version ¤ The backup version timestamp identifier for backup and restore operations, in YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS format (e.g. 20251212-021316 for December 12, 2025 at 02:13:16). Required for the restore and restore-database actions, and when installing Db2 from an existing backup Auto-generated for backup operations Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Auto-generated in format YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS Uniquely identifies a specific backup version, allowing multiple backups to coexist and enabling point-in-time restore operations. Determines the backup directory name ( backup-<version>-db2u-<app> ), is used to locate backup files during restore, and is recorded in the backup metadata file for verification. override_storageclass ¤ Controls whether to override storage classes during Db2 installation from backup ( true / false ). Only used in Db2 instance restore. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_STORAGECLASS Default: false When true , uses custom_storage_class_rwo and custom_storage_class_rwx if set (otherwise cluster default storage classes) instead of the backup metadata values — useful when restoring to a different cluster or when the original storage classes are not available in the target cluster. When false , uses the storage classes from the backup metadata (original instance configuration). custom_storage_class_rwo ¤ Custom ReadWriteOnce (RWO) storage class for Db2 restore operations — a valid storage class name available in the target cluster, e.g. ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWO Default: None When set (with override_storageclass: true ), provides a single storage class override for all RWO PVCs, simplifying configuration when all RWO volumes can use the same storage class. Applies to data, logs, temp, archivelogs, and audit_logs storage; specific Db2 storage class variables take precedence when also set. custom_storage_class_rwx ¤ Custom ReadWriteMany (RWX) storage class for Db2 restore operations — a valid storage class name available in the target cluster, e.g. ocs-storagecluster-cephfs . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWX Default: None When set (with override_storageclass: true ), provides a single storage class override for all RWX PVCs. Applies to meta and backup storage; specific Db2 storage class variables take precedence when also set. backup_type ¤ Type of backup operation to perform on the Db2 database — online (database remains available during backup; recommended for production systems requiring high availability) or offline (database is unavailable during backup; faster completion and works with circular logging). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_TYPE Default: online Important If your Db2 instance has circular logging enabled ( LOGARCHMETH1: OFF and/or LOGARCHMETH2: OFF — the default configuration), you can only use the offline backup type. If archive logging is enabled, you can use either type. Check the LOGARCHMETH1 / LOGARCHMETH2 settings in db2_database_db_config to determine whether online backup is supported. backup_vendor ¤ Storage backend for database backup files only — disk (backups stored locally and copied to mas_backup_dir ) or s3 (backups sent directly to an S3-compatible bucket for cloud-based backups, long-term retention, or disaster recovery). Optional Environment Variable: BACKUP_VENDOR Default: disk Instance resources (secrets, certificates, CRs) are always stored locally in mas_backup_dir , regardless of this setting — only database backup files go to S3. When set to s3 , requires backup_s3_endpoint , backup_s3_bucket , backup_s3_access_key , and backup_s3_secret_key . backup_s3_endpoint ¤ S3-compatible object storage endpoint URL — an HTTPS URL (e.g. https://s3.us-east.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , https://s3.amazonaws.com ) that must be accessible from the Db2 pod. Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT Default: None Supports AWS S3, IBM Cloud Object Storage, MinIO, and other S3-compatible services. Db2 connects to this endpoint to upload/download backup files, so an incorrect endpoint will cause backup/restore failures. backup_s3_bucket ¤ S3 bucket name for storing database backups — a valid S3 bucket name (e.g. mas-db2-backups ). The bucket must exist before running the backup, and the credentials must have read/write permissions on it. Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_BUCKET Default: None Backup files are stored in this bucket under path <backup_version>/ . backup_s3_access_key ¤ S3 access key ID for authentication, used together with backup_s3_secret_key — must have read/write permissions to backup_s3_bucket . Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Invalid credentials cause backup/restore to fail with authentication errors. Store securely using Ansible Vault or environment variables — never commit to version control. backup_s3_secret_key ¤ S3 secret access key for authentication, used together with backup_s3_access_key — must correspond to the access key ID. Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY Default: None Store securely using Ansible Vault or environment variables — never commit to version control. backup_s3_alias ¤ Db2 storage access alias name for the S3 configuration — an internal Db2 identifier for the S3 connection (alphanumeric, no spaces). Optional Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_ALIAS Default: S3DB2COS Only used when backup_vendor is s3 . Usually leave as the default; change only if you need to match existing Db2 storage access configurations — changing this is rarely necessary. Migrating from Db2uCluster to Db2uInstance ¤ The db2u-migration action enables migration of existing Db2uCluster deployments to the current Db2uInstance resource type. This migration is necessary as Db2uCluster is deprecated and will reach end-of-life in future releases. Migration Requirements ¤ Version : Db2uCluster must be running v12.x (migration will fail for v11 or earlier) CLI Tool : The db2u_migrate command-line tool must be available on the machine running the Ansible role Namespace : Migration is namespace-scoped; specify the namespace containing the Db2uCluster No Conflicts : No Db2uInstance with the same name should exist in the namespace Migration Behavior ¤ Non-destructive : The original Db2uCluster CR remains after migration and is not automatically deleted Data Preservation : Database data and configuration are preserved during migration Service Continuity : The migration creates a new Db2uInstance that maintains connectivity to the existing database JdbcCfg Update : Optionally updates MAS JdbcCfg if mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are provided Migration Process ¤ The migration action performs the following steps: Validation : Verifies namespace exists Confirms Db2uCluster exists and is v12.x Checks for Db2uInstance naming conflicts Execution : Runs db2u_migrate --namespace <namespace> --name <name> Monitors command output and handles errors Verification : Waits for Db2uInstance to reach Ready state Waits for Db2uEngine to reach Ready state Optionally updates MAS JdbcCfg Post-Migration : Displays success status Reminds user that Db2uCluster still exists Provides guidance for optional cleanup Usage Example ¤ Basic Migration export DB2_ACTION=db2u-migration export DB2_NAMESPACE=db2u export DB2_INSTANCE_NAME=db2u-db01 ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Migration with MAS JdbcCfg Update export DB2_ACTION=db2u-migration export DB2_NAMESPACE=db2u export DB2_INSTANCE_NAME=db2u-manage export MAS_INSTANCE_ID=inst1 export MAS_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/masconfig ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Post-Migration Steps ¤ Verify Migration Success # Check Db2uInstance status oc get db2uinstance -n db2u # Check Db2uEngine status oc get db2uengine -n db2u # Verify database connectivity oc exec -n db2u c-db2u-db01-db2u-0 -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 connect to BLUDB" Optional: Clean Up Db2uCluster After verifying the migration succeeded and the Db2uInstance is functioning correctly, you may optionally delete the original Db2uCluster: # Delete the Db2uCluster CR (optional) oc delete db2ucluster db2u-db01 -n db2u Note : Only delete the Db2uCluster after thoroughly verifying the migrated Db2uInstance is working correctly. Troubleshooting Migration ¤ Migration Fails: Version Check Error: Migration requires Db2uCluster to be v12.x Current version: 11.5.8.0 Resolution : Upgrade your Db2uCluster to v12 before attempting migration: export DB2_ACTION=upgrade export DB2_VERSION=12.0.0.0 export DB2_CHANNEL=v12.0.0-cn1 ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Migration Fails: Db2uInstance Already Exists Error: Db2uInstance 'db2u-db01' already exists in namespace 'db2u' Resolution : Either delete the existing Db2uInstance or choose a different name: # Option 1: Delete existing instance oc delete db2uinstance db2u-db01 -n db2u # Option 2: Use different name export DB2_INSTANCE_NAME=db2u-db01-migrated Migration Fails: db2u_migrate Command Not Found Error: db2u_migrate: command not found Resolution : Install the db2u_migrate CLI tool on the machine running the Ansible role. Contact IBM support or refer to Db2 operator documentation for installation instructions. ibm.mas_devops.db2 Backup Directory Structure (Disk) ¤ /tmp/masbr/ └── backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-db2u-<app_id>/ ├── data/ │ ├── db2-<app_id>-BLUDB-backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.tar.gz │ └── db2-backup-info.yaml └── resources/ ├── db2uclusters/ ├── secrets/ ├── certificates/ └── issuers/ └── {kind}s/ Database Backup Metadata (db2-backup-info.yaml) ¤ source_db2_backup_version: "20251212-021316" source_db2_backup_timestamp: "20251212021316" source_db2_instance_name: "db2u-manage" source_db2_instance_version: "11.5.8.0-cn7" database: "BLUDB" backup_vendor: "disk" vendor_backup_path: "/mnt/backup/20251212-021316/data" local_backup_path: "/tmp/masbr/backup-20251212-021316-db2u/data/db2-BLUDB-backup-20251212-021316.tar.gz" status: "SUCCESS" Important Considerations ¤ Version Compatibility: The restore operation requires the target Db2 version to match the backup version Always verify version compatibility before attempting a restore Backup Types: If your Db2 instance has circular logging enabled (i.e. LOGARCHMETH1: OFF and/or LOGARCHMETH2: OFF ), you can only use the offline backup type. If your Db2 instance has circular logging disabled, you can use either the online or offline backup type. If you are unsure, you can use the default online backup type. Online Backup : Database remains available during backup (recommended for production) Offline Backup : Database is taken offline during backup (faster but requires downtime) Storage Options: Disk Storage : Backups stored locally and copied to backup directory S3 Storage : Backups stored directly to S3-compatible object storage (no local storage required) Security: Backup files contain sensitive data and credentials Secure the backup directory with appropriate permissions Consider encrypting backup files for long-term storage Performance: Online backups may impact Db2 performance during execution Schedule backups during low-usage periods Monitor Db2 resource utilization during backup Backup and Restore Troubleshooting ¤ Backup Failures ¤ Check Db2 pod logs: oc logs -n <namespace> <db2-pod-name> -c db2u Review backup script logs in the pod: /tmp/db2_backup.log Verify S3 credentials and connectivity (for S3 backups) Ensure sufficient storage space in the backup PVC(/mnt/backup) Issue: Backup fails with "insufficient storage space" Error: SQL2062N An error occurred while accessing media "backup_path" Solution: Check available disk space on the Db2 pod: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- df -h Verify backup storage PVC has sufficient capacity For S3 backups, ensure bucket has adequate space and proper permissions Consider using compression or incremental backups to reduce storage requirements Issue: Backup fails with "database is in use" Error: SQL1035N The database is currently in use. SQLSTATE=57019 Solution: For offline backups, ensure all applications are disconnected Use online backup instead: export DB2_BACKUP_TYPE=online Check active connections: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 list applications" Force disconnect if necessary: db2 force applications all Issue: S3 backup fails with authentication errors Error: Unable to authenticate with S3 endpoint Solution: Verify S3 credentials are correct: BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY and BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY Test S3 connectivity from the Db2 pod Ensure S3 endpoint URL is correct and accessible Check firewall rules and network policies allow S3 access Verify bucket exists and credentials have write permissions Issue: Backup script execution timeout Error: Backup operation timed out after 3600 seconds Solution: Large databases may require extended timeout periods Monitor backup progress: oc logs -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -f Check Db2 performance and resource utilization Consider scheduling backups during low-usage periods For very large databases, use incremental backups Restore Failures ¤ Verify backup version exists and is complete Check Db2 version compatibility Review restore script logs: /tmp/db2_restore_disk.log or /tmp/db2_restore_s3.log Ensure the Db2 instance is running and healthy before database restore For S3 restores, verify S3 connectivity and credentials Issue: Restore fails with version mismatch Error: DB2 version mismatch. Backup version: 11.5.8.0, Target version: 11.5.9.0 Solution: Ensure target Db2 version matches backup version Check backup metadata: cat <backup_dir>/data/db2-backup-info.yaml Install matching Db2 version: export DB2_VERSION=11.5.8.0-cn7 Alternatively, upgrade backup to target version (requires manual intervention) Issue: Restore fails with "database already exists" Error: SQL1005N The database alias "BLUDB" already exists Solution: Drop existing database before restore: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 drop database BLUDB" Or use a different database name during restore Verify database state: db2 list database directory Issue: Restore fails with corrupted backup files Error: SQL2025N The database cannot be restored from backup image Solution: Verify backup file integrity: bash tar -tzf <backup-file>.tar.gz > /dev/null Check backup metadata for status: status: SUCCESS Re-run backup if corruption detected For S3 restores, verify file was completely uploaded Check storage system for hardware errors Issue: Restore fails with insufficient permissions Error: SQL0551N User does not have required authorization Solution: Verify db2inst1 user has proper permissions Check pod security context and service account Ensure restore scripts have execute permissions Review OpenShift security policies (SCC) Issue: S3 restore fails to download backup files Error: Failed to download backup from S3 bucket Solution: Verify S3 credentials have read permissions Check S3 bucket name and path are correct Test S3 connectivity: aws s3 ls s3://<bucket-name>/ Ensure network policies allow outbound S3 access Verify backup files exist in S3 bucket Performance Issues ¤ Issue: Backup taking too long Solution: Use online backups to avoid database downtime Schedule backups during low-usage periods Increase Db2 pod resources (CPU/memory) Use compression to reduce backup size Consider incremental backups for large databases Check network bandwidth for S3 backups Issue: Restore taking too long Solution: Ensure adequate resources allocated to Db2 pod Monitor pod resource utilization during restore Check storage performance (IOPS, throughput) For S3 restores, verify network bandwidth Consider using faster storage classes Validation and Verification ¤ Issue: How to verify backup completed successfully Solution: Check backup metadata file: bash cat <backup_dir>/data/db2-backup-info.yaml Verify status: SUCCESS Verify backup file exists and has reasonable size: bash ls -lh <backup_dir>/data/db2-*.tar.gz For S3 backups, verify files in bucket: bash aws s3 ls s3://<bucket-name>/<backup-version>/ Check Db2 backup history: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 list history backup all for BLUDB" Issue: How to verify restore completed successfully Solution: Check database is online: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 connect to BLUDB" Verify table counts and data integrity: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 'select count(*) from <table_name>'" Check database configuration: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 get db cfg for BLUDB" Review restore logs for errors: bash oc logs -n <namespace> <db2-pod> | grep -i error Diagnostic Commands ¤ Check Db2 pod status: oc get pods -n <namespace> | grep db2 oc describe pod <db2-pod> -n databases" Check backup storage: oc get pvc -n <namespace> oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- df -h /mnt/backup View Db2 diagnostic logs: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- tail -f /var/log/db2u.log oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- cat /database/config/db2inst1/sqllib/db2dump/db2diag.log Check S3 configuration (if using S3): oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 list storage access" Getting Help ¤ If you encounter issues not covered in this troubleshooting guide: Check Db2 logs : Review /var/log/db2u.log and db2diag.log for detailed error messages Review backup metadata : Check db2-backup-info.yaml for backup details and status Verify prerequisites : Ensure all required variables are set correctly Test connectivity : Verify network access to storage (S3 or PVC) Check resources : Ensure adequate CPU, memory, and storage are available Open an issue : Report problems at the project repository with logs and configuration details Upgrading Db2 from v11 to v12 ¤ Upgrading from Db2 v11 to v12 is a major version change that requires explicit opt-in and a valid Db2 Warehouse license. Without a license, Db2 v12 will operate under a 30-day trial license — this will cause your production system to go offline after expiry . Prerequisites ¤ A valid Db2 Warehouse license file ( .lic format) — see Db2 v12 License File Format below The db2_v12_upgrade flag set to true A v12 target channel (e.g., v12.0.0-cn1 ) Required Variables ¤ Variable Environment Variable Description db2_v12_upgrade DB2_V12_UPGRADE Must be true to authorize the upgrade db2_license_file DB2_LICENSE_FILE Path to the Db2 v12 license file db2_channel DB2_CHANNEL Target v12 channel (e.g., v12.0.0-cn1 ) db2_namespace DB2_NAMESPACE Namespace containing the Db2 instances to upgrade Example Usage ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: db2_action: upgrade db2_namespace: db2u db2_channel: v12.0.0-cn1 db2_v12_upgrade: true db2_license_file: /path/to/db2wh.lic roles: - ibm.mas_devops.db2 Or using environment variables: export DB2_ACTION=upgrade export DB2_NAMESPACE=db2u export DB2_CHANNEL=v12.0.0-cn1 export DB2_V12_UPGRADE=true export DB2_LICENSE_FILE=/path/to/db2wh.lic ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.oneclick_upgrade_db2 Db2 v12 License File Format ¤ IBM distributes the Db2 Warehouse license under several names — you may have received it as db2wh.lic , db2ese.lic , db2aese.lic , or simply as an "activation key" or "entitlement file". The file is a plain-text file with the following structure: [LicenseCertificate] CheckSum=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX TimeStamp=YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS PasswordVersion=5 VendorName=IBM Corporation VendorPassword=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX ProductName=IBM Db2 Warehouse ProductID=5765-F41 ProductVersion=12.0 ProductAnnotation= LicenseType=Permanent ... Note This is a sample structure only — not a real license. Use it to verify that the file you have from IBM matches this format. The file should contain [LicenseCertificate] as the first line and include ProductName=IBM Db2 Warehouse or similar. If your file looks significantly different, you may have the wrong entitlement file. What Happens Without a License ¤ If db2_license_file is not provided when upgrading to v12, the role will fail immediately with a clear error message. This is intentional — it prevents a silent downgrade from a full production license to a 30-day trial license, which would cause your database to go offline after the trial period expires. Note New installations ( db2_action=install ) do not require a license file. Only upgrades from v11 to v12 enforce this requirement. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: db2_action: install db2_instance_name: db2u-manage db2_namespace: db2u db2_meta_storage_class: ocs-storagecluster-cephfs db2_data_storage_class: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ibm_entitlement_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY') }}" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.db2 Run Role Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can easily run the role standalone using the run_role playbook provided. export DB2_ACTION=install export DB2_INSTANCE_NAME=db2u-manage export DB2_NAMESPACE=db2u export DB2_META_STORAGE_CLASS=ocs-storagecluster-cephfs export DB2_DATA_STORAGE_CLASS=ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd export IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY=xxx ROLE_NAME=db2 ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: This role creates, upgrades, migrates, or manages Db2 instances using the Db2u Operator. When installing Db2, the Db2u operator will be installed into the same namespace as the Db2 instance. IMPORTANT: The Db2uCluster resource is deprecated (replaced by Db2uInstance). This Ansible collection will retain support for Db2uCluster until its eventual EOL. Use the db2u-migration action to migrate existing Db2uCluster deployments to Db2uInstance. If you already have the Db2 operator and Db2 instances running in separate namespaces, this role will migrate the Db2 operators (not the instances) from ibm-common-services to the namespace defined by the db2_namespace property (in case of a new role execution for a Db2 install or Db2 upgrade). A private root CA certificate is created and is used to secure the TLS connections to the database. A Db2 Warehouse cluster will be created along with a public TLS encrypted route to allow external access to the cluster (access is via the ssl-server nodeport port on the *-db2u-engn-svc service). Internal access is via the *-db2u-engn-svc service and port 50001. Both the external route and the internal service use the same server certificate. The private root CA certificate and the server certificate are available from the db2u-ca and db2u-certificate secrets in the Db2 namespace. The default user is db2inst1 and the password is available in the instancepassword secret in the same namespace. You can examine the deployed resources in the Db2 namespace. This example assumes the default namespace db2u : oc -n db2u get db2uinstance NAME STATE MAINTENANCESTATE AGE db2u-db01 Ready None 29m It typically takes 20-30 minutes from the Db2uCluster being created until it is ready. If the Db2uCluster is not ready after that period then check that all the PersistentVolumeClaims in the Db2 namespace are ready and that the pods in the namespace are not stuck in init state. If the c-<db2_instance_name>-db2u-0 pod is running then you can exec into the pod and check the /var/log/db2u.log for any issue. If the mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are provided then the role will generate the JdbcCfg yaml that can be used to configure MAS to connect to this database. It does not apply the yaml to the cluster but does provide you with the yaml files to apply if needed. When upgrading Db2, specify the existing namespace where the Db2uInstance instances exist. All the instances under that namespace will be upgraded to the Db2 version specified. The version of Db2 must match the channel of Db2 being used for the upgrade.
docs.title: db2
