docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Db2 deployment type — db2ucluster (deprecated Db2uCluster CR, for maintaining existing deployments only) or db2uinstance (current Db2uInstance CR, recommended for all new deployments). Both types use the same underlying configuration variables. Optional Environment Variable: DB2U_KIND Default: db2ucluster The default of db2ucluster preserves backward compatibility with existing automation and scripts. Strict validation ensures DB2U_KIND matches the existing deployment type — the deployment type of an existing instance cannot be changed, and attempting to change it fails with a clear error message. Warning Db2uCluster is deprecated. Use db2uinstance for all new deployments; existing Db2uCluster deployments continue to work but cannot be automatically converted — use the db2u-migration action to migrate them (see Migrating from Db2uCluster to Db2uInstance ).
docs.title: db2u_kind

docs.text: OpenShift namespace where IBM Common Services is installed — leave as the default for standard installations, and set only when Common Services is installed in a non-standard namespace. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_COMMON_SERVICES_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-common-services The role uses this namespace to locate the Common Services components shared by the Db2u operator; an incorrect namespace causes the role to fail when accessing them. Works with db2_namespace to manage operator and instance placement.
docs.title: ibm_common_services_namespace

docs.text: Operation to perform on the Db2 database — one of install , upgrade , backup , backup-database , restore , restore-database , or db2u-migration (details below). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ACTION Default: install Valid actions: install (default) — creates a new Db2 operator and instance; when db2_backup_version is provided, installs from backup (instance + database) upgrade — upgrades ALL instances in db2_namespace to db2_version backup — backs up both the instance resources (secrets, certificates, Db2uCluster/Db2uInstance CR, ConfigMaps) and the database; enables full disaster recovery and install-from-backup, but is slower backup-database — backs up only the database data; faster, but restore requires an existing Db2 instance restore — creates a new Db2 operator and instance from the backup of the Db2 instance resources and restores the database data to the created instance restore-database — restores the database to an existing running Db2 instance (does not restore instance resources) db2u-migration — migrates an existing Db2uCluster to Db2uInstance using the db2u_migrate CLI tool (namespace-scoped, requires v12) Related variables by action: db2_version is required for upgrade (and must match the operator channel); db2_instance_name is required for db2u-migration (which Db2uCluster to migrate); db2_backup_version is required for restore / restore-database and optional for backup (defaults to YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS ); override_storageclass controls storage class handling during restore; mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir optionally update the MAS JdbcCfg during migration. Warning The upgrade action upgrades all Db2 instances in db2_namespace — plan accordingly. The db2u-migration action requires the Db2uCluster to be running v12.x; the original Db2uCluster CR is not automatically deleted after migration (see the migration guide for optional cleanup steps).
docs.title: db2_action

docs.text: OpenShift namespace where the Db2u operator and Db2 instances will be deployed — use the default ( db2u ) for standard single-instance deployments, or a custom namespace (e.g. db2u , db2-prod , mas-db2 ) when organizing multiple Db2 deployments. Must match the existing namespace when upgrading Db2 instances. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_NAMESPACE Default: db2u All Db2 resources (operator, instances, secrets, services) are created in this namespace. If the Db2 operator and instances already run in separate namespaces, the role migrates the Db2 operators (not the instances) from ibm-common-services to this namespace during a new install or upgrade. When db2_action=upgrade , all instances in this namespace are upgraded together.
docs.title: db2_namespace

docs.text: Subscription channel for the Db2 Universal Operator, determining which operator version stream you receive and which Db2 engine versions are available — e.g. v2.2 , v3.0 , v3.1 . Leave unset for new installations (the default channel is recommended); when upgrading, the channel must be compatible with db2_version . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CHANNEL Default: Operator package default channel (automatically selected) Channels typically correspond to major Db2 versions. Check the operator package for available channels and their supported versions; changing channels may require operator migration.
docs.title: db2_channel

docs.text: Unique name for the Db2 instance (the Db2uCluster/Db2uInstance resource) — a valid Kubernetes resource name, lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens (e.g. db01 , mas-db , manage-db ), unique within the namespace. Use a descriptive name indicating purpose (e.g. maximo-db , iot-db , manage-db ). Required Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None The name is embedded throughout the Db2 deployment — the CR name, service names (e.g. {instance_name}-db2u-engn-svc ), pod names (e.g. c-{instance_name}-db2u-0 ), and secret names — and is used in the generated JdbcCfg when mas_instance_id is provided. It cannot easily be changed after creation. Also required for the db2u-migration action, to specify which Db2uCluster to migrate.
docs.title: db2_instance_name

docs.text: IBM Container Library entitlement key for pulling Db2 container images from the IBM Container Registry — obtain it from the IBM Container Library using your IBM ID. Required Environment Variable: IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Without a valid key, Db2 container images cannot be pulled and installation will fail; the key is stored in an image pull secret in the Db2 namespace. The same key is used across all IBM MAS components. Treat it as a credential — keep it secure and do not commit it to source control.
docs.title: ibm_entitlement_key

docs.text: Name of the database to create within the Db2 instance — a valid Db2 database name, uppercase alphanumeric up to 8 characters (e.g. BLUDB , MAXDB , MASDB ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DBNAME Default: BLUDB BLUDB is the standard database name for Db2 Warehouse and most MAS deployments; set a custom name only when organizational standards require it. The name is used in connection strings and the generated JdbcCfg — applications must use this exact name to connect.
docs.title: db2_dbname

docs.text: Db2 engine version to use for installation or upgrade — a valid Db2 engine version supported by the operator (e.g. 11.5.8.0 , 11.5.9.0 ). Required when using db2_action=upgrade (specifies the target version) Environment Variable: DB2_VERSION Default: Latest version supported by the installed Db2 operator (auto-detected from the db2u-release configmap) Leave unset for new installations to use the latest supported version. The version must be available in the operator's channel — when upgrading, ALL instances in db2_namespace are upgraded to this version. Supported versions are listed in the db2u-release configmap in the ibm-common-services namespace.
docs.title: db2_version

docs.text: Path to the Db2 Warehouse license file on the local filesystem — an absolute path to a valid license file in .lic format, e.g. /path/to/db2wh.lic . Required when upgrading from Db2 v11 to v12 (with db2_v12_upgrade=true ) Optional for new Db2 installations (Db2 v12 uses a 30-day trial license when not provided) Environment Variable: DB2_LICENSE_FILE Default: None IBM may refer to this file by different names — "Db2 Warehouse license", "Db2 activation key", db2wh.lic , or db2ese.lic ; see Upgrading Db2 from v11 to v12 for an example of the expected file format. Must be combined with db2_v12_upgrade=true and a v12 channel (e.g. v12.0.0-cn1 ). Warning Without a valid license, Db2 v12 operates under a 30-day trial license — when the trial expires the database becomes unavailable. This is especially critical for production systems.
docs.title: db2_license_file

docs.text: Explicit opt-in flag required to authorize a major version upgrade from Db2 v11 to v12 — a safety gate ( true / false ) preventing accidental major version upgrades, which are significant and irreversible operations requiring explicit user consent. Required when upgrading from Db2 v11 to v12 Environment Variable: DB2_V12_UPGRADE Default: false Must be combined with db2_license_file and a v12 db2_channel (e.g. v12.0.0-cn1 ). The upgrade fails if the license file is not provided — this is intentional, to prevent a silent downgrade from a full production license to a 30-day trial license.
docs.title: db2_v12_upgrade

docs.text: Db2 instance type, optimized for specific workload patterns — db2wh (data warehouse/analytical queries, recommended for MAS Manage) or db2oltp (online transaction processing with high concurrency). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TYPE Default: db2wh Affects resource allocation and database tuning. Align with db2_workload and db2_table_org .
docs.title: db2_type

docs.text: Server timezone for the Db2 instance, used for timestamp operations and scheduling — a valid timezone code (e.g. GMT , EST , PST , CET , UTC ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TIMEZONE Default: None (the Db2 engine defaults to UTC) Set to the local timezone when all users are in the same timezone. Mismatched timezones between Db2 and applications can cause data inconsistencies. Important If using this Db2 instance with MAS Manage, you must also set MAS_APP_SETTINGS_SERVER_TIMEZONE to the same value to ensure consistent timestamp handling.
docs.title: db2_timezone

docs.text: Controls support for storage devices with 4K sector sizes — ON (required for most modern storage systems, including OCS and Portworx) or OFF (legacy storage with 512-byte sectors only). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_4K_DEVICE_SUPPORT Default: ON Check your storage specifications if unsure; keep ON unless you have specific legacy storage requirements. Works with the storage class configuration to ensure compatibility.
docs.title: db2_4k_device_support

docs.text: Workload profile for Db2 instance optimization — ANALYTICS (balanced optimization for mixed analytical workloads, suitable for most MAS deployments) or PUREDATA_OLAP (pure data warehouse/OLAP query patterns). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_WORKLOAD Default: ANALYTICS Affects memory allocation, query optimization, and other performance parameters. Align with db2_type and db2_table_org ; change only if you have specific OLAP requirements.
docs.title: db2_workload

docs.text: Default table organization for database tables — ROW (row-by-row storage, better for OLTP, updates, and mixed workloads; required by MAS Manage) or COLUMN (column-by-column storage, better for analytical queries and aggregations). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TABLE_ORG Default: ROW This sets the default — individual tables can override it. Align with db2_type and db2_workload ; use COLUMN only for dedicated analytical/reporting databases.
docs.title: db2_table_org

docs.text: Custom LDAP username for Db2 authentication, configured in Db2's local LDAP registry and used in the generated MAS JdbcCfg — leave unset to use the default db2inst1 user. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LDAP_USERNAME Default: None (uses the default db2inst1 user) Set when you need a custom database user for MAS connections or when organizational policies require specific usernames. When set, the user is created in Db2's LDAP registry with the necessary database permissions, and db2_ldap_password must also be provided.
docs.title: db2_ldap_username

docs.text: Password for the LDAP user specified in db2_ldap_username — a strong password string meeting security requirements. Required when db2_ldap_username is set for initial user creation Environment Variable: DB2_LDAP_PASSWORD Default: None The password is stored in Db2's LDAP registry and included in the generated JdbcCfg for MAS. It is required at creation time because db2_rotate_password defaults to false and only works with existing users — it cannot create new users. Keep the password secure and do not commit it to source control.
docs.title: db2_ldap_password

docs.text: Rotate the password of an existing Db2 LDAP user ( true / false ) by generating a new strong random password and updating both Db2's LDAP registry and the MAS JdbcCfg. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LDAP_ROTATE_PASSWORD Default: False Warning This feature is only for existing users — it fails if the user does not already exist in Db2's LDAP registry, and cannot be used to create new users. Typical workflow — first deployment creates the user with a known password ( db2_ldap_username + db2_ldap_password , db2_rotate_password: false ); subsequent deployments set only db2_ldap_username and db2_rotate_password: true to rotate to an auto-generated password ( db2_ldap_password is not needed during rotation). The auto-generated password is stored securely in Kubernetes secrets and MAS configuration; mas_instance_id is required to update the MAS JDBC configuration.
docs.title: db2_rotate_password

docs.text: We recommend reviewing the Db2 documentation about the certified storage options for Db2 on Red Hat OpenShift. Please ensure your storage class meets the specified deployment requirements for Db2uInstance and for Db2uCluster .
docs.title: Storage Variables

docs.text: Storage class for the Db2 metadata persistent volume — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for shared access across Db2 pods; typically file-based storage (e.g. ibmc-file-gold , ocs-storagecluster-cephfs ). Required when the cluster has no default RWX storage class (auto-detection fails and the role exits with an error) Environment Variable: DB2_META_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWX storage class (auto-detected) Metadata storage (system catalogs, configuration files, and other operational data) is critical for Db2 operation — a storage class that does not support RWX will cause the deployment to fail. See Db2 certified storage options for supported storage.
docs.title: db2_meta_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the metadata persistent volume, in Kubernetes storage size format (e.g. 10Gi , 20Gi , 50Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_META_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 10Gi 10Gi is sufficient for most deployments; increase for large-scale deployments with many databases or complex configurations. Metadata storage requirements are typically much smaller than data storage — monitor usage and adjust if the metadata volume fills up.
docs.title: db2_meta_storage_size

docs.text: Access mode for the metadata storage volume — ReadWriteMany (RWX), required so Db2 metadata is accessible from multiple pods. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_META_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteMany Do not change from the default: Db2 requires RWX access mode for metadata storage, and db2_meta_storage_class must support it.
docs.title: db2_meta_storage_accessmode

docs.text: Storage class for the Db2 user data persistent volume (database tables, indexes, and all user data) — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode; typically high-performance block storage (e.g. ibmc-block-gold , ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ). Required when the cluster has no default RWO storage class (auto-detection fails and the role exits with an error) Environment Variable: DB2_DATA_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected) Choose high-performance storage for production workloads — a storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. See Db2 certified storage options for supported storage.
docs.title: db2_data_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the user data persistent volume, in Kubernetes storage size format (e.g. 50Gi , 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DATA_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 50Gi 50Gi is suitable for development/test environments and small deployments only — production MAS Manage deployments typically require 500Gi or more. Insufficient data storage causes database operations to fail when the volume fills up; size for expected data volume plus growth, monitor usage, and expand as needed.
docs.title: db2_data_storage_size

docs.text: Access mode for the user data storage volume — ReadWriteOnce (RWO), the correct mode for Db2 data storage which is accessed by a single pod at a time. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DATA_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce Do not change from the default: Db2 data storage is designed for RWO access mode, and db2_data_storage_class must support it.
docs.title: db2_data_storage_accessmode

docs.text: Storage class for the Db2 backup persistent volume — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for shared access during backup operations; typically file-based storage. Set to None to drop the backup storage from the Db2uCluster CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWX storage class (auto-detected) Warning Setting this to None disables backup capability — only do this for non-production environments. Production systems should always have backup storage configured.
docs.title: db2_backup_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the backup persistent volume, in Kubernetes storage size format (e.g. 50Gi , 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 50Gi The volume stores database backups for disaster recovery and point-in-time recovery. Insufficient backup storage causes backup operations to fail — a common practice is to size it at 2-3x the data storage size, to accommodate multiple full backups plus transaction logs per your retention policy.
docs.title: db2_backup_storage_size

docs.text: Access mode for the backup storage volume — ReadWriteMany (RWX), required for Db2 backup operations to be accessible from multiple pods. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteMany Do not change from the default: Db2 backup operations require RWX access mode, and db2_backup_storage_class must support it.
docs.title: db2_backup_storage_accessmode

docs.text: Storage class used for transaction logs — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Set to None to drop the logs storage from the Db2uCluster CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LOGS_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected)
docs.title: db2_logs_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the transaction logs persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LOGS_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 30Gi
docs.title: db2_logs_storage_size

docs.text: The access mode for the transaction logs storage — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_LOGS_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce
docs.title: db2_logs_storage_accessmode

docs.text: Storage class used for temporary data — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Set to None to drop the temp storage from the Db2uCluster CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TEMP_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected)
docs.title: db2_temp_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the temporary persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TEMP_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 10Gi
docs.title: db2_temp_storage_size

docs.text: The access mode for the temporary storage — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TEMP_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce
docs.title: db2_temp_storage_accessmode

docs.text: Storage class used for audit logs — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Set to None to drop the audit logs storage from the Db2uInstance CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AUDIT_LOGS_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default RWO storage class (auto-detected)
docs.title: db2_audit_logs_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the audit logs persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AUDIT_LOGS_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 30Gi
docs.title: db2_audit_logs_storage_size

docs.text: The access mode for the audit logs storage — must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AUDIT_LOGS_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: ReadWriteOnce
docs.title: db2_audit_logs_storage_accessmode

docs.text: Storage class used for archive logs — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for Db2uInstance and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode for Db2uCluster . Set to None to drop the archivelogs storage from the Db2uInstance CR. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ARCHIVELOGS_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster default storage class (auto-detected; RWX for Db2uInstance , RWO for Db2uCluster )
docs.title: db2_archivelogs_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the archive logs persistent volume. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ARCHIVELOGS_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 30Gi
docs.title: db2_archivelogs_storage_size

docs.text: The access mode for the storage — must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for Db2uInstance and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode for Db2uCluster . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ARCHIVELOGS_STORAGE_ACCESSMODE Default: Dynamically set according to the kind of Db2 ( Db2uInstance or Db2uCluster )
docs.title: db2_archivelogs_storage_accessmode

docs.text: These variables allow you to customize the resources available to the Db2 pod in your cluster. In most circumstances you will want to set these properties because it is impossible for us to provide a default value that will be appropriate for all users. We have set defaults that are suitable for deploying Db2 onto a dedicated worker node with 4 CPU and 16GB memory. Tip Note that you must take into account the system overhead on any given node when setting these parameters, if you set the requests equal to the number of CPU or amount of memory on your node then the scheduler will not be able to schedule the Db2 pod because not 100% of the worker nodes' resource will be available to pod on that node, even if there's only a single pod on it. Db2 is sensitive to both CPU and memory issues, particularly memory, we recommend setting requests and limits to the same values, ensuring the scheduler always reserves the resources that Db2 expects to be available to it.
docs.title: Resource Requests

docs.text: Define the Kubernetes CPU request for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CPU_REQUESTS Default: 4000m
docs.title: db2_cpu_requests

docs.text: Define the Kubernetes CPU limit for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CPU_LIMITS Default: 6000m
docs.title: db2_cpu_limits

docs.text: Define the Kubernetes memory request for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_MEMORY_REQUESTS Default: 8Gi
docs.title: db2_memory_requests

docs.text: Define the Kubernetes memory limit for the Db2 pod. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_MEMORY_LIMITS Default: 16Gi
docs.title: db2_memory_limits

docs.text: Specify both db2_affinity_key and db2_affinity_value to configure requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity with appropriately labelled nodes.
docs.title: Node Label Affinity

docs.text: Specify the key of a node label to declare affinity with. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AFFINITY_KEY Default: None
docs.title: db2_affinity_key

docs.text: Specify the value of a node label to declare affinity with. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_AFFINITY_VALUE Default: None
docs.title: db2_affinity_value

docs.text: Specify db2_tolerate_key , db2_tolerate_value , and db2_tolerate_effect to configure a toleration policy to allow the Db2 instance to be scheduled on nodes with the specified taint.
docs.title: Node Taint Toleration

docs.text: Specify the key of the taint that is to be tolerated. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TOLERATE_KEY Default: None
docs.title: db2_tolerate_key

docs.text: Specify the value of the taint that is to be tolerated. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TOLERATE_VALUE Default: None
docs.title: db2_tolerate_value

docs.text: Specify the type of taint effect that will be tolerated ( NoSchedule , PreferNoSchedule , or NoExecute ). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TOLERATE_EFFECT Default: None
docs.title: db2_tolerate_effect

docs.text: The following variables overwrite the Db2uCluster default properties for the Db2 configuration sections: spec.environment.database.dbConfig spec.environment.instance.dbmConfig spec.environment.instance.registry
docs.title: Database Configuration Overrides

docs.text: Overwrites the Db2uCluster database configuration settings under the spec.environment.database.dbConfig section. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DATABASE_DB_CONFIG Default: Built-in defaults ( db2_default_config.dbConfig ) The built-in defaults set APPLHEAPSZ: 8192 AUTOMATIC and circular logging ( LOGARCHMETH1: OFF , LOGARCHMETH2: OFF ) — see the backup_type variable for how this affects online versus offline backups.
docs.title: db2_database_db_config

docs.text: Overwrites the Db2uCluster instance database manager configuration settings under the spec.environment.instance.dbmConfig section. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_DBM_CONFIG Default: None (Db2u built-in defaults are used) Important Do not set instance_memory . The Db2 engine does not know Db2 is running inside a container, setting dbmConfig.INSTANCE_MEMORY: automatic will cause it to read the cgroups of the node and potentially go beyond the pod memory limit. Db2U has logic built in to use a normalized percentage that takes into account the memory limit and free memory of the node.
docs.title: db2_instance_dbm_config

docs.text: Overwrites the Db2uCluster instance registry settings under the spec.environment.instance.registry section. You can define parameters to be included in this section using semicolon separated values. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_REGISTRY Default: Built-in defaults ( db2_default_config.registry ) The built-in defaults set DB2AUTH: OSAUTHDB,ALLOW_LOCAL_FALLBACK,PLUGIN_AUTO_RELOAD , DB2_FMP_RUN_AS_CONNECTED_USER: NO , and DB2_4K_DEVICE_SUPPORT / DB2_WORKLOAD (derived from the db2_4k_device_support and db2_workload variables).
docs.title: db2_instance_registry

docs.text: Warning Do not use these variables if you intend to use the Db2 instance with IBM Maximo Application Suite; no MAS application supports Db2 MPP
docs.title: Db2 MPP Configuration

docs.text: The number of logical nodes (i.e. database partitions) to create. Note: ensure that the application using this Db2 can support Db2 MPP (which is created when DB2_MLN_COUNT is greater than 1). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_MLN_COUNT Default: 1
docs.title: db2_mln_count

docs.text: The number of Db2 pods to create in the instance. Note that db2_num_pods must be less than or equal to db2_mln_count . A single db2u pod can contain multiple logical nodes, so avoid specifying a large number for db2_mln_count while specifying a small number for db2_num_pods ; if in doubt, make db2_mln_count = db2_num_pods . For more information refer to the Db2 documentation . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_NUM_PODS Default: 1
docs.title: db2_num_pods

docs.text: Audit add-on configuration for the Db2 instance, provided as a YAML string. When set, the content is injected into the spec.addOns.audit section of the Db2uInstance custom resource, enabling configuration of the Db2 audit facility add-on. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_ADDONS_AUDIT_CONFIG Default: ""
docs.title: db2_addons_audit_config

docs.text: When both mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are provided the role generates the JdbcCfg YAML that can be used to configure MAS to connect to this database. It does not apply the YAML to the cluster but does provide you with the files to apply if needed.
docs.title: MAS Configuration

docs.text: MAS instance identifier (e.g. inst1 , masinst1 ) — providing this together with mas_config_dir instructs the role to generate a JdbcCfg template for configuring MAS to connect to this database. Optional for JdbcCfg generation; Required for backup and restore operations (identifies the MAS instance associated with the Db2 backup, used for organizing backups and ensuring restore operations target the correct instance) Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Also used by db2_rotate_password to update the MAS JDBC configuration, and optionally by the db2u-migration action to update the MAS JdbcCfg after migration.
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: Directory where the generated JdbcCfg YAML files are written — providing this together with mas_instance_id instructs the role to generate the JdbcCfg template for configuring MAS to connect to this database. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The role does not apply the generated YAML to the cluster; it provides the files for you to apply if needed.
docs.title: mas_config_dir

docs.text: Scope for the generated MAS configuration — supported values are system , ws , app , or wsapp . This is only used when both mas_config_dir and mas_instance_id are set. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_SCOPE Default: system
docs.title: mas_config_scope

docs.text: Workspace identifier — only used when both mas_config_dir and mas_instance_id are set, and mas_config_scope is set to either ws or wsapp . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None
docs.title: mas_workspace_id

docs.text: MAS application identifier (e.g. manage , iot , monitor ) — used when mas_config_scope is set to either app or wsapp , and required for backup and restore operations (identifies the MAS application that uses this Db2 database, used for organizing backups and database-specific operations). Optional for JdbcCfg generation; Required for backup and restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None
docs.title: mas_application_id

docs.text: mas_instance_id and mas_application_id (see MAS Configuration ) are also required for backup and restore operations.
docs.title: Backup and Restore Variables

docs.text: Local directory path where backups will be stored or restored from (e.g. /tmp/mas_backups , /backup/db2 ) — must be accessible from the system running the Ansible playbook and have sufficient disk space for database backups. Required for backup and restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None This directory serves as the staging area for all backup and restore operations. Backup files and metadata are stored in subdirectories structured <mas_backup_dir>/backup-<version>-db2u-<app>/ . When backup_vendor is s3 , database backups go to S3 but instance resources still use this directory.
docs.title: mas_backup_dir

docs.text: The backup version timestamp identifier for backup and restore operations, in YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS format (e.g. 20251212-021316 for December 12, 2025 at 02:13:16). Required for the restore and restore-database actions, and when installing Db2 from an existing backup Auto-generated for backup operations Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Auto-generated in format YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS Uniquely identifies a specific backup version, allowing multiple backups to coexist and enabling point-in-time restore operations. Determines the backup directory name ( backup-<version>-db2u-<app> ), is used to locate backup files during restore, and is recorded in the backup metadata file for verification.
docs.title: db2_backup_version

docs.text: Controls whether to override storage classes during Db2 installation from backup ( true / false ). Only used in Db2 instance restore. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_STORAGECLASS Default: false When true , uses custom_storage_class_rwo and custom_storage_class_rwx if set (otherwise cluster default storage classes) instead of the backup metadata values — useful when restoring to a different cluster or when the original storage classes are not available in the target cluster. When false , uses the storage classes from the backup metadata (original instance configuration).
docs.title: override_storageclass

docs.text: Custom ReadWriteOnce (RWO) storage class for Db2 restore operations — a valid storage class name available in the target cluster, e.g. ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWO Default: None When set (with override_storageclass: true ), provides a single storage class override for all RWO PVCs, simplifying configuration when all RWO volumes can use the same storage class. Applies to data, logs, temp, archivelogs, and audit_logs storage; specific Db2 storage class variables take precedence when also set.
docs.title: custom_storage_class_rwo

docs.text: Custom ReadWriteMany (RWX) storage class for Db2 restore operations — a valid storage class name available in the target cluster, e.g. ocs-storagecluster-cephfs . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWX Default: None When set (with override_storageclass: true ), provides a single storage class override for all RWX PVCs. Applies to meta and backup storage; specific Db2 storage class variables take precedence when also set.
docs.title: custom_storage_class_rwx

docs.text: Type of backup operation to perform on the Db2 database — online (database remains available during backup; recommended for production systems requiring high availability) or offline (database is unavailable during backup; faster completion and works with circular logging). Optional Environment Variable: DB2_BACKUP_TYPE Default: online Important If your Db2 instance has circular logging enabled ( LOGARCHMETH1: OFF and/or LOGARCHMETH2: OFF — the default configuration), you can only use the offline backup type. If archive logging is enabled, you can use either type. Check the LOGARCHMETH1 / LOGARCHMETH2 settings in db2_database_db_config to determine whether online backup is supported.
docs.title: backup_type

docs.text: Storage backend for database backup files only — disk (backups stored locally and copied to mas_backup_dir ) or s3 (backups sent directly to an S3-compatible bucket for cloud-based backups, long-term retention, or disaster recovery). Optional Environment Variable: BACKUP_VENDOR Default: disk Instance resources (secrets, certificates, CRs) are always stored locally in mas_backup_dir , regardless of this setting — only database backup files go to S3. When set to s3 , requires backup_s3_endpoint , backup_s3_bucket , backup_s3_access_key , and backup_s3_secret_key .
docs.title: backup_vendor

docs.text: S3-compatible object storage endpoint URL — an HTTPS URL (e.g. https://s3.us-east.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud , https://s3.amazonaws.com ) that must be accessible from the Db2 pod. Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT Default: None Supports AWS S3, IBM Cloud Object Storage, MinIO, and other S3-compatible services. Db2 connects to this endpoint to upload/download backup files, so an incorrect endpoint will cause backup/restore failures.
docs.title: backup_s3_endpoint

docs.text: S3 bucket name for storing database backups — a valid S3 bucket name (e.g. mas-db2-backups ). The bucket must exist before running the backup, and the credentials must have read/write permissions on it. Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_BUCKET Default: None Backup files are stored in this bucket under path <backup_version>/ .
docs.title: backup_s3_bucket

docs.text: S3 access key ID for authentication, used together with backup_s3_secret_key — must have read/write permissions to backup_s3_bucket . Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Invalid credentials cause backup/restore to fail with authentication errors. Store securely using Ansible Vault or environment variables — never commit to version control.
docs.title: backup_s3_access_key

docs.text: S3 secret access key for authentication, used together with backup_s3_access_key — must correspond to the access key ID. Required when backup_vendor is s3 Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY Default: None Store securely using Ansible Vault or environment variables — never commit to version control.
docs.title: backup_s3_secret_key

docs.text: Db2 storage access alias name for the S3 configuration — an internal Db2 identifier for the S3 connection (alphanumeric, no spaces). Optional Environment Variable: BACKUP_S3_ALIAS Default: S3DB2COS Only used when backup_vendor is s3 . Usually leave as the default; change only if you need to match existing Db2 storage access configurations — changing this is rarely necessary.
docs.title: backup_s3_alias

docs.text: The db2u-migration action enables migration of existing Db2uCluster deployments to the current Db2uInstance resource type. This migration is necessary as Db2uCluster is deprecated and will reach end-of-life in future releases.
docs.title: Migrating from Db2uCluster to Db2uInstance

docs.text: Version : Db2uCluster must be running v12.x (migration will fail for v11 or earlier) CLI Tool : The db2u_migrate command-line tool must be available on the machine running the Ansible role Namespace : Migration is namespace-scoped; specify the namespace containing the Db2uCluster No Conflicts : No Db2uInstance with the same name should exist in the namespace
docs.title: Migration Requirements

docs.text: Non-destructive : The original Db2uCluster CR remains after migration and is not automatically deleted Data Preservation : Database data and configuration are preserved during migration Service Continuity : The migration creates a new Db2uInstance that maintains connectivity to the existing database JdbcCfg Update : Optionally updates MAS JdbcCfg if mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are provided
docs.title: Migration Behavior

docs.text: The migration action performs the following steps: Validation : Verifies namespace exists Confirms Db2uCluster exists and is v12.x Checks for Db2uInstance naming conflicts Execution : Runs db2u_migrate --namespace <namespace> --name <name> Monitors command output and handles errors Verification : Waits for Db2uInstance to reach Ready state Waits for Db2uEngine to reach Ready state Optionally updates MAS JdbcCfg Post-Migration : Displays success status Reminds user that Db2uCluster still exists Provides guidance for optional cleanup
docs.title: Migration Process

docs.text: Basic Migration export DB2_ACTION=db2u-migration export DB2_NAMESPACE=db2u export DB2_INSTANCE_NAME=db2u-db01 ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Migration with MAS JdbcCfg Update export DB2_ACTION=db2u-migration export DB2_NAMESPACE=db2u export DB2_INSTANCE_NAME=db2u-manage export MAS_INSTANCE_ID=inst1 export MAS_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/masconfig ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role
docs.title: Usage Example

docs.text: Verify Migration Success # Check Db2uInstance status oc get db2uinstance -n db2u # Check Db2uEngine status oc get db2uengine -n db2u # Verify database connectivity oc exec -n db2u c-db2u-db01-db2u-0 -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 connect to BLUDB" Optional: Clean Up Db2uCluster After verifying the migration succeeded and the Db2uInstance is functioning correctly, you may optionally delete the original Db2uCluster: # Delete the Db2uCluster CR (optional) oc delete db2ucluster db2u-db01 -n db2u Note : Only delete the Db2uCluster after thoroughly verifying the migrated Db2uInstance is working correctly.
docs.title: Post-Migration Steps

docs.text: Migration Fails: Version Check Error: Migration requires Db2uCluster to be v12.x Current version: 11.5.8.0 Resolution : Upgrade your Db2uCluster to v12 before attempting migration: export DB2_ACTION=upgrade export DB2_VERSION=12.0.0.0 export DB2_CHANNEL=v12.0.0-cn1 ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Migration Fails: Db2uInstance Already Exists Error: Db2uInstance 'db2u-db01' already exists in namespace 'db2u' Resolution : Either delete the existing Db2uInstance or choose a different name: # Option 1: Delete existing instance oc delete db2uinstance db2u-db01 -n db2u # Option 2: Use different name export DB2_INSTANCE_NAME=db2u-db01-migrated Migration Fails: db2u_migrate Command Not Found Error: db2u_migrate: command not found Resolution : Install the db2u_migrate CLI tool on the machine running the Ansible role. Contact IBM support or refer to Db2 operator documentation for installation instructions.
docs.title: Troubleshooting Migration

docs.title: Backup Directory Structure (Disk)

docs.text: source_db2_backup_version: "20251212-021316" source_db2_backup_timestamp: "20251212021316" source_db2_instance_name: "db2u-manage" source_db2_instance_version: "11.5.8.0-cn7" database: "BLUDB" backup_vendor: "disk" vendor_backup_path: "/mnt/backup/20251212-021316/data" local_backup_path: "/tmp/masbr/backup-20251212-021316-db2u/data/db2-BLUDB-backup-20251212-021316.tar.gz" status: "SUCCESS"
docs.title: Database Backup Metadata (db2-backup-info.yaml)

docs.text: Version Compatibility: The restore operation requires the target Db2 version to match the backup version Always verify version compatibility before attempting a restore Backup Types: If your Db2 instance has circular logging enabled (i.e. LOGARCHMETH1: OFF and/or LOGARCHMETH2: OFF ), you can only use the offline backup type. If your Db2 instance has circular logging disabled, you can use either the online or offline backup type. If you are unsure, you can use the default online backup type. Online Backup : Database remains available during backup (recommended for production) Offline Backup : Database is taken offline during backup (faster but requires downtime) Storage Options: Disk Storage : Backups stored locally and copied to backup directory S3 Storage : Backups stored directly to S3-compatible object storage (no local storage required) Security: Backup files contain sensitive data and credentials Secure the backup directory with appropriate permissions Consider encrypting backup files for long-term storage Performance: Online backups may impact Db2 performance during execution Schedule backups during low-usage periods Monitor Db2 resource utilization during backup
docs.title: Important Considerations

docs.text: Check Db2 pod logs: oc logs -n <namespace> <db2-pod-name> -c db2u Review backup script logs in the pod: /tmp/db2_backup.log Verify S3 credentials and connectivity (for S3 backups) Ensure sufficient storage space in the backup PVC(/mnt/backup) Issue: Backup fails with "insufficient storage space" Error: SQL2062N An error occurred while accessing media "backup_path" Solution: Check available disk space on the Db2 pod: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- df -h Verify backup storage PVC has sufficient capacity For S3 backups, ensure bucket has adequate space and proper permissions Consider using compression or incremental backups to reduce storage requirements Issue: Backup fails with "database is in use" Error: SQL1035N The database is currently in use. SQLSTATE=57019 Solution: For offline backups, ensure all applications are disconnected Use online backup instead: export DB2_BACKUP_TYPE=online Check active connections: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 list applications" Force disconnect if necessary: db2 force applications all Issue: S3 backup fails with authentication errors Error: Unable to authenticate with S3 endpoint Solution: Verify S3 credentials are correct: BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY and BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY Test S3 connectivity from the Db2 pod Ensure S3 endpoint URL is correct and accessible Check firewall rules and network policies allow S3 access Verify bucket exists and credentials have write permissions Issue: Backup script execution timeout Error: Backup operation timed out after 3600 seconds Solution: Large databases may require extended timeout periods Monitor backup progress: oc logs -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -f Check Db2 performance and resource utilization Consider scheduling backups during low-usage periods For very large databases, use incremental backups
docs.title: Backup Failures

docs.text: Verify backup version exists and is complete Check Db2 version compatibility Review restore script logs: /tmp/db2_restore_disk.log or /tmp/db2_restore_s3.log Ensure the Db2 instance is running and healthy before database restore For S3 restores, verify S3 connectivity and credentials Issue: Restore fails with version mismatch Error: DB2 version mismatch. Backup version: 11.5.8.0, Target version: 11.5.9.0 Solution: Ensure target Db2 version matches backup version Check backup metadata: cat <backup_dir>/data/db2-backup-info.yaml Install matching Db2 version: export DB2_VERSION=11.5.8.0-cn7 Alternatively, upgrade backup to target version (requires manual intervention) Issue: Restore fails with "database already exists" Error: SQL1005N The database alias "BLUDB" already exists Solution: Drop existing database before restore: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 drop database BLUDB" Or use a different database name during restore Verify database state: db2 list database directory Issue: Restore fails with corrupted backup files Error: SQL2025N The database cannot be restored from backup image Solution: Verify backup file integrity: bash tar -tzf <backup-file>.tar.gz > /dev/null Check backup metadata for status: status: SUCCESS Re-run backup if corruption detected For S3 restores, verify file was completely uploaded Check storage system for hardware errors Issue: Restore fails with insufficient permissions Error: SQL0551N User does not have required authorization Solution: Verify db2inst1 user has proper permissions Check pod security context and service account Ensure restore scripts have execute permissions Review OpenShift security policies (SCC) Issue: S3 restore fails to download backup files Error: Failed to download backup from S3 bucket Solution: Verify S3 credentials have read permissions Check S3 bucket name and path are correct Test S3 connectivity: aws s3 ls s3://<bucket-name>/ Ensure network policies allow outbound S3 access Verify backup files exist in S3 bucket
docs.title: Restore Failures

docs.text: Issue: Backup taking too long Solution: Use online backups to avoid database downtime Schedule backups during low-usage periods Increase Db2 pod resources (CPU/memory) Use compression to reduce backup size Consider incremental backups for large databases Check network bandwidth for S3 backups Issue: Restore taking too long Solution: Ensure adequate resources allocated to Db2 pod Monitor pod resource utilization during restore Check storage performance (IOPS, throughput) For S3 restores, verify network bandwidth Consider using faster storage classes
docs.title: Performance Issues

docs.text: Issue: How to verify backup completed successfully Solution: Check backup metadata file: bash cat <backup_dir>/data/db2-backup-info.yaml Verify status: SUCCESS Verify backup file exists and has reasonable size: bash ls -lh <backup_dir>/data/db2-*.tar.gz For S3 backups, verify files in bucket: bash aws s3 ls s3://<bucket-name>/<backup-version>/ Check Db2 backup history: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 list history backup all for BLUDB" Issue: How to verify restore completed successfully Solution: Check database is online: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 connect to BLUDB" Verify table counts and data integrity: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 'select count(*) from <table_name>'" Check database configuration: bash oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 get db cfg for BLUDB" Review restore logs for errors: bash oc logs -n <namespace> <db2-pod> | grep -i error
docs.title: Validation and Verification

docs.text: Check Db2 pod status: oc get pods -n <namespace> | grep db2 oc describe pod <db2-pod> -n <namespace> Check Db2 instance status: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2pd -" Check database status: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 list active databases" Check backup storage: oc get pvc -n <namespace> oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- df -h /mnt/backup View Db2 diagnostic logs: oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- tail -f /var/log/db2u.log oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- cat /database/config/db2inst1/sqllib/db2dump/db2diag.log Check S3 configuration (if using S3): oc exec -n <namespace> <db2-pod> -- su - db2inst1 -c "db2 list storage access"
docs.title: Diagnostic Commands

docs.text: If you encounter issues not covered in this troubleshooting guide: Check Db2 logs : Review /var/log/db2u.log and db2diag.log for detailed error messages Review backup metadata : Check db2-backup-info.yaml for backup details and status Verify prerequisites : Ensure all required variables are set correctly Test connectivity : Verify network access to storage (S3 or PVC) Check resources : Ensure adequate CPU, memory, and storage are available Open an issue : Report problems at the project repository with logs and configuration details
docs.title: Getting Help

docs.text: Upgrading from Db2 v11 to v12 is a major version change that requires explicit opt-in and a valid Db2 Warehouse license. Without a license, Db2 v12 will operate under a 30-day trial license — this will cause your production system to go offline after expiry .
docs.title: Upgrading Db2 from v11 to v12

docs.text: A valid Db2 Warehouse license file ( .lic format) — see Db2 v12 License File Format below The db2_v12_upgrade flag set to true A v12 target channel (e.g., v12.0.0-cn1 )
docs.title: Prerequisites

docs.text: Variable Environment Variable Description db2_v12_upgrade DB2_V12_UPGRADE Must be true to authorize the upgrade db2_license_file DB2_LICENSE_FILE Path to the Db2 v12 license file db2_channel DB2_CHANNEL Target v12 channel (e.g., v12.0.0-cn1 ) db2_namespace DB2_NAMESPACE Namespace containing the Db2 instances to upgrade
docs.title: Required Variables

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: db2_action: upgrade db2_namespace: db2u db2_channel: v12.0.0-cn1 db2_v12_upgrade: true db2_license_file: /path/to/db2wh.lic roles: - ibm.mas_devops.db2 Or using environment variables: export DB2_ACTION=upgrade export DB2_NAMESPACE=db2u export DB2_CHANNEL=v12.0.0-cn1 export DB2_V12_UPGRADE=true export DB2_LICENSE_FILE=/path/to/db2wh.lic ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.oneclick_upgrade_db2
docs.title: Example Usage

docs.text: IBM distributes the Db2 Warehouse license under several names — you may have received it as db2wh.lic , db2ese.lic , db2aese.lic , or simply as an "activation key" or "entitlement file". The file is a plain-text file with the following structure: [LicenseCertificate] CheckSum=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX TimeStamp=YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS PasswordVersion=5 VendorName=IBM Corporation VendorPassword=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX ProductName=IBM Db2 Warehouse ProductID=5765-F41 ProductVersion=12.0 ProductAnnotation= LicenseType=Permanent ... Note This is a sample structure only — not a real license. Use it to verify that the file you have from IBM matches this format. The file should contain [LicenseCertificate] as the first line and include ProductName=IBM Db2 Warehouse or similar. If your file looks significantly different, you may have the wrong entitlement file.
docs.title: Db2 v12 License File Format

docs.text: If db2_license_file is not provided when upgrading to v12, the role will fail immediately with a clear error message. This is intentional — it prevents a silent downgrade from a full production license to a 30-day trial license, which would cause your database to go offline after the trial period expires. Note New installations ( db2_action=install ) do not require a license file. Only upgrades from v11 to v12 enforce this requirement.
docs.title: What Happens Without a License

docs.text: download_backup_archive ¤ Downloads and extracts MAS backup archives from AWS S3 or Artifactory. This role automates the process of downloading MAS backup archives from remote storage locations and extracting them to a local directory for restore operations. It supports downloading from both AWS S3 (or S3-compatible storage) and Artifactory repositories. The role handles archive verification, extraction, and cleanup operations. Key features: Downloads compressed tar.gz archives from AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage Downloads compressed tar.gz archives from Artifactory repositories Support for downloading multiple archives in a single operation Auto-generation of archive names based on component versions Archive management option to keep downloaded archives organized Automatic extraction of downloaded archives Configurable download timeouts for large archives Optional cleanup of temporary files after extraction Verification of downloaded archive integrity Prerequisites ¤ For S3 Download ¤ AWS CLI or boto3 Python library must be installed amazon.aws Ansible collection must be installed AWS credentials with S3 read permissions S3 bucket must exist and be accessible For Artifactory Download ¤ curl command-line tool must be installed Artifactory API token with download permissions Artifactory repository must exist and be accessible Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_restore_dir Yes manage_db2_backup_version No Value of backup_version facilities_backup_version No Value of backup_version facilities_db2_backup_version No Value of backup_version aws_access_key_id Conditional None include_manage_app_archive No true include_manage_db_archive No true include_facilities_app_archive No true include_facilities_db_archive No true The download source determines which credentials are required: provide the S3 variables to download from AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage, or the Artifactory variables to download from Artifactory. If S3 credentials are provided, S3 download takes precedence over Artifactory. Restore Target ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ Instance ID of the MAS instance, used to identify the backup directories. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None mas_restore_dir ¤ Directory where the backup archive will be downloaded and extracted — the parent directory where all component backup directories will be restored. Required Environment Variable: MAS_RESTORE_DIR Default: None Backup Selection ¤ backup_version ¤ Version identifier for the backup to download. This must match the version used when the backup was created; when downloading multiple archives it is used as the default version for all components unless specific component versions are provided. Required Environment Variable: BACKUP_VERSION Default: None backup_archive_names ¤ List of archive names to download, provided either as a comma-separated string ( "archive1.tar.gz,archive2.tar.gz" ) or as a list ( ["archive1.tar.gz", "archive2.tar.gz"] ). Optional Environment Variable: BACKUP_ARCHIVE_NAMES Default: Auto-generated from component versions When not provided, the role auto-generates archive names based on mas_instance_id and the component backup versions (for example mas-<mas_instance_id>-backup-<version>-suite.tar.gz ), filtered by the include_*_archive variables. Component-Specific Backup Versions ¤ ibm_catalogs_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the IBM catalogs component, used to auto-generate the -catalog.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_CATALOGS_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version certmanager_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the cert-manager component, used to auto-generate the -certmanager.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: CERTMANAGER_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version mongodb_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the MongoDB component, used to auto-generate the -mongoce.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version sls_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the SLS (Suite License Service) component, used to auto-generate the -sls.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version suite_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the MAS Suite component, used to auto-generate the -suite.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: SUITE_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version manage_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the Manage application component, used to auto-generate the -app-manage.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: MANAGE_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version manage_db2_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the Manage Db2 component, used to auto-generate the -db2u-manage.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: MANAGE_DB2_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version facilities_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the Facilities application component, used to auto-generate the -app-facilities.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: FACILITIES_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version facilities_db2_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the Facilities Db2 component, used to auto-generate the -db2u-facilities.tar.gz archive name when backup_archive_names is not provided. Optional Environment Variable: FACILITIES_DB2_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version S3 Download ¤ aws_access_key_id ¤ AWS access key ID for authentication to S3 or S3-compatible storage. Required for S3 download Environment Variable: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None aws_secret_access_key ¤ AWS secret access key for authentication to S3 or S3-compatible storage. Required for S3 download Environment Variable: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None s3_bucket_name ¤ Name of the S3 bucket where the archive is stored. Required for S3 download Environment Variable: S3_BUCKET_NAME Default: None s3_region ¤ AWS region where the S3 bucket is located. Optional Environment Variable: S3_REGION Default: us-east-1 s3_endpoint_url ¤ Custom S3 endpoint URL for S3-compatible storage services (e.g., MinIO, Wasabi, IBM Cloud Object Storage). Optional Environment Variable: S3_ENDPOINT_URL Default: None (uses AWS S3 endpoints) Artifactory Download ¤ artifactory_username ¤ Artifactory username for authentication. Required for Artifactory download Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None artifactory_token ¤ Artifactory API token for authentication. Required for Artifactory download Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None artifactory_repository ¤ Name of the Artifactory repository where the archive is stored. Required for Artifactory download Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_REPOSITORY Default: None artifactory_url ¤ Base URL of the Artifactory server (e.g., https://artifactory.example.com/artifactory ). Optional Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_URL Default: https://na.artifactory.swg-devops.com/artifactory Download and Extraction Behavior ¤ backup_temp_dir ¤ Temporary directory where the archive will be downloaded before extraction. The directory is created if it doesn't exist and can be cleaned up after extraction. Optional Environment Variable: None Default: <mas_restore_dir>/mas-<mas_instance_id>-restore-<backup_version> download_timeout ¤ Maximum time in seconds to wait for the download to complete — useful for large archives or slow network connections. Optional Environment Variable: DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECS Default: 10800 (3 hours) extract_archive ¤ Whether to automatically extract the downloaded archive. Set to false to only download the archive without extracting it. Optional Environment Variable: EXTRACT_ARCHIVE Default: true cleanup_archive ¤ Whether to remove the archive file and temporary directory after successful extraction. Set to false to keep the downloaded archive. Optional Environment Variable: CLEANUP_ARCHIVE Default: true Component Archive Selection ¤ include_sls_archive ¤ Whether to download the SLS archive ( -sls.tar.gz ) from S3 or Artifactory. When set to false , the role automatically skips it, preventing unnecessary downloads when the SLS component restore is not needed. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_SLS_ARCHIVE Default: true include_mongo_archive ¤ Whether to download the Mongo archive ( -mongoce.tar.gz ) from S3 or Artifactory. When set to false , the role automatically skips it, preventing unnecessary downloads when the Mongo component restore is not needed. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_MONGO_ARCHIVE Default: true include_manage_app_archive ¤ Whether to download the Manage app archive ( -app-manage.tar.gz ) from S3 or Artifactory. When set to false , the role automatically skips it, preventing unnecessary downloads when the Manage component restore is not needed. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_MANAGE_APP_ARCHIVE Default: true include_manage_db_archive ¤ Whether to download the Manage DB2 archive ( -db2u-manage.tar.gz ) from S3 or Artifactory. When set to false , the role automatically skips it, preventing unnecessary downloads when the Manage component restore is not needed. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_MANAGE_DB_ARCHIVE Default: true include_facilities_app_archive ¤ Whether to download the Facilities app archive ( -app-facilities.tar.gz ) from S3 or Artifactory. When set to false , the role automatically skips it, preventing unnecessary downloads when the Facilities component restore is not needed. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_FACILITIES_APP_ARCHIVE Default: true include_facilities_db_archive ¤ Whether to download the Facilities DB2 archive ( -db2u-facilities.tar.gz ) from S3 or Artifactory. When set to false , the role automatically skips it, preventing unnecessary downloads when the Facilities component restore is not needed. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_FACILITIES_DB_ARCHIVE Default: true Example Playbook ¤ Download Multiple Archives from S3 (Auto-generated names) ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - docs.text: dro ¤ DRO will be supported on the following MAS versions MAS 8.10.6 + MAS 8.11.2 + MAS 9.0 + Installs Data Reporter Operator in the redhat-marketplace namespace. If mas_instance_id and the other associated parameters are provided then the role will also generate a configuration file that can be directly applied to IBM Maximo Application Suite. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default dro_action No install dro_namespace No redhat-marketplace ibm_entitlement_key Yes None dro_storage_class No Auto-detected dro_endpoint_url No None dro_api_key No None dro_crt_path No None mas_instance_id No None mas_config_dir No None dro_contact.email Conditional None dro_contact.first_name Conditional None dro_contact.last_name Conditional None dro_include_isrg_root_cert No true custom_labels No None mas_pod_templates_dir No None Some variables are conditionally required: generating a BasCfg requires both mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir (plus the dro_contact fields), and connecting to an existing DRO instance requires all three of dro_endpoint_url , dro_api_key , and dro_crt_path . Installation ¤ dro_action ¤ Action to perform with the Data Reporter Operator deployment — install (deploy and configure DRO) or uninstall (remove DRO from the cluster). The uninstall action removes all DRO resources from the specified namespace. Optional Environment Variable: DRO_ACTION Default: install DRO is supported on MAS 8.10.6+, 8.11.2+, and 9.0+. The namespace must be specified during uninstall operations (see dro_namespace ). dro_namespace ¤ Namespace where the Data Reporter Operator will be deployed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: DRO_NAMESPACE Default: redhat-marketplace Override the default on OCP clusters where redhat* namespaces have restricted access, or when organizational policies require custom namespace naming. Ensure the namespace has appropriate permissions for DRO operator deployment. ibm_entitlement_key ¤ IBM entitlement key for accessing container images — obtain from the IBM Container Library . Required Environment Variable: IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Authenticates access to the IBM container registry for pulling DRO operator images; without a valid key the images cannot be pulled and installation will fail. Keep the key secure and do not commit it to version control. dro_storage_class ¤ Storage class for DRO persistent volumes — any storage class available in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode, for example ibmc-block-gold / ibmc-block-silver (IBM Cloud ROKS), gp2 / gp3 (AWS), or managed-premium (Azure). Optional (auto-detected if not provided) Environment Variable: DRO_STORAGE_CLASS Default: None (automatically determined) Provides persistent storage for DRO data and metrics. Specify explicitly when using customized storage solutions or when automatic detection fails; verify available storage classes with oc get storageclass . Connecting to an Existing DRO Instance ¤ dro_endpoint_url ¤ URL of an existing DRO instance to connect to — a valid HTTPS URL such as https://ibm-data-reporter.apps.cluster.domain.com , obtained from the ibm-data-reporter route in the DRO namespace. Optional Environment Variable: DRO_ENDPOINT_URL Default: None When set, the role will not install DRO but will generate configuration to connect to the existing instance. All three of dro_endpoint_url , dro_api_key , and dro_crt_path must be provided to connect to an existing DRO instance. dro_api_key ¤ API token for authenticating to an existing DRO instance, obtained from the ibm-data-reporter-operator-api-token secret in the DRO namespace. Optional Environment Variable: DRO_APIKEY Default: None Extract the token with oc get secret ibm-data-reporter-operator-api-token -n <dro-namespace> -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d . Keep the API key secure. dro_crt_path ¤ Path to the DRO certificate file (.pem) used for TLS verification when connecting to an existing DRO instance. DRO uses the default OCP cluster ingress certificates. Optional Environment Variable: DRO_CERTIFICATE_PATH Default: None Obtain the certificate from the router-certs-default secret in the openshift-ingress namespace or the trustedCA configmap in the openshift-config namespace, for example oc get secret router-certs-default -n openshift-ingress -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d > /tmp/dro-cert.pem . Without the certificate, TLS verification will fail. BASCfg Generation ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier (lowercase alphanumeric, max 12 characters) that the generated DRO BasCfg configuration will target. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Required when generating MAS configuration files. If not set (along with mas_config_dir ), no BasCfg template will be generated — both must be set to generate BasCfg templates. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory (with write permissions) for saving the generated BasCfg resource definitions. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None Required when generating MAS configuration files. The generated file can be manually applied or used as input to the suite_config role; if not set (along with mas_instance_id ), no BasCfg template will be generated. dro_contact.email ¤ Contact email address (valid email format) for the DRO configuration, used for administrative and support purposes. Required when generating BasCfg (when mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are set) Environment Variable: DRO_CONTACT_EMAIL Default: None Use a monitored email address for receiving DRO-related notifications. dro_contact.first_name ¤ Contact first name for the DRO configuration, used for administrative identification purposes. Required when generating BasCfg (when mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are set) Environment Variable: DRO_CONTACT_FIRSTNAME Default: None Required for BasCfg generation along with email and last name. dro_contact.last_name ¤ Contact last name for the DRO configuration, used for administrative identification purposes. Required when generating BasCfg (when mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are set) Environment Variable: DRO_CONTACT_LASTNAME Default: None Required for BasCfg generation along with email and first name. dro_include_isrg_root_cert ¤ Whether to include the ISRG Root X1 (the default root certificate used by Let's Encrypt) in the generated BasCfg — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: DRO_INCLUDE_ISRG_ROOT_CERT Default: true Mainly needed for IBM Cloud hosted services, where including the root certificate ensures proper TLS trust validation for DRO connections. custom_labels ¤ Custom labels to apply to DRO instance resources, as a comma-separated list of key=value pairs (e.g., env=prod,team=platform,cost-center=12345 ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels must follow Kubernetes label syntax (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores, dots) and are useful for cost allocation, resource queries, and automation scripts. mas_pod_templates_dir ¤ Directory containing pod template configurations for DRO — must contain a file named ibm-mas-bascfg.yml whose content is a YAML block for the podTemplates element. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None The pod template configuration is inserted into the BasCfg spec under the podTemplates element, customizing resource limits, node selectors, tolerations, and other pod-level settings. See the BestEfforts reference configuration for examples and Customizing Pod Templates for full documentation. Example Playbook ¤ Install in-cluster and generate MAS configuration ¤ To install DRO export IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY=<valid ibm entitlement key> export DRO_CONTACT_EMAIL=xxx@xxx.com export DRO_CONTACT_FIRSTNAME=xxx export DRO_CONTACT_LASTNAME=xxx export DRO_ACTION=install export MAS_CONFIG_DIR=<valid local path to the config folder> export MAS_INSTANCE_ID=<valid mas instance id> export DRO_STORAGE_CLASS=<valid storage class name> export ROLE_NAME='dro' export DRO_NAMESPACE=ibm-dro ansible-playbook playbooks/run_role.yml To connect to an existing DRO export DRO_ENDPOINT_URL=<valid DRO url> export DRO_APIKEY=<valid DRO apikey> export DRO_CERTIFICATE_PATH=/temp/cert.pem export IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY=<valid ibm entitlement key> export DRO_CONTACT_EMAIL=xxx@xxx.com export DRO_CONTACT_FIRSTNAME=xxx export DRO_CONTACT_LASTNAME=xxx export MAS_CONFIG_DIR=<valid local path to the config folder> export MAS_INSTANCE_ID=<valid mas instance id> export DRO_ACTION=install export ROLE_NAME='dro' ansible-playbook playbooks/run_role.yml To uninstall DRO export DRO_ACTION=uninstall export ROLE_NAME='dro' export DRO_NAMESPACE=ibm-dro ansible-playbook playbooks/run_role.yml - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: masinst1 mas_config_dir: ~/masconfig dro_contact: email: 'john@email.com' first_name: 'john' last_name: 'winter' roles: - ibm.mas_devops.dro License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: eck ¤ This role provides support to install Elastic Cloud on Kubernetes (ECK). Elasticsearch is configured with a default user named elastic , you can obtain the password for this user by running the following command: oc -n eck get secret mas-es-elastic-user -o go-template='{{.data.elastic | base64decode}}'; echo Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default eck_action No install eck_enable_elasticsearch No false eck_enable_kibana No false eck_enable_logstash No false eck_enable_filebeat No false eck_remote_es_hosts Conditional None eck_remote_es_username Conditional None eck_remote_es_password Conditional None es_domain No None kibana_domain No None letsencrypt_email No None The three remote Elasticsearch variables are only required when forwarding logs to a remote Elasticsearch instance, and must all be set together. ECK Components ¤ eck_action ¤ Action to perform on the ECK deployment — install (the default and currently only supported value). Optional Environment Variable: ECK_ACTION Default: install Installs the ECK operator and, based on the enable flags below, optionally deploys Elasticsearch, Kibana, Logstash, and Filebeat components. eck_enable_elasticsearch ¤ Deploy Elasticsearch for log storage and search — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ECK_ENABLE_ELASTICSEARCH Default: false Leave as false when using an external Elasticsearch instance. Elasticsearch is required for Kibana, and for local log forwarding from Logstash and Filebeat. The default elastic user is created — retrieve its password with the command shown above. eck_enable_kibana ¤ Deploy Kibana for log visualization and analysis — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ECK_ENABLE_KIBANA Default: false Kibana requires Elasticsearch — ensure eck_enable_elasticsearch is true when enabling Kibana. A custom domain can be set with kibana_domain . eck_enable_logstash ¤ Deploy Logstash for log processing and forwarding — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ECK_ENABLE_LOGSTASH Default: false When the remote Elasticsearch variables are set, Logstash forwards logs to that remote instance; otherwise logs are sent to the local Elasticsearch (if enabled). eck_enable_filebeat ¤ Deploy Filebeat as a DaemonSet on the Kubernetes cluster nodes for log collection — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ECK_ENABLE_FILEBEAT Default: false Filebeat collects logs from the cluster nodes and forwards them to Elasticsearch or Logstash. Remote Elasticsearch ¤ When eck_remote_es_hosts , eck_remote_es_username , and eck_remote_es_password are all set, and eck_enable_logstash is true , the Logstash server will be configured to send log messages to the remote Elasticsearch instance defined. eck_remote_es_hosts ¤ Remote Elasticsearch hosts for Logstash to forward logs to — a comma-separated list of hosts (e.g. https://es1.example.com:9200,https://es2.example.com:9200 ). Required for remote Elasticsearch forwarding, together with the username and password Environment Variable: ECK_REMOTE_ES_HOSTS Default: None Only applies when eck_enable_logstash is true . eck_remote_es_username ¤ Username for authenticating with the remote Elasticsearch instance — a valid Elasticsearch username string. Required for remote Elasticsearch forwarding, together with the hosts and password Environment Variable: ECK_REMOTE_ES_USERNAME Default: None Only applies when eck_enable_logstash is true . Without valid credentials, log forwarding will fail. eck_remote_es_password ¤ Password for authenticating with the remote Elasticsearch instance — a valid Elasticsearch password string. Required for remote Elasticsearch forwarding, together with the hosts and username Environment Variable: ECK_REMOTE_ES_PASSWORD Default: None Store the password securely — it is stored in Kubernetes secrets along with the username. Without valid credentials, log forwarding will fail. Domains and Certificates ¤ Elasticsearch and Kibana can be configured with a custom domain and a certificate signed by LetsEncrypt . es_domain ¤ Custom domain for external access to Elasticsearch — a valid domain name routable to the target OCP cluster (e.g. es.example.com ). Optional Environment Variable: ECK_ELASTICSEARCH_DOMAIN Default: None When set, a route with the custom domain is created for Elasticsearch access instead of the default cluster route; combined with letsencrypt_email , a LetsEncrypt certificate is provisioned automatically. Requires eck_enable_elasticsearch to be true . kibana_domain ¤ Custom domain for external access to the Kibana UI — a valid domain name routable to the target OCP cluster (e.g. kibana.example.com ). Optional Environment Variable: ECK_KIBANA_DOMAIN Default: None When set, a route with the custom domain is created for Kibana access instead of the default cluster route; combined with letsencrypt_email , a LetsEncrypt certificate is provisioned automatically. Requires eck_enable_kibana to be true . letsencrypt_email ¤ Email address for LetsEncrypt certificate registration — a valid email address that receives certificate expiration notifications.
