docs.text: entitlement_key_rotation ¤ This role creates/updates the entitlement username and password that are stored in the secrets used to pull images throughout all MAS related namespaces for one or multiple clusters. The main secret that is updated by this role is the ibm-entitlement which holds the credentials needed to pull the MAS images used by MAS Core or the MAS applications. By default, this role will search for all MAS related namespaces that might contain the secret that holds the entitlement key to be updated. The list of namespaces to be updated with new username/password credentials are: All namespaces starting with mas- , which means by default it will update the ibm-entitlement secret with the new username/password credentials for all MAS namespaces/instances in the cluster. SLS namespace - holds ibm-entitlement which pulls Suite License Services related images. openshift-marketplace - holds wiot-docker-local which pulls the pre-release/development catalog source image for ibm-operator-catalog . Requires the artifactory_username and artifactory_token to be set. Note This role uses ocp_login to login into the target clusters, therefore make sure you export the corresponding environment variables accordingly to the cluster type you want to target. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default artifactory_username Conditional None artifactory_token Conditional None mas_entitlement_username Conditional None mas_entitlement_key Conditional None cluster_name Yes None sls_namespace No ibm-sls mas_clusters_entitlement_key_rotation_list No Uses cluster_name mas_namespaces_entitlement_key_rotation_list No All MAS namespaces The credential variables are conditional: artifactory_username / artifactory_token rotate the ibm-entitlement and wiot-docker-local secrets used for development installs and pre-release catalog sources, while mas_entitlement_username / mas_entitlement_key rotate the ibm-entitlement secret only, for MAS installs using release catalog sources. Target Cluster ¤ cluster_name ¤ The target cluster to rotate the credentials/entitlement key secrets. Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None sls_namespace ¤ Defines the SLS namespace that holds the ibm-entitlement secret which pulls Suite License Services related images. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-sls Credentials ¤ artifactory_username ¤ Artifactory username used to rotate the ibm-entitlement and wiot-docker-local secret credentials, which are used to pull images across MAS namespaces for development installs and pre-release catalog sources. Required to rotate development/pre-release credentials Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None artifactory_token ¤ Artifactory token used together with artifactory_username . Required to rotate development/pre-release credentials Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None mas_entitlement_username ¤ Entitlement username used to rotate the ibm-entitlement secret credentials only, which is used to pull images across MAS namespaces for MAS installs using release catalog sources. Required to rotate release credentials Environment Variable: MAS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME Default: None mas_entitlement_key ¤ Entitlement key used together with mas_entitlement_username . Required to rotate release credentials Environment Variable: MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Advanced Mode ¤ Use the following variables to change the default behavior of this role to only rotate the entitlement key for specific clusters or namespaces, instead of running it for all MAS related namespaces. mas_clusters_entitlement_key_rotation_list ¤ Optionally define a list of clusters to loop through for the entitlement key rotation. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CLUSTERS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY_ROTATION_LIST Default: If not set, the cluster_name property will be used to target the cluster while executing this role. Example: export MAS_CLUSTERS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY_ROTATION_LIST='cluster1,cluster2' mas_namespaces_entitlement_key_rotation_list ¤ Optionally define a specific list of namespaces to loop through for the entitlement key rotation. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_NAMESPACES_ENTITLEMENT_KEY_ROTATION_LIST Default: If not set, all MAS related namespaces for all MAS instances will be targeted for entitlement key rotation. Example: export MAS_NAMESPACES_ENTITLEMENT_KEY_ROTATION_LIST='ibm-sls,openshift-marketplace' Example Playbook ¤ Rotate entitlement credentials across all MAS instances for a given target cluster: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cluster_name: "{{ lookup('env', 'CLUSTER_NAME') }}" cluster_type: "{{ lookup('env', 'CLUSTER_TYPE') }}" ibmcloud_apikey: "{{ lookup('env', 'IBMCLOUD_APIKEY') }}" artifactory_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME') }}" artifactory_token: "{{ lookup('env', 'ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN') }}" mas_entitlement_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME') }}" mas_entitlement_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY') }}" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.entitlement_key_rotation Rotate entitlement credentials across a specific list of namespaces, targeting multiple clusters: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cluster_name: "{{ lookup('env', 'CLUSTER_NAME') }}" # this is the original cluster that will keep the login session context at the end of the rotation loop. cluster_type: "{{ lookup('env', 'CLUSTER_TYPE') }}" ibmcloud_apikey: "{{ lookup('env', 'IBMCLOUD_APIKEY') }}" artifactory_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME') }}" artifactory_token: "{{ lookup('env', 'ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN') }}" mas_entitlement_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME') }}" mas_entitlement_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY') }}" mas_clusters_entitlement_key_rotation_list: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_CLUSTERS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY_ROTATION_LIST') }}" mas_namespaces_entitlement_key_rotation_list: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_NAMESPACES_ENTITLEMENT_KEY_ROTATION_LIST') }}" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.entitlement_key_rotation License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: eso ¤ Deploy External Secrets Operator for Kubernetes, enabling seamless integration with external secret management systems like AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager, HashiCorp Vault, and many others. External Secrets Operator is a Kubernetes operator that integrates external secret management systems. It reads information from external APIs and automatically injects the values into Kubernetes Secrets, keeping them synchronized with the external source. Features ¤ Multi-Provider Support : Integrates with 20+ secret management providers Automatic Synchronization : Keeps Kubernetes secrets in sync with external sources Secure by Design : Secrets are fetched at runtime, not stored in Git Flexible Configuration : Supports namespace-scoped and cluster-wide secret stores Template Support : Transform and combine secrets before injection High Availability : Configurable replica counts for production deployments Deployed Components ¤ After installation, the following deployments will be available: kubectl get deployments -n external-secrets-system NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE external-secrets 1/1 1 1 5m external-secrets-cert-controller 1/1 1 1 5m external-secrets-webhook 1/1 1 1 5m Custom Resource Definitions ¤ The operator creates the following CRDs: kubectl get crd | grep external-secrets clustersecretstores.external-secrets.io externalsecrets.external-secrets.io secretstores.external-secrets.io clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io pushsecrets.external-secrets.io Additional Resources ¤ External Secrets Documentation Getting Started Guide Provider Documentation Helm Chart Values Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default eso_action No install eso_namespace No external-secrets-system eso_release_name No external-secrets eso_repo_url No https://charts.external-secrets.io eso_chart_version No Latest eso_values No {} eso_cleanup_crds No false eso_cleanup_namespace No false eso_provider No ibm eso_store_name No ibm-secrets-manager ibm_sm_instance_url Conditional None ibm_sm_api_key Conditional Falls back to IBMCLOUD_APIKEY ibm_sm_store_namespace Conditional None The IBM Secrets Manager variables are only required for the secret store actions: ibm_sm_instance_url and ibm_sm_api_key when creating a ClusterSecretStore or SecretStore, and ibm_sm_store_namespace when creating or deleting a namespace-scoped SecretStore. Operator Installation ¤ eso_action ¤ Action to perform — one of install , uninstall , create-clustersecretstore , delete-clustersecretstore , create-secretstore , or delete-secretstore . Optional Environment Variable: ESO_ACTION Default: install Installation is idempotent and can be run multiple times safely; uninstallation behavior depends on the cleanup flags. The create-* / delete-* actions manage IBM Secrets Manager stores and require the IBM Secrets Manager configuration variables. A ClusterSecretStore is cluster-wide and can be used by ExternalSecrets in any namespace, whereas a SecretStore is namespace-scoped and can only be used by ExternalSecrets in the same namespace. eso_namespace ¤ Namespace for the External Secrets Operator installation — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: ESO_NAMESPACE Default: external-secrets-system All operator resources (deployments, services, webhooks) are created in this namespace, which is created if it doesn't exist. The default follows the operator's standard convention — override only for specific namespace requirements or multiple operator instances. CRDs are cluster-scoped regardless of namespace. eso_release_name ¤ Helm release name for the External Secrets Operator — a valid Helm release name (alphanumeric with hyphens), unique within the namespace. Optional Environment Variable: ESO_RELEASE_NAME Default: external-secrets Used for Helm operations (install, upgrade, uninstall) and appears in helm list and other Helm commands; use the default unless deploying multiple instances or following specific naming conventions. eso_repo_url ¤ Helm repository URL for External Secrets charts — any valid HTTPS URL to a Helm repository. Optional Environment Variable: ESO_REPO_URL Default: https://charts.external-secrets.io The default points to the official External Secrets Helm repository; override for private mirrors, custom repositories, or air-gapped/restricted environments. eso_chart_version ¤ Specific version of the External Secrets Helm chart to install — a valid semantic version (e.g., 0.9.11 , 0.10.0 ). Optional Environment Variable: ESO_CHART_VERSION Default: "" (latest version) Leave empty to install the latest available version (suitable for development/testing); pin a specific version for production deployments, version upgrades, or rollbacks. Check the releases page for available versions — pinning versions is recommended in production. eso_values ¤ Custom Helm values to override the default chart configuration — a dictionary of valid Helm chart values. Optional Environment Variable: None (must be set in playbook) Default: {} (empty dictionary) Use to override resource limits and requests, replica counts for high availability, security contexts, provider-specific configurations, and feature flags. Values are merged with the defaults in templates/values.yml.j2 , overriding any conflicts — see Helm chart values for available options and the Example Playbooks below for usage. Uninstallation Cleanup ¤ eso_cleanup_crds ¤ Flag to control CRD deletion during uninstallation — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ESO_CLEANUP_CRDS Default: false With false (recommended unless performing complete removal), CRDs and custom resources remain after uninstall; with true , all CRDs and custom resources are deleted. CRDs are cluster-scoped and affect all namespaces. Warning Setting this to true deletes all ExternalSecret and SecretStore resources in the cluster. eso_cleanup_namespace ¤ Flag to control namespace deletion during uninstallation — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ESO_CLEANUP_NAMESPACE Default: false With false (recommended unless performing complete removal), the namespace remains after uninstall; with true , the namespace is deleted, including any remaining resources. Namespace deletion will fail if resources still exist in it. Secret Store Management ¤ eso_provider ¤ Provider type for secret store creation — currently only ibm (IBM Secrets Manager) is supported. Optional Environment Variable: ESO_PROVIDER Default: ibm Only used when eso_action is one of the secret store actions (not install / uninstall ); it determines which provider-specific tasks are executed. Future versions may support additional providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, HashiCorp Vault, etc.). eso_store_name ¤ Name for the SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore resource — a valid Kubernetes resource name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: ESO_STORE_NAME Default: ibm-secrets-manager Only used with the secret store actions; the name must be unique within the cluster for a ClusterSecretStore (cluster-scoped) and is referenced by ExternalSecret resources. The associated credentials secret is named {eso_store_name}-apikey . Override the default if you need multiple store instances or have specific naming requirements. ibm_sm_instance_url ¤ IBM Secrets Manager instance URL — a valid HTTPS URL (e.g., https://my-instance.secrets-manager.cloud.ibm.com ). Required when using the create-clustersecretstore or create-secretstore actions Environment Variable: IBM_SM_INSTANCE_URL Default: None Determines which IBM Secrets Manager instance the External Secrets Operator will connect to; the instance must be accessible from your Kubernetes cluster. ibm_sm_api_key ¤ IBM Cloud API key for authenticating with IBM Secrets Manager — a valid key with IAM permissions to access the Secrets Manager instance. Required when using the create-clustersecretstore or create-secretstore actions Environment Variable: IBM_SM_API_KEY or IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: Falls back to IBMCLOUD_APIKEY if IBM_SM_API_KEY is not set Used to authenticate the External Secrets Operator with IBM Secrets Manager; the API key is stored as a Kubernetes secret (named {eso_store_name}-apikey ) in the operator namespace. The IBMCLOUD_APIKEY fallback follows the collection pattern for convenience. ibm_sm_store_namespace ¤ Namespace for the IBM Secrets Manager SecretStore (namespace-scoped) — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Required when using the create-secretstore or delete-secretstore actions Environment Variable: IBM_SM_STORE_NAMESPACE Default: None Determines which namespace the SecretStore and its credentials secret will be created in; the namespace is created if it doesn't exist during create-secretstore . A SecretStore can only be used by ExternalSecrets in the same namespace — for cluster-wide access, use create-clustersecretstore instead (which does not require this variable). Example Playbooks ¤ Basic Installation ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: eso_namespace: external-secrets-system roles: - ibm.mas_devops.eso Installation with Specific Version ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: eso_namespace: external-secrets-system eso_chart_version: "0.9.11" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.eso Installation with Custom Values ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: eso_namespace: external-secrets-system eso_values: replicaCount: 3 resources: requests: cpu: 50m memory: 128Mi limits: cpu: 200m memory: 256Mi webhook: replicaCount: 2 roles: - docs.text: Deploy External Secrets Operator for Kubernetes, enabling seamless integration with external secret management systems like AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager, HashiCorp Vault, and many others. External Secrets Operator is a Kubernetes operator that integrates external secret management systems. It reads information from external APIs and automatically injects the values into Kubernetes Secrets, keeping them synchronized with the external source.
docs.title: eso

docs.text: Multi-Provider Support : Integrates with 20+ secret management providers Automatic Synchronization : Keeps Kubernetes secrets in sync with external sources Secure by Design : Secrets are fetched at runtime, not stored in Git Flexible Configuration : Supports namespace-scoped and cluster-wide secret stores Template Support : Transform and combine secrets before injection High Availability : Configurable replica counts for production deployments
docs.title: Features

docs.text: After installation, the following deployments will be available: kubectl get deployments -n external-secrets-system NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE external-secrets 1/1 1 1 5m external-secrets-cert-controller 1/1 1 1 5m external-secrets-webhook 1/1 1 1 5m
docs.title: Deployed Components

docs.text: The operator creates the following CRDs: kubectl get crd | grep external-secrets clustersecretstores.external-secrets.io externalsecrets.external-secrets.io secretstores.external-secrets.io clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io pushsecrets.external-secrets.io

docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Action to perform — one of install , uninstall , create-clustersecretstore , delete-clustersecretstore , create-secretstore , or delete-secretstore . Optional Environment Variable: ESO_ACTION Default: install Installation is idempotent and can be run multiple times safely; uninstallation behavior depends on the cleanup flags. The create-* / delete-* actions manage IBM Secrets Manager stores and require the IBM Secrets Manager configuration variables. A ClusterSecretStore is cluster-wide and can be used by ExternalSecrets in any namespace, whereas a SecretStore is namespace-scoped and can only be used by ExternalSecrets in the same namespace.
docs.title: eso_action

docs.text: Namespace for the External Secrets Operator installation — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: ESO_NAMESPACE Default: external-secrets-system All operator resources (deployments, services, webhooks) are created in this namespace, which is created if it doesn't exist. The default follows the operator's standard convention — override only for specific namespace requirements or multiple operator instances. CRDs are cluster-scoped regardless of namespace.
docs.title: eso_namespace

docs.text: Helm release name for the External Secrets Operator — a valid Helm release name (alphanumeric with hyphens), unique within the namespace. Optional Environment Variable: ESO_RELEASE_NAME Default: external-secrets Used for Helm operations (install, upgrade, uninstall) and appears in helm list and other Helm commands; use the default unless deploying multiple instances or following specific naming conventions.
docs.title: eso_release_name

docs.text: Helm repository URL for External Secrets charts — any valid HTTPS URL to a Helm repository. Optional Environment Variable: ESO_REPO_URL Default: https://charts.external-secrets.io The default points to the official External Secrets Helm repository; override for private mirrors, custom repositories, or air-gapped/restricted environments.
docs.title: eso_repo_url

docs.text: Specific version of the External Secrets Helm chart to install — a valid semantic version (e.g., 0.9.11 , 0.10.0 ). Optional Environment Variable: ESO_CHART_VERSION Default: "" (latest version) Leave empty to install the latest available version (suitable for development/testing); pin a specific version for production deployments, version upgrades, or rollbacks. Check the releases page for available versions — pinning versions is recommended in production.
docs.title: eso_chart_version

docs.text: Custom Helm values to override the default chart configuration — a dictionary of valid Helm chart values. Optional Environment Variable: None (must be set in playbook) Default: {} (empty dictionary) Use to override resource limits and requests, replica counts for high availability, security contexts, provider-specific configurations, and feature flags. Values are merged with the defaults in templates/values.yml.j2 , overriding any conflicts — see Helm chart values for available options and the Example Playbooks below for usage.
docs.title: eso_values

docs.text: Flag to control CRD deletion during uninstallation — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ESO_CLEANUP_CRDS Default: false With false (recommended unless performing complete removal), CRDs and custom resources remain after uninstall; with true , all CRDs and custom resources are deleted. CRDs are cluster-scoped and affect all namespaces. Warning Setting this to true deletes all ExternalSecret and SecretStore resources in the cluster.
docs.title: eso_cleanup_crds

docs.text: Flag to control namespace deletion during uninstallation — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ESO_CLEANUP_NAMESPACE Default: false With false (recommended unless performing complete removal), the namespace remains after uninstall; with true , the namespace is deleted, including any remaining resources. Namespace deletion will fail if resources still exist in it.
docs.title: eso_cleanup_namespace

docs.text: Provider type for secret store creation — currently only ibm (IBM Secrets Manager) is supported. Optional Environment Variable: ESO_PROVIDER Default: ibm Only used when eso_action is one of the secret store actions (not install / uninstall ); it determines which provider-specific tasks are executed. Future versions may support additional providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, HashiCorp Vault, etc.).
docs.title: eso_provider

docs.text: Name for the SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore resource — a valid Kubernetes resource name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: ESO_STORE_NAME Default: ibm-secrets-manager Only used with the secret store actions; the name must be unique within the cluster for a ClusterSecretStore (cluster-scoped) and is referenced by ExternalSecret resources. The associated credentials secret is named {eso_store_name}-apikey . Override the default if you need multiple store instances or have specific naming requirements.
docs.title: eso_store_name

docs.text: IBM Secrets Manager instance URL — a valid HTTPS URL (e.g., https://my-instance.secrets-manager.cloud.ibm.com ). Required when using the create-clustersecretstore or create-secretstore actions Environment Variable: IBM_SM_INSTANCE_URL Default: None Determines which IBM Secrets Manager instance the External Secrets Operator will connect to; the instance must be accessible from your Kubernetes cluster.
docs.title: ibm_sm_instance_url

docs.text: IBM Cloud API key for authenticating with IBM Secrets Manager — a valid key with IAM permissions to access the Secrets Manager instance. Required when using the create-clustersecretstore or create-secretstore actions Environment Variable: IBM_SM_API_KEY or IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: Falls back to IBMCLOUD_APIKEY if IBM_SM_API_KEY is not set Used to authenticate the External Secrets Operator with IBM Secrets Manager; the API key is stored as a Kubernetes secret (named {eso_store_name}-apikey ) in the operator namespace. The IBMCLOUD_APIKEY fallback follows the collection pattern for convenience.
docs.title: ibm_sm_api_key

docs.text: Namespace for the IBM Secrets Manager SecretStore (namespace-scoped) — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Required when using the create-secretstore or delete-secretstore actions Environment Variable: IBM_SM_STORE_NAMESPACE Default: None Determines which namespace the SecretStore and its credentials secret will be created in; the namespace is created if it doesn't exist during create-secretstore . A SecretStore can only be used by ExternalSecrets in the same namespace — for cluster-wide access, use create-clustersecretstore instead (which does not require this variable).
docs.title: ibm_sm_store_namespace

docs.text: gencfg_jdbc ¤ Generate JDBC configuration files for connecting Maximo Application Suite to external databases. This role creates JdbcCfg custom resources that can be applied to MAS instances to configure database connectivity for various applications including Manage, Health, Predict, and others. The role supports multiple database types (Db2, Oracle, SQL Server) with both secure and insecure connection options, and can generate configurations scoped at system, workspace, application, or workspace-application levels. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default db_instance_id No dbinst db_username Yes None jdbc_instance_password Yes None jdbc_url Yes None ssl_enabled Yes None db_pem_file Conditional None mas_config_scope Yes None mas_instance_id Yes None mas_workspace_id Conditional None mas_application_id Conditional None mas_config_dir Yes None custom_labels No None db_pem_file is required when ssl_enabled is true ; mas_workspace_id is required when mas_config_scope is ws or wsapp , and mas_application_id when the scope is app or wsapp . Database Connection ¤ db_instance_id ¤ Database instance identifier used in the generated configuration — an alphanumeric string, typically lowercase with no spaces (for example maxdb01 , manage-prod , or oracle-dev ). Optional Environment Variable: DB_INSTANCE_ID Default: dbinst This ID is used to reference the database connection in application configurations and must be unique within the scope of the MAS instance; the default dbinst is suitable for simple single-database deployments, but use descriptive names in multi-database environments to avoid confusion. db_username ¤ Database username that MAS applications will use to connect to the database; the user must have the privileges the target application needs — for Manage, full access to the MAXIMO schema. Required Environment Variable: MAS_JDBC_USER Default: None Insufficient permissions will cause application failures. For Oracle, the schema prefix may need to be included in some configurations, and the user should have appropriate connection limits configured in the database. jdbc_instance_password ¤ Password for the database user account specified in db_username . Required Environment Variable: MAS_JDBC_PASSWORD Default: None The password is stored as a Kubernetes secret in the MAS namespace. Ensure the password doesn't contain characters that require URL encoding if it is embedded in connection strings. jdbc_url ¤ Complete JDBC connection string including host, port, database name, and connection parameters, formatted for the target database type — for example jdbc:db2://dbserver.example.com:50000/maxdb for IBM Db2 (insecure), jdbc:db2://dbserver.example.com:50000/maxdb:sslConnection=true; for Db2 (secure), or jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbserver.example.com:1521:maximo for Oracle. Required Environment Variable: MAS_JDBC_URL Default: None SQL Server URLs take the form jdbc:sqlserver://;serverName=dbserver.example.com;portNumber=1433;databaseName=maxdb;integratedSecurity=false;sendStringParametersAsUnicode=false;selectMethod=cursor;encrypt=false;trustServerCertificate=false; — use encrypt=true;trustServerCertificate=true; for secure connections. Port numbers and database names must match your actual database, some databases require specific JDBC driver parameters for optimal performance, and the SSL/TLS settings must match ssl_enabled and the database server configuration. Always test the JDBC URL with a database client before using it in MAS. ssl_enabled ¤ Whether SSL/TLS encryption is enabled for the database connection — true (encryption enabled) or false (insecure connection). Required Environment Variable: SSL_ENABLED Default: None Explicitly declares the SSL/TLS status for applications that cannot determine this from the JDBC URL alone; a mismatch with the SSL settings in jdbc_url will cause connection failures in some MAS applications. Always use true for production environments, and provide db_pem_file when it is set. db_pem_file ¤ Local file path to the database SSL/TLS certificate in PEM format — for example /tmp/db-ca.pem or ./certs/database-cert.pem . Optional , required when ssl_enabled is true Environment Variable: MAS_JDBC_CERT_LOCAL_FILE Default: None The certificate is embedded in the generated JdbcCfg resource; without the correct certificate, SSL connections will fail with certificate validation errors. The file must be accessible from the Ansible controller and be PEM format (Base64-encoded with BEGIN/END markers). For self-signed certificates this should be the CA certificate, and for commercial certificates you may need to include the full certificate chain. MAS Configuration ¤ mas_config_scope ¤ Configuration scope level at which the generated JDBC configuration will be available within MAS — system (all workspaces and applications), ws (a specific workspace), app (a specific application across all workspaces), or wsapp (a specific application in a specific workspace). Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_SCOPE Default: None Use system for shared databases used by multiple applications, and wsapp for dedicated databases per workspace-application combination. The scope cannot be changed after creation; changing it requires recreating the configuration. mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier that the configuration is being generated for — typically 3-12 lowercase alphanumeric characters, case-sensitive, matching the instance ID used during MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The generated configuration is namespace-scoped to mas-<instance_id>-core ; an incorrect instance ID will cause the configuration to be created in the wrong namespace. mas_workspace_id ¤ MAS workspace identifier for workspace-scoped configurations — for example masdev , prod , or test . Required if mas_config_scope is ws or wsapp Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None The JDBC configuration will only be available to the specified workspace; the workspace must exist before applying the configuration. Use workspace-scoped configs for tenant isolation in multi-tenant deployments. mas_application_id ¤ MAS application identifier for application-scoped configurations — valid values are manage , health , predict , monitor , assist , visualinspection , iot , optimizer , and safety . Required if mas_config_scope is app or wsapp Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None The JDBC configuration will only be available to the specified application; the application must be installed before applying the configuration. Most commonly used with manage for Manage-specific databases. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory path where the generated JdbcCfg YAML file will be saved — the directory is created if it doesn't exist. Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The generated file is named jdbccfg-<db_instance_id>.yml and can be applied using kubectl apply or the suite_config role; keep generated files for documentation and disaster recovery purposes. Resource Labels ¤ custom_labels ¤ Custom Kubernetes labels to apply to the generated JdbcCfg resource, as comma-separated key=value pairs — for example env=prod,team=platform,cost-center=12345 . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels are useful for environment identification, cost tracking, GitOps workflows, and selection with label selectors in automation scripts; they must follow Kubernetes naming conventions. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.gencfg_jdbc License ¤ EPL-2.0

Always use true for production environments, and provide db_pem_file when it is set.
docs.title: ssl_enabled

docs.text: Local file path to the database SSL/TLS certificate in PEM format — for example /tmp/db-ca.pem or ./certs/database-cert.pem . Optional , required when ssl_enabled is true Environment Variable: MAS_JDBC_CERT_LOCAL_FILE Default: None The certificate is embedded in the generated JdbcCfg resource; without the correct certificate, SSL connections will fail with certificate validation errors. The file must be accessible from the Ansible controller and be PEM format (Base64-encoded with BEGIN/END markers). For self-signed certificates this should be the CA certificate, and for commercial certificates you may need to include the full certificate chain.
docs.title: db_pem_file

docs.text: Configuration scope level at which the generated JDBC configuration will be available within MAS — system (all workspaces and applications), ws (a specific workspace), app (a specific application across all workspaces), or wsapp (a specific application in a specific workspace). Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_SCOPE Default: None Use system for shared databases used by multiple applications, and wsapp for dedicated databases per workspace-application combination. The scope cannot be changed after creation; changing it requires recreating the configuration.
docs.title: mas_config_scope

docs.text: MAS instance identifier that the configuration is being generated for — typically 3-12 lowercase alphanumeric characters, case-sensitive, matching the instance ID used during MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The generated configuration is namespace-scoped to mas-<instance_id>-core ; an incorrect instance ID will cause the configuration to be created in the wrong namespace.
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: MAS workspace identifier for workspace-scoped configurations — for example masdev , prod , or test . Required if mas_config_scope is ws or wsapp Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None The JDBC configuration will only be available to the specified workspace; the workspace must exist before applying the configuration. Use workspace-scoped configs for tenant isolation in multi-tenant deployments.
docs.title: mas_workspace_id

docs.text: MAS application identifier for application-scoped configurations — valid values are manage , health , predict , monitor , assist , visualinspection , iot , optimizer , and safety . Required if mas_config_scope is app or wsapp Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None The JDBC configuration will only be available to the specified application; the application must be installed before applying the configuration. Most commonly used with manage for Manage-specific databases.
docs.title: mas_application_id

docs.text: Local directory path where the generated JdbcCfg YAML file will be saved — the directory is created if it doesn't exist. Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The generated file is named jdbccfg-<db_instance_id>.yml and can be applied using kubectl apply or the suite_config role; keep generated files for documentation and disaster recovery purposes.
docs.title: mas_config_dir

docs.text: Custom Kubernetes labels to apply to the generated JdbcCfg resource, as comma-separated key=value pairs — for example env=prod,team=platform,cost-center=12345 . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels are useful for environment identification, cost tracking, GitOps workflows, and selection with label selectors in automation scripts; they must follow Kubernetes naming conventions.
docs.title: custom_labels

docs.text: gencfg_mongo ¤ Generate MongoDB configuration files for connecting Maximo Application Suite to external MongoDB or MongoDB-compatible databases. This role creates MongoCfg custom resources that can be applied to MAS instances to configure the system database connectivity. The role supports various MongoDB deployments including MongoDB Community Edition, MongoDB Enterprise, IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB, and Amazon DocumentDB, with flexible authentication mechanisms and SSL/TLS support. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mongodb_admin_username Yes None mongodb_admin_password Yes None mongodb_hosts Yes None mongodb_authentication_mechanism No DEFAULT mongodb_authentication_database No admin mongodb_retry_writes No true mongodb_ca_pem_local_file Yes None mongodb_namespace No mongoce mas_instance_id Yes None mas_config_dir Yes None custom_labels No None MongoDB Connection ¤ mongodb_admin_username ¤ MongoDB user account that MAS will use to connect to the MongoDB system database — for SCRAM authentication a standard MongoDB username, for LDAP authentication an LDAP distinguished name or username. Required Environment Variable: MONGODB_ADMIN_USERNAME Default: None The user must have read/write access ( readWrite role) to the MAS databases; insufficient permissions will cause MAS core services to fail. Consider using a dedicated service account rather than the MongoDB admin user. mongodb_admin_password ¤ Password for the MongoDB user account specified in mongodb_admin_username . Required Environment Variable: MONGODB_ADMIN_PASSWORD Default: None The password is stored as a Kubernetes secret in the MAS namespace. For Amazon DocumentDB, use the master user password or IAM authentication. mongodb_hosts ¤ MongoDB connection endpoints as a comma-separated list of hostname:port pairs — for example mongodb.example.com:27017 for a single node, mongo-1.example.com:27017,mongo-2.example.com:27017,mongo-3.example.com:27017 for a replica set, or docdb-cluster.abc123.us-east-1.docdb.amazonaws.com:27017 for Amazon DocumentDB. Required Environment Variable: MONGODB_HOSTS Default: None Always include the port number (typically 27017) and list all replica set members for redundancy and automatic failover. Hostnames must be resolvable from the OpenShift cluster, and for cloud databases verify network connectivity and firewall rules. mongodb_authentication_mechanism ¤ Authentication mechanism for connecting to MongoDB — DEFAULT for MongoDB's standard SCRAM authentication (SCRAM-SHA-256 or SCRAM-SHA-1), or PLAIN for LDAP authentication (requires MongoDB Enterprise with LDAP integration). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_AUTHENTICATION_MECHANISM Default: DEFAULT Must match the authentication configuration of your MongoDB deployment. Amazon DocumentDB uses SCRAM authentication, so use DEFAULT ; when using PLAIN , ensure mongodb_authentication_database is set to $external . mongodb_authentication_database ¤ MongoDB database that contains the user credentials for authentication — admin for standard MongoDB authentication, $external for LDAP authentication, or a custom database name if users are stored elsewhere. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_AUTHENTICATION_DATABASE Default: admin Must be $external when mongodb_authentication_mechanism is PLAIN ; for Amazon DocumentDB use admin . Rarely needs changing from the default unless using custom user databases. mongodb_retry_writes ¤ Whether the MongoDB driver automatically retries write operations that fail due to transient network errors or replica set elections — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_RETRY_WRITES Default: true Recommended true for MongoDB 3.6+ replica sets; standalone MongoDB instances may not support retryable writes. Warning Must be set to false for Amazon DocumentDB — DocumentDB does not support retryable writes, and connections will fail if this is enabled. mongodb_ca_pem_local_file ¤ Local file path to the MongoDB SSL/TLS CA certificate in PEM format — for example /tmp/mongo-ca.pem or ./certs/mongodb-cert.pem . Required Environment Variable: MONGODB_CA_PEM_LOCAL_FILE Default: None MongoDB connections should always use SSL/TLS encryption. The certificate is embedded in the generated MongoCfg resource; without the correct CA certificate, SSL/TLS connections will fail with certificate validation errors. The file must be accessible from the Ansible controller and be in PEM format (Base64-encoded with BEGIN/END markers). For Amazon DocumentDB download the CA certificate from AWS, for IBM Cloud Databases from the IBM Cloud console, and for self-signed certificates provide the CA that signed the MongoDB server certificate. Configuration Generation ¤ mongodb_namespace ¤ Namespace identifier used as a suffix in the generated configuration filename ( mongo-<namespace>.yml ) — for example mongoce , docdb , or prod-mongo . Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_NAMESPACE Default: mongoce Only affects the generated filename, not the MongoDB connection or MAS configuration; the default mongoce indicates MongoDB Community Edition. Use descriptive names when managing multiple MongoDB instances. mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier that the MongoDB configuration is being generated for — typically 3-12 lowercase alphanumeric characters, case-sensitive, matching the instance ID used during MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The generated configuration is namespace-scoped to mas-<instance_id>-core ; an incorrect instance ID will cause the configuration to be created in the wrong namespace. MongoDB is the system database for MAS core services. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory path where the generated MongoCfg YAML file will be saved — the directory is created if it doesn't exist. Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The generated file is named mongo-<mongodb_namespace>.yml and can be applied using kubectl apply or used as input to the suite_config role; keep generated files for documentation and disaster recovery purposes. Resource Labels ¤ custom_labels ¤ Custom Kubernetes labels to apply to the generated MongoCfg resource, as comma-separated key=value pairs — for example env=prod,team=platform,cost-center=12345 . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels are useful for environment identification, cost tracking, GitOps workflows, and selection with label selectors in automation scripts; they must follow Kubernetes naming conventions. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mongodb_namespace: mongoce mongodb_admin_username: mongoadmin mongodb_admin_password: mongo-strong-password mongodb_hosts: docdb-1.abc.ca-central-1.docdb.amazonaws.com:27017,docdb-2.def.ca-central-1.docdb.amazonaws.com:27017 mongodb_retry_writes: false mongodb_ca_pem_local_file: /tmp/mongo-ca.pem mas_instance_id: masinst1 mas_config_dir: ~/masconfig roles: - ibm.mas_devops.gencfg_mongo License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: gencfg_watsonstudio ¤ Generate Watson Studio configuration files for connecting Maximo Application Suite to IBM Cloud Pak for Data Watson Studio instances. This role creates WatsonStudioCfg custom resources that enable MAS applications (particularly Predict and Health) to leverage Watson Studio's machine learning and analytics capabilities. The role supports flexible configuration scoping to make Watson Studio available at system, workspace, application, or workspace-application levels within MAS. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_config_scope No system mas_workspace_id Conditional None mas_application_id Conditional None mas_config_dir Yes None cpd_admin_url Yes None cpd_admin_username Yes None cpd_admin_password Yes None custom_labels No None mas_workspace_id is required only when mas_config_scope is ws or wsapp , and mas_application_id only when the scope is app or wsapp . MAS Configuration ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier for which the Watson Studio configuration is being generated — a valid MAS instance ID (typically 3-12 lowercase alphanumeric characters) that must match the instance ID used during MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The generated configuration is namespace-scoped to mas-<instance-id>-core ; an incorrect instance ID will cause the configuration to be created in the wrong namespace. The value is case-sensitive. Watson Studio integration is primarily used by the Predict and Health applications for AI/ML model training and deployment in MAS. mas_config_scope ¤ Configuration scope level for the generated Watson Studio configuration — system (available to all workspaces and applications, the default), ws (a specific workspace), app (a specific application across all workspaces), or wsapp (a specific application in a specific workspace). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_SCOPE Default: system Determines which MAS components can access the Watson Studio configuration; an incorrect scope may prevent applications from finding the Watson Studio connection. The default system scope is suitable for most deployments, while wsapp is useful for dedicated Watson Studio instances per workspace-application. The scope cannot be changed after creation — it requires recreating the configuration. mas_workspace_id ¤ MAS workspace identifier for workspace-scoped configurations — a valid MAS workspace ID, typically lowercase alphanumeric, for example masdev , prod , or test . Required when mas_config_scope is ws or wsapp Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None The Watson Studio configuration is only available to the specified workspace; applications in other workspaces cannot access this Watson Studio instance. The workspace must exist before applying the configuration. Use workspace-scoped configs for tenant isolation in multi-tenant deployments, where each workspace can have its own Watson Studio instance for data isolation. mas_application_id ¤ MAS application identifier for application-scoped configurations — typically predict or health , the primary Watson Studio consumers. Required when mas_config_scope is app or wsapp Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None The Watson Studio configuration is only available to the specified application; other applications cannot access this Watson Studio instance. The application must be installed before applying the configuration. Use application-scoped configs when different applications need different Watson Studio instances. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory path where the generated YAML configuration file will be saved — a valid directory path (absolute or relative) where the Ansible controller has write permissions. Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The generated file ( watsonstudiocfg-<scope>.yml ) can be applied using kubectl apply or used as input to the suite_config role; the directory is created if it does not exist. Keep the generated files for documentation and disaster recovery purposes. Cloud Pak for Data Connection ¤ cpd_admin_url ¤ Cloud Pak for Data console URL for Watson Studio access — the full HTTPS URL to the CP4D console, for example https://cpd-cpd.apps.ocp.example.com . Required Environment Variable: CPD_ADMIN_URL Default: None MAS applications use this URL to access Watson Studio APIs; an incorrect or inaccessible URL will prevent AI/ML functionality. The URL must be accessible from the OpenShift cluster where MAS is running (verify network connectivity and firewall rules) and must point to the CP4D console route, not individual service routes. For multi-cluster deployments, ensure proper routing is configured. cpd_admin_username ¤ Cloud Pak for Data administrative username for Watson Studio access — a valid Cloud Pak for Data username with Watson Studio access rights. Required Environment Variable: CPD_ADMIN_USERNAME Default: None This user must have permissions to create and manage Watson Studio projects, deployments, and models; insufficient permissions will cause Predict/Health AI features to fail. Consider using a dedicated service account rather than a personal admin account, with appropriate resource quotas for ML workloads. cpd_admin_password ¤ Cloud Pak for Data password for authentication — a strong password string meeting Cloud Pak for Data security requirements. Required Environment Variable: CPD_ADMIN_PASSWORD Default: None The password for the user account specified in cpd_admin_username is stored securely as a Kubernetes secret in the MAS namespace; an incorrect password will prevent MAS from connecting to Watson Studio. Follow your organization's password and rotation policies, and ensure the password does not expire in a way that could break the integration. Resource Labels ¤ custom_labels ¤ Custom Kubernetes labels to apply to the generated WatsonStudioCfg resource, as a comma-separated list of key=value pairs — for example env=prod,team=ai-ml,cost-center=12345 . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels must follow Kubernetes naming conventions; they can be used with label selectors for filtering, GitOps workflows, and automation scripts, and are helpful for tracking Watson Studio configurations across multiple environments. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.gencfg_watsonstudio License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: gencfg_workspace ¤ This role generates a Workspace custom resource configuration file for Maximo Application Suite. The generated configuration can be applied manually or automatically using the suite_config role. The configuration file is saved to local disk in the directory specified by mas_config_dir . Tip Workspaces are logical containers in MAS that isolate data and configurations for different business units, environments, or use cases. Each workspace can have its own applications, users, and data. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_workspace_id Yes None mas_workspace_name Yes None mas_config_dir Yes None custom_labels No None Workspace Definition ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier the workspace will be associated with — a lowercase alphanumeric string, 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , masinst1 ), matching the instance ID from the MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The generated configuration file is named and structured for this specific instance. Multiple workspaces can exist within a single MAS instance, each with its own ID and configuration. mas_workspace_id ¤ Unique technical identifier for the workspace within the MAS instance — a lowercase alphanumeric string, typically 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , masdev , qa ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None This ID is used in URLs (e.g. https://instance.mas.com/masdev ), API calls, Kubernetes resource names, and the generated filename. Choose a meaningful ID that reflects the workspace purpose — it cannot be changed after workspace creation. mas_workspace_name ¤ Human-readable display name for the workspace, shown in the MAS user interface — any string, typically 3-50 characters (e.g. Production , Development , MAS Development , QA Environment ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_NAME Default: None Unlike the workspace ID, this name can include spaces and special characters, and it can be changed after creation if needed. Configuration Output ¤ mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory where the generated workspace configuration YAML file is written — a valid, writable local filesystem path such as /home/user/masconfig or ~/masconfig/inst1 . Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The directory is created if it doesn't exist. The generated file can then be applied manually with oc apply or automatically with the suite_config role; organizing configs by instance ID (e.g. /masconfig/inst1/ , /masconfig/inst2/ ) keeps things clear. custom_labels ¤ Custom Kubernetes labels to add to the generated workspace resources — comma-separated key=value pairs (e.g. env=prod,team=operations,cost-center=12345 ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Useful for resource organization and filtering, cost allocation and tracking, automation and policy enforcement, and organizational categorization — common in multi-tenant or managed environments. Labels must follow Kubernetes naming conventions (alphanumeric, hyphens, dots, max 63 chars per segment); common uses include environment tags, team ownership, and cost center tracking. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: "inst1" mas_workspace_id: "masdev" mas_workspace_name: "MAS Development" mas_config_dir: "/home/david/masconfig/inst1" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.gencfg_workspace License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: This role generates a Workspace custom resource configuration file for Maximo Application Suite. The generated configuration can be applied manually or automatically using the suite_config role. The configuration file is saved to local disk in the directory specified by mas_config_dir . Tip Workspaces are logical containers in MAS that isolate data and configurations for different business units, environments, or use cases. Each workspace can have its own applications, users, and data.
docs.title: gencfg_workspace

docs.text: Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_workspace_id Yes None mas_workspace_name Yes None mas_config_dir Yes None custom_labels No None
docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: MAS instance identifier the workspace will be associated with — a lowercase alphanumeric string, 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , masinst1 ), matching the instance ID from the MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The generated configuration file is named and structured for this specific instance. Multiple workspaces can exist within a single MAS instance, each with its own ID and configuration.
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: Unique technical identifier for the workspace within the MAS instance — a lowercase alphanumeric string, typically 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , masdev , qa ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None This ID is used in URLs (e.g. https://instance.mas.com/masdev ), API calls, Kubernetes resource names, and the generated filename. Choose a meaningful ID that reflects the workspace purpose — it cannot be changed after workspace creation.
docs.title: mas_workspace_id

docs.text: Human-readable display name for the workspace, shown in the MAS user interface — any string, typically 3-50 characters (e.g. Production , Development , MAS Development , QA Environment ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_NAME Default: None Unlike the workspace ID, this name can include spaces and special characters, and it can be changed after creation if needed.
docs.title: mas_workspace_name

docs.text: Local directory where the generated workspace configuration YAML file is written — a valid, writable local filesystem path such as /home/user/masconfig or ~/masconfig/inst1 . Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The directory is created if it doesn't exist. The generated file can then be applied manually with oc apply or automatically with the suite_config role; organizing configs by instance ID (e.g. /masconfig/inst1/ , /masconfig/inst2/ ) keeps things clear.
docs.title: mas_config_dir

docs.text: Custom Kubernetes labels to add to the generated workspace resources — comma-separated key=value pairs (e.g. env=prod,team=operations,cost-center=12345 ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Useful for resource organization and filtering, cost allocation and tracking, automation and policy enforcement, and organizational categorization — common in multi-tenant or managed environments. Labels must follow Kubernetes naming conventions (alphanumeric, hyphens, dots, max 63 chars per segment); common uses include environment tags, team ownership, and cost center tracking.

docs.text: grafana ¤ Installs and configures an instance of Grafana for use with IBM Maximo Application Suite, using the community grafana operator Note The credentials for the grafana admin user are stored in grafana-admin-credentials secret in the grafana namespace. A route is created in the grafana namespace to allow access to the grafana UI. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default grafana_action No install grafana_major_version No 5 grafana_v4_namespace No grafana grafana_v5_namespace No grafana5 grafana_instance_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected grafana_instance_storage_size No 10Gi grafana_instance_storage_class is only required when the cluster has none of the supported storage classes that the role auto-detects. Installation ¤ grafana_action ¤ Action to perform on the Grafana installation — one of install (deploy the Grafana operator and instance), update (upgrade from Grafana v4 to v5), or uninstall (remove the Grafana operator and instance). Optional Environment Variable: GRAFANA_ACTION Default: install update creates a new v5 instance with a new URL; grafana_major_version controls the version to install or upgrade to, and grafana_v4_namespace / grafana_v5_namespace define the namespaces used by each version. Warning When upgrading from v4 to v5, the new instance will have a different URL and will not inherit the user database. The admin password will be reset, user accounts must be recreated, and the v4 instance remains until manually removed. grafana_major_version ¤ Grafana operator major version to install — 4 (legacy deployments only) or 5 (the current supported version, recommended for all new deployments). Optional Environment Variable: GRAFANA_MAJOR_VERSION Default: 5 Version 5 uses a different namespace ( grafana_v5_namespace ) and has breaking changes from version 4. Upgrading from v4 to v5 requires grafana_action=update and results in a new instance with a different URL and no user database migration. grafana_v4_namespace ¤ Namespace where the Grafana v4 operator and instance are installed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name. Only applies when grafana_major_version is 4 ; override the default ( grafana ) only if namespace conflicts exist. Optional Environment Variable: GRAFANA_NAMESPACE Default: grafana When upgrading from v4 to v5, both namespaces coexist: the v4 instance remains in this namespace until manually removed. grafana_v5_namespace ¤ Namespace where the Grafana v5 operator and instance are installed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name. Applies when grafana_major_version is 5 (the default); override the default ( grafana5 ) only if namespace conflicts exist. Optional Environment Variable: GRAFANA_V5_NAMESPACE Default: grafana5 The separate namespace from grafana_v4_namespace allows v4 and v5 to coexist during upgrades. After upgrading, the v4 instance remains in its namespace until manually removed. Storage ¤ grafana_instance_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the Grafana persistent volume that stores user data, dashboards, and configurations — any storage class supporting ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode; ReadWriteMany (RWX) classes also work. Required if the cluster has no supported storage class available Environment Variable: GRAFANA_INSTANCE_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-detected ( ibmc-file-gold-gid , ocs-storagecluster-cephfs , or azurefiles-premium ) RWO access mode is sufficient for Grafana; the RWX classes listed above also work but are not required, and the role auto-detects these common classes if available. An incorrect or unavailable storage class will cause the deployment to fail. grafana_instance_storage_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for Grafana user data, dashboards, and configurations — a Kubernetes storage size such as 10Gi , 20Gi , or 50Gi . Optional Environment Variable: GRAFANA_INSTANCE_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 10Gi The default 10Gi is sufficient for typical MAS monitoring deployments; increase it for environments with many dashboards or extensive data. When upgrading from v4 to v5, the new instance inherits the v4 storage size unless explicitly overridden. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: grafana_instance_storage_class: "ibmc-file-gold-gid" grafana_instance_storage_size: "15Gi" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.grafana To Upgrade from Grafana Operator from V4 to V5 - hosts: localhost vars: grafana_action: "update" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.grafana Note The upgraded v5 grafana inherits the storage class and size from the v4 configuration unless they are defined as environment variables. docs.text: ibm_catalogs ¤ This role installs the IBM Maximo Operator Catalog , which is a curated Operator Catalog derived from the IBM Operator Catalog , with all content certified compatible with IBM Maximo Application Suite. Additionally, for IBM employees only, the pre-release development operator catalog can be installed; this is achieved by setting both the artifactory_username and artifactory_token variables. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default ibm_catalogs_action No install mas_catalog_version No @@MAS_LATEST_CATALOG@@ artifactory_username No None artifactory_token No None mas_backup_dir Conditional None ibm_catalogs_backup_version Conditional Auto-generated mas_backup_dir is required when ibm_catalogs_action is backup or restore , and ibm_catalogs_backup_version is required when the action is restore . Catalog Installation ¤ ibm_catalogs_action ¤ Action to perform on the IBM Operator Catalog — valid values are install (default), backup , restore , uninstall , or none (skip the role entirely). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_CATALOGS_ACTION Default: install The backup and restore actions are described in detail in the Backup and Restore Operations section. mas_catalog_version ¤ Version of the IBM Maximo Operator Catalog to install — a valid catalog version string, for example v8-240625-amd64 or v9-250115-amd64 . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CATALOG_VERSION Default: @@MAS_LATEST_CATALOG@@ (latest stable version) Determines which operator versions are available for installation; the catalog version must be compatible with your target MAS version, otherwise MAS installation or upgrades may fail. Leave as default to install the latest stable catalog version (recommended), or pin to a specific version for reproducible deployments — the default value is automatically updated to the latest stable catalog version with each release. Development Variables ¤ artifactory_username ¤ Artifactory username for accessing pre-release development catalogs (IBM employees only). Optional Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None Provides authentication to IBM Artifactory for installing development catalog sources containing pre-release MAS operators, enabling testing of upcoming MAS versions before general availability. Must be set together with artifactory_token ; without both credentials, only production catalogs are available. Warning IBM employees only — for pre-release testing only. Never use development catalogs in production. Keep credentials secure and do not commit them to source control. artifactory_token ¤ Artifactory API token for accessing pre-release development catalogs (IBM employees only). Optional Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None Provides API token authentication to IBM Artifactory for installing development catalog sources containing pre-release MAS operators. Must be set together with artifactory_username ; without both credentials, only production catalogs are available. Generate tokens from IBM Artifactory. Warning IBM employees only — for pre-release testing only. Never use development catalogs in production. Keep this token secure and do not commit it to source control. Backup and Restore Variables ¤ mas_backup_dir ¤ Directory path where IBM Operator Catalog backup files will be stored — any valid local filesystem path, for example /backup/mas or /home/user/catalog-backups . Required when ibm_catalogs_action is backup or restore Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None Specifies the local filesystem directory where backup archives are created (for backup) or read from (for restore). All backup files and metadata are stored in a timestamped directory structure under this path: {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-catalog/ . Use a persistent location with sufficient storage space, and back it up to external storage for disaster recovery. ibm_catalogs_backup_version ¤ Version identifier for the backup, used to create unique backup directories — any string suitable for directory names (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores). Optional for backup (auto-generated if not provided) Required for restore Environment Variable: IBM_CATALOGS_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Auto-generated timestamp in format YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS (e.g., 20260122-131500 ) For backup, leaving this unset auto-generates a timestamp-based version and creates the directory {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-catalog/ ; for restore, you must specify the exact version identifier of the backup to restore, which is looked up in {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-catalog/ . When restoring, list the contents of mas_backup_dir to see the available backups. Backup and Restore Operations ¤ This section provides comprehensive information about IBM Operator Catalog backup and restore operations. Action Comparison ¤ Action Purpose Instance Resources Prerequisites Use Case backup Create backup Yes (catalog and related resources) Running IBM Operator Catalog Regular backups, disaster recovery preparation restore Full restore Yes (recreates catalog and related resources) Backup archive Disaster recovery, cluster migration, complete restoration Backup Process ¤ The IBM Operator Catalog backup operation creates a backup of your catalog installation resources: Catalog Resources : Backs up Kubernetes resources including: CatalogSource ( ibm-operator-catalog ) Secrets (for development catalogs: wiotp-docker-local ) ServiceAccounts ( ibm-operator-catalog , default ) Auto-discovered Secrets : Any secrets referenced by the backed-up resources are automatically discovered and included Note : The backup includes development catalog credentials if they were configured during installation. Backup Directory Structure: {mas_backup_dir}/ └── backup-{version}-catalog/ └── resources/ ├── catalogsources/ ├── secrets/ └── serviceaccounts/ Restore Process ¤ The IBM Operator Catalog restore operation performs a complete restoration of the catalog: Steps: Validates backup files and required variables Restores Secrets (or creates new wiotp-docker-local secret if artifactory_username and artifactory_token are provided) Restores ServiceAccounts Restores CatalogSource Waits for CatalogSource to be ready (up to 30 minutes) When to use: Disaster recovery scenarios Migrating IBM Operator Catalog to a new cluster Recreating a deleted catalog Setting up a new environment from backup Important Considerations ¤ Version Compatibility: Target catalog version should match the backup version The restore process validates version compatibility before proceeding Storage Requirements: Ensure sufficient storage in the backup directory Backup directory structure: {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-catalog/ Monitor disk space during backup operations Security: Backup files contain catalog configuration and credentials (for development catalogs) Secure backup directory with appropriate permissions (chmod 700 recommended) Consider encrypting backups for long-term storage Restrict access to backup files to authorized personnel only Development Catalog Credentials: If restoring with new artifactory_username and artifactory_token , the restore will create a new secret instead of using the backed-up one This allows updating credentials during restore if needed Backup and Restore Best Practices ¤ Regular Backups : Schedule automated backups at regular intervals, especially before upgrades Test Restores : Periodically test restore procedures in non-production environments Monitor Operations : Implement monitoring and alerting for backup failures Backup Validation : Verify backup integrity after completion Retention Policy : Implement and document backup retention policies Disaster Recovery : Include IBM Operator Catalog backup/restore in your DR plan Coordinate with Operators : Coordinate catalog backups with operator backups that depend on it Example Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - hosts: localhost roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ibm_catalogs Run Role Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can easily run the role standalone using the run_role playbook provided. ROLE_NAME=ibm_catalogs ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ibmcloud_resource_key ¤ Create IBM Cloud resource keys (apikeys for specific services associated to the account) Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default service_instance Yes None service_resource_key_name No <service_instance>_resource-key delete_service_key No False output_service_key_details_to_file No False output_dir No . Service Instance and Key ¤ service_instance ¤ The name of the IBM Cloud service instance for which to create or manage resource keys — must match the exact, case-sensitive name of an existing instance in your account (e.g., mas-db2-instance , mas-mongodb , mas-cos-bucket , cp4d-instance ). Required Environment Variable: SERVICE_INSTANCE Default: None The service instance must already exist, and you must have appropriate IAM permissions to create resource keys for it. The generated credentials are scoped to this specific instance; different service types (Db2, COS, etc.) generate different credential formats, and each instance can have multiple resource keys for different purposes. service_resource_key_name ¤ The name to assign to the resource key (service credentials) — any string following IBM Cloud resource naming conventions (alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores), unique within the service instance; recommended format <purpose>-<service>-key (e.g., mas-db2-key , backup-cos-key ). Optional Environment Variable: SERVICE_RESOURCE_KEY_NAME Default: <service_instance>_resource-key (derived from service_instance ) Used to identify the resource key in the IBM Cloud console and CLI, and is required when deleting a specific key. Set a custom name when you need multiple keys for the same service instance or want to follow naming conventions; the name cannot be changed after creation (deletion and recreation required). Keep track of key names for future deletion or rotation. Key Lifecycle ¤ delete_service_key ¤ Controls whether to delete the specified resource key instead of creating it — True to permanently delete the resource key identified by service_resource_key_name , False to create a new key (default). Optional Environment Variable: DELETE_SERVICE_KEY Default: False Useful for credential rotation, cleanup, or deprovisioning operations. The deletion does not affect the service instance itself, only the access credentials, and will fail if the key doesn't exist (this is not an error condition). Warning Deletion is irreversible — credentials cannot be recovered, and applications using them will immediately lose access. Ensure no applications are using the credentials before deletion; consider creating a new key first for zero-downtime rotation, and always verify the key name to avoid removing the wrong credentials. Output ¤ output_service_key_details_to_file ¤ Controls whether to save the resource key credentials to a JSON file — True to export the complete resource key details and credentials to service-key_<service_resource_key_name>.json , False to create no output file (default). Optional Environment Variable: OUTPUT_SERVICE_KEY_DETAILS_TO_FILE Default: False Useful for manual configuration, backup or documentation purposes, or integration with automation tools that consume JSON credentials. The JSON structure varies by service type (Db2, COS, MongoDB, etc.). Warning The output file contains sensitive credentials including connection strings, passwords, and API keys — protect it appropriately, do not commit it to version control, and consider encrypting it or storing it in a secrets manager. output_dir ¤ The directory path where the resource key JSON file will be saved — any valid local filesystem path (relative or absolute, e.g., ~/credentials , /opt/mas/keys , ./config ); the directory is created if it doesn't exist. Optional Environment Variable: OUTPUT_DIR Default: . (current directory, typically ibm/mas_devops ) Only used when output_service_key_details_to_file is True . The default . is relative to where Ansible is executed — for production use, specify an absolute path, ideally a dedicated credentials directory with restricted access. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: ibmcloud_apikey: xxx service_instance: xxx service_resource_key_name: xxx output_service_key_details_to_file: True OR False delete_service_key: True OR False roles: - ibmcloud_resource_key License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: Variable Required Default service_instance Yes None service_resource_key_name No <service_instance>_resource-key delete_service_key No False output_service_key_details_to_file No False output_dir No .
docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: The name of the IBM Cloud service instance for which to create or manage resource keys — must match the exact, case-sensitive name of an existing instance in your account (e.g., mas-db2-instance , mas-mongodb , mas-cos-bucket , cp4d-instance ). Required Environment Variable: SERVICE_INSTANCE Default: None The service instance must already exist, and you must have appropriate IAM permissions to create resource keys for it. The generated credentials are scoped to this specific instance; different service types (Db2, COS, etc.) generate different credential formats, and each instance can have multiple resource keys for different purposes.
docs.title: service_instance

docs.text: The name to assign to the resource key (service credentials) — any string following IBM Cloud resource naming conventions (alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores), unique within the service instance; recommended format <purpose>-<service>-key (e.g., mas-db2-key , backup-cos-key ). Optional Environment Variable: SERVICE_RESOURCE_KEY_NAME Default: <service_instance>_resource-key (derived from service_instance ) Used to identify the resource key in the IBM Cloud console and CLI, and is required when deleting a specific key. Set a custom name when you need multiple keys for the same service instance or want to follow naming conventions; the name cannot be changed after creation (deletion and recreation required). Keep track of key names for future deletion or rotation.
docs.title: service_resource_key_name

docs.text: Controls whether to delete the specified resource key instead of creating it — True to permanently delete the resource key identified by service_resource_key_name , False to create a new key (default). Optional Environment Variable: DELETE_SERVICE_KEY Default: False Useful for credential rotation, cleanup, or deprovisioning operations. The deletion does not affect the service instance itself, only the access credentials, and will fail if the key doesn't exist (this is not an error condition). Warning Deletion is irreversible — credentials cannot be recovered, and applications using them will immediately lose access. Ensure no applications are using the credentials before deletion; consider creating a new key first for zero-downtime rotation, and always verify the key name to avoid removing the wrong credentials.
docs.title: delete_service_key

docs.text: Controls whether to save the resource key credentials to a JSON file — True to export the complete resource key details and credentials to service-key_<service_resource_key_name>.json , False to create no output file (default). Optional Environment Variable: OUTPUT_SERVICE_KEY_DETAILS_TO_FILE Default: False Useful for manual configuration, backup or documentation purposes, or integration with automation tools that consume JSON credentials. The JSON structure varies by service type (Db2, COS, MongoDB, etc.). Warning The output file contains sensitive credentials including connection strings, passwords, and API keys — protect it appropriately, do not commit it to version control, and consider encrypting it or storing it in a secrets manager.
docs.title: output_service_key_details_to_file

docs.text: The directory path where the resource key JSON file will be saved — any valid local filesystem path (relative or absolute, e.g., ~/credentials , /opt/mas/keys , ./config ); the directory is created if it doesn't exist. Optional Environment Variable: OUTPUT_DIR Default: . (current directory, typically ibm/mas_devops ) Only used when output_service_key_details_to_file is True . The default . is relative to where Ansible is executed — for production use, specify an absolute path, ideally a dedicated credentials directory with restricted access.
docs.title: output_dir

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: ibmcloud_apikey: xxx service_instance: xxx service_resource_key_name: xxx output_service_key_details_to_file: True OR False delete_service_key: True OR False roles: - ibmcloud_resource_key
