docs.text: kafka ¤ This role provides support to install a Kafka Cluster using Strimzi , Red Hat AMQ Streams , IBM Event Streams or AWS MSK and generate configuration that can be directly applied to Maximo Application Suite. Both Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ streams component are massively scalable, distributed, and high-performance data streaming platform based on the Apache Kafka project. Both offer a distributed backbone that allows microservices and other applications to share data with high throughput and low latency. As more applications move to Kubernetes and Red Hat OpenShift, it is increasingly important to be able to run the communication infrastructure on the same platform. Red Hat OpenShift, as a highly scalable platform, is a natural fit for messaging technologies such as Kafka. The AMQ streams component makes running and managing Apache Kafka OpenShift native through the use of powerful operators that simplify the deployment, configuration, management, and use of Apache Kafka on Red Hat OpenShift. The AMQ streams component is part of the Red Hat AMQ family, which also includes the AMQ broker, a longtime innovation leader in Java™ Message Service (JMS) and polyglot messaging, as well as the AMQ interconnect router, a wide-area, peer-to-peer messaging solution. Under the covers, AMQ streams leverages Strimzi's architecture, resources and configurations. Note: The MAS license does not include entitlement for AMQ streams. The MAS Devops Collection supports this Kafka deployment as an example only. Therefore, we recommend the use of Strimzi for an opensource Kafka provider. Tip The role will generate a yaml file containing the definition of a Secret and KafkaCfg resource that can be used to configure the deployed cluster as the MAS system Kafka. This file can be directly applied using oc apply -f $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/kafkacfg-amqstreams-system.yaml or used in conjunction with the suite_config role. Prerequisites ¤ To run this role successfully you must have already installed the AWS CLI . Also, you need to have AWS user credentials configured via aws configure command or simply export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables with your corresponding AWS username credentials prior running this role. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default kafka_action No install kafka_provider No strimzi mas_instance_id Conditional None mas_config_dir Conditional None kafka_version No Provider-specific kafka_namespace No Provider-specific kafka_cluster_name No maskafka kafka_cluster_size No small kafka_storage_class No Auto-detected (RWO) kafka_storage_size No 100Gi zookeeper_storage_class No Auto-detected (RWO) zookeeper_storage_size No 10Gi kafka_user_name No masuser kafka_user_password No Auto-generated custom_labels No None ibmcloud_apikey Conditional None eventstreams_resourcegroup No Default / IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP eventstreams_name Conditional None eventstreams_plan No standard eventstreams_location No us-east / IBMCLOUD_REGION eventstreams_retention No 1209600000 eventstreams_create_manage_jms_topics No True aws_region Conditional None vpc_id Conditional None aws_msk_cidr_az1 Conditional None aws_msk_cidr_az2 Conditional None aws_msk_cidr_az3 Conditional None aws_msk_ingress_cidr Conditional None aws_msk_egress_cidr Conditional None aws_kafka_user_name Conditional None aws_kafka_user_password No None aws_msk_instance_type No kafka.m5.large aws_msk_volume_size No 100 aws_msk_instance_number No 3 aws_msk_secret No AmazonMSK_SECRET_{{kafka_cluster_name}} mas_instance_id and mas_config_dir are required together to generate the MAS KafkaCfg configuration. The IBM Event Streams variables marked conditional are required when kafka_provider is ibm , and the AWS MSK variables marked conditional are required when kafka_provider is aws . Actions and Providers ¤ kafka_action ¤ Specifies which operation to perform on the Kafka cluster — install , upgrade , or uninstall . Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_ACTION Default: install install deploys the Kafka operator and creates the cluster, upgrade upgrades an existing Kafka cluster, and uninstall removes the Kafka cluster and operator. The upgrade action is only available for the strimzi and redhat providers — IBM Event Streams and AWS MSK do not support in-place upgrades through this role. When upgrading, kafka_version defines the target version. kafka_provider ¤ Specifies which Kafka provider to use for deployment — strimzi , redhat , ibm , or aws . Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_PROVIDER Default: strimzi strimzi (default, recommended) deploys open-source Kafka on OpenShift using the Strimzi operator with no additional license, redhat deploys AMQ Streams (requires a separate Red Hat AMQ license not included with MAS), ibm provisions IBM Event Streams in IBM Cloud (managed service, requires an IBM Cloud account and incurs costs), and aws provisions AWS MSK in your AWS account (managed service, requires an AWS account and incurs costs). Different providers require different additional variables, and kafka_action=upgrade is only supported for strimzi and redhat . Important The MAS license does not include entitlement for Red Hat AMQ Streams — Strimzi is recommended for open-source Kafka. MAS Configuration Generation ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance ID for generating the KafkaCfg configuration — a lowercase alphanumeric string of 3-12 characters (e.g., prod , dev , inst1 ). Optional — required together with mas_config_dir for KafkaCfg generation Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Must match the instance ID of your MAS installation. When set along with mas_config_dir , the role generates a KafkaCfg YAML file targeting this MAS instance; if either variable is not set, no KafkaCfg template is generated and you will need to configure MAS manually. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory path where the generated KafkaCfg will be saved — any valid local filesystem path (e.g., /home/user/masconfig , ~/masconfig , ./config ). Optional — required together with mas_instance_id for KafkaCfg generation Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None When set with mas_instance_id , generates kafkacfg-{provider}-system.yaml in this directory; the file can be applied with oc apply or used with the suite_config role. Use the same directory across all MAS setup roles for consistency, and ensure the directory exists and is writable. If either mas_instance_id or mas_config_dir is not set, no KafkaCfg template is generated. Red Hat AMQ Streams & Strimzi Variables ¤ kafka_version ¤ Kafka version to deploy — a valid Kafka version supported by the operator (e.g., 3.8.0 , 3.9.0 ). Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_VERSION Default: 3.9.0 for Strimzi, 3.8.0 for Red Hat AMQ Streams, 3.3.1 for AWS MSK For Strimzi, the supported versions for strimzi-cluster-operator.v0.45.0 are 3.8.0 , 3.8.1 , and 3.9.0 . Before changing this value, verify the version is supported by your AMQ Streams operator or Strimzi operator — incompatible versions will cause deployment failures. This variable only applies to the Strimzi, Red Hat AMQ Streams, and AWS MSK providers, not IBM Event Streams. kafka_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the Kafka operator and cluster will be deployed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (e.g., strimzi , amq-streams , kafka-prod ). Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_NAMESPACE Default: strimzi for the Strimzi provider, amq-streams for Red Hat AMQ Streams All Kafka resources (operator, cluster, topics, users) are created in this namespace. Use the default for standard single-cluster deployments, and set a custom namespace (unique per cluster) when organizing multiple Kafka deployments. This variable only applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat providers. kafka_cluster_name ¤ Name for the Kafka cluster resource — a valid Kubernetes resource name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, e.g., maskafka , kafka-prod , mas-kafka ). Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_CLUSTER_NAME Default: maskafka This name is used throughout the Kafka deployment in resource names (services, pods, secrets) and appears in the generated KafkaCfg for MAS. For AWS MSK it is also used in the generated AWS resource names (security group, cluster configuration, KMS key, and secret). Choose a meaningful name — the default maskafka is suitable for single-cluster MAS deployments. kafka_cluster_size ¤ Predefined configuration size for the Kafka cluster — small or large . Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_CLUSTER_SIZE Default: small small allocates fewer resources, suitable for development, test, or small workloads; large allocates more resources (CPU, memory, replicas) for production workloads with higher throughput requirements. kafka_storage_size and zookeeper_storage_size should align with the cluster size — production environments typically require the large configuration for adequate performance and reliability. kafka_storage_class ¤ Storage class for Kafka broker persistent storage, where Kafka stores message logs and data — any storage class name supporting ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-detected from available storage classes in the cluster Leave unset for automatic detection (recommended), or set explicitly when you need a specific storage class. Kafka broker performance depends heavily on storage performance — block-based storage classes (e.g., ibmc-block-gold , ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ) typically provide better performance and are recommended for production workloads. A storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. This variable only applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers. kafka_storage_size ¤ Size of persistent storage for Kafka brokers, where Kafka stores all message logs and topic data — Kubernetes storage size format (e.g., 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti , 2Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 100Gi The default is suitable for small deployments only — production environments typically require 500Gi or more depending on message volume and retention (plan storage based on daily message volume × retention days). Insufficient storage will cause Kafka to stop accepting messages when volumes fill up; monitor usage and expand as needed. zookeeper_storage_class ¤ Storage class for Zookeeper persistent storage, where Zookeeper stores cluster metadata and coordination data — any storage class name supporting ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: ZOOKEEPER_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-detected from available storage classes in the cluster Leave unset for automatic detection (recommended), or set explicitly when you need a specific storage class — it can be the same as or different from kafka_storage_class . Zookeeper is critical for Kafka cluster coordination, so reliable storage is essential; a storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. This variable only applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers. zookeeper_storage_size ¤ Size of persistent storage for Zookeeper nodes, which store cluster metadata, configuration, and coordination data — Kubernetes storage size format (e.g., 10Gi , 20Gi , 50Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: ZOOKEEPER_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 10Gi The default is sufficient for most deployments — Zookeeper storage requirements are typically much smaller than Kafka broker storage and grow slowly with cluster size. Increase only for very large Kafka clusters with a very large number of topics and partitions. kafka_user_name ¤ Username for MAS to authenticate with Kafka — a valid Kafka username string (e.g., masuser , mas-kafka-user ), unique within the Kafka cluster. Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_USER_NAME Default: masuser This user is created in Kafka with the necessary permissions for MAS operations, and its credentials are included in the generated KafkaCfg when mas_instance_id is provided. Set a custom name when organizational policies require specific usernames. This variable only applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers. kafka_user_password ¤ Password for the Kafka user, used for SCRAM-SHA authentication — a strong password string meeting security requirements. Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_USER_PASSWORD Default: Randomly generated if not specified Leave unset for automatic random password generation (recommended for security); this feature requires Strimzi operator 0.25.0 or AMQ Streams 2.x+. The password is stored in Kafka secrets and included in the generated KafkaCfg for MAS — keep passwords secure and do not commit them to source control. custom_labels ¤ Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to Kafka resources (e.g., env=prod,team=platform,component=kafka ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Use for organizational metadata (e.g., cost-center=engineering , environment=production ), resource tracking, cost allocation, and custom automation or monitoring. Labels can be used for filtering with oc get commands, monitoring queries, and automation scripts, but do not affect Kafka functionality. This variable applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers, and is especially useful in multi-tenant environments. IBM Event Streams Variables ¤ ibmcloud_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API Key — must have access to manage (provision/deprovision) IBM Cloud Event Streams. Required when kafka_provider is ibm Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None eventstreams_resourcegroup ¤ IBM Cloud Resource Group to target the Event Streams instance. Optional Environment Variable: EVENTSTREAMS_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Default or the value defined by IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP eventstreams_name ¤ Event Streams instance name. Required when kafka_provider is ibm Environment Variable: EVENTSTREAMS_NAME Default: None eventstreams_plan ¤ Event Streams instance plan. Optional Environment Variable: EVENTSTREAMS_PLAN Default: standard eventstreams_location ¤ IBM Cloud location where the Event Streams instance will be provisioned. Optional Environment Variable: EVENTSTREAMS_LOCATION Default: us-east or the value defined by IBMCLOUD_REGION eventstreams_retention ¤ Event Streams topic retention period, in milliseconds. Optional Environment Variable: EVENTSTREAMS_RETENTION Default: 1209600000 eventstreams_create_manage_jms_topics ¤ Defines whether to create specific Manage application JMS topics by default. Optional Environment Variable: EVENTSTREAMS_CREATE_MANAGE_JMS_TOPICS Default: True AWS MSK Variables ¤ See kafka_version (default 3.3.1 for AWS MSK) and kafka_cluster_name (used in the generated AWS resource names) — both apply to AWS MSK as well. aws_region ¤ AWS region where the MSK cluster will be deployed. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: AWS_REGION Default: None vpc_id ¤ The AWS Virtual Private Cloud identifier (VPC ID) where the MSK instance will be hosted. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: VPC_ID Default: None aws_msk_cidr_az1 ¤ The CIDR address for the first Availability Zone subnet. This information is found in the subnet details under your VPC. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_CIDR_AZ1 Default: None aws_msk_cidr_az2 ¤ The CIDR address for the second Availability Zone subnet. This information is found in the subnet details under your VPC. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_CIDR_AZ2 Default: None aws_msk_cidr_az3 ¤ The CIDR address for the third Availability Zone subnet. This information is found in the subnet details under your VPC. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_CIDR_AZ3 Default: None aws_msk_ingress_cidr ¤ The IPv4 CIDR address for ingress connection. This information is found in the subnet details under your VPC. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_INGRESS_CIDR Default: None aws_msk_egress_cidr ¤ The IPv4 CIDR address for egress connection. This information is found in the subnet details under your VPC. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_EGRESS_CIDR Default: None aws_kafka_user_name ¤ The name of the user to setup in the cluster for MAS. Required when kafka_provider is aws Environment Variable: AWS_KAFKA_USER_NAME Default: None aws_kafka_user_password ¤ The password of the user to setup in the cluster for MAS. Optional Environment Variable: AWS_KAFKA_USER_PASSWORD Default: None aws_msk_instance_type ¤ The type/flavor of your MSK instance. Optional Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_INSTANCE_TYPE Default: kafka.m5.large aws_msk_volume_size ¤ The storage/volume size of your MSK instance. Optional Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_VOLUME_SIZE Default: 100 aws_msk_instance_number ¤ The number of broker/instances of your MSK instance. Optional Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_INSTANCE_NUMBER Default: 3 aws_msk_secret ¤ AWS MSK Secret name — the secret name must begin with the prefix AmazonMSK_ . Optional Environment Variable: AWS_MSK_SECRET Default: AmazonMSK_SECRET_{{kafka_cluster_name}} Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # Set storage class suitable for use on IBM Cloud ROKS kafka_storage_class: ibmc-block-gold # Generate a KafkaCfg template mas_instance_id: masinst1 mas_config_dir: ~/masconfig roles: - ibm.mas_devops.kafka Install AWS MSK ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: aws_region: ca-central-1 aws_access_key_id: ***** aws_secret_access_key: ***** kafka_version: 3.3.1 kafka_provider: aws kafka_action: install kafka_cluster_name: msk-abcd0zyxw kafka_namespace: msk-abcd0zyxw vpc_id: vpc-07088da510b3c35c5 aws_kafka_user_name: mskuser-abcd0zyxw aws_msk_instance_type: kafka.t3.small aws_msk_volume_size: 100 aws_msk_instance_number: 3 aws_msk_cidr_az1: "10.0.128.0/20" aws_msk_cidr_az2: "10.0.144.0/20" aws_msk_cidr_az3: "10.0.160.0/20" aws_msk_ingress_cidr: "10.0.0.0/16" aws_msk_egress_cidr: "10.0.0.0/16" # Generate a KafkaCfg template mas_config_dir: /var/tmp/masconfigdir mas_instance_id: abcd0zyxw roles: - ibm.mas_devops.kafka Uninstall AWS MSK ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: aws_region: ca-central-1 aws_access_key_id: ***** aws_secret_access_key: ***** vpc_id: vpc-07088da510b3c35c5 kafka_provider: aws kafka_action: uninstall kafka_cluster_name: msk-abcd0zyxw aws_msk_cidr_az1: "10.0.128.0/20" aws_msk_cidr_az2: "10.0.144.0/20" aws_msk_cidr_az3: "10.0.160.0/20" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.kafka Run Role Playbook ¤ export KAFKA_STORAGE_CLASS=ibmc-block-gold export MAS_INSTANCE_ID=masinst1 export MAS_CONFIG_DIR=~/masconfig ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_CLUSTER_NAME Default: maskafka This name is used throughout the Kafka deployment in resource names (services, pods, secrets) and appears in the generated KafkaCfg for MAS. For AWS MSK it is also used in the generated AWS resource names (security group, cluster configuration, KMS key, and secret). Choose a meaningful name — the default maskafka is suitable for single-cluster MAS deployments.
docs.title: kafka_cluster_name

docs.text: Predefined configuration size for the Kafka cluster — small or large . Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_CLUSTER_SIZE Default: small small allocates fewer resources, suitable for development, test, or small workloads; large allocates more resources (CPU, memory, replicas) for production workloads with higher throughput requirements. kafka_storage_size and zookeeper_storage_size should align with the cluster size — production environments typically require the large configuration for adequate performance and reliability.
docs.title: kafka_cluster_size

docs.text: Storage class for Kafka broker persistent storage, where Kafka stores message logs and data — any storage class name supporting ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-detected from available storage classes in the cluster Leave unset for automatic detection (recommended), or set explicitly when you need a specific storage class. Kafka broker performance depends heavily on storage performance — block-based storage classes (e.g., ibmc-block-gold , ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd ) typically provide better performance and are recommended for production workloads. A storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. This variable only applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers.
docs.title: kafka_storage_class

docs.text: Size of persistent storage for Kafka brokers, where Kafka stores all message logs and topic data — Kubernetes storage size format (e.g., 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti , 2Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 100Gi The default is suitable for small deployments only — production environments typically require 500Gi or more depending on message volume and retention (plan storage based on daily message volume × retention days). Insufficient storage will cause Kafka to stop accepting messages when volumes fill up; monitor usage and expand as needed.
docs.title: kafka_storage_size

docs.text: Storage class for Zookeeper persistent storage, where Zookeeper stores cluster metadata and coordination data — any storage class name supporting ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: ZOOKEEPER_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-detected from available storage classes in the cluster Leave unset for automatic detection (recommended), or set explicitly when you need a specific storage class — it can be the same as or different from kafka_storage_class . Zookeeper is critical for Kafka cluster coordination, so reliable storage is essential; a storage class that does not support RWO will cause the deployment to fail. This variable only applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers.
docs.title: zookeeper_storage_class

docs.text: Size of persistent storage for Zookeeper nodes, which store cluster metadata, configuration, and coordination data — Kubernetes storage size format (e.g., 10Gi , 20Gi , 50Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: ZOOKEEPER_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 10Gi The default is sufficient for most deployments — Zookeeper storage requirements are typically much smaller than Kafka broker storage and grow slowly with cluster size. Increase only for very large Kafka clusters with a very large number of topics and partitions.
docs.title: zookeeper_storage_size

docs.text: Username for MAS to authenticate with Kafka — a valid Kafka username string (e.g., masuser , mas-kafka-user ), unique within the Kafka cluster. Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_USER_NAME Default: masuser This user is created in Kafka with the necessary permissions for MAS operations, and its credentials are included in the generated KafkaCfg when mas_instance_id is provided. Set a custom name when organizational policies require specific usernames. This variable only applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers.
docs.title: kafka_user_name

docs.text: Password for the Kafka user, used for SCRAM-SHA authentication — a strong password string meeting security requirements. Optional Environment Variable: KAFKA_USER_PASSWORD Default: Randomly generated if not specified Leave unset for automatic random password generation (recommended for security); this feature requires Strimzi operator 0.25.0 or AMQ Streams 2.x+. The password is stored in Kafka secrets and included in the generated KafkaCfg for MAS — keep passwords secure and do not commit them to source control.
docs.title: kafka_user_password

docs.text: Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to Kafka resources (e.g., env=prod,team=platform,component=kafka ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Use for organizational metadata (e.g., cost-center=engineering , environment=production ), resource tracking, cost allocation, and custom automation or monitoring. Labels can be used for filtering with oc get commands, monitoring queries, and automation scripts, but do not affect Kafka functionality. This variable applies to the Strimzi and Red Hat AMQ Streams providers, and is especially useful in multi-tenant environments.
docs.title: custom_labels

docs.text: longhorn ¤ Deploy Longhorn distributed block storage system for Kubernetes, providing both ReadWriteMany (RWX) and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) storage for Maximo Application Suite. Longhorn is a lightweight, reliable, and easy-to-use distributed block storage system for Kubernetes. Originally developed by Rancher Labs, it is now an incubating project of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). Features ¤ Unified Storage Solution : Provides both RWX and RWO storage classes for MAS High Availability : Configurable replica count for data redundancy Web UI : Management interface available at https://longhorn-ui-longhorn-system.{clusterdomain} (OpenShift OAuth authentication) Dynamic Provisioning : Automatic volume provisioning for MAS workloads Snapshot Support : Built-in backup and snapshot capabilities Deployed Components ¤ After installation, the following deployments will be available: oc -n longhorn-system get deployments NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE csi-attacher 3/3 3 3 38m csi-provisioner 3/3 3 3 38m csi-resizer 3/3 3 3 38m csi-snapshotter 3/3 3 3 38m longhorn-driver-deployer 1/1 1 1 40m longhorn-ui 2/2 2 2 40m Storage Classes ¤ Two storage classes are automatically created: oc get storageclass | grep longhorn longhorn (default) driver.longhorn.io Delete Immediate true 40m longhorn-static driver.longhorn.io Delete Immediate true 40m Note : MAS uses dynamic provisioning with the longhorn storage class. The longhorn-static storage class is not used by MAS. Additional Resources ¤ What is Longhorn? Longhorn Helm Chart Settings Longhorn on OpenShift Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default longhorn_namespace No longhorn-system longhorn_replica_count No 3 Longhorn Deployment ¤ longhorn_namespace ¤ Namespace for the Longhorn installation (valid Kubernetes namespace name; created if it doesn't exist). Optional Environment Variable: LONGHORN_NAMESPACE Default: longhorn-system All Longhorn resources (deployments, services, storage classes) are created in this namespace, and the UI is accessible at https://longhorn-ui-{namespace}.{clusterdomain} . Storage classes are cluster-wide regardless of namespace. longhorn_replica_count ¤ Number of data replicas for Longhorn volumes — an integer between 1 and the number of worker nodes. Optional Environment Variable: LONGHORN_REPLICA_COUNT Default: 3 3 (production, tolerates 2 node failures) is recommended; 2 tolerates 1 node failure with reduced storage overhead; 1 is development only with no redundancy. Each replica consumes storage (3 replicas = 3x storage usage) and replicas are distributed across different nodes, so ensure the cluster has enough nodes and capacity. The replica count cannot be changed after volumes are created without recreating them. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: longhorn_namespace: longhorn-system longhorn_replica_count: 3 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.longhorn For development environments with reduced storage requirements: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: longhorn_namespace: longhorn-system longhorn_replica_count: 1 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.longhorn License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: minio ¤ Deploy a MinIO object storage instance in OpenShift for development and testing with IBM Maximo Application Suite. MinIO provides S3-compatible object storage and is deployed with persistent volume for data storage. The role creates a namespace, persistent volume claim, deployment, service, and route to make MinIO accessible within the cluster. The MinIO container image ( quay.io/ibmmas/minio ) and its digest are selected based on the MAS catalog. Development and Testing Only This MinIO deployment is intended for development and testing purposes only . For production environments, use enterprise-grade object storage solutions such as IBM Cloud Object Storage, AWS S3, or Azure Blob Storage. Features ¤ S3-Compatible API : Full compatibility with Amazon S3 API Persistent Storage : Data stored on persistent volumes Web Console : Built-in web interface for management, exposed via an edge-terminated route OpenShift Integration : Deployed as native OpenShift resources Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default minio_namespace No minio minio_instance_name No minio minio_root_user No minio minio_root_password No None primary_storage_class No Cluster default RWX storage class ocp_enable_ipv6 No false MinIO Deployment ¤ minio_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where MinIO is deployed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name; the namespace is created if it does not exist. Optional Environment Variable: MINIO_NAMESPACE Default: minio All MinIO resources (namespace, PVC, deployment, service, and route) are created in this namespace. Use different namespaces when deploying multiple MinIO instances. minio_instance_name ¤ Name for the MinIO deployment and associated resources — a valid Kubernetes resource name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: MINIO_INSTANCE_NAME Default: minio Used in the deployment name and the service selector. Use descriptive names for multiple instances (e.g. minio-dev , minio-test ). minio_root_user ¤ Root username for MinIO console and S3 API access — an alphanumeric string (minimum 3 characters). Optional Environment Variable: MINIO_ROOT_USER Default: minio The root user has full administrative access to MinIO. The default is acceptable for development and testing only. minio_root_password ¤ Root password for MinIO console and S3 API access — MinIO requires a password of at least 8 characters. Optional Environment Variable: MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD Default: None The role does not generate a password — set it explicitly and store it securely for future access. Storage ¤ primary_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the MinIO persistent volume claim — a valid storage class name available in the cluster. Optional Environment Variable: MINIO_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Cluster's default RWX storage class (auto-detected). The role fails if the value is not set and no default can be detected. The PVC ( minio-pvc ) requests 40Gi with ReadWriteOnce access mode using this storage class. Verify available storage classes with oc get storageclass ; consider the performance characteristics of the storage class when selecting it. Networking ¤ ocp_enable_ipv6 ¤ Configure MinIO to use IPv6 addressing — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ENABLE_IPV6 Default: false When true , the service is configured as SingleStack IPv6 and the MinIO server binds to IPv6 addresses for both the API (port 9000) and console (port 9090). Example Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - hosts: localhost vars: minio_namespace: minio minio_instance_name: minio-dev minio_root_user: admin minio_root_password: mySecurePassword123 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.minio Run Role Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can easily run the role standalone using the run_role playbook provided. export MINIO_NAMESPACE=minio export MINIO_INSTANCE_NAME=minio-dev export MINIO_ROOT_USER=admin export MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=mySecurePassword123 ROLE_NAME=minio ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

images are also mirrored: registry.redhat.io/openshift-service-mesh/istio-operator-bundle (specific digest) Requirements ¤ oc tool must be installed oc-mirror plugin must be installed Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mirror_mode Yes None mirror_working_dir Yes None mirror_redhat_platform No false mirror_redhat_operators No false redhat_pullsecret Yes None ocp_release Yes None ocp_min_version No None (mirrors all versions) ocp_max_version No None (mirrors all versions) registry_public_host Yes None registry_public_port Yes None registry_is_ecr No false registry_ecr_aws_region Conditional None registry_prefix_redhat No '' registry_username Conditional None registry_password Conditional None registry_ecr_aws_region is only required when registry_is_ecr=true ; registry_username and registry_password are required unless mirroring to AWS ECR, where AWS credentials are used instead. Mirror Actions ¤ mirror_mode ¤ Mirroring operation mode for Red Hat content — direct (mirror directly from Red Hat registries to the target registry; fastest, requires network access to both), to-filesystem (mirror to the local filesystem for offline transfer, enabling air-gapped deployment), or from-filesystem (mirror from the local filesystem to the target registry, completing the air-gapped deployment). Required Environment Variable: MIRROR_MODE Default: None Tip For air-gapped environments, use to-filesystem on a connected system, transfer the files, then use from-filesystem on the disconnected system. mirror_working_dir ¤ Working directory for mirroring operations — an absolute filesystem path (e.g. /tmp/mirror , /mnt/mirror-storage ) used to store manifests, temporary files, and disk-based mirror archives. The directory is created if it doesn't exist. Required Environment Variable: MIRROR_WORKING_DIR Default: None For to-filesystem mode, ensure the directory has sufficient space for all images — platform plus operator content can be hundreds of GB, and insufficient space will cause mirroring to fail. The directory structure is preserved for from-filesystem mode. mirror_redhat_platform ¤ Whether to mirror Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform release images — required for installing or upgrading OpenShift in disconnected environments. Optional Environment Variable: MIRROR_REDHAT_PLATFORM Default: false Platform images are a large download (tens of GB) — only enable this if you need to install or upgrade OpenShift in a disconnected environment. The patch version range mirrored is controlled by ocp_min_version and ocp_max_version within ocp_release . mirror_redhat_operators ¤ Whether to mirror selected content from the Red Hat operator catalogs — only the operators directly used by MAS are mirrored (see the catalog list above), not entire catalogs. Optional Environment Variable: MIRROR_REDHAT_OPERATORS Default: false When true , selected operators are mirrored from the certified, community, and redhat-operator-index catalogs; operator compatibility follows ocp_release . redhat_pullsecret ¤ Path to your Red Hat pull secret file, used to authenticate and pull images from Red Hat registries during mirroring — an absolute path to the pull secret JSON file (e.g. ~/pull-secret.json , /tmp/pull-secret.json ), obtained from the Red Hat OpenShift Console . Required Environment Variable: REDHAT_PULLSECRET Default: None The pull secret must be valid, non-expired, and associated with an active Red Hat account — without it, pulling Red Hat images fails and mirroring cannot proceed. Keep the file secure, as it contains authentication credentials. OpenShift Version ¤ ocp_release ¤ The Red Hat release you are mirroring content for — an OpenShift major.minor version (e.g. 4.22 , 4.21 , 4.20 , 4.19 , 4.18 , 4.17 , 4.16 ) that must match the OpenShift version in your target environment. Required Environment Variable: OCP_RELEASE Default: None Determines which platform images and operator versions are mirrored. Use the major.minor format (e.g. 4.22 , not the full version 4.22.2 ) — the patch version range is controlled by ocp_min_version and ocp_max_version . ocp_min_version ¤ The minimum version of the Red Hat release to mirror platform content for — a full OpenShift version (e.g. 4.19.10 , 4.19.15 ). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_MIN_VERSION Default: None (mirrors all versions) Only platform images for this version and newer are mirrored, reducing mirror size but limiting available versions. Only applies when mirror_redhat_platform is true , and only affects platform image mirroring, not operators. ocp_max_version ¤ The maximum version of the Red Hat release to mirror platform content for — a full OpenShift version (e.g. 4.19.20 , 4.19.25 ). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_MAX_VERSION Default: None (mirrors all versions) Only platform images for this version and older are mirrored, reducing mirror size but limiting available versions. Only applies when mirror_redhat_platform is true , and only affects platform image mirroring, not operators. Target Registry ¤ registry_public_host ¤ Target registry hostname for mirrored images — a valid hostname or IP address (e.g. registry.example.com , 10.0.0.100 ), used for the direct and from-filesystem modes. Required Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PUBLIC_HOST Default: None The registry must be accessible and have sufficient storage space for the Red Hat content (can be hundreds of GB). registry_public_port ¤ Target registry port for mirrored images — a valid port number, commonly 443 (HTTPS), 5000 (HTTP), or 32500 (NodePort). Required Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PUBLIC_PORT Default: None Ensure the port is accessible from the mirroring system. registry_is_ecr ¤ Whether the target registry is AWS Elastic Container Registry (ECR), enabling ECR-specific authentication and configuration. Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_IS_ECR Default: false When true , AWS credentials must be configured and registry_ecr_aws_region set; standard registry authentication ( registry_username / registry_password ) is used otherwise. registry_ecr_aws_region ¤ AWS region where the ECR registry is located — a valid AWS region (e.g. us-east-1 , eu-west-1 , ap-southeast-1 ), required for ECR authentication and access. Optional (Required when registry_is_ecr=true ) Environment Variable: REGISTRY_ECR_AWS_REGION Default: None AWS credentials must have permissions to push images to ECR in the specified region. registry_prefix_redhat ¤ Optional path prefix in the target registry for Red Hat images — a valid registry path (e.g. ocp419 , redhat , openshift ) used to organize Red Hat images separately from IBM or other content. Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PREFIX_REDHAT Default: '' When set, images are mirrored to {host}[:{port}]/{prefix}/{reponame} ; when unset, they are mirrored to the registry root ( {host}[:{port}]/{reponame} ). registry_username ¤ Username for authenticating to the target registry, which is used to push images during mirroring — must have push permissions to the target registry. Required (unless mirroring to AWS ECR with AWS credentials) Environment Variable: REGISTRY_USERNAME Default: None Without valid credentials the image push will fail. Keep credentials secure — use environment variables or secure vaults rather than hardcoding them in playbooks. registry_password ¤ Password for authenticating to the target registry, paired with registry_username . Required (unless mirroring to AWS ECR with AWS credentials) Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PASSWORD Default: None Warning Keep passwords secure. Never commit them to version control — use environment variables or secure vaults, and rotate them regularly. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: registry_public_host: myregistry.mycompany.com registry_public_port: 5000 registry_prefix_redhat: "ocp416" registry_username: user1 registry_password: 8934jk77s862! # Not a real password, don't worry security folks mirror_mode: direct mirror_working_dir: /tmp/mirror mirror_redhat_platform: false mirror_redhat_operators: true ocp_release: 4.22 redhat_pullsecret: ~/pull-secret.json roles: - ibm.mas_devops.mirror_ocp License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: mongodb ¤ This role currently supports provisioning of mongodb in four different providers: - community - aws (documentdb) - ibm - atlas (MongoDB Atlas) Important Notice Support for the atlas (MongoDB Atlas) provider is currently in Proof of Concept (PoC) stage. It is intended for testing and development purposes only and is not recommended for production deployments at this time. If the selected provider is community then the MongoDB Community Kubernetes Operator will be configured and deployed into the specified namespace. By default a three member MongoDB replica set will be created. The cluster will bind six PVCs, these provide persistence for the data and system logs across the three nodes. Currently there is no support built-in for customizing the cluster beyond this configuration. Tip The role will generate a yaml file containing the definition of a Secret and MongoCfg resource that can be used to configure the deployed instance as the MAS system MongoDB. This file can be directly applied using oc apply -f $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/mongocfg-mongoce-system.yaml or used in conjunction with the suite_config role. Prerequisites ¤ General Prerequisites ¤ To run this role with providers as ibm or aws you must have already installed the AWS CLI . Also, you need to have AWS user credentials configured via aws configure command or simply export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables with your corresponding AWS username credentials prior running this role when provider is either ibm or aws or atlas . To run the docdb_secret_rotate MONGODB_ACTION when the provider is aws you must have already installed the Mongo Shell . This role will install a GrafanaDashboard used for monitoring the MongoDB instance when the provider is community and you have run the grafana role previously. If you did not run the grafana role then the GrafanaDashboard won't be installed. MongoDB Atlas Prerequisites ¤ When using mongodb_provider=atlas , you must complete the following prerequisites: 1. Create AWS Secrets Manager Secret (Required) ¤ Create a secret in AWS Secrets Manager to store your Atlas API credentials. The secret must follow this naming convention: Secret Name : <atlas_account_id>/mongodb-atlas Where <atlas_account_id> is your AWS account ID (e.g., 123456789012/mongodb-atlas ). Secret Format : The secret must contain a JSON object with these exact field names: { "mongodb_atlas_api_pub_key": "your-atlas-public-key", "mongodb_atlas_api_pri_key": "your-atlas-private-key" } How to create the secret : # Replace 123456789012 with your AWS account ID export ACCOUNT_ID="123456789012" export SECRET_NAME="${ACCOUNT_ID}/mongodb-atlas" # Create the secret with Atlas API credentials aws secretsmanager create-secret \ --name "${SECRET_NAME}" \ --description "MongoDB Atlas API credentials for account ${ACCOUNT_ID}" \ --secret-string '{"mongodb_atlas_api_pub_key":"YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY","mongodb_atlas_api_pri_key":"YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"}' \ --region us-east-1 # Or update an existing secret aws secretsmanager put-secret-value \ --secret-id "${SECRET_NAME}" \ --secret-string '{"mongodb_atlas_api_pub_key":"YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY","mongodb_atlas_api_pri_key":"YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"}' \ --region us-east-1 Note : The field names must be exactly mongodb_atlas_api_pub_key and mongodb_atlas_api_pri_key as shown above. 2. Add IP Address to Atlas API Access List ¤ Add your IP address to the Atlas API Access List before running this role: Log in to MongoDB Atlas Console Navigate to your Organization → Access Manager → API Keys Select your API key Click "Edit" and add your current IP address to the Access List Note : The role cannot automatically add IP addresses to the Atlas API Access List. If your IP is not whitelisted, API calls will fail with 403 IP_ADDRESS_NOT_ON_ACCESS_LIST error. Variables marked Conditional are only required for a specific provider or action — the exact condition is noted in each entry below. Most variables only apply to the provider selected in mongodb_provider . Instance Configuration Variables ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ Unique identifier for the MAS instance that will use this MongoDB deployment — a lowercase alphanumeric string of 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , inst1 ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None When set together with mas_config_dir , the role generates a MongoCfg YAML file (containing a Secret and MongoCfg resource) at $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/mongocfg-mongoce-system.yaml , which can be applied with oc apply -f or used with the suite_config role to connect MAS to this MongoDB instance. Without it, no MAS configuration file is created. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory path where the generated MongoCfg resource file will be saved — any valid filesystem path (e.g. ~/masconfig , ./config ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None Must be set together with mas_instance_id for MongoCfg generation. Use the same directory across multiple dependency roles (mongodb, db2, sls) to collect all MAS configuration files in one place; the suite_config role applies them from there. mongodb_provider ¤ Selects which MongoDB deployment option to use: community (MongoDB Community Edition Operator, self-managed on OpenShift), ibm (IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB managed service), aws (AWS DocumentDB, MongoDB-compatible managed service), or atlas (MongoDB Atlas). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_PROVIDER Default: community Each provider has different requirements: community needs cluster storage ( mongodb_storage_class and related storage/resource variables); ibm needs ibmcloud_apikey ; aws needs aws_access_key_id , aws_secret_access_key , vpc_id and the docdb_* variables; atlas needs aws_access_key_id , aws_secret_access_key and atlas_account_id . The provider also determines which mongodb_action values are supported. Warning The provider cannot be changed after initial deployment. Migration between providers requires backup and restore procedures. mongodb_action ¤ Specifies which operation to perform on the MongoDB instance; valid values are provider-specific (see below). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_ACTION Default: install Valid values by provider: community : install , uninstall , backup , backup-database , restore , restore-database aws : install , uninstall , docdb_secret_rotate , destroy-data ibm : install , uninstall , backup , restore , create-mongo-service-credentials atlas : install , uninstall , restore , restore-database Use install for initial deployment or updates, uninstall to remove the instance, backup / restore for backup operations (see Backup and Restore Operations ), docdb_secret_rotate to rotate DocumentDB credentials (aws only), and create-mongo-service-credentials to generate service credentials (ibm only). Warning Destructive actions like uninstall and destroy-data permanently delete data and cannot be undone. Always back up data before performing destructive operations. CE Operator Variables ¤ mongodb_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the MongoDB Community Operator and MongoDB cluster will be deployed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_NAMESPACE Default: mongoce All MongoDB resources (operator, replica set pods, PVCs, secrets, services) are created in this namespace, and the namespace is referenced in MongoCfg generation for service endpoints. Change it only for multiple MongoDB instances or namespace naming requirements; changing it after deployment requires reinstallation. mongodb_version ¤ MongoDB version to deploy — for example 7.0.12 , 7.0.22 , 7.0.23 , 8.0.13 , 8.0.17 , 8.0.20 , or 8.0.23 (check the MAS compatibility matrix for supported versions). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_VERSION Default: Automatically defined by the mongo version specified in the latest MAS case bundle available Leave as default for standard deployments; the default aligns with the tested and supported version for your MAS release. Upgrades between major versions require the corresponding mongodb_v5_upgrade , mongodb_v6_upgrade , mongodb_v7_upgrade , or mongodb_v8_upgrade confirmation flag. Warning Never downgrade MongoDB versions, and always create scheduled backups before version changes. MongoDB 5.0+ requires the AVX instruction set — see Troubleshooting if replica set pods will not start after an upgrade. mongodb_override_spec ¤ Forces the role to use environment variables instead of preserving existing MongoDB spec settings ( true or false ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_OVERRIDE_SPEC Default: false When false , existing CPU, memory, storage, and replica settings ( mongodb_cpu_limits , mongodb_mem_limits , mongodb_cpu_requests , mongodb_mem_requests , mongodb_storage_class , mongodb_storage_capacity_data , mongodb_storage_capacity_logs , mongodb_replicas ) are preserved during reinstall/upgrade. When true , all settings are taken from environment variables and unset variables revert to defaults. Warning Check the existing MongoDB installation before enabling this. If environment variables don't match the current spec, resources may be reset to defaults, potentially causing disruption. Unknown settings are not preserved. mongodb_storage_class ¤ Kubernetes storage class for MongoDB persistent volumes — any storage class in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Required when mongodb_provider=community Environment Variable: MONGODB_STORAGE_CLASS Default: None Six PVCs are created by default (data + logs for each of 3 replicas), so the storage class determines MongoDB performance, reliability, and cost. It cannot be changed after deployment without data migration. Tip Verify available storage classes with oc get storageclass before deployment. mongodb_storage_capacity_data ¤ Size of the persistent volume claim (PVC) for MongoDB data storage on each replica set member — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g. 20Gi , 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_STORAGE_CAPACITY_DATA Default: 20Gi Total data storage = this value × number of replicas. PVCs can be expanded (if the storage class supports volume expansion) but not shrunk, so plan for growth when setting the initial size; larger volumes also take longer to back up. Monitor usage to avoid running out of space. mongodb_storage_capacity_logs ¤ Size of the persistent volume claim (PVC) for MongoDB log storage on each replica set member — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g. 10Gi , 20Gi , 50Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_STORAGE_CAPACITY_LOGS Default: 20Gi Total log storage = this value × number of replicas. Insufficient log space can cause MongoDB operational issues; PVCs can be expanded but not shrunk, so monitor log usage and size for production logging volumes. mongodb_cpu_limits ¤ Maximum CPU cores allocated to each MongoDB container — CPU units as decimal (e.g. 0.5 , 1 , 2 , 4 ) or millicores (e.g. 500m , 1000m , 2000m ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_CPU_LIMITS Default: 1 Set higher than mongodb_cpu_requests to allow burst capacity; the default (1 core) suits development or light workloads, production workloads with high query volumes need more. Total CPU limit = this value × number of replicas. mongodb_mem_limits ¤ Maximum memory allocated to each MongoDB container (e.g. 1Gi , 2Gi , 4Gi , 8Gi , 16Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_MEM_LIMITS Default: 1Gi MongoDB uses memory for caching data and indexes, so performance depends heavily on it: the default (1Gi) is only suitable for development/testing, production deployments typically need 4Gi-8Gi per replica. Set higher than mongodb_mem_requests for burst capacity; total memory limit = this value × number of replicas. mongodb_cpu_requests ¤ Guaranteed CPU cores reserved for each MongoDB container — CPU units as decimal (e.g. 0.5 , 1 , 2 ) or millicores (e.g. 500m , 1000m , 2000m ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_CPU_REQUESTS Default: 500m The Kubernetes scheduler uses this to place pods on nodes with sufficient CPU. Set based on expected baseline usage (not peak) and lower than mongodb_cpu_limits — the difference provides burst capacity. Also affects the pod Quality of Service (QoS) class; total CPU request = this value × number of replicas. mongodb_mem_requests ¤ Guaranteed memory reserved for each MongoDB container (e.g. 1Gi , 2Gi , 4Gi , 8Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_MEM_REQUESTS Default: 1Gi The Kubernetes scheduler uses this to place pods on nodes with sufficient memory. Set based on expected baseline usage (not peak) and lower than mongodb_mem_limits ; production deployments typically need 2Gi-4Gi requests. Also affects the pod Quality of Service (QoS) class; total memory request = this value × number of replicas. mongodb_replicas ¤ Number of MongoDB replica set members to deploy — positive integers, typically 1, 3, or 5 (odd numbers are recommended for proper election quorum). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_REPLICAS Default: 3 Use 3 (default) or more for production high availability, 5+ for critical workloads, and 1 only for Single Node OpenShift (SNO) clusters or development environments. Each replica requires its own data and log PVCs, and total resources = (CPU + memory + storage) × replicas. Changing the replica count after deployment requires careful planning. custom_labels ¤ Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to MongoDB resources (e.g. env=prod,team=platform,app=mongodb ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels add organizational metadata for resource tracking, cost allocation, filtering with oc get commands, and custom automation. They do not affect MongoDB functionality. mongodb_v5_upgrade ¤ Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 4.x to version 5. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V5_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to a 5.x version, triggers the upgrade from 4.2/4.4 to 5.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Warning Always back up before upgrading and test in non-production environments first. Review the MongoDB 5.0 release notes for breaking changes and new requirements (e.g. the AVX instruction set). mongodb_v6_upgrade ¤ Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 5 to version 6. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V6_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to a 6.x version, triggers the upgrade from 5.x to 6.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Always back up before upgrading and review the MongoDB 6.0 release notes for breaking changes. mongodb_v7_upgrade ¤ Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 6 to version 7. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V7_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to a 7.x version, triggers the upgrade from 6.x to 7.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Always back up before upgrading and review the MongoDB 7.0 release notes for breaking changes. mongodb_v8_upgrade ¤ Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 7 to version 8. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V8_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to an 8.x version, triggers the upgrade from 7.x to 8.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Always back up before upgrading and review the MongoDB 8.0 release notes for breaking changes. Backup and Restore (CE Operator) ¤ For backup and restore operations, set mongodb_action to one of the following: backup : Creates a complete backup including database data and Kubernetes resources (secrets, certificates, CRs) backup-database : Creates a backup of database data only restore : Performs a full restore by recreating the MongoDB instance from backup resources and then restoring database data restore-database : Restores only the database data to an already running MongoDB instance without touching instance resources See Backup and Restore Operations for the full process description, requirements, and troubleshooting. mas_backup_dir ¤ Local directory path where backup files will be stored or read from (e.g. /tmp/masbr ). Required when performing backup or restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None mongodb_backup_version ¤ The backup version timestamp to restore from, automatically generated during backup in the format YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS (e.g. 20251212-021316 ). Required when performing restore operations Environment Variable: MONGODB_BACKUP_VERSION Default: None mongodb_instance_name ¤ The name of the MongoDB instance to back up or restore. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_INSTANCE_NAME Default: mas-mongo-ce override_storageclass ¤ Controls whether to override the storage class for the MongoDB instance during restore — set to true to override the storage class with the MONGODB_STORAGE_CLASS value or the cluster's default storage class. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_STORAGECLASS Default: false mas_app_id ¤ Specific MAS application ID for targeted backup/restore operations — when set, only that application's MongoDB databases are backed up; otherwise all MongoDB databases are backed up. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None IBM Cloud ¤ ibm_mongo_name ¤ Name for the IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB instance — a valid IBM Cloud resource name (alphanumeric and hyphens, must start with a letter). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_NAME Default: mongo-<mas_instance_id> The name identifies the instance in the IBM Cloud console, billing reports, and resource lists, and is used as the prefix for the credential secret names. It cannot be changed after creation without recreating the instance; the default derives from mas_instance_id . ibm_mongo_admin_password ¤ Administrator password for the IBM Cloud MongoDB instance — a string meeting IBM Cloud password requirements (minimum length, complexity). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD Default: Auto-generated 20-character string If not provided, a secure random password is generated and stored in the Kubernetes secret named by ibm_mongo_admin_credentials_secret_name . Auto-generated passwords are recommended; set explicitly only if you need to know the password in advance or integrate with external password management. ibm_mongo_admin_credentials_secret_name ¤ Name of the Kubernetes secret containing MongoDB admin credentials. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from ibm_mongo_name ) Default: <ibm_mongo_name>-admin-credentials The secret (admin username and password) is created automatically by the role; other roles and applications reference it for database connectivity. ibm_mongo_service_credentials_secret_name ¤ Name of the Kubernetes secret containing MongoDB service credentials. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from ibm_mongo_name ) Default: <ibm_mongo_name>-service-credentials The secret contains connection strings and credentials for application-level MongoDB access; MAS applications use it to connect to the database. ibm_mongo_resourcegroup ¤ IBM Cloud resource group for MongoDB instance placement — the name of an existing resource group in your account. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Value of ibmcloud_resourcegroup ( Default ) Determines access control and billing allocation. Users need appropriate IAM permissions to create resources in the specified resource group — ensure the group exists and your API key has access to it. ibm_mongo_region ¤ IBM Cloud region where the MongoDB instance will be deployed — for example us-east , us-south , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok , or au-syd . Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_REGION Default: Value of ibmcloud_region ( us-east ) Choose the region closest to your OpenShift cluster for lowest latency, and consider data residency requirements. The region cannot be changed after creation. ibmcloud_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API key for authentication and resource management — the key must have permissions to create and manage Databases for MongoDB instances in the target resource group and region. Required when mongodb_provider=ibm Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Insufficient permissions cause deployment failures. Store the key securely (e.g. Ansible Vault or an external secret manager) — never commit API keys to source control. ibm_mongo_plan ¤ IBM Cloud service plan for the MongoDB instance — standard or enterprise (check IBM Cloud documentation for current plan options). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_PLAN Default: standard The plan affects pricing, performance characteristics, SLA, and available features, and cannot be changed after creation without recreating the instance. ibm_mongo_service ¤ IBM Cloud service type identifier for MongoDB — a fixed value used internally by the role. Required (read-only constant) Environment Variable: None (internal constant) Default: databases-for-mongodb This is set automatically by the role and used in IBM Cloud API calls to specify the service type; it does not need to be set by users. ibm_mongo_service_endpoints ¤ Network endpoint type for MongoDB connectivity — public (accessible over the internet) or private (accessible only via the IBM Cloud private network). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_SERVICE_ENDPOINTS Default: public private is recommended for production deployments: it is more secure and has lower latency, but requires the OpenShift cluster to reach the IBM Cloud private network. Use public when the cluster lacks private network connectivity (with appropriate firewall rules). ibm_mongo_version ¤ MongoDB version to deploy in IBM Cloud — versions supported by IBM Cloud Databases (e.g. 4.2 , 4.4 , 5.0 , 6.0 ). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_VERSION Default: 4.4 The default ( 4.4 ) suits older MAS versions; check the MAS compatibility matrix before selecting a newer version. Versions cannot easily be downgraded, and newer MongoDB versions may require MAS updates. ibm_mongo_memory ¤ Memory allocation per MongoDB member in MB — integer, minimum varies by plan (typically 1024 MB). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_MEMORY Default: 3840 (3.75 GB) Memory affects caching performance and query execution; IBM Cloud charges based on the allocation. The default suits development or small deployments — production workloads typically need 8192 MB or more per member. ibm_mongo_disk ¤ Disk storage allocation per MongoDB member in MB — integer, minimum varies by plan (typically 5120 MB). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_DISK Default: 30720 (30 GB) Storage holds databases, indexes, and operational logs. Disk can be expanded online but not reduced, so plan for data growth and monitor storage usage; total storage = this value × number of members. ibm_mongo_cpu ¤ Dedicated CPU cores per MongoDB member — 0 (shared CPU) or an integer ≥ 3 for dedicated cores. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_CPU Default: 0 (shared CPU) 0 gives lower cost with variable performance (suitable for development and light workloads); dedicated CPUs (≥3) significantly increase cost but provide the consistent performance production workloads typically need. Available CPU ranges vary by plan. ibm_mongo_backup_id ¤ IBM Cloud backup CRN (Cloud Resource Name) to restore from — format crn:v1:... , obtained from the IBM Cloud console or CLI. Required when is_restore=true Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_BACKUP_ID Default: None Leave unset for new deployments. Restoring replaces all current data with the state captured in the specified backup — verify the backup CRN before restoring and test restore procedures in non-production first. is_restore ¤ Flag to enable restore from an IBM Cloud backup instead of creating a new MongoDB instance ( true or false ). Optional Environment Variable: IS_RESTORE Default: false When true , requires ibm_mongo_backup_id and restored_mongodb_service_name . Always verify backup details before setting to true — restore operations cannot be undone without another backup. restored_mongodb_service_name ¤ Name for the MongoDB service created when restoring from backup — a valid IBM Cloud resource name, which can be the same as or different from the original. Required when is_restore=true Environment Variable: RESTORED_MONGO_SERVICE_NAME Default: None Using a different name than ibm_mongo_name allows restoring alongside the existing instance for side-by-side comparison before switching over. AWS DocumentDB ¤ aws_access_key_id ¤ AWS account access key ID for authentication — the key must have IAM permissions for DocumentDB, EC2 (VPC/subnets/security groups), and related services. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None Used together with aws_secret_access_key to authenticate all AWS API calls; insufficient permissions cause deployment failures. Warning Never commit AWS credentials to source control. Store them securely (e.g. Ansible Vault or an external secret manager). aws_secret_access_key ¤ AWS account secret access key — must correspond to the provided aws_access_key_id . Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Invalid or mismatched credentials cause authentication failures. Rotate credentials regularly following AWS security best practices. aws_region ¤ AWS region where the DocumentDB cluster will be deployed — a valid AWS region code (e.g. us-east-1 , us-east-2 , us-west-2 , eu-west-1 , ap-southeast-1 ). Optional Environment Variable: AWS_REGION Default: us-east-2 Choose the region closest to your OpenShift cluster for lowest latency, and consider data residency requirements. The VPC must exist in this region and the region cannot be changed after creation. vpc_id ¤ AWS VPC ID where DocumentDB resources will be created (format vpc-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ). Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: VPC_ID Default: None The DocumentDB cluster, subnets, and security groups are created in this VPC — use the same VPC as your OpenShift cluster for direct connectivity. The VPC must exist in aws_region and have sufficient available IP addresses and appropriate routing; DocumentDB is only accessible from resources within this VPC or connected networks. The docdb_cidr_az1 / docdb_cidr_az2 / docdb_cidr_az3 subnets are created within it, and the ingress/egress CIDRs should match its ranges. docdb_cluster_name ¤ Name for the AWS DocumentDB cluster — a valid cluster identifier (lowercase, alphanumeric, hyphens, must start with a letter), unique within your AWS account and region. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CLUSTER_NAME Default: None The name appears in the AWS console, CloudWatch metrics, and billing, and is used as the prefix for related resources: the subnet group ( docdb_subnet_group_name ), security group ( docdb_security_group_name ), and admin credentials secret ( docdb_admin_credentials_secret_name ). Choose a meaningful name as it cannot easily be changed. docdb_subnet_group_name ¤ Name for the DocumentDB subnet group, which associates the cluster with specific subnets across availability zones. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from docdb_cluster_name ) Default: docdb-<docdb_cluster_name> The subnet group is created automatically by the role and includes the subnets defined by docdb_cidr_az1 , docdb_cidr_az2 , and docdb_cidr_az3 . Default naming is recommended for consistency. docdb_security_group_name ¤ Name for the DocumentDB security group, which controls network access to the cluster. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from docdb_cluster_name ) Default: docdb-<docdb_cluster_name> The security group is created automatically by the role; its firewall rules are based on docdb_ingress_cidr and docdb_egress_cidr . Default naming is recommended for consistency. docdb_admin_credentials_secret_name ¤ Name of the Kubernetes secret containing DocumentDB admin credentials. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from docdb_cluster_name ) Default: <docdb_cluster_name>-admin-credentials The secret is created automatically by the role in the MAS core namespace and contains the admin username and password ( docdb_master_username ); MAS and other applications reference it for database connectivity. docdb_engine_version ¤ DocumentDB engine version to deploy. Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_ENGINE_VERSION Default: 5.0.0 Determines MongoDB compatibility and available features. MAS requires DocumentDB 5.0.0 — it is the only version MAS is certified with. Warning Do not change this value unless MAS documentation explicitly supports other versions. docdb_master_username ¤ Master username for DocumentDB cluster administration — a valid DocumentDB username (alphanumeric, must start with a letter, 1-63 characters). Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_MASTER_USERNAME Default: docdbadmin This user has full administrative privileges; the username is stored in the Kubernetes secret specified by docdb_admin_credentials_secret_name . Choose carefully — it cannot be changed after cluster creation. docdb_instance_class ¤ AWS instance class for DocumentDB instances — e.g. db.t3.medium , db.r5.large , db.r5.xlarge , db.r6g.large . Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_CLASS Default: db.t3.medium Determines compute and memory capacity per instance, affecting CPU, memory, network performance, and cost. Use db.t3.medium for development or small deployments, db.r5.large or larger for production (typical), and consider ARM-based db.r6g instances for better price/performance. Total cost = instance class cost × docdb_instance_number . docdb_instance_number ¤ Number of DocumentDB instances in the cluster — an integer from 1 to 16. Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_NUMBER Default: 3 Instances are distributed across the availability zones defined by the docdb_cidr_az* subnets for fault tolerance. Use 3 (default) or more for production high availability, 5+ for critical workloads, and 1 only for development/testing (a single instance has no failover capability). Total cost = instance class cost × this value. docdb_instance_identifier_prefix ¤ Prefix for DocumentDB instance identifiers — lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens; instance names are formed as {prefix}-1 , {prefix}-2 , etc. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_IDENTIFIER_PREFIX Default: None Instance identifiers appear in the AWS console and CloudWatch metrics; typically the prefix matches or relates to docdb_cluster_name . docdb_ingress_cidr ¤ IPv4 CIDR block allowed to connect to the DocumentDB cluster (e.g. 10.0.0.0/16 , 172.31.0.0/16 ), used in security group ingress rules. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_INGRESS_CIDR Default: None Typically set to the CIDR of your OpenShift cluster's VPC so applications in the VPC can reach DocumentDB; tighter subnet CIDRs improve security. Only traffic from this range can connect — too restrictive blocks legitimate traffic, too permissive reduces security. docdb_egress_cidr ¤ IPv4 CIDR block for outbound connections from the DocumentDB cluster (e.g. 10.0.0.0/16 , 172.31.0.0/16 ), used in security group egress rules. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_EGRESS_CIDR Default: None Usually set to the same value as docdb_ingress_cidr (the VPC CIDR for standard deployments). DocumentDB can only send traffic to this range, which affects its ability to respond to client connections. docdb_cidr_az1 ¤ IPv4 CIDR block for the DocumentDB subnet in availability zone 1 — valid IPv4 CIDR within the VPC range (e.g. 10.0.1.0/24 ) that does not overlap other subnets in the VPC. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CIDR_AZ1 Default: None If a subnet with the tag Name: <docdb_cluster_name> already exists it is reused; otherwise a new subnet is created. Each DocumentDB instance needs an IP address — use /24 or larger subnets for flexibility. docdb_cidr_az2 ¤ IPv4 CIDR block for the DocumentDB subnet in availability zone 2 — valid IPv4 CIDR within the VPC range (e.g. 10.0.2.0/24 ) that does not overlap other subnets in the VPC. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CIDR_AZ2 Default: None If a subnet with the tag Name: <docdb_cluster_name> already exists it is reused; otherwise a new subnet is created. Use different availability zones for AZ1, AZ2, and AZ3 to ensure high availability across zones. docdb_cidr_az3 ¤ IPv4 CIDR block for the DocumentDB subnet in availability zone 3 — valid IPv4 CIDR within the VPC range (e.g. 10.0.3.0/24 ) that does not overlap other subnets in the VPC. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CIDR_AZ3 Default: None If a subnet with the tag Name: <docdb_cluster_name> already exists it is reused; otherwise a new subnet is created. Three availability zones provide the best fault tolerance — ensure the subnets are in different AZs for proper distribution. AWS DocumentDB Secret Rotation Variables ¤ The following variables are used for rotating DocumentDB credentials. These are typically used with mongodb_action=docdb_secret_rotate . docdb_mongo_instance_name ¤ DocumentDB instance name for secret rotation — must match an existing DocumentDB instance identifier. Required when rotating secrets ( mongodb_action=docdb_secret_rotate ) Environment Variable: DOCDB_MONGO_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None Identifies the specific DocumentDB instance whose credentials will be rotated; it belongs to the cluster named by docdb_cluster_name and is reachable at docdb_host . Verify the instance name before rotation to avoid affecting the wrong instance. docdb_host ¤ DocumentDB instance host address for the connection during secret rotation — any instance hostname or endpoint from the cluster, obtained from the AWS console or the DocumentDB cluster endpoint. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_HOST Default: None Used with docdb_port to connect to DocumentDB for the rotation operation; any instance host from the cluster can be used. docdb_port ¤ DocumentDB instance port number — typically 27017 (the default DocumentDB port unless customized during cluster creation). Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_PORT Default: None (typically 27017 ) Used with docdb_host to establish the connection for credential rotation. docdb_instance_username ¤ DocumentDB username whose password is being rotated — an existing DocumentDB user, typically the application user or admin user. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_USERNAME Default: None This user's password is changed during rotation; applications using this username must be able to handle the new password (e.g. connection pooling with reconnection logic). The current password is provided via docdb_instance_password_old . docdb_instance_password_old ¤ Current password for the user being rotated. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_PASSWORD_OLD Default: None Used to authenticate before changing the password — an incorrect password causes the rotation to fail. After rotation this password is no longer valid; store it securely. docdb_master_password ¤ DocumentDB master user password for administrative operations during rotation — the master user has the privileges to change other users' passwords. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_MASTER_PASSWORD Default: None Must be the current master password, paired with docdb_master_username . Store master credentials securely and never commit them to source control. docdb_master_username ¤ DocumentDB master username used to authenticate the rotation — see docdb_master_username in AWS DocumentDB for the full entry. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_MASTER_USERNAME Default: None Must match the master username set during DocumentDB cluster creation (typically docdbadmin , the default of the variable above).
