Variables marked Conditional are only required for a specific provider or action — the exact condition is noted in each entry below. Most variables only apply to the provider selected in mongodb_provider .
docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Unique identifier for the MAS instance that will use this MongoDB deployment — a lowercase alphanumeric string of 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , inst1 ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None When set together with mas_config_dir , the role generates a MongoCfg YAML file (containing a Secret and MongoCfg resource) at $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/mongocfg-mongoce-system.yaml , which can be applied with oc apply -f or used with the suite_config role to connect MAS to this MongoDB instance. Without it, no MAS configuration file is created.
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: Local directory path where the generated MongoCfg resource file will be saved — any valid filesystem path (e.g. ~/masconfig , ./config ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None Must be set together with mas_instance_id for MongoCfg generation. Use the same directory across multiple dependency roles (mongodb, db2, sls) to collect all MAS configuration files in one place; the suite_config role applies them from there.
docs.title: mas_config_dir

docs.text: Selects which MongoDB deployment option to use: community (MongoDB Community Edition Operator, self-managed on OpenShift), ibm (IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB managed service), aws (AWS DocumentDB, MongoDB-compatible managed service), or atlas (MongoDB Atlas). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_PROVIDER Default: community Each provider has different requirements: community needs cluster storage ( mongodb_storage_class and related storage/resource variables); ibm needs ibmcloud_apikey ; aws needs aws_access_key_id , aws_secret_access_key , vpc_id and the docdb_* variables; atlas needs aws_access_key_id , aws_secret_access_key and atlas_account_id . The provider also determines which mongodb_action values are supported. Warning The provider cannot be changed after initial deployment. Migration between providers requires backup and restore procedures.
docs.title: mongodb_provider

docs.text: Specifies which operation to perform on the MongoDB instance; valid values are provider-specific (see below). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_ACTION Default: install Valid values by provider: community : install , uninstall , backup , backup-database , restore , restore-database aws : install , uninstall , docdb_secret_rotate , destroy-data ibm : install , uninstall , backup , restore , create-mongo-service-credentials atlas : install , uninstall , restore , restore-database Use install for initial deployment or updates, uninstall to remove the instance, backup / restore for backup operations (see Backup and Restore Operations ), docdb_secret_rotate to rotate DocumentDB credentials (aws only), and create-mongo-service-credentials to generate service credentials (ibm only). Warning Destructive actions like uninstall and destroy-data permanently delete data and cannot be undone. Always back up data before performing destructive operations.
docs.title: mongodb_action

docs.text: OpenShift namespace where the MongoDB Community Operator and MongoDB cluster will be deployed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_NAMESPACE Default: mongoce All MongoDB resources (operator, replica set pods, PVCs, secrets, services) are created in this namespace, and the namespace is referenced in MongoCfg generation for service endpoints. Change it only for multiple MongoDB instances or namespace naming requirements; changing it after deployment requires reinstallation.
docs.title: mongodb_namespace

docs.text: MongoDB version to deploy — for example 7.0.12 , 7.0.22 , 7.0.23 , 8.0.13 , 8.0.17 , 8.0.20 , or 8.0.23 (check the MAS compatibility matrix for supported versions). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_VERSION Default: Automatically defined by the mongo version specified in the latest MAS case bundle available Leave as default for standard deployments; the default aligns with the tested and supported version for your MAS release. Upgrades between major versions require the corresponding mongodb_v5_upgrade , mongodb_v6_upgrade , mongodb_v7_upgrade , or mongodb_v8_upgrade confirmation flag. Warning Never downgrade MongoDB versions, and always create scheduled backups before version changes. MongoDB 5.0+ requires the AVX instruction set — see Troubleshooting if replica set pods will not start after an upgrade.
docs.title: mongodb_version

docs.text: Forces the role to use environment variables instead of preserving existing MongoDB spec settings ( true or false ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_OVERRIDE_SPEC Default: false When false , existing CPU, memory, storage, and replica settings ( mongodb_cpu_limits , mongodb_mem_limits , mongodb_cpu_requests , mongodb_mem_requests , mongodb_storage_class , mongodb_storage_capacity_data , mongodb_storage_capacity_logs , mongodb_replicas ) are preserved during reinstall/upgrade. When true , all settings are taken from environment variables and unset variables revert to defaults. Warning Check the existing MongoDB installation before enabling this. If environment variables don't match the current spec, resources may be reset to defaults, potentially causing disruption. Unknown settings are not preserved.
docs.title: mongodb_override_spec

docs.text: Kubernetes storage class for MongoDB persistent volumes — any storage class in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Required when mongodb_provider=community Environment Variable: MONGODB_STORAGE_CLASS Default: None Six PVCs are created by default (data + logs for each of 3 replicas), so the storage class determines MongoDB performance, reliability, and cost. It cannot be changed after deployment without data migration. Tip Verify available storage classes with oc get storageclass before deployment.
docs.title: mongodb_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the persistent volume claim (PVC) for MongoDB data storage on each replica set member — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g. 20Gi , 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_STORAGE_CAPACITY_DATA Default: 20Gi Total data storage = this value × number of replicas. PVCs can be expanded (if the storage class supports volume expansion) but not shrunk, so plan for growth when setting the initial size; larger volumes also take longer to back up. Monitor usage to avoid running out of space.
docs.title: mongodb_storage_capacity_data

docs.text: Size of the persistent volume claim (PVC) for MongoDB log storage on each replica set member — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g. 10Gi , 20Gi , 50Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_STORAGE_CAPACITY_LOGS Default: 20Gi Total log storage = this value × number of replicas. Insufficient log space can cause MongoDB operational issues; PVCs can be expanded but not shrunk, so monitor log usage and size for production logging volumes.
docs.title: mongodb_storage_capacity_logs

docs.text: Maximum CPU cores allocated to each MongoDB container — CPU units as decimal (e.g. 0.5 , 1 , 2 , 4 ) or millicores (e.g. 500m , 1000m , 2000m ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_CPU_LIMITS Default: 1 Set higher than mongodb_cpu_requests to allow burst capacity; the default (1 core) suits development or light workloads, production workloads with high query volumes need more. Total CPU limit = this value × number of replicas.
docs.title: mongodb_cpu_limits

docs.text: Maximum memory allocated to each MongoDB container (e.g. 1Gi , 2Gi , 4Gi , 8Gi , 16Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_MEM_LIMITS Default: 1Gi MongoDB uses memory for caching data and indexes, so performance depends heavily on it: the default (1Gi) is only suitable for development/testing, production deployments typically need 4Gi-8Gi per replica. Set higher than mongodb_mem_requests for burst capacity; total memory limit = this value × number of replicas.
docs.title: mongodb_mem_limits

docs.text: Guaranteed CPU cores reserved for each MongoDB container — CPU units as decimal (e.g. 0.5 , 1 , 2 ) or millicores (e.g. 500m , 1000m , 2000m ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_CPU_REQUESTS Default: 500m The Kubernetes scheduler uses this to place pods on nodes with sufficient CPU. Set based on expected baseline usage (not peak) and lower than mongodb_cpu_limits — the difference provides burst capacity. Also affects the pod Quality of Service (QoS) class; total CPU request = this value × number of replicas.
docs.title: mongodb_cpu_requests

docs.text: Guaranteed memory reserved for each MongoDB container (e.g. 1Gi , 2Gi , 4Gi , 8Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_MEM_REQUESTS Default: 1Gi The Kubernetes scheduler uses this to place pods on nodes with sufficient memory. Set based on expected baseline usage (not peak) and lower than mongodb_mem_limits ; production deployments typically need 2Gi-4Gi requests. Also affects the pod Quality of Service (QoS) class; total memory request = this value × number of replicas.
docs.title: mongodb_mem_requests

docs.text: Number of MongoDB replica set members to deploy — positive integers, typically 1, 3, or 5 (odd numbers are recommended for proper election quorum). Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_REPLICAS Default: 3 Use 3 (default) or more for production high availability, 5+ for critical workloads, and 1 only for Single Node OpenShift (SNO) clusters or development environments. Each replica requires its own data and log PVCs, and total resources = (CPU + memory + storage) × replicas. Changing the replica count after deployment requires careful planning.
docs.title: mongodb_replicas

docs.text: Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to MongoDB resources (e.g. env=prod,team=platform,app=mongodb ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels add organizational metadata for resource tracking, cost allocation, filtering with oc get commands, and custom automation. They do not affect MongoDB functionality.
docs.title: custom_labels

docs.text: Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 4.x to version 5. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V5_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to a 5.x version, triggers the upgrade from 4.2/4.4 to 5.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Warning Always back up before upgrading and test in non-production environments first. Review the MongoDB 5.0 release notes for breaking changes and new requirements (e.g. the AVX instruction set).
docs.title: mongodb_v5_upgrade

docs.text: Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 5 to version 6. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V6_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to a 6.x version, triggers the upgrade from 5.x to 6.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Always back up before upgrading and review the MongoDB 6.0 release notes for breaking changes.
docs.title: mongodb_v6_upgrade

docs.text: Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 6 to version 7. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V7_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to a 7.x version, triggers the upgrade from 6.x to 7.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Always back up before upgrading and review the MongoDB 7.0 release notes for breaking changes.
docs.title: mongodb_v7_upgrade

docs.text: Confirmation flag ( true or false ) to upgrade MongoDB from version 7 to version 8. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_V8_UPGRADE Default: false When true and mongodb_version is set to an 8.x version, triggers the upgrade from 7.x to 8.x — a one-way operation that cannot be reversed without restoring from backup. Always back up before upgrading and review the MongoDB 8.0 release notes for breaking changes.
docs.title: mongodb_v8_upgrade

docs.text: For backup and restore operations, set mongodb_action to one of the following: backup : Creates a complete backup including database data and Kubernetes resources (secrets, certificates, CRs) backup-database : Creates a backup of database data only restore : Performs a full restore by recreating the MongoDB instance from backup resources and then restoring database data restore-database : Restores only the database data to an already running MongoDB instance without touching instance resources See Backup and Restore Operations for the full process description, requirements, and troubleshooting.
docs.title: Backup and Restore (CE Operator)

docs.text: Local directory path where backup files will be stored or read from (e.g. /tmp/masbr ). Required when performing backup or restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None
docs.title: mas_backup_dir

docs.text: The backup version timestamp to restore from, automatically generated during backup in the format YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS (e.g. 20251212-021316 ). Required when performing restore operations Environment Variable: MONGODB_BACKUP_VERSION Default: None
docs.title: mongodb_backup_version

docs.text: The name of the MongoDB instance to back up or restore. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_INSTANCE_NAME Default: mas-mongo-ce
docs.title: mongodb_instance_name

docs.text: Controls whether to override the storage class for the MongoDB instance during restore — set to true to override the storage class with the MONGODB_STORAGE_CLASS value or the cluster's default storage class. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_STORAGECLASS Default: false
docs.title: override_storageclass

docs.text: Specific MAS application ID for targeted backup/restore operations — when set, only that application's MongoDB databases are backed up; otherwise all MongoDB databases are backed up. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None
docs.title: mas_app_id

docs.text: Name for the IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB instance — a valid IBM Cloud resource name (alphanumeric and hyphens, must start with a letter). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_NAME Default: mongo-<mas_instance_id> The name identifies the instance in the IBM Cloud console, billing reports, and resource lists, and is used as the prefix for the credential secret names. It cannot be changed after creation without recreating the instance; the default derives from mas_instance_id .
docs.title: ibm_mongo_name

docs.text: Administrator password for the IBM Cloud MongoDB instance — a string meeting IBM Cloud password requirements (minimum length, complexity). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_ADMIN_PASSWORD Default: Auto-generated 20-character string If not provided, a secure random password is generated and stored in the Kubernetes secret named by ibm_mongo_admin_credentials_secret_name . Auto-generated passwords are recommended; set explicitly only if you need to know the password in advance or integrate with external password management.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_admin_password

docs.text: Name of the Kubernetes secret containing MongoDB admin credentials. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from ibm_mongo_name ) Default: <ibm_mongo_name>-admin-credentials The secret (admin username and password) is created automatically by the role; other roles and applications reference it for database connectivity.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_admin_credentials_secret_name

docs.text: Name of the Kubernetes secret containing MongoDB service credentials. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from ibm_mongo_name ) Default: <ibm_mongo_name>-service-credentials The secret contains connection strings and credentials for application-level MongoDB access; MAS applications use it to connect to the database.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_service_credentials_secret_name

docs.text: IBM Cloud resource group for MongoDB instance placement — the name of an existing resource group in your account. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Value of ibmcloud_resourcegroup ( Default ) Determines access control and billing allocation. Users need appropriate IAM permissions to create resources in the specified resource group — ensure the group exists and your API key has access to it.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_resourcegroup

docs.text: IBM Cloud region where the MongoDB instance will be deployed — for example us-east , us-south , eu-gb , eu-de , jp-tok , or au-syd . Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_REGION Default: Value of ibmcloud_region ( us-east ) Choose the region closest to your OpenShift cluster for lowest latency, and consider data residency requirements. The region cannot be changed after creation.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_region

docs.text: IBM Cloud API key for authentication and resource management — the key must have permissions to create and manage Databases for MongoDB instances in the target resource group and region. Required when mongodb_provider=ibm Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Insufficient permissions cause deployment failures. Store the key securely (e.g. Ansible Vault or an external secret manager) — never commit API keys to source control.
docs.title: ibmcloud_apikey

docs.text: IBM Cloud service plan for the MongoDB instance — standard or enterprise (check IBM Cloud documentation for current plan options). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_PLAN Default: standard The plan affects pricing, performance characteristics, SLA, and available features, and cannot be changed after creation without recreating the instance.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_plan

docs.text: IBM Cloud service type identifier for MongoDB — a fixed value used internally by the role. Required (read-only constant) Environment Variable: None (internal constant) Default: databases-for-mongodb This is set automatically by the role and used in IBM Cloud API calls to specify the service type; it does not need to be set by users.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_service

docs.text: Network endpoint type for MongoDB connectivity — public (accessible over the internet) or private (accessible only via the IBM Cloud private network). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_SERVICE_ENDPOINTS Default: public private is recommended for production deployments: it is more secure and has lower latency, but requires the OpenShift cluster to reach the IBM Cloud private network. Use public when the cluster lacks private network connectivity (with appropriate firewall rules).
docs.title: ibm_mongo_service_endpoints

docs.text: MongoDB version to deploy in IBM Cloud — versions supported by IBM Cloud Databases (e.g. 4.2 , 4.4 , 5.0 , 6.0 ). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_VERSION Default: 4.4 The default ( 4.4 ) suits older MAS versions; check the MAS compatibility matrix before selecting a newer version. Versions cannot easily be downgraded, and newer MongoDB versions may require MAS updates.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_version

docs.text: Memory allocation per MongoDB member in MB — integer, minimum varies by plan (typically 1024 MB). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_MEMORY Default: 3840 (3.75 GB) Memory affects caching performance and query execution; IBM Cloud charges based on the allocation. The default suits development or small deployments — production workloads typically need 8192 MB or more per member.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_memory

docs.text: Disk storage allocation per MongoDB member in MB — integer, minimum varies by plan (typically 5120 MB). Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_DISK Default: 30720 (30 GB) Storage holds databases, indexes, and operational logs. Disk can be expanded online but not reduced, so plan for data growth and monitor storage usage; total storage = this value × number of members.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_disk

docs.text: Dedicated CPU cores per MongoDB member — 0 (shared CPU) or an integer ≥ 3 for dedicated cores. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_CPU Default: 0 (shared CPU) 0 gives lower cost with variable performance (suitable for development and light workloads); dedicated CPUs (≥3) significantly increase cost but provide the consistent performance production workloads typically need. Available CPU ranges vary by plan.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_cpu

docs.text: IBM Cloud backup CRN (Cloud Resource Name) to restore from — format crn:v1:... , obtained from the IBM Cloud console or CLI. Required when is_restore=true Environment Variable: IBM_MONGO_BACKUP_ID Default: None Leave unset for new deployments. Restoring replaces all current data with the state captured in the specified backup — verify the backup CRN before restoring and test restore procedures in non-production first.
docs.title: ibm_mongo_backup_id

docs.text: Flag to enable restore from an IBM Cloud backup instead of creating a new MongoDB instance ( true or false ). Optional Environment Variable: IS_RESTORE Default: false When true , requires ibm_mongo_backup_id and restored_mongodb_service_name . Always verify backup details before setting to true — restore operations cannot be undone without another backup.
docs.title: is_restore

docs.text: Name for the MongoDB service created when restoring from backup — a valid IBM Cloud resource name, which can be the same as or different from the original. Required when is_restore=true Environment Variable: RESTORED_MONGO_SERVICE_NAME Default: None Using a different name than ibm_mongo_name allows restoring alongside the existing instance for side-by-side comparison before switching over.
docs.title: restored_mongodb_service_name

docs.text: AWS account access key ID for authentication — the key must have IAM permissions for DocumentDB, EC2 (VPC/subnets/security groups), and related services. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None Used together with aws_secret_access_key to authenticate all AWS API calls; insufficient permissions cause deployment failures. Warning Never commit AWS credentials to source control. Store them securely (e.g. Ansible Vault or an external secret manager).
docs.title: aws_access_key_id

docs.text: AWS account secret access key — must correspond to the provided aws_access_key_id . Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Invalid or mismatched credentials cause authentication failures. Rotate credentials regularly following AWS security best practices.
docs.title: aws_secret_access_key

docs.text: AWS region where the DocumentDB cluster will be deployed — a valid AWS region code (e.g. us-east-1 , us-east-2 , us-west-2 , eu-west-1 , ap-southeast-1 ). Optional Environment Variable: AWS_REGION Default: us-east-2 Choose the region closest to your OpenShift cluster for lowest latency, and consider data residency requirements. The VPC must exist in this region and the region cannot be changed after creation.
docs.title: aws_region

docs.text: AWS VPC ID where DocumentDB resources will be created (format vpc-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ). Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: VPC_ID Default: None The DocumentDB cluster, subnets, and security groups are created in this VPC — use the same VPC as your OpenShift cluster for direct connectivity. The VPC must exist in aws_region and have sufficient available IP addresses and appropriate routing; DocumentDB is only accessible from resources within this VPC or connected networks. The docdb_cidr_az1 / docdb_cidr_az2 / docdb_cidr_az3 subnets are created within it, and the ingress/egress CIDRs should match its ranges.
docs.title: vpc_id

docs.text: Name for the AWS DocumentDB cluster — a valid cluster identifier (lowercase, alphanumeric, hyphens, must start with a letter), unique within your AWS account and region. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CLUSTER_NAME Default: None The name appears in the AWS console, CloudWatch metrics, and billing, and is used as the prefix for related resources: the subnet group ( docdb_subnet_group_name ), security group ( docdb_security_group_name ), and admin credentials secret ( docdb_admin_credentials_secret_name ). Choose a meaningful name as it cannot easily be changed.
docs.title: docdb_cluster_name

docs.text: Name for the DocumentDB subnet group, which associates the cluster with specific subnets across availability zones. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from docdb_cluster_name ) Default: docdb-<docdb_cluster_name> The subnet group is created automatically by the role and includes the subnets defined by docdb_cidr_az1 , docdb_cidr_az2 , and docdb_cidr_az3 . Default naming is recommended for consistency.
docs.title: docdb_subnet_group_name

docs.text: Name for the DocumentDB security group, which controls network access to the cluster. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from docdb_cluster_name ) Default: docdb-<docdb_cluster_name> The security group is created automatically by the role; its firewall rules are based on docdb_ingress_cidr and docdb_egress_cidr . Default naming is recommended for consistency.
docs.title: docdb_security_group_name

docs.text: Name of the Kubernetes secret containing DocumentDB admin credentials. Optional Environment Variable: None (derived from docdb_cluster_name ) Default: <docdb_cluster_name>-admin-credentials The secret is created automatically by the role in the MAS core namespace and contains the admin username and password ( docdb_master_username ); MAS and other applications reference it for database connectivity.
docs.title: docdb_admin_credentials_secret_name

docs.text: DocumentDB engine version to deploy. Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_ENGINE_VERSION Default: 5.0.0 Determines MongoDB compatibility and available features. MAS requires DocumentDB 5.0.0 — it is the only version MAS is certified with. Warning Do not change this value unless MAS documentation explicitly supports other versions.
docs.title: docdb_engine_version

docs.text: Master username for DocumentDB cluster administration — a valid DocumentDB username (alphanumeric, must start with a letter, 1-63 characters). Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_MASTER_USERNAME Default: docdbadmin This user has full administrative privileges; the username is stored in the Kubernetes secret specified by docdb_admin_credentials_secret_name . Choose carefully — it cannot be changed after cluster creation.
docs.title: docdb_master_username

docs.text: AWS instance class for DocumentDB instances — e.g. db.t3.medium , db.r5.large , db.r5.xlarge , db.r6g.large . Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_CLASS Default: db.t3.medium Determines compute and memory capacity per instance, affecting CPU, memory, network performance, and cost. Use db.t3.medium for development or small deployments, db.r5.large or larger for production (typical), and consider ARM-based db.r6g instances for better price/performance. Total cost = instance class cost × docdb_instance_number .
docs.title: docdb_instance_class

docs.text: Number of DocumentDB instances in the cluster — an integer from 1 to 16. Optional Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_NUMBER Default: 3 Instances are distributed across the availability zones defined by the docdb_cidr_az* subnets for fault tolerance. Use 3 (default) or more for production high availability, 5+ for critical workloads, and 1 only for development/testing (a single instance has no failover capability). Total cost = instance class cost × this value.
docs.title: docdb_instance_number

docs.text: Prefix for DocumentDB instance identifiers — lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens; instance names are formed as {prefix}-1 , {prefix}-2 , etc. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_IDENTIFIER_PREFIX Default: None Instance identifiers appear in the AWS console and CloudWatch metrics; typically the prefix matches or relates to docdb_cluster_name .
docs.title: docdb_instance_identifier_prefix

docs.text: IPv4 CIDR block allowed to connect to the DocumentDB cluster (e.g. 10.0.0.0/16 , 172.31.0.0/16 ), used in security group ingress rules. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_INGRESS_CIDR Default: None Typically set to the CIDR of your OpenShift cluster's VPC so applications in the VPC can reach DocumentDB; tighter subnet CIDRs improve security. Only traffic from this range can connect — too restrictive blocks legitimate traffic, too permissive reduces security.
docs.title: docdb_ingress_cidr

docs.text: IPv4 CIDR block for outbound connections from the DocumentDB cluster (e.g. 10.0.0.0/16 , 172.31.0.0/16 ), used in security group egress rules. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_EGRESS_CIDR Default: None Usually set to the same value as docdb_ingress_cidr (the VPC CIDR for standard deployments). DocumentDB can only send traffic to this range, which affects its ability to respond to client connections.
docs.title: docdb_egress_cidr

docs.text: IPv4 CIDR block for the DocumentDB subnet in availability zone 1 — valid IPv4 CIDR within the VPC range (e.g. 10.0.1.0/24 ) that does not overlap other subnets in the VPC. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CIDR_AZ1 Default: None If a subnet with the tag Name: <docdb_cluster_name> already exists it is reused; otherwise a new subnet is created. Each DocumentDB instance needs an IP address — use /24 or larger subnets for flexibility.
docs.title: docdb_cidr_az1

docs.text: IPv4 CIDR block for the DocumentDB subnet in availability zone 2 — valid IPv4 CIDR within the VPC range (e.g. 10.0.2.0/24 ) that does not overlap other subnets in the VPC. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CIDR_AZ2 Default: None If a subnet with the tag Name: <docdb_cluster_name> already exists it is reused; otherwise a new subnet is created. Use different availability zones for AZ1, AZ2, and AZ3 to ensure high availability across zones.
docs.title: docdb_cidr_az2

docs.text: IPv4 CIDR block for the DocumentDB subnet in availability zone 3 — valid IPv4 CIDR within the VPC range (e.g. 10.0.3.0/24 ) that does not overlap other subnets in the VPC. Required when mongodb_provider=aws Environment Variable: DOCDB_CIDR_AZ3 Default: None If a subnet with the tag Name: <docdb_cluster_name> already exists it is reused; otherwise a new subnet is created. Three availability zones provide the best fault tolerance — ensure the subnets are in different AZs for proper distribution.
docs.title: docdb_cidr_az3

docs.text: The following variables are used for rotating DocumentDB credentials. These are typically used with mongodb_action=docdb_secret_rotate .
docs.title: AWS DocumentDB Secret Rotation Variables

docs.text: DocumentDB instance name for secret rotation — must match an existing DocumentDB instance identifier. Required when rotating secrets ( mongodb_action=docdb_secret_rotate ) Environment Variable: DOCDB_MONGO_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None Identifies the specific DocumentDB instance whose credentials will be rotated; it belongs to the cluster named by docdb_cluster_name and is reachable at docdb_host . Verify the instance name before rotation to avoid affecting the wrong instance.
docs.title: docdb_mongo_instance_name

docs.text: DocumentDB instance host address for the connection during secret rotation — any instance hostname or endpoint from the cluster, obtained from the AWS console or the DocumentDB cluster endpoint. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_HOST Default: None Used with docdb_port to connect to DocumentDB for the rotation operation; any instance host from the cluster can be used.
docs.title: docdb_host

docs.text: DocumentDB instance port number — typically 27017 (the default DocumentDB port unless customized during cluster creation). Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_PORT Default: None (typically 27017 ) Used with docdb_host to establish the connection for credential rotation.
docs.title: docdb_port

docs.text: DocumentDB username whose password is being rotated — an existing DocumentDB user, typically the application user or admin user. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_INSTANCE_USERNAME Default: None This user's password is changed during rotation; applications using this username must be able to handle the new password (e.g. connection pooling with reconnection logic). The current password is provided via docdb_instance_password_old .
docs.title: docdb_instance_username

docs.text: Current password for the user being rotated. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_PASSWORD_OLD Default: None Used to authenticate before changing the password — an incorrect password causes the rotation to fail. After rotation this password is no longer valid; store it securely.
docs.title: docdb_instance_password_old

docs.text: DocumentDB master user password for administrative operations during rotation — the master user has the privileges to change other users' passwords. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_MASTER_PASSWORD Default: None Must be the current master password, paired with docdb_master_username . Store master credentials securely and never commit them to source control.
docs.title: docdb_master_password

docs.text: DocumentDB master username used to authenticate the rotation — see docdb_master_username in AWS DocumentDB for the full entry. Required when rotating secrets Environment Variable: DOCDB_MASTER_USERNAME Default: None Must match the master username set during DocumentDB cluster creation (typically docdbadmin , the default of the variable above).
docs.title: docdb_master_username

docs.text: The specified MAS instance ID — see mas_instance_id in Instance Configuration Variables for the full entry. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: MongoDB username used to connect to the instance. Required when mongodb_action=destroy-data Environment Variable: MONGO_USERNAME Default: None
docs.title: mongo_username

docs.text: MongoDB password used to connect to the instance. Required when mongodb_action=destroy-data Environment Variable: MONGO_PASSWORD Default: None
docs.title: mongo_password

docs.text: MongoDB connection configuration (configDb, authMechanism, retryWrites, hosts) — refer to the destroy-data example playbook for the structure. Required Environment Variable: CONFIG Default: None
docs.title: config

docs.text: MongoDB TLS certificates (list with alias and crt fields) — refer to the destroy-data example playbook for the structure. Required Environment Variable: CERTIFICATES Default: None
docs.title: certificates

docs.text: The MongoDB Atlas provider automates the complete lifecycle of Atlas cluster provisioning, including: Project Creation : Creates or verifies an Atlas project within your organization Backup Compliance Policy : Configures automated backup policies with compliance settings Cluster Provisioning : Creates a MongoDB cluster with specified configuration Database Users : Creates instance-specific database users with scoped permissions Secret Management : Stores connection information in AWS Secrets Manager Cluster-level secret : <account_id>/<cluster_name>/mongo (empty credentials for cluster metadata) Instance-level secrets : <account_id>/<cluster_name>/<instance_id>/mongo (with user credentials)
docs.title: MongoDB Atlas

docs.text: MongoDB Atlas organization ID where the project will be created — a 24-character hexadecimal string (e.g. 507f1f77bcf86cd799439011 ). Required when creating a new project (when atlas_project_id is not provided) Environment Variable: ATLAS_ORG_ID Default: None Determines which organization owns the project and its billing. Find it in the Atlas Console under Organization Settings → Organization ID.
docs.title: atlas_org_id

docs.text: Name for the Atlas project to create or find — alphanumeric string with spaces, hyphens, and underscores allowed. Required when atlas_project_id is not provided Environment Variable: ATLAS_PROJECT_NAME Default: None If a project with this name exists in the organization it will be reused; otherwise a new project is created. Use instead of atlas_project_id when you want the role to find or create a project by name; creating a new project also requires atlas_org_id .
docs.title: atlas_project_name

docs.text: MongoDB Atlas project ID where the cluster will be created — a 24-character hexadecimal string (e.g. 507f1f77bcf86cd799439011 ). Required when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_PROJECT_ID Default: None All Atlas resources are organized under projects; this determines billing, access control, and resource organization for the cluster. Obtain it from the Atlas console under Project Settings (not required for the restore-database action).
docs.title: atlas_project_id

docs.text: AWS account ID used to construct the AWS Secrets Manager secret name for Atlas API credentials — a 12-digit number (e.g. 123456789012 ). Required when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_ACCOUNT_ID Default: None The Atlas API credentials are only retrieved from the AWS Secrets Manager secret named <atlas_account_id>/mongodb-atlas (looked up in the region set by atlas_aws_region ); the role fails if the secret does not exist or cannot be accessed. The secret must be created before running this role — see Prerequisites for the creation instructions.
docs.title: atlas_account_id

docs.text: Name of the MongoDB Atlas cluster to create or manage — alphanumeric string, 1-64 characters, can include hyphens. Required when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Identifies the cluster within the project for all cluster operations; the name appears in the Atlas console and connection strings and cannot be changed after cluster creation.
docs.title: atlas_cluster_name

docs.text: Cloud provider where the Atlas cluster will be deployed. Required when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_CLUSTER_PROVIDER Default: AWS Currently only AWS is supported; it determines the available regions, instance sizes, and pricing. The cluster region is set with atlas_aws_region and must be valid for the selected provider. VPC peering is only supported when using AWS .
docs.title: atlas_cluster_provider

docs.text: Atlas cluster tier/instance size — M10 , M20 , M30 , M40 , M50 , M60 , M80 , M140 , M200 , M300 , M400 , or M700 . Required when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_CLUSTER_SIZE Default: None Determines cluster compute and memory resources, affecting performance, storage capacity, and hourly cost. M10 is the minimum for production; the M0/M2/M5 free/shared tiers are not supported. The tier cannot be decreased, only increased.
docs.title: atlas_cluster_size

docs.text: MongoDB version to deploy in the Atlas cluster — 6.0 , 7.0 , or 8.0 (check Atlas for currently supported versions). Optional Environment Variable: ATLAS_MONGODB_VERSION Default: 7.0 Determines the available MongoDB features and compatibility. Version upgrades are supported but downgrades are not.
docs.title: atlas_mongodb_version

docs.text: Enable automated backups for the Atlas cluster ( true or false ). Optional Environment Variable: ATLAS_BACKUP_ENABLED Default: false When enabled, Atlas creates continuous backups with point-in-time recovery (affects cluster cost). Enable for production clusters; disable only for temporary/test clusters. Must be true when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled is enabled.
docs.title: atlas_backup_enabled

docs.text: MongoDB Atlas Auditing captures database operations for compliance and security monitoring. It records authentication events, authorization failures, and database operations, which is required for FedRAMP, HIPAA, and other regulatory compliance.
docs.title: Atlas Audit Logging Configuration

docs.text: Enable audit logging for the Atlas project ( true or false ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_AUDIT_ENABLED Default: false Captures audit events based on the configured filter; logs are accessible via the Atlas UI or API and additional costs may apply based on log volume. Audit logging is configured at the project level and applies to all clusters in the project. Enable for environments requiring regulatory compliance (FedRAMP, HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI-DSS) or security monitoring.
docs.title: atlas_audit_enabled

docs.text: JSON filter defining which audit events to capture, following MongoDB query language syntax — for example {"atype": "authenticate"} (authentication only), {"result": {"$ne": 0}} (failed operations), {"param.ns": {"$regex": "^mydb\\."}} (specific database), {"param.db": "admin"} (admin database operations), or {} (all events). Optional when atlas_audit_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_AUDIT_FILTER Default: None — a default comprehensive filter is generated automatically When not provided, the generated filter excludes MAS instance users (from atlas_mas_instances ) while capturing authentication events, authorization failures, and critical database operations (DDL, DML, user/role management). More specific filters reduce log volume and performance impact; the filter choice maps to common compliance needs (SOC 2 authentication/authorization tracking, HIPAA PHI access monitoring, PCI-DSS cardholder data logging, FedRAMP comprehensive audit trail). Warning Invalid JSON will cause the configuration to fail.
docs.title: atlas_audit_filter

docs.text: Log successful authorization events in addition to failures ( true or false ). Optional when atlas_audit_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_AUDIT_AUTHORIZATION_SUCCESS Default: true Set to true for the comprehensive audit trails required by strict compliance frameworks (it significantly increases log volume); set to false to reduce log volume by only capturing authorization failures. Most compliance frameworks require logging of both successful and failed authorization attempts.
docs.title: atlas_audit_authorization_success

docs.text: MongoDB Atlas can export audit logs to AWS S3 for long-term retention and compliance using the Log Integrations API ( /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/logIntegrations ). This provides a cost-effective way to store audit logs beyond Atlas's retention period and enables integration with external log analysis tools. The export covers both MONGOD_AUDIT and MONGOS_AUDIT log types, automatically creates and configures all required AWS infrastructure, and is fully idempotent (safe to run multiple times). Prerequisites: atlas_audit_enabled must be set to true , AWS credentials must be configured (via AWS CLI or environment variables), and the credentials need sufficient IAM permissions to create S3 buckets and IAM roles.
docs.title: Atlas S3 Audit Log Export Configuration

docs.text: Enable export of audit logs to AWS S3 ( true or false ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_S3_AUDIT_EXPORT_ENABLED Default: false When enabled, the role creates an encrypted S3 bucket (name auto-generated from the Atlas project name as <project-name>-atlas-audit-logs , with special characters replaced by hyphens and converted to lowercase), sets up an IAM role for MongoDB Atlas with cross-account access, configures cloud provider access in Atlas, creates the log integration via the Atlas Log Integrations API, and applies lifecycle policies for cost optimization. Enable for long-term audit log retention (beyond Atlas's retention period) and compliance archival.
docs.title: atlas_s3_audit_export_enabled

docs.text: Prefix (folder path) within the S3 bucket — a valid S3 object key prefix (e.g. audit-logs/mongodb , compliance/atlas-audit , logs/production/mongodb ). Optional when atlas_s3_audit_export_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_S3_AUDIT_BUCKET_PREFIX Default: mongodb-atlas-audit-logs Organizes audit logs within the bucket; logs are stored at s3://<bucket_name>/<prefix>/<project_id>/... .
docs.title: atlas_s3_audit_bucket_prefix

docs.text: Number of days to retain audit logs in S3 — positive integer (365 days / 1 year by default). Optional when atlas_s3_audit_export_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_S3_AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS Default: 365 Creates an S3 lifecycle policy that deletes logs after the retention period; logs transition to Glacier storage after atlas_s3_audit_glacier_transition_days . This helps manage storage costs while meeting compliance requirements.
docs.title: atlas_s3_audit_log_retention_days

docs.text: Enable S3 bucket versioning for audit logs ( true or false ), protecting against accidental deletion or modification. Optional when atlas_s3_audit_export_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_S3_AUDIT_BUCKET_ENABLE_VERSIONING Default: false When true , all versions of objects are retained (increasing storage costs) and noncurrent versions are deleted after atlas_s3_audit_noncurrent_version_retention_days ; total retention = atlas_s3_audit_log_retention_days + noncurrent retention. Enable for strict compliance requirements that mandate immutable audit logs.
docs.title: atlas_s3_audit_bucket_enable_versioning

docs.text: Days before transitioning audit logs to Glacier storage — integer ≥ 30 (AWS requirement); common values are 30, 60, 90, and 180 days. Optional when atlas_s3_audit_export_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_S3_AUDIT_GLACIER_TRANSITION_DAYS Default: 90 Reduces storage costs: logs remain in Standard storage for faster access during this period, after which retrieval times increase but costs decrease significantly. Must be less than atlas_s3_audit_log_retention_days .
docs.title: atlas_s3_audit_glacier_transition_days

docs.text: Days to retain noncurrent versions of audit logs when versioning is enabled — positive integer. Optional when atlas_s3_audit_bucket_enable_versioning=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_S3_AUDIT_NONCURRENT_VERSION_RETENTION_DAYS Default: 30 Only applies when versioning is enabled; it extends total retention time — for example with 365 days retention and 30 days noncurrent retention, audit logs can be stored for up to 395 days total.
docs.title: atlas_s3_audit_noncurrent_version_retention_days

docs.text: MongoDB Atlas Alert Monitoring provides proactive notifications for cluster health, performance, and security events. Alerts are configured per cluster using matchers that target atlas_cluster_name , so each alert configuration only applies to the specified cluster. When atlas_enable_alerts=true , basic alerts (CPU, memory, and connection count — warning and critical thresholds) are automatically configured. Additional categories require explicit enablement: cluster health alerts ( atlas_enable_cluster_health_alerts ), performance alerts ( atlas_enable_performance_alerts ), and security alerts ( atlas_enable_security_alerts ).
docs.title: Atlas Alert Monitoring Configuration

docs.text: Enable basic alert monitoring for the Atlas cluster ( true or false ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_ENABLE_ALERTS Default: false Automatically configures 6 basic alerts (CPU, memory, connections — warning and critical) with email notifications, helping prevent downtime by alerting before critical issues occur. Enable for production and staging environments; requires atlas_alert_notification_emails to be configured with at least one email address.
docs.title: atlas_enable_alerts

docs.text: List of email addresses to receive alert notifications — comma-separated list (e.g. ocm-team@example.com,monitoring@example.com ) or JSON array (e.g. ["ocm-team@example.com", "monitoring@example.com"] ). Required when atlas_enable_alerts=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ALERT_NOTIFICATION_EMAILS Default: [] All specified addresses receive notifications for all configured alerts. Important Use OCM (Operations Center Manager) email addresses only. OCM emails are integrated with incident management systems and ensure proper alert routing and escalation — do not configure generic or personal email addresses. At least one OCM email address is required when alerts are enabled.
docs.title: atlas_alert_notification_emails

docs.text: Enable alerts for cluster health issues ( true or false ). Optional when atlas_enable_alerts=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ENABLE_CLUSTER_HEALTH_ALERTS Default: false Configures alerts for replication oplog window running out (< 1 hour), primary elected (replica set election), no primary available, and cluster mongos missing. Enable for production and staging environments to monitor cluster stability.
docs.title: atlas_enable_cluster_health_alerts

docs.text: Enable alerts for performance issues ( true or false ). Optional when atlas_enable_alerts=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_ALERTS Default: false Configures alerts for CPU usage, memory usage, disk usage, connection count (warning and critical thresholds, controlled by the atlas_alert_*_thresholds variables), and query performance (scanned objects per returned). Enable for production and staging environments to monitor resource utilization.
docs.title: atlas_enable_performance_alerts

docs.text: Enable alerts for security events ( true or false ). Optional when atlas_enable_alerts=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ENABLE_SECURITY_ALERTS Default: false Configures alerts for too many unhealthy connections and users without multi-factor authentication. Enable for all environments to monitor security posture.
docs.title: atlas_enable_security_alerts

docs.text: CPU utilization percentage thresholds for WARNING and CRITICAL alerts — JSON array of two integers between 0-100, as [warning, critical] . Optional when atlas_enable_performance_alerts=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ALERT_CPU_THRESHOLDS Default: [70, 80] The warning alert triggers at the first value and the critical alert at the second; lower values trigger alerts earlier, and the critical threshold should be higher than the warning for proper escalation. export ATLAS_ALERT_CPU_THRESHOLDS='[70, 80]'
docs.title: atlas_alert_cpu_thresholds

docs.text: Memory utilization percentage thresholds for WARNING and CRITICAL alerts — JSON array of two integers between 0-100, as [warning, critical] . Optional when atlas_enable_performance_alerts=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ALERT_MEMORY_THRESHOLDS Default: [70, 80] The warning alert triggers at the first value and the critical alert at the second; memory exhaustion can cause performance degradation and OOM errors. export ATLAS_ALERT_MEMORY_THRESHOLDS='[70, 80]'
docs.title: atlas_alert_memory_thresholds

docs.text: Connection count thresholds, as a percentage of maximum, for WARNING and CRITICAL alerts — JSON array of two integers between 0-100, as [warning, critical] . Optional when atlas_enable_performance_alerts=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ALERT_CONNECTION_THRESHOLDS Default: [70, 80] The warning alert triggers at the first value and the critical alert at the second; connection exhaustion can prevent new connections and cause application failures. export ATLAS_ALERT_CONNECTION_THRESHOLDS='[70, 80]'
docs.title: atlas_alert_connection_thresholds

docs.text: Interval in minutes for metric threshold alert evaluation — positive integer. Optional Environment Variable: ATLAS_ALERT_INTERVAL_MIN Default: 60 Defines how frequently Atlas evaluates metric thresholds for all performance alerts (CPU, memory, connections, query performance — all OUTSIDE_METRIC_THRESHOLD alert types). This is a required parameter for Atlas metric threshold alerts: lower values (e.g. 1-5 minutes) give faster detection but may increase alert noise; higher values (e.g. 10-15 minutes) reduce noise but delay detection. The default of 60 minutes balances responsiveness with stability.
docs.title: atlas_alert_interval_min

docs.text: The backup compliance policy enforces backup retention and protection rules at the project level. When enabled, it applies to all clusters in the project.
docs.title: Atlas Backup Compliance Policy Configuration

docs.text: Enable the backup compliance policy for the Atlas project ( true or false ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_BACKUP_COMPLIANCE_ENABLED Default: false Enforces backup retention policies, prevents unauthorized backup deletion, and enables compliance features. Requires atlas_backup_enabled set to true on the cluster, plus the atlas_compliance_* variables below for configuration. Enable for production environments requiring regulatory compliance or strict backup retention policies. Warning Once enabled, the compliance policy cannot be disabled without contacting Atlas support.
docs.title: atlas_backup_compliance_enabled

docs.text: Email address of the authorized user for compliance policy changes — a valid email address. Required when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_AUTHORIZED_EMAIL Default: admin@example.com Used for the audit trail and authorization of compliance policy changes.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_authorized_email

docs.text: First name of the authorized user for compliance policy changes. Required when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_AUTHORIZED_FIRST_NAME Default: Admin
docs.title: atlas_compliance_authorized_first_name

docs.text: Last name of the authorized user for compliance policy changes. Required when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_AUTHORIZED_LAST_NAME Default: User
docs.title: atlas_compliance_authorized_last_name

docs.text: Enable copy protection for backups ( true or false ). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_COPY_PROTECTION Default: false Prevents copying of backup snapshots to other regions or projects — when enabled, backups cannot be copied outside the configured region.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_copy_protection

docs.text: Enable encryption at rest for backups ( true or false ). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_ENCRYPTION_AT_REST Default: false Ensures all backup snapshots are encrypted at rest, adding an encryption layer to backup storage.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_encryption_at_rest

docs.text: Enable point-in-time restore for compliance backups ( true or false ). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_PIT_ENABLED Default: false Enables continuous backup with point-in-time recovery capability — allows restore to any point in time within the retention window and increases backup storage costs.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_pit_enabled

docs.text: Number of days for the restore window — integer (1-365). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_RESTORE_WINDOW_DAYS Default: 7 Defines how many days of continuous backup history are maintained for point-in-time restore; determines the maximum age of data that can be restored.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_restore_window_days

docs.text: Frequency interval for hourly backups, in hours — integer (1, 2, 4, 6, 8, or 12). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_HOURLY_FREQUENCY_INTERVAL Default: 6 How often hourly snapshots are taken; more frequent backups provide finer recovery granularity but increase storage costs.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_hourly_frequency_interval

docs.text: Retention unit for hourly backups — days , weeks , or months . Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_HOURLY_RETENTION_UNIT Default: days
docs.title: atlas_compliance_hourly_retention_unit

docs.text: Retention value for hourly backups — integer (1-365 for days, 1-52 for weeks, 1-36 for months). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_HOURLY_RETENTION_VALUE Default: 7 How long hourly backups are retained; longer retention increases storage costs.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_hourly_retention_value

docs.text: Frequency interval for daily backups, in days — integer (1-365). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_DAILY_FREQUENCY_INTERVAL Default: 1 How often daily snapshots are taken.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_daily_frequency_interval

docs.text: Retention unit for daily backups — days , weeks , or months . Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_DAILY_RETENTION_UNIT Default: days
docs.title: atlas_compliance_daily_retention_unit

docs.text: Retention value for daily backups — integer (1-365 for days, 1-52 for weeks, 1-36 for months). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_DAILY_RETENTION_VALUE Default: 7 How long daily backups are retained.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_daily_retention_value

docs.text: Frequency interval for weekly backups, in weeks — integer (1-52). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_WEEKLY_FREQUENCY_INTERVAL Default: 1 How often weekly snapshots are taken.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_weekly_frequency_interval

docs.text: Retention unit for weekly backups — weeks , months , or years . Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_WEEKLY_RETENTION_UNIT Default: weeks
docs.title: atlas_compliance_weekly_retention_unit

docs.text: Retention value for weekly backups — integer (1-52 for weeks, 1-36 for months, 1-10 for years). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_WEEKLY_RETENTION_VALUE Default: 4 How long weekly backups are retained.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_weekly_retention_value

docs.text: Frequency interval for monthly backups, in months — integer (1-12). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_MONTHLY_FREQUENCY_INTERVAL Default: 1 How often monthly snapshots are taken.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_monthly_frequency_interval

docs.text: Retention unit for monthly backups — months or years . Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_MONTHLY_RETENTION_UNIT Default: months
docs.title: atlas_compliance_monthly_retention_unit

docs.text: Retention value for monthly backups — integer (1-36 for months, 1-10 for years). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_MONTHLY_RETENTION_VALUE Default: 12 How long monthly backups are retained.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_monthly_retention_value

docs.text: Frequency interval for yearly backups, in years — integer (1-10). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_YEARLY_FREQUENCY_INTERVAL Default: 1 How often yearly snapshots are taken.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_yearly_frequency_interval

docs.text: Retention unit for yearly backups — years . Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_YEARLY_RETENTION_UNIT Default: years
docs.title: atlas_compliance_yearly_retention_unit

docs.text: Retention value for yearly backups — integer (1-10). Optional when atlas_backup_compliance_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_COMPLIANCE_YEARLY_RETENTION_VALUE Default: 1 How long yearly backups are retained; longer retention increases storage costs significantly.
docs.title: atlas_compliance_yearly_retention_value

docs.text: List of MAS instance names that will use this cluster — a list or comma-separated string (e.g. ["inst1", "inst2"] or "inst1,inst2" ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_MAS_INSTANCES Default: [] Each instance gets a dedicated database user with scoped permissions (username format <instance_name>-user ). Used with atlas_store_credentials_in_secret to create instance-level secrets.
docs.title: atlas_mas_instances

docs.text: Multi-user database configuration for the Atlas cluster — a dictionary of user configurations with username , auth_database_name , and roles . Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas (alternative to atlas_db_username / atlas_db_password ) Environment Variable: Not supported (use playbook vars) Default: None Defines multiple database users with different roles and permissions, with auto-generated passwords stored in Atlas — the recommended approach for production deployments requiring multiple users with different access levels. atlas_database_users: user1: username: "app_user" auth_database_name: "admin" roles: - database_name: "admin" role_name: "readWriteAnyDatabase"
docs.title: atlas_database_users

docs.text: Legacy single database user username — a valid MongoDB username string. Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas (alternative to atlas_database_users ) Environment Variable: ATLAS_DB_USERNAME Default: None Creates a single database user; must be used with atlas_db_password . For simple deployments only — consider atlas_database_users for production.
docs.title: atlas_db_username

docs.text: Legacy single database user password — a strong password string. Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas (alternative to atlas_database_users ) Environment Variable: ATLAS_DB_PASSWORD Default: None Sets the password for the single database user; must be used with atlas_db_username . Store securely and never commit to version control.
docs.title: atlas_db_password

docs.text: AWS account ID for the secret naming convention — see atlas_account_id in Atlas Project and Cluster Configuration for the full entry. Required when atlas_store_credentials_in_secret=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ACCOUNT_ID Default: None Used to construct the secret names <account_id>/<cluster_name>/mongo and <account_id>/<cluster_name>/<instance_id>/mongo in AWS Secrets Manager.
docs.title: atlas_account_id

docs.text: Store Atlas connection information in AWS Secrets Manager ( true or false ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_STORE_CREDENTIALS_IN_SECRET Default: false When enabled, the role creates/updates two types of secrets after provisioning: a cluster-level secret <account_id>/<cluster_name>/mongo containing cluster metadata (hosts, port, CA certificates) with empty username/password fields, and instance-level secrets <account_id>/<cluster_name>/<instance_id>/mongo containing instance-specific credentials plus the cluster metadata. Requires atlas_account_id , atlas_cluster_name , and atlas_aws_region , plus the AWS CLI configured with appropriate IAM permissions; works with atlas_mas_instances to create the instance-level secrets. Enable for production deployments to centralize credential management and let MAS retrieve connection information. { "info": "# YAML content with hosts, port, CA certificates", "username": "instance-user", "password": "generated-password" } The cluster-level secret has empty username and password fields (or docdb_username / docdb_password for compatibility), while instance-level secrets contain actual credentials.
docs.title: atlas_store_credentials_in_secret

docs.text: Enable AWS PrivateLink for secure, private connectivity between the Atlas cluster and your AWS VPC ( true or false ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas Environment Variable: ATLAS_PRIVATELINK_ENABLED Default: false When enabled, PrivateLink configuration requires atlas_vpc_id , atlas_aws_region , atlas_project_id , atlas_subnet_ids , and atlas_rosa_cidr_ranges . Private connectivity is only supported for AWS deployments.
docs.title: atlas_privatelink_enabled

docs.text: AWS VPC ID for the PrivateLink connection with the Atlas cluster (e.g. vpc-0123456789abcdef0 ). Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas and configuring PrivateLink Environment Variable: ATLAS_VPC_ID Default: None Enables private network connectivity between the AWS VPC and the Atlas cluster; used together with atlas_aws_region and atlas_subnet_ids .
docs.title: atlas_vpc_id

docs.text: AWS region for the PrivateLink configuration, the Atlas credentials secret lookup, and the S3 audit export bucket — for example US_EAST_1 or us-east-1 . Optional when mongodb_provider=atlas and configuring PrivateLink Environment Variable: ATLAS_AWS_REGION Default: None Must match the region of the AWS VPC. The role converts the region to Atlas format automatically (e.g. us-east-1 → US_EAST_1 ), so either AWS or Atlas format works.
docs.title: atlas_aws_region

docs.text: AWS subnet IDs for VPC Endpoint placement (private connectivity edge subnets) — provided as a list or comma-separated string (e.g. subnet-111,subnet-222,subnet-333 ). Optional when atlas_privatelink_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_SUBNET_IDS Default: [] Required when PrivateLink is enabled; the endpoints are placed in these subnets.
docs.title: atlas_subnet_ids

docs.text: ROSA cluster CIDR ranges for the PrivateLink security group ingress rules — provided as a list or comma-separated string (e.g. 10.0.0.0/16 ). Optional when atlas_privatelink_enabled=true Environment Variable: ATLAS_ROSA_CIDR_RANGES Default: [] Required when PrivateLink is enabled; allows the ROSA cluster to reach the private endpoint.
docs.title: atlas_rosa_cidr_ranges

docs.text: MongoDB Atlas provides a fully managed backup service with automated backups, point-in-time recovery, and easy restore capabilities through the Atlas console and API — for normal backup and restore operations, use the Atlas managed backup service (enabled by default with atlas_backup_enabled ). The manual restore functionality documented here is intended for data migration from AWS DocumentDB scenarios only .
docs.title: Atlas Restore (Data Migration)

docs.text: MongoDB Atlas cluster hostname for the restore connection (e.g. cluster0.abc123.mongodb.net ). Required when mongodb_provider=atlas and mongodb_action=restore|restore-database Environment Variable: ATLAS_MONGODB_HOST Default: None Used with atlas_mongodb_username and atlas_mongodb_password to build the MongoDB connection URI for the mongorestore command. Use the SRV hostname format without the mongodb+srv:// prefix.
docs.title: atlas_mongodb_host

docs.text: MongoDB database username for the restore connection — must have readWriteAnyDatabase or equivalent write permissions. Required when mongodb_provider=atlas and mongodb_action=restore|restore-database Environment Variable: ATLAS_MONGODB_USERNAME Default: None Used for authentication during the mongorestore operation.
docs.title: atlas_mongodb_username

docs.text: MongoDB database password for the restore connection — the password for the specified username. Required when mongodb_provider=atlas and mongodb_action=restore|restore-database Environment Variable: ATLAS_MONGODB_PASSWORD Default: None Used for authentication during the mongorestore operation. Store securely and never commit to version control.
docs.title: atlas_mongodb_password

docs.text: Local path to the MongoDB backup archive file ( .tar.gz , e.g. /path/to/mongodb-backup-20240621.tar.gz ). Required when mongodb_provider=atlas and mongodb_action=restore|restore-database Environment Variable: ATLAS_BACKUP_ARCHIVE_PATH Default: None The role extracts this archive and restores the data to the Atlas cluster. Used with atlas_index_file_path — this is for the restore-database action which uses local files, not the restore action which downloads from S3.
docs.title: atlas_backup_archive_path

docs.text: Local path to the MongoDB index backup JSON file (e.g. /path/to/mongodb-indexes-20240621.json ). Required when mongodb_provider=atlas and mongodb_action=restore|restore-database Environment Variable: ATLAS_INDEX_FILE_PATH Default: None The role reads this file and recreates the indexes after the data restore; the file must be valid JSON containing index definitions for each database and collection. Used with atlas_backup_archive_path — this is for the restore-database action which uses local files, not the restore action which downloads from S3.
docs.title: atlas_index_file_path

docs.text: This section provides comprehensive information about MongoDB backup and restore operations for the Community Edition (CE) operator.
docs.title: Backup and Restore Operations

docs.text: Action Purpose Instance Resources Database Data Prerequisites Use Case backup Create backup Yes Yes Running MongoDB instance Regular backups, disaster recovery preparation backup-database Database-only backup No Yes Running MongoDB instance Regular backups, disaster recovery preparation restore Full restore Yes (recreates instance) Yes Backup with instance resources Disaster recovery, cluster migration, complete restoration restore-database Database-only restore No (preserves existing) Yes Running MongoDB instance with matching version Data recovery, selective restore, testing
docs.title: Action Comparison

docs.text: The MongoDB backup operation creates a backup of your MongoDB instance and databases associated with your MAS instance: Database Backup : Uses mongodump to export databases with filter "^(mas|iot|sls|ibm-sls)(_|-)({{ mas_instance_id }}|sls)_(?!.*monitor$)" to match databases like mas-<instance-id>_<app-id> or iot-<instance-id>_<app-id> or ibm-sls_sls_licensing or sls-<instance-id>_sls_licensing . Instance Resources : Backs up Kubernetes resources including: CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) MongoDBCommunity Custom Resource (CR) Secrets (TLS certificates, credentials) Certificate resources Issuer resources Mongodb operator deployment service monitoring grafana dashboards Backup Directory Structure: /tmp/masbr/ └── backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-mongoce/ ├── data/ │ ├── mongodump-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.tar.gz │ └── mongodb-info.yaml └── resources/ ├── mongodbcommunitys/ ├── secrets/ ├── certificates/ └── issuers/ └── {kind}s/
docs.title: Backup Process

docs.text: The MongoDB role supports two types of restore operations:
docs.title: Restore Process

docs.text: Performs a complete restoration of both the MongoDB instance and its databases: Steps: Validates backup files and required variables Restores the namespace (Project) Restores Secrets and ConfigMaps Restores CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) Restores RBAC resources (ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding) Configures anyuid permissions for MongoDB service accounts Restores the MongoDB Operator Deployment Waits for MongoDB operator to be ready Restores Certificate Manager resources (Issuer, Certificate) Restores the MongoDBCommunity Custom Resource (Overrides storageclass if flag is set) Waits for MongoDB StatefulSets to be ready Restores ServiceMonitor and GrafanaDashboard resources Restores database data using mongorestore When to use: Disaster recovery scenarios Migrating MongoDB to a new cluster Recreating a deleted MongoDB instance Setting up a new environment from backup Requirements: mas_instance_id : MAS instance identifier mas_backup_dir : Directory containing the backup mongodb_backup_version : Timestamp of the backup to restore override_storageclass : Set to true to override storage class during instance restore
docs.title: 1. Full Restore (restore action)

docs.text: Restores only the database data to an existing MongoDB instance: Steps: Validates backup files and required variables Verifies existing MongoDB installation is running Checks MongoDB version compatibility Restores database data using mongorestore When to use: Restoring data to an existing MongoDB instance Recovering from data corruption without recreating the instance Selective database restoration Testing data restoration without affecting instance configuration Requirements: mas_instance_id : MAS instance identifier mas_backup_dir : Directory containing the backup mongodb_backup_version : Timestamp of the backup to restore mongodb_namespace : Namespace where MongoDB is running mongodb_instance_name : Name of the existing MongoDB instance MongoDB instance must already be running and accessible
docs.title: 2. Database-Only Restore (restore-database action)

docs.text: Version Compatibility: Target MongoDB version must match the backup version exactly Version upgrades should be performed separately, not during restore The restore process validates version compatibility before proceeding For restore-database action, the existing MongoDB instance must be running the same version as the backup Storage Requirements: Ensure sufficient storage in the backup directory Plan for at least 2x the database size for backup storage Backup directory structure: /tmp/masbr/backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-mongoce/ Monitor disk space during backup operations Security: Backup files contain sensitive data and credentials Secure backup directory with appropriate permissions (chmod 700 recommended) Consider encrypting backups for long-term storage Backup includes TLS certificates and admin credentials Restrict access to backup files to authorized personnel only Performance: Backup operations may impact MongoDB performance Schedule backups during low-usage periods Monitor resource utilization during backup/restore Large databases may take significant time to backup/restore Network bandwidth may affect backup/restore speed Restore Action Differences: restore action : Recreates the entire MongoDB instance from scratch, including all Kubernetes resources and restores database restore-database action : Only restores database data to an existing instance, preserving current configuration
docs.title: Important Considerations

docs.text: Regular Backups : Schedule automated backups at regular intervals Test Restores : Periodically test restore procedures in non-production environments Monitor Operations : Implement monitoring and alerting for backup failures Backup Validation : Verify backup integrity after completion Retention Policy : Implement and document backup retention policies Disaster Recovery : Include MongoDB backup/restore in your DR plan
docs.title: Backup and Restore Best Practices

docs.text: Backup Failures: Permission Errors : Verify backup role and user creation succeeded. Check MongoDB pod logs with oc logs -n mongoce <pod-name> -c mongod Disk Space Issues : Ensure sufficient space in backup directory. Clean up old backups if needed like /tmp/<mongodb_backup_version> . Check with df -h . Pod Access Issues : Verify pod is running and accessible. Check network connectivity to the cluster Restore Failures: Version Mismatch : Ensure target MongoDB version matches backup version. Deploy correct version before restoring Authentication Errors : Verify admin credentials are correct. Check MongoDB health status Missing Backup Files : Verify backup directory path and version. Ensure backup completed successfully Data Inconsistency : Verify backup integrity. Check restore logs for errors. Consider re-running restore General Issues: Pods Not Starting After Restore : Check pod events with oc describe pod -n mongoce <pod-name> . Verify PVCs are bound. Check resource limits and node capacity Connection Issues : Verify network policies and service configurations. Check certificate validity
docs.title: Backup and Restore Issues

docs.text: Restore MongoDB databases from a backup to an existing MongoDB instance without recreating the instance resources. Use Case : This action is ideal when you need to restore database data to an already running MongoDB instance, such as recovering from data corruption or restoring specific databases. Prerequisites : MongoDB instance must already be installed and running MongoDB version must match the backup version Backup files must be available in the specified backup directory - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mongodb_action: restore-database mas_instance_id: masinst1 mongodb_backup_version: 20251212-021316 mas_backup_dir: /tmp/masbr mongodb_namespace: mongoce mongodb_instance_name: mas-mongo-ce roles: - ibm.mas_devops.mongodb What this does : Validates that the backup exists at the specified location Verifies the MongoDB instance is running in the specified namespace Checks version compatibility between backup and running instance Restores database data using mongorestore command Preserves all existing instance configuration and resources Note : This action does NOT restore instance resources (secrets, certificates, CRs). Use the restore action for full instance restoration.
docs.title: Restore Database (CE Operator)

docs.text: Perform a complete restoration of MongoDB instance including all Kubernetes resources and database data from a backup. Use Case : This action is ideal for disaster recovery scenarios where you need to recreate the entire MongoDB instance from scratch, including all configuration, secrets, certificates, and data. Prerequisites : Backup files must be available in the specified backup directory Backup must include instance resources (secrets, certificates, CRs) Target cluster must have cert-manager installed Sufficient storage and resources available - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mongodb_action: restore mas_instance_id: masinst1 mongodb_backup_version: 20251212-021316 mas_backup_dir: /tmp/masbr roles: - ibm.mas_devops.mongodb What this does : Validates backup files and required variables Restores namespace, secrets, and ConfigMaps Restores CRDs and RBAC resources Restores MongoDB Operator deployment Restores Certificate Manager resources Restores MongoDBCommunity Custom Resource Waits for MongoDB instance to be fully operational Restores database data using mongorestore Note : This is a complete restoration that recreates the MongoDB instance from scratch. Use restore-database action if you only need to restore data to an existing instance.
docs.title: Full Restore (CE Operator)
