docs.text: This example demonstrates how to backup an AWS DocumentDB cluster. The backup creates two files: mongodb-backup.tar.gz - Compressed database backup collection-indexes.json - Collection indexes for restore - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mongodb_provider: aws mongodb_action: backup-database docdb_cluster_name: massre-mas-cluster-8-mongo.cluster-cvwxreialrtj.us-east-1.docdb.amazonaws.com docdb_master_username: masinst_inst04 docdb_master_password: "{{ lookup('env', 'DOCDB_MASTER_PASSWORD') }}" docdb_port: 27017 aws_region: us-east-1 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.mongodb Command Line Example: ansible-playbook ibm/mas_devops/playbooks/docdb_backup_simple.yml \ -e "docdb_cluster_name=massre-mas-cluster-8-mongo.cluster-cvwxreialrtj.us-east-1.docdb.amazonaws.com" \ -e "docdb_master_username=masinst_inst04" \ -e "docdb_master_password=fn9Uh5wZ4KsZy4OZ0OXx" \ -e "aws_region=us-east-1" \ -e "mongodb_provider=aws" \ -e "mongodb_action=backup-database" \ -e "docdb_port=27017" Backup Output: The backup process creates the following files in /tmp/docdb-backup-<timestamp>/ : mongodb-backup.tar.gz - Full database backup (compressed) collection-indexes.json - Collection indexes metadata Important Notes: The backup does NOT upload to S3 automatically Both files are created locally in the backup directory Temporary files (logs, scripts, CA certificates) are automatically cleaned up after backup The backup uses mongodump with TLS/SSL connection to DocumentDB Collection indexes are extracted separately for easier restore operations Required Variables: docdb_cluster_name - DocumentDB cluster endpoint docdb_master_username - Admin username docdb_master_password - Admin password (use environment variable or vault) aws_region - AWS region where DocumentDB is deployed mongodb_provider - Must be set to aws mongodb_action - Must be set to backup-database or backup Optional Variables: docdb_port - DocumentDB port (default: 27017) docdb_backup_dir - Custom backup directory (default: /tmp/docdb-backup-<timestamp> ) docdb_ca_cert_url - Custom CA certificate URL (default: AWS global bundle)

docs.text: Important Please be cautious while performing any of the troubleshooting steps outlined below. It is important to understand that the MongoDB Community operator persists data within Persistent Volume Claims. These claims should not be removed. Inadvertent deletion of the mongoce namespace could result in data loss.
docs.title: Troubleshooting

docs.text: MongoDB 5 has introduced new platform specific requirements. Please consult the Platform Support Notes for detailed information. It is of particular importance to confirm that the AVX instruction set is exposed or available to the MongoDB workloads. This can easily be determined by entering any running pod on the same OpenShift cluster where MongoDB replica set members are failing to start. Once inside of a running pod the following command can be executed to confirm if the AVX instruction set is available: cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep flags | grep avx If avx is not found in the available flags then either the physical processor hosting the OpenShift cluster does not provide the AVX instruction set or the virtual host configuration is not exposing the AVX instruction set. If the latter is suspected the virtual hosting documentation should be referenced for details on how to expose the AVX instruction set.
docs.title: MongoDB Replica Set Pods Will Not Start

docs.text: If authenticating via LDAP with PLAIN specified for authMechanism then configDb must be set to $external in the MongoCfg. The field configDb in the MongoCfg refers to the authentication database.

docs.text: Warning If the MongoDB CA Certificate expires the MongoDB replica set will become unusable. Replica set members will not be able to communicate with each other and client applications (i.e. Maximo Application Suite components) will not be able to connect. In order to renew the CA Certificate used by the MongoDB replica set the following steps must be taken: Delete the CA Certificate resource Delete the MongoDB server Certificate resource Delete the Secrets resources associated with both the CA Certificate and Server Certificate Delete the Secret resource which contains the MongoDB configuration parameters Delete the ConfigMap resources which contains the CA certificate Delete the Secret resource which contains the server certificate and private key The following steps illustrate the process required to renew the CA Certificate, server certificate and reconfigure the MongoDB replica set with the new CA and server certificates. The first step is to stop the Mongo replica set and MongoDB CE Operator pod. oc project mongoce oc delete deployment mongodb-kubernetes-operator Important Make sure the MongoDB Community operator pod has terminated before proceeding. oc delete statefulset mas-mongo-ce Important Make sure all pods in the mongoce namespace have terminated before proceeding Remove expired CA Certificate and Server Certificate resources. Clean up MongoDB Community configuration and then run the mongodb role. oc delete certificate mongo-ca-crt oc delete certificate mongo-server oc delete secret mongo-ca-secret oc delete secret mongo-server-cert oc delete secret mas-mongo-ce-config oc delete configmap mas-mongo-ce-cert-map oc delete secret mas-mongo-ce-server-certificate-key export ROLE_NAME=mongodb ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Once the mongodb role has completed the MongoDB CE Operator pod and Mongo replica set should be configured. After the CA and server Certificates have been renewed you must ensure that the MongoCfg Suite CR is updated with the new CA Certificate. First obtain the CA Certificate from the Secret resource mongo-ca-secret . Then edit the Suite MongoCfg CR in the Maximo Application Suite core namespace. This is done by updating the appropriate certificate under .spec.certificates in the MongoCfg CR: spec: certificates: - alias: ca crt: | -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- -----END CERTIFICATE----- If an IBM Suite Licensing Service (SLS) is also connecting to the MongoDB replica set the LicenseService CR must also be updated to reflect the new MongoDB CA. This can be added to the .spec.mongo.certificates section of the LicenseService CR. mongo: certificates: - alias: mongoca crt: | -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- -----END CERTIFICATE----- Once the CA certificate has been updated for the MongoCfg and LicenseService CRs several pods in the core and SLS namespaces might need to be restarted to pick up the changes. This would include but is not limited to coreidp, coreapi, api-licensing.
docs.title: CA Certificate Renewal

docs.text: nvidia_gpu ¤ This role installs and configures the NVIDIA GPU Operator on OpenShift clusters to enable GPU workloads. The GPU Operator manages the lifecycle of NVIDIA software components required to run GPU-accelerated applications. The role automatically installs the Node Feature Discovery (NFD) Operator as a prerequisite, then deploys the NVIDIA GPU Operator and creates a ClusterPolicy to configure GPU support across the cluster. This is required for applications like Maximo Visual Inspection that need GPU acceleration. Prerequisites ¤ OpenShift cluster with GPU-enabled worker nodes Cluster administrator access GPU-capable hardware (NVIDIA GPUs) available in the cluster Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default gpu_namespace No nvidia-gpu-operator gpu_channel No v26.3 (OCP >= 4.21) / v25.3 (OCP < 4.21) gpu_driver_version No None gpu_driver_repository_path No nvcr.io/nvidia nfd_namespace No openshift-nfd nfd_channel No stable GPU Operator Variables ¤ gpu_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the NVIDIA GPU Operator and its components (deployments, services, ClusterPolicy) are deployed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: GPU_NAMESPACE Default: nvidia-gpu-operator The namespace is created if it doesn't exist, and the GPU Operator manages cluster-wide GPU resources regardless of namespace. The default is recommended for most deployments; override only for specific namespace requirements or multiple GPU operator instances. gpu_channel ¤ NVIDIA GPU Operator subscription channel, determining which version stream is installed from OperatorHub — for example v26.3 , v25.3 , v24.9 , or v24.6 . Optional Environment Variable: GPU_CHANNEL Default: v26.3 for OpenShift >= 4.21, v25.3 for OpenShift < 4.21 (auto-detected from the cluster's OpenShift version) Newer channels provide the latest features and driver support but may require newer OpenShift versions. Check the NVIDIA GPU Operator platform support matrix for compatibility, and set a channel explicitly only to pin to a specific version. gpu_driver_version ¤ Specific NVIDIA GPU driver version to install — a valid NVIDIA driver version string such as 535.129.03 or 550.54.15 — instead of the latest version provided by the operator channel. Optional Environment Variable: GPU_DRIVER_VERSION Default: None (uses latest compatible version) Specify only when you need a particular driver version for compatibility, stability, or certification requirements; the latest driver is usually recommended otherwise. Verify compatibility with your GPU hardware via the NVIDIA driver compatibility matrix , and ensure the version is available in the specified repository. gpu_driver_repository_path ¤ Container registry path where NVIDIA GPU driver container images are stored — a valid registry path such as nvcr.io/nvidia or registry.example.com/nvidia-drivers . Optional Environment Variable: GPU_DRIVER_REPOSITORY_PATH Default: nvcr.io/nvidia The GPU Operator pulls driver container images from this registry location. Override for air-gapped environments using a mirrored registry (mirror the images to an internal registry accessible from the cluster); private registries may require image pull secrets. Node Feature Discovery Variables ¤ nfd_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the Node Feature Discovery (NFD) Operator is deployed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). NFD detects GPU hardware and labels nodes with hardware features for the GPU Operator to use. Optional Environment Variable: NFD_NAMESPACE Default: openshift-nfd NFD is automatically installed by this role as a prerequisite for the GPU Operator and must be installed before it. The namespace is created if it doesn't exist; the default openshift-nfd is the standard namespace for NFD. nfd_channel ¤ Node Feature Discovery Operator subscription channel, determining which version stream is installed from OperatorHub — typically stable , with version-specific channels possibly available. Optional Environment Variable: NFD_CHANNEL Default: stable The stable channel provides production-ready releases and is recommended for production. Check OperatorHub for available channels in your OpenShift version; the NFD version should be compatible with the OpenShift version. Example Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - hosts: localhost vars: gpu_namespace: nvidia-gpu-operator gpu_channel: v26.3 nfd_namespace: openshift-nfd roles: - ibm.mas_devops.nvidia_gpu Run Role Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can easily run the role standalone using the run_role playbook provided. export GPU_NAMESPACE=nvidia-gpu-operator export GPU_CHANNEL=v26.3 export NFD_NAMESPACE=openshift-nfd ROLE_NAME=nvidia_gpu ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_cluster_monitoring ¤ Configure OpenShift Container Platform cluster monitoring with persistent storage and user-defined project monitoring. This role enables comprehensive monitoring capabilities essential for MAS deployments, including metrics collection, alerting, and user workload monitoring. Key capabilities: User-defined project monitoring : Enable monitoring for user applications and MAS workloads Persistent storage : Configure durable storage for Prometheus metrics and AlertManager data Version-aware configuration : Automatically applies appropriate templates for OpenShift 4.18+ or earlier versions The role configures both the platform monitoring stack (for OpenShift infrastructure) and user workload monitoring (for MAS applications) in the openshift-monitoring namespace. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cluster_monitoring_action No install prometheus_retention_period No 15d prometheus_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected prometheus_storage_size No 20Gi prometheus_alertmgr_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected prometheus_alertmgr_storage_size No 20Gi prometheus_userworkload_retention_period No 15d prometheus_userworkload_storage_class No prometheus_storage_class prometheus_userworkload_storage_size No 20Gi The storage class variables are only required when auto-detection does not find a known storage class; for production deployments we recommend always setting them explicitly. Actions ¤ cluster_monitoring_action ¤ Action to perform on the cluster monitoring stack. Optional Environment Variable: CLUSTER_MONITORING_ACTION Default: install Valid values are install (configure monitoring with persistent storage) and uninstall (remove the persistent storage configuration). All other variables only apply when the action is install . Warning Uninstalling does not remove the monitoring stack itself, only the persistent storage configuration. Monitoring reverts to ephemeral storage and all metrics data will be lost when pods restart — back up any important metrics before uninstalling. Platform Monitoring ¤ prometheus_retention_period ¤ Retention period for platform Prometheus metrics, as a duration string with unit suffix — for example 7d (minimal troubleshooting), 15d (most deployments), 30d (extended analysis), or 90d (compliance). Optional Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_RETENTION_PERIOD Default: 15d Only applies when both prometheus_storage_class and prometheus_alertmgr_storage_class are set. As a rule of thumb, a typical MAS deployment generates ~1-2GB of metrics per day — size prometheus_storage_size accordingly for your retention period. prometheus_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the platform Prometheus metrics persistent volume. Must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode; block storage is recommended for performance. Required when auto-detection does not find a known storage class Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-detected ( ibmc-block-gold , ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd , or managed-premium ) Common values by platform: IBM Cloud ibmc-block-gold / ibmc-block-silver , OpenShift Container Storage ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd , Azure managed-premium / managed-standard , AWS gp3 / gp2 . Tip Verify available storage classes with oc get storageclass . When this variable is not set, the role auto-detects the common storage classes listed above. prometheus_storage_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for platform Prometheus metrics — for example 20Gi (default, clusters with fewer than 50 nodes), 50Gi (50-100 nodes), 100Gi (100-200 nodes), or 200Gi and above (very large clusters or long retention periods). Optional Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 20Gi Only applies when both storage classes are set. Storage can be estimated as ~1-2GB per day × retention days × number of nodes / 50. Usage can be monitored with oc get pvc -n openshift-monitoring , and volumes can typically be expanded later (depending on the storage class). AlertManager ¤ prometheus_alertmgr_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the AlertManager persistent volume. Must support ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode for the multi-replica AlertManager deployment — file storage is required, because block storage does not support RWX. Required when auto-detection does not find a known storage class Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_ALERTMGR_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-detected ( ibmc-file-gold-gid , ocs-storagecluster-cephfs , or azurefiles-premium ) Common values by platform: IBM Cloud ibmc-file-gold-gid / ibmc-file-silver-gid , OpenShift Container Storage ocs-storagecluster-cephfs , Azure azurefiles-premium / azurefiles-standard , AWS efs-sc (requires the EFS CSI driver). prometheus_alertmgr_storage_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for AlertManager. AlertManager uses far less storage than Prometheus: 20Gi is sufficient for most deployments, 50Gi for a large number of alert rules or notification channels. Optional Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_ALERTMGR_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 20Gi Only applies when both storage classes are set. User Workload Monitoring ¤ prometheus_userworkload_retention_period ¤ Retention period for the user workload Prometheus instance, covering metrics from user applications and MAS workloads (not platform metrics) — for example 7d , 15d (default), or 30d for extended application analysis. Optional Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_USERWORKLOAD_RETENTION_PERIOD Default: 15d MAS applications (especially Manage) generate substantial metrics data — take this into account when setting retention and prometheus_userworkload_storage_size . prometheus_userworkload_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the user workload Prometheus metrics persistent volume. Must support ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_USERWORKLOAD_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Value of prometheus_storage_class Typically inherits from prometheus_storage_class ; set explicitly only if user workload metrics require different storage characteristics. prometheus_userworkload_storage_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for user workload metrics — for example 20Gi (default, 1-2 MAS applications), 50Gi (3-5 applications), or 100Gi (full MAS suite with extended retention). Optional Environment Variable: PROMETHEUS_USERWORKLOAD_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 20Gi Size based on the number of MAS applications × retention period × expected metrics volume. Usage can be monitored with oc get pvc -n openshift-user-workload-monitoring , and volumes can typically be expanded later. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: prometheus_storage_class: "ibmc-block-gold" prometheus_alertmgr_storage_class: "ibmc-file-gold-gid" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_cluster_monitoring License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_config ¤ Configure OpenShift Container Platform cluster-level settings for optimal MAS deployment. This role provides essential tuning for ingress timeouts, TLS cipher compatibility with IBM Java Semeru FIPS mode, and OperatorHub catalog source management. Key capabilities: Ingress timeout tuning : Prevent request failures for long-running operations FIPS-compatible TLS ciphers : Enable IBM Java Semeru runtime in FIPS mode Catalog source management : Disable default Red Hat catalogs for air-gapped environments Path-based routing : Configure namespace ownership for multi-namespace route support This role configures: Tune the IngressController to avoid request failures due to timeout for long running requests Configure the IngressController namespace ownership for path-based routing support Update APIServer and IngressController to set a custom tlsSecurityProfile to accommodate ciphers supported by IBM Java Semeru runtime. This is required for allowing the Java applications using Semeru runtime to run in FIPS mode. The following ciphers will be enabled: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA Disable the default Red Hat CatalogSources : certified-operators community-operators redhat-operators Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default ocp_update_ciphers_for_semeru No false ocp_ingress_controller_name No default ocp_ingress_update_timeouts No false ocp_ingress_client_timeout No 30s ocp_ingress_server_timeout No 30s ocp_ingress_namespace_ownership No Not set ocp_operatorhub_disable_redhat_sources No false ocp_enable_ipv6 No false cluster_type No None cluster_name No Not set rosa_token Conditional None ocp_update_allowed_registries No false ocp_allowed_registries No [] ocp_add_mas_registries No true ocp_add_rh_registries No true ocp_update_additional_trusted_ca No false ocp_additional_trusted_ca_dir No /tmp rosa_token is only required when cluster_type=rosa-hcp ; the allowed registries and additional trusted CA settings currently work with ROSA HCP clusters only. API Server ¤ ocp_update_ciphers_for_semeru ¤ Apply a custom TLS security profile — including ciphers compatible with the IBM Java Semeru runtime — to both the APIServer and IngressController resources. Required when running MAS applications (particularly Manage) in FIPS mode with IBM Java Semeru runtime. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_UPDATE_CIPHERS_FOR_SEMERU Default: false When enabled, the tlsSecurityProfile on both resources is updated to enable TLS 1.3 ciphers TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 , TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 , and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 , plus TLS 1.2 ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 , ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 , ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 , ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 , ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 , ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 , DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 , DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 , ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 , ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA , and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA . Warning Changes affect the cluster-wide TLS configuration, may require a cluster restart to fully apply, and should be verified for compatibility with other applications in the cluster. Ingress Controller ¤ ocp_ingress_controller_name ¤ Name of the Ingress Controller to configure — default (the default cluster Ingress Controller, most common) or any custom Ingress Controller name in your cluster. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_CONTROLLER_NAME Default: default Both the timeout settings ( ocp_ingress_update_timeouts ) and the namespace ownership policy ( ocp_ingress_namespace_ownership ) are applied to this controller. Custom Ingress Controllers are rare and typically used for advanced routing scenarios — verify the controller name exists before configuring. ocp_ingress_update_timeouts ¤ Whether to apply custom client and server timeout values to the Ingress Controller — enable when experiencing timeout issues with long-running MAS operations such as large file uploads, report generation, or data imports. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_UPDATE_TIMEOUTS Default: false When enabled, the IngressController is updated with the values from ocp_ingress_client_timeout and ocp_ingress_server_timeout . The default OpenShift timeout (30s) may be insufficient for MAS Manage operations — enabling this is recommended for production MAS deployments. Changes apply to all routes in the cluster. ocp_ingress_client_timeout ¤ Client-side timeout duration for ingress connections — how long a connection is held open while waiting for a client to send data or complete a request. A duration string with unit suffix (e.g. 30s , 5m , 1h ). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_CLIENT_TIMEOUT Default: 30s Common values: 30s (default, suitable for most operations), 5m (recommended for MAS Manage file uploads), 10m (very large file operations). Only applies when ocp_ingress_update_timeouts is true ; affects all routes in the cluster. Consider network latency and file sizes when setting — too short may cause upload failures, too long may consume resources. ocp_ingress_server_timeout ¤ Server-side timeout duration for ingress connections — how long a connection is held open while waiting for a backend application to respond. A duration string with unit suffix (e.g. 30s , 5m , 1h ). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_SERVER_TIMEOUT Default: 30s Common values: 30s (default, suitable for most operations), 5m (recommended for MAS Manage report generation), 10m (complex data processing operations), 30m (very long-running batch operations). Only applies when ocp_ingress_update_timeouts is true ; affects all routes in the cluster — monitor application logs to determine appropriate values. ocp_ingress_namespace_ownership ¤ Namespace ownership policy for the Ingress Controller — set to InterNamespaceAllowed to enable path-based routing support, which allows routes to claim the same hostname across different namespaces. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_NAMESPACE_OWNERSHIP Default: Not set Note When both timeout settings and namespace ownership are configured, they are applied in a single atomic operation to the IngressController resource. OperatorHub ¤ ocp_operatorhub_disable_redhat_sources ¤ Whether to disable the default Red Hat OperatorHub catalog sources ( certified-operators , community-operators , redhat-operators ) — required for air-gapped/disconnected environments where external catalog sources are not accessible, and useful to enforce the use of mirrored catalogs only. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_OPERATORHUB_DISABLE_REDHAT_SOURCES Default: false When true , the three default Red Hat catalog sources are disabled and operators must be installed from custom or mirrored catalogs — ensure custom catalogs are configured before disabling the defaults. Affects all operator installations in the cluster. Warning Setting to false does not re-enable disabled sources. Operators cannot be installed from Red Hat catalogs after disabling. IPv6 Networking ¤ ocp_enable_ipv6 ¤ Enable dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 networking on the cluster — adds an IPv6 cluster network ( fd01::/48 ) and service network ( fd02::/112 ), then waits for all cluster operators and nodes to become healthy, verifies all workers have IPv6 configured, and approves any pending node CSRs. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ENABLE_IPV6 Default: false Only required for Fyre clusters at the RTP (Research Triangle Park) site — SVL (San Jose/Silicon Valley, the default site) and other sites use IPv4. ROSA-HCP Settings ¤ cluster_type ¤ Deployment model of OpenShift — currently only used for rosa-hcp (AWS ROSA HCP), which triggers the deployment-model-specific tasks such as updating allowed registries and additional trusted CAs. Optional Environment Variable: CLUSTER_TYPE Default: None cluster_name ¤ Name of the OpenShift cluster — used as the target cluster for rosa CLI commands. Optional Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: Not set Currently only used for rosa-hcp . rosa_token ¤ ROSA login token for the rosa CLI, authenticating it against the ROSA cluster. Required (when cluster_type=rosa-hcp ) Environment Variable: ROSA_TOKEN Default: None Allowed Registries ¤ ocp_update_allowed_registries ¤ Whether to update the cluster's allowed registries list, restricting image pulls to only the defined registries — required for air-gapped/disconnected environments. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_UPDATE_ALLOWED_REGISTRIES Default: false When true , the allowed registries are set from ocp_allowed_registries , optionally extended by ocp_add_mas_registries and ocp_add_rh_registries ; all other registries are blocked. ROSA HCP automatically adds the Red Hat required registries image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 , quay.io , and registry.redhat.io . Warning Currently works with ROSA HCP only. Setting to false does not remove the allowed registries list. ocp_allowed_registries ¤ List of allowed registries to add to the cluster, beyond those defined by MAS and Red Hat — for air-gapped/disconnected environments, provide the domain(s) of your own image registry or registries. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ALLOWED_REGISTRIES Default: [] Pods in the cluster can pull images only from the registries in the defined list. Warning Currently works with ROSA HCP only. Setting to [] does not remove the allowed registries list. When exporting OCP_ALLOWED_REGISTRIES , use a comma-separated string — for example export OCP_ALLOWED_REGISTRIES=mas.ibm.com,abc.com . ocp_add_mas_registries ¤ Whether to add the MAS-specific registries icr.io , cp.icr.io , quay.io , and gcr.io on top of those defined in ocp_allowed_registries . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ADD_MAS_REGISTRIES Default: true Warning Currently works with ROSA HCP only. ocp_add_rh_registries ¤ Whether to add the Red Hat-specific registries icr.io , registry.redhat.io , registry.connect.redhat.com , ghcr.io , docker.io , nvcr.io , and gcr.io on top of those defined in ocp_allowed_registries . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ADD_RH_REGISTRIES Default: true Warning Currently works with ROSA HCP only. Additional Trusted CA ¤ ocp_update_additional_trusted_ca ¤ Whether to update the cluster's additional trusted CAs — adding the CAs of the image registries to be used so that the cluster can trust them. Required for air-gapped/disconnected environments. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_UPDATE_ADDITIONAL_TRUSTED_CA Default: false Warning Currently works with ROSA HCP only, and setting to false does not remove additional trusted CAs. If ocp_additional_trusted_ca_dir contains no files, an empty JSON is generated and uploaded to the cluster, which removes all additional trusted CAs. ocp_additional_trusted_ca_dir ¤ Path to the directory containing the additional trusted CAs to configure in the cluster — it can contain none, one, or more CAs. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ADDITIONAL_TRUSTED_CA_DIR Default: /tmp CA file names must match the registry URL and end with .crt (e.g. ibm.com.crt ). A JSON file named additional_trusted_ca.json is created in the same path and deleted at the end. Only applies when ocp_update_additional_trusted_ca is true ; currently works with ROSA HCP only. docs.text: Configure OpenShift Container Platform cluster-level settings for optimal MAS deployment. This role provides essential tuning for ingress timeouts, TLS cipher compatibility with IBM Java Semeru FIPS mode, and OperatorHub catalog source management. Key capabilities: Ingress timeout tuning : Prevent request failures for long-running operations FIPS-compatible TLS ciphers : Enable IBM Java Semeru runtime in FIPS mode Catalog source management : Disable default Red Hat catalogs for air-gapped environments Path-based routing : Configure namespace ownership for multi-namespace route support This role configures: Tune the IngressController to avoid request failures due to timeout for long running requests Configure the IngressController namespace ownership for path-based routing support Update APIServer and IngressController to set a custom tlsSecurityProfile to accommodate ciphers supported by IBM Java Semeru runtime. This is required for allowing the Java applications using Semeru runtime to run in FIPS mode. The following ciphers will be enabled: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA Disable the default Red Hat CatalogSources : certified-operators community-operators redhat-operators

docs.text: Apply a custom TLS security profile — including ciphers compatible with the IBM Java Semeru runtime — to both the APIServer and IngressController resources. Required when running MAS applications (particularly Manage) in FIPS mode with IBM Java Semeru runtime. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_UPDATE_CIPHERS_FOR_SEMERU Default: false When enabled, the tlsSecurityProfile on both resources is updated to enable TLS 1.3 ciphers TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 , TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 , and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 , plus TLS 1.2 ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 , ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 , ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 , ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 , ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 , ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305 , DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 , DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 , ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 , ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA , and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA . Warning Changes affect the cluster-wide TLS configuration, may require a cluster restart to fully apply, and should be verified for compatibility with other applications in the cluster.
docs.title: ocp_update_ciphers_for_semeru

docs.text: Name of the Ingress Controller to configure — default (the default cluster Ingress Controller, most common) or any custom Ingress Controller name in your cluster. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_CONTROLLER_NAME Default: default Both the timeout settings ( ocp_ingress_update_timeouts ) and the namespace ownership policy ( ocp_ingress_namespace_ownership ) are applied to this controller. Custom Ingress Controllers are rare and typically used for advanced routing scenarios — verify the controller name exists before configuring.
docs.title: ocp_ingress_controller_name

docs.text: Whether to apply custom client and server timeout values to the Ingress Controller — enable when experiencing timeout issues with long-running MAS operations such as large file uploads, report generation, or data imports. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_UPDATE_TIMEOUTS Default: false When enabled, the IngressController is updated with the values from ocp_ingress_client_timeout and ocp_ingress_server_timeout . The default OpenShift timeout (30s) may be insufficient for MAS Manage operations — enabling this is recommended for production MAS deployments. Changes apply to all routes in the cluster.
docs.title: ocp_ingress_update_timeouts

docs.text: Client-side timeout duration for ingress connections — how long a connection is held open while waiting for a client to send data or complete a request. A duration string with unit suffix (e.g. 30s , 5m , 1h ). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_CLIENT_TIMEOUT Default: 30s Common values: 30s (default, suitable for most operations), 5m (recommended for MAS Manage file uploads), 10m (very large file operations). Only applies when ocp_ingress_update_timeouts is true ; affects all routes in the cluster. Consider network latency and file sizes when setting — too short may cause upload failures, too long may consume resources.
docs.title: ocp_ingress_client_timeout

docs.text: Server-side timeout duration for ingress connections — how long a connection is held open while waiting for a backend application to respond. A duration string with unit suffix (e.g. 30s , 5m , 1h ). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_SERVER_TIMEOUT Default: 30s Common values: 30s (default, suitable for most operations), 5m (recommended for MAS Manage report generation), 10m (complex data processing operations), 30m (very long-running batch operations). Only applies when ocp_ingress_update_timeouts is true ; affects all routes in the cluster — monitor application logs to determine appropriate values.
docs.title: ocp_ingress_server_timeout

docs.text: Namespace ownership policy for the Ingress Controller — set to InterNamespaceAllowed to enable path-based routing support, which allows routes to claim the same hostname across different namespaces. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_NAMESPACE_OWNERSHIP Default: Not set Note When both timeout settings and namespace ownership are configured, they are applied in a single atomic operation to the IngressController resource.
docs.title: ocp_ingress_namespace_ownership

docs.text: Whether to disable the default Red Hat OperatorHub catalog sources ( certified-operators , community-operators , redhat-operators ) — required for air-gapped/disconnected environments where external catalog sources are not accessible, and useful to enforce the use of mirrored catalogs only. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_OPERATORHUB_DISABLE_REDHAT_SOURCES Default: false When true , the three default Red Hat catalog sources are disabled and operators must be installed from custom or mirrored catalogs — ensure custom catalogs are configured before disabling the defaults. Affects all operator installations in the cluster. Warning Setting to false does not re-enable disabled sources. Operators cannot be installed from Red Hat catalogs after disabling.
docs.title: ocp_operatorhub_disable_redhat_sources

docs.text: Enable dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 networking on the cluster — adds an IPv6 cluster network ( fd01::/48 ) and service network ( fd02::/112 ), then waits for all cluster operators and nodes to become healthy, verifies all workers have IPv6 configured, and approves any pending node CSRs. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ENABLE_IPV6 Default: false Only required for Fyre clusters at the RTP (Research Triangle Park) site — SVL (San Jose/Silicon Valley, the default site) and other sites use IPv4.
docs.title: ocp_enable_ipv6

docs.text: ocp_deprovision ¤ Deprovision OCP cluster in Fyre, IBM Cloud, & ROSA. Destructive Operation Deprovisioning permanently deletes the cluster and all of its resources. This operation cannot be undone — always verify the cluster type and name, and back up any critical data, before running this role. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cluster_type Yes None cluster_name Yes None ibmcloud_apikey Conditional None rosa_token Conditional None fyre_username Conditional None fyre_apikey Conditional None fyre_site No svl ipi_dir No ~/openshift-install ipi_platform Conditional None aws_access_key_id Conditional None aws_secret_access_key Conditional None aws_region No eu-west-2 gcp_service_account_file Conditional None The provider-specific credentials are only required when cluster_type matches that provider (and, for the cloud credentials, when ipi_platform matches the platform). Cluster Identification ¤ cluster_type ¤ Infrastructure provider the cluster was provisioned with — one of fyre (IBM DevIT Fyre), roks (IBM Cloud Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Service), roks-vpc (ROKS on VPC infrastructure), rosa (Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS), or ipi (Installer-Provisioned Infrastructure on AWS or GCP). Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_TYPE Default: None Determines the deprovisioning workflow and which provider-specific variables are required. quickburn is accepted as a backwards-compatible alias for fyre . The value must match the provider used to create the cluster, otherwise deprovisioning will fail. cluster_name ¤ Name of the cluster to deprovision — a string that must exactly match the cluster name in the provider's system. Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Identifies which cluster is located and deleted in the provider's system. Verify the name carefully before proceeding — an incorrect name may cause the wrong cluster to be deleted. ROKS ¤ ibmcloud_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API key used to authenticate with IBM Cloud for ROKS cluster deletion — a key string (typically 40+ characters) whose IAM permissions allow cluster deletion in the resource group. Required when cluster_type is roks or roks-vpc Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None The same API key used for cluster provisioning can be reused. Without a valid API key with delete permissions, cluster deprovisioning will fail. ROSA ¤ rosa_token ¤ ROSA API token used to authenticate with the ROSA service — obtained from OpenShift Cluster Manager ; the token must be valid and not expired. Required when cluster_type is rosa Environment Variable: ROSA_TOKEN Default: None Tokens expire periodically, so obtain a fresh token before deprovisioning. ROSA deprovisioning also uses aws_access_key_id , aws_secret_access_key , and aws_region to clean up the cluster's EFS file storage. Fyre ¤ fyre_username ¤ Fyre username for authenticating with the IBM DevIT Fyre API — a valid Fyre account username (IBM intranet ID). Required when cluster_type is fyre Environment Variable: FYRE_USERNAME Default: None Fyre is an internal IBM development platform — access requires IBM credentials and appropriate permissions. fyre_apikey ¤ Fyre API key for authentication, paired with fyre_username — obtained from the Fyre portal; keys may expire and need renewal. Required when cluster_type is fyre Environment Variable: FYRE_APIKEY Default: None Keep the API key secure and rotate it regularly. fyre_site ¤ Fyre datacenter site where the cluster was provisioned — a valid Fyre site code (e.g. svl , rtp , raleigh ). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_SITE Default: svl svl (San Jose/Silicon Valley) is the default and most commonly used site. Must match the site used during provisioning — an incorrect site will cause deprovisioning to fail. IPI ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi . ipi_dir ¤ Working directory for IPI deprovisioning, containing the openshift-install executable and the cluster metadata required for deprovisioning — an absolute filesystem path. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_DIR Default: ~/openshift-install Must match the directory used during cluster provisioning; the cluster metadata (under config/{cluster_name} in this directory) is required for proper cleanup of all resources. An incorrect path will cause deprovisioning to fail. ipi_platform ¤ Cloud platform the IPI cluster was deployed on — aws or gcp . Required when cluster_type is ipi Environment Variable: IPI_PLATFORM Default: None Must match the platform used during cluster provisioning. Determines which cloud credentials are required: aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key for aws , or gcp_service_account_file for gcp . AWS ¤ The following variables are used when cluster_type = ipi and ipi_platform = aws ; aws_access_key_id , aws_secret_access_key , and aws_region are also used by ROSA deprovisioning to clean up EFS file storage. aws_access_key_id ¤ AWS access key ID for authenticating with AWS — a key ID string (typically 20 characters, starting with AKIA ). Required when deprovisioning an IPI cluster with ipi_platform=aws Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None The associated IAM user or role must have permissions to delete all cluster resources (VPC, EC2, ELB, Route53, IAM, etc.) — incomplete permissions may leave orphaned resources. For AWS IPI deprovisioning the credentials must be provided as environment variables (the OpenShift installer reads them from the environment), not just as Ansible variables. aws_secret_access_key ¤ AWS secret access key for authentication, paired with aws_access_key_id — a key string (typically 40 characters). Required when deprovisioning an IPI cluster with ipi_platform=aws Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Keep the secret key secure and rotate it regularly. Like the access key ID, it must be provided as an environment variable for AWS IPI deprovisioning. aws_region ¤ AWS region used when cleaning up cluster resources with the AWS CLI — for example eu-west-2 . Optional Environment Variable: AWS_DEFAULT_REGION Default: eu-west-2 Used by ROSA deprovisioning to locate and delete the cluster's EFS file storage. GCP ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi and ipi_platform = gcp . gcp_service_account_file ¤ Path to the GCP service account credentials file — an absolute path to a valid service account JSON key file, whose service account has permissions to delete instances and networking resources. Required when cluster_type is ipi and ipi_platform is gcp Environment Variable: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS Default: None The service account must have permissions to delete all cluster resources (Compute, Networking, IAM, etc.); the same service account used for provisioning can be reused. Incomplete permissions may leave orphaned resources. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: cluster_name: mycluster cluster_type: roks ibmcloud_apikey: xxxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_deprovision License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_efs ¤ Provision and configure AWS Elastic File System (EFS) storage for Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) clusters. This role automates the complete EFS setup including security group configuration, EFS instance creation, access points, mount targets, and StorageClass creation. EFS provides ReadWriteMany (RWX) persistent storage essential for MAS applications that require shared file access across multiple pods, such as Manage attachments and customer files. The role performs the following operations: Configures security group inbound rules for NFS access Creates EFS file system in the cluster's VPC Establishes mount targets in all availability zones Creates access points for isolated storage Deploys EFS CSI driver and StorageClass Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default aws_access_key_id Yes None aws_secret_access_key Yes None aws_region No eu-west-2 cluster_name Yes None efs_unique_id No Value of cluster_name creation_token_prefix No mas_devops. create_storage_class No true AWS Credentials ¤ aws_access_key_id ¤ AWS access key ID for authentication — a valid 20-character alphanumeric AWS access key ID. Required Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None Must have IAM permissions for EFS, EC2, and VPC operations (creating EFS resources, modifying security groups, and managing VPC resources); insufficient permissions will cause provisioning failures. Consider using IAM roles instead of access keys for better security, and store credentials securely, never in version control. aws_secret_access_key ¤ AWS secret access key for authentication — a valid 40-character alphanumeric AWS secret access key corresponding to aws_access_key_id . Required Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Keep the secret key secure and never expose it in logs or version control; rotate credentials regularly per security best practices, and consider AWS STS temporary credentials for enhanced security. Cluster and Region ¤ aws_region ¤ AWS region where the EFS instance will be provisioned — a valid AWS region code, for example us-east-1 (US East, N. Virginia), us-west-2 (US West, Oregon), eu-west-1 (Europe, Ireland), eu-west-2 (Europe, London, default), or ap-southeast-1 (Asia Pacific, Singapore). Optional Environment Variable: AWS_DEFAULT_REGION Default: eu-west-2 EFS must be in the same region as the ROSA cluster — cross-region access is not supported. Verify the cluster region with rosa describe cluster -c <cluster-name> ; EFS pricing varies by region. cluster_name ¤ Name of the ROSA cluster to attach EFS storage — a valid ROSA cluster name as shown in rosa list clusters , case-sensitive. Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None The cluster must exist before running this role. The role uses this name to find the cluster's VPC ID, configure EFS mount targets in the correct network, and tag AWS resources for cost tracking. EFS Configuration ¤ efs_unique_id ¤ Unique identifier for the EFS instance and StorageClass — an alphanumeric string, typically lowercase (e.g., mas-prod , manage-storage , shared-files ). Optional Environment Variable: EFS_UNIQUE_ID Default: Value of cluster_name The StorageClass is named efs-<efs_unique_id> , and the EFS file system and creation tokens are tagged with this identifier. Set it when you need multiple EFS instances in the same cluster (e.g., mas-attachments , mas-logs ) or want a more descriptive name than the cluster name; it must be unique within the cluster when creating multiple instances. creation_token_prefix ¤ Prefix for AWS resource creation tokens — a string prefix, typically ending with a dot or dash (e.g., mas_devops. , myorg- , prod_ ). Optional Environment Variable: CREATION_TOKEN_PREFIX Default: mas_devops. Creation tokens are built by concatenating this prefix with efs_unique_id to ensure idempotent resource creation. The default mas_devops. identifies resources created by this collection; change it to distinguish resources from other automation tools. create_storage_class ¤ Enable automatic StorageClass creation for the EFS instance — true to create a StorageClass named efs-<efs_unique_id> (default), false to skip creation. Optional Environment Variable: CREATE_STORAGE_CLASS Default: true When true , the created StorageClass supports dynamic provisioning with RWX access mode for PVCs backed by EFS. Set to false only if you need custom StorageClass parameters — you must then create the StorageClass manually. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: # Add required variables here roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_efs License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_github_oauth ¤ Configure OpenShift cluster authentication using GitHub OAuth. This role enables users to log into OpenShift using their GitHub credentials, with support for both public GitHub and GitHub Enterprise. It also manages user groups and cluster role bindings based on GitHub organization membership. Prerequisites : GitHub OAuth application must be configured in your GitHub organization before using this role OAuth application must use ibmgithub as the OAuth ID Requires GitHub organization admin permissions The role creates OAuth configuration, manages user groups, and assigns cluster roles based on GitHub organization membership. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default oauth.github_client_secret_value Yes None oauth.github_client_id_value Yes None oauth.github_hostname No github.com oauth.organizations Yes None oauth.groups No None oauth.groups.name Conditional None oauth.groups.users Conditional None oauth.groups.groups_cluster_rolebindings Conditional None The oauth.groups.* variables are only required when defining entries in the oauth.groups list. OAuth Configuration ¤ oauth.github_client_secret_value ¤ GitHub OAuth application client secret, generated by GitHub and obtained from your GitHub OAuth app settings. Required Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: None Used to authenticate the OpenShift cluster with GitHub; an incorrect secret will prevent GitHub authentication. The secret is stored as a Kubernetes secret in the cluster — keep it secure, never commit it to version control, and regenerate it if compromised. oauth.github_client_id_value ¤ GitHub OAuth application client ID, generated by GitHub and obtained from your GitHub OAuth app settings. Required Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: None Identifies the OAuth application to GitHub during the authentication flow. It is a public value, but should still be managed securely, and must match the OAuth app configured with ibmgithub as the OAuth ID. oauth.github_hostname ¤ GitHub server hostname for authentication — github.com for public GitHub (default), github.ibm.com for IBM GitHub Enterprise, or a custom GitHub Enterprise hostname (e.g., github.example.com ). Optional Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: github.com (public GitHub) Determines which GitHub server handles authentication requests. The hostname must be accessible from the OpenShift cluster and have properly configured SSL certificates. oauth.organizations ¤ List of GitHub organizations allowed to authenticate to the OpenShift cluster — for example ['ibm', 'redhat'] or ['myorg'] . Required Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: None Only users who are members of at least one listed organization can authenticate to the cluster; membership is verified during each login. Organization names are case-sensitive, and multiple organizations can be specified for broader access. Group Mappings ¤ oauth.groups ¤ List of OpenShift groups to create, each mapping GitHub users to cluster role bindings. Optional Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: None Each entry is an object with name (OpenShift group name), users (list of GitHub usernames), and groups_cluster_rolebindings (list of cluster roles to bind to the group). Groups are created if they don't exist, enabling role-based access control (RBAC); users must be members of the specified organizations. oauth.groups.name ¤ Name of the OpenShift group to create — a valid Kubernetes group name (alphanumeric with hyphens, e.g., mas-admins , developers , or viewers ). Required when defining groups Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: None Required for each group definition in the oauth.groups list. Use descriptive names that reflect the group's purpose (common patterns: <project>-admins , <team>-developers ); group names must be unique within the cluster. oauth.groups.users ¤ List of GitHub usernames to add to the group — for example ['user1', 'user2', 'user3'] . Required when defining groups Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: None Listed users are added to the group upon first login and inherit all associated cluster role bindings. GitHub usernames are case-sensitive, users must be members of the specified GitHub organizations, and the list can be updated to add or remove user access. oauth.groups.groups_cluster_rolebindings ¤ List of cluster roles to bind to the group — common values are cluster-admin (full cluster administration), admin (full access to project resources), edit (modify project resources), view (read-only access), or custom cluster roles. Required when defining groups Environment Variable: None (passed as variable) Default: None Group members receive all permissions defined by the specified cluster roles; multiple roles can be assigned to a single group. Verify that roles exist with oc get clusterroles , and use the least privilege principle when assigning them. Warning cluster-admin grants full cluster control — assign it sparingly. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: # Add required variables here roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_github_oauth License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_idms ¤ Installs an ImageDigestMirrorSet (IDMS) for IBM Maximo Application Suite's Maximo Operator Catalog. Also install IDMS suitable for the Red Hat Operator Catalogs created by mirror_ocp . If there are legacy ImageContentSourcePolicies installed by previous versions of this role, they will be deleted. If PRODUCT_FAMILY is aiservice then it will install an ImageTagMirrorSet for OpenDataHub Warning This role doesn't work on IBMCloud ROKS. IBM Cloud RedHat OpenShift Service does not implement support for ImageDigestMirrorSet . If you want to use image mirroring you must manually configure each worker node individually using the IBM Cloud command line tool. IBM Maximo Operator Catalog Content All content used in the MAS install is sourced from three registries: icr.io , cp.icr.io , & quay.io : icr.io/cpopen All IBM operators icr.io/ibm-truststore-mgr IBM truststore manager worker image icr.io/ibm-sls IBM SLS content icr.io/db2u IBM Db2 Universal operator content cp.icr.io/cp All IBM entitled container images quay.io/opencloudio IBM common services quay.io/mongodb MongoDb Community Edition Operator & associated container images quay.io/amlen Eclipse Amlen - Message Broker for IoT/Mobile/Web quay.io/ibmmas Non-product IBM Maximo Application Suite images (e.g. MAS CLI) Red Hat Operator Catalog Content All content from the subset of the Red Hat operator catalogs supported by mirror_ocp is sourced from eight registries: icr.io , docker.io , quay.io , gcr.io , ghcr.io , nvcr.io , registry.connect.redhat.com , and registry.redhat.io : icr.io/cpopen docker.io/grafana quay.io/community-operator-pipeline-prod quay.io/operator-pipeline-prod quay.io/openshift-community-operators quay.io/strimzi quay.io/rh-marketplace gcr.io/kubebuilder ghcr.io/grafana ghcr.io/open-telemetry nvcr.io/nvidia registry.connect.redhat.com/crunchydata registry.connect.redhat.com/nvidia registry.connect.redhat.com/turbonomic registry.connect.redhat.com/rh-marketplace registry.redhat.io/openshift4 registry.redhat.io/source-to-image registry.redhat.io/odf4 registry.redhat.io/cert-manager registry.redhat.io/rhceph registry.redhat.io/amq-streams registry.redhat.io/ubi8 registry.redhat.io/openshift-pipelines registry.redhat.io/openshift-serverless-1 registry.redhat.io/lvms4 Note A content source policy for this content is only configured when setup_redhat_catalogs is set to True . If you are managing the Red Hat Operator Catalogs yourself the content therein may well be different depending how you have configured mirroring. Hosted Control Planes ¤ When working with hosted control planes such as ROSA with HCP , management of the IDMS requires a specialized process because access to critical resources is restricted via standard Kubernetes resources. This collection has specific support for ROSA with HCP. Before running this role, use the ocp_config role to: Add the image registry to allowed registries on the cluster Add the image registry's CA as an additional trusted CA Running this role will then: Add each IDMS individually using the rosa cli commands Important Note that on ROSA with HCP there is no way to access MachinePoolConfigs to figure out the state of the nodes (e.g. whether it is updating ). Therefore, we cannot reliably determine when (or if) the changes have been successfully applied. This is a limitation of the ROSA with HCP implementation; we recommend to wait up to an hour after running this role for the changes to be applied across all workers on a large cluster and contact ROSA support if the IDMS does not apply successfully. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cluster_type Conditional None product_family No mas setup_redhat_release No false setup_redhat_catalogs No false registry_private_host Yes None registry_private_port No None registry_private_ca_file Yes None registry_username Yes None registry_password Yes None registry_prefix No None registry_prefix_redhat Conditional None redhat_catalogs_prefix No None machine_config_multiupdate No false cluster_name Conditional None ocp_idms_working_dir No /tmp rosa_token Conditional None The ROSA HCP variables ( cluster_type , cluster_name , rosa_token ) are only required when working with a ROSA with HCP cluster, and registry_prefix_redhat is required when setup_redhat_release or setup_redhat_catalogs is true . Mirror Configuration ¤ cluster_type ¤ Cluster type for the ImageDigestMirrorSet configuration — rosa-hcp for a ROSA with HCP cluster (currently the only supported value). Optional — only used when working with a ROSA with HCP cluster Environment Variable: CLUSTER_TYPE Default: None To set up the IDMS for ROSA HCP you first need to run the ocp_config role to configure allowed registries, and cluster_name must identify the target cluster. product_family ¤ Product family whose image source registries are configured — mas or aiservice . Optional Environment Variable: PRODUCT_FAMILY Default: mas mas creates an IDMS for the MAS-related registries (icr.io, cp.icr.io, quay.io); aiservice creates an ImageTagMirrorSet for the OpenDataHub registries. The two product families use different image source registries, so the IDMS/ITMS configuration varies accordingly. setup_redhat_release ¤ Enables an ImageDigestMirrorSet for mirrored Red Hat OpenShift platform release content — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SETUP_REDHAT_RELEASE Default: false When true , creates an IDMS named ibm-mas-redhat-release for platform images. Only enable if you have mirrored OpenShift platform images with the mirror_ocp role ( mirror_redhat_platform=true ) — typically for air-gapped OpenShift installations or upgrades. Requires registry_prefix_redhat to be set. setup_redhat_catalogs ¤ Enables CatalogSources and an ImageDigestMirrorSet for mirrored Red Hat operator catalogs — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SETUP_REDHAT_CATALOGS Default: false When true , creates CatalogSources for certified-operator-index, community-operator-index, and redhat-operator-index, plus an IDMS named ibm-mas-redhat-catalogs for operator images. Required for air-gapped deployments using Red Hat operators; only enable if you mirrored operator catalogs with the mirror_ocp role ( mirror_redhat_operators=true ). Requires registry_prefix_redhat to be set. Target Registry ¤ registry_private_host ¤ Private hostname of the mirror registry accessible from within the OpenShift cluster — for example registry.internal.example.com or 10.0.0.100 . Required Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PRIVATE_HOST Default: None Cluster nodes pull images from this registry via the IDMS, so an incorrect hostname causes image pull failures. It must be the hostname accessible from within the cluster, not necessarily the public hostname — in disconnected environments this is typically an internal registry. registry_private_port ¤ Private port of the mirror registry — for example 443 , 5000 , or 32500 . Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PRIVATE_PORT Default: None Set only if the registry uses a non-standard port; when unset, the registry URL omits the port (standard HTTPS port 443 is assumed). An incorrect port causes image pull failures. registry_private_ca_file ¤ Path to the mirror registry's CA certificate file — for example ~/registry-ca.crt or /tmp/registry-ca.pem . Required Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PRIVATE_CA_FILE Default: None Must be the CA certificate that signed the registry's TLS certificate — required even if the registry uses self-signed certificates. The CA is added to all cluster nodes via MachineConfig, which causes the nodes to reboot, so ensure the certificate is valid and matches the registry's TLS certificate. registry_username ¤ Username for authenticating to the mirror registry. Required Environment Variable: REGISTRY_USERNAME Default: None The credentials are added to the cluster's global pull secret and must have pull permissions from the mirror registry. Keep credentials secure. registry_password ¤ Password for authenticating to the mirror registry, paired with registry_username . Required Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PASSWORD Default: None The credentials are added to the cluster's global pull secret. Keep the password secure and never commit it to version control. registry_prefix ¤ Optional path prefix for IBM content in the mirror registry — for example mas-241107 or mas-241205 . Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PREFIX Default: None The IDMS redirects image pulls to {host}:{port}/{prefix}/{reponame} , so this must match the prefix used when mirroring the images. A catalog datestamp prefix is recommended to help organize multiple mirror versions in the same registry. Red Hat content uses the separate registry_prefix_redhat . registry_prefix_redhat ¤ Optional path prefix for Red Hat release and operator catalog content in the mirror registry — for example ocp-412 , ocp-414 , or ocp-419 . Required when setup_redhat_release or setup_redhat_catalogs is true Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PREFIX_REDHAT Default: None The IDMS redirects Red Hat image pulls to {host}:{port}/{prefix}/{reponame} , so this must match the prefix used when mirroring the Red Hat content with the mirror_ocp role. OpenShift release prefixes help organize multiple OCP versions in the same registry. redhat_catalogs_prefix ¤ Optional prefix for the Red Hat CatalogSource names — for example ibm-mas , mas , or custom . Optional Environment Variable: REDHAT_CATALOGS_PREFIX Default: None Only applies when setup_redhat_catalogs is true . When set to ibm-mas it creates ibm-mas-certified-operator-index , ibm-mas-community-operator-index , and ibm-mas-redhat-operator-index ; when unset it creates certified-operator-index , community-operator-index , and redhat-operator-index . Use a prefix to distinguish these CatalogSources from others in the cluster or to avoid naming conflicts. machine_config_multiupdate ¤ Enables parallel worker node updates when applying MachineConfig changes (for CA certificate installation) — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: MACHINE_CONFIG_MULTIUPDATE Default: false Warning Only enable during initial cluster setup when nodes are lightly loaded and can be safely drained in parallel. In production, leave as false — MachineConfig changes cause node reboots, and updating one node at a time ensures workload availability during node updates. ROSA HCP ¤ Ensure you have rosa cli 1.2.61 or greater installed. cluster_name ¤ Cluster name of the ROSA HCP cluster, used to target the cluster via the rosa cli. Required when cluster_type is rosa-hcp Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None ocp_idms_working_dir ¤ Temporary working directory where the IDMS yamls are generated so they can be applied individually to the cluster. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_IDMS_WORKING_DIR Default: /tmp Ensure you have read and write access to the directory. Only used when running this role for a rosa-hcp cluster type. rosa_token ¤ Login token for the rosa cli, authenticating it to the ROSA cluster. Required when cluster_type is rosa-hcp Environment Variable: ROSA_TOKEN Default: None Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: registry_private_host: myocp-5f1320191125833da1cac8216c06779e-0000.us-south.containers.appdomain.cloud registry_private_port: 32500 registry_private_ca_file: ~/registry-ca.crt registry_username: admin registry_password: 8934jk77s862! # Not a real password, don't worry security folks setup_redhat_catalogs: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_idms License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: When working with hosted control planes such as ROSA with HCP , management of the IDMS requires a specialized process because access to critical resources is restricted via standard Kubernetes resources. This collection has specific support for ROSA with HCP. Before running this role, use the ocp_config role to: Add the image registry to allowed registries on the cluster Add the image registry's CA as an additional trusted CA Running this role will then: Add each IDMS individually using the rosa cli commands Important Note that on ROSA with HCP there is no way to access MachinePoolConfigs to figure out the state of the nodes (e.g. whether it is updating ). Therefore, we cannot reliably determine when (or if) the changes have been successfully applied. This is a limitation of the ROSA with HCP implementation; we recommend to wait up to an hour after running this role for the changes to be applied across all workers on a large cluster and contact ROSA support if the IDMS does not apply successfully.

docs.text: ocp_login ¤ This role provides support to login to a cluster using the oc CLI by looking up cluster information from the infrastructure provider's APIs, it also supports setting ocp_server and ocp_token directly to support login to any Kubernetes cluster. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cluster_name Conditional None cluster_type Conditional None ocp_server Conditional None ocp_token Conditional None ocp_skip_tls_verify No true ibmcloud_apikey Conditional None ibmcloud_endpoint No https://cloud.ibm.com fyre_username Conditional None fyre_apikey Conditional None fyre_site No svl rosa_token Conditional None rosa_cluster_admin_password Conditional None There are two login methods: either provide cluster_name and cluster_type for automatic credential lookup from the infrastructure provider's API (which also requires that provider's credentials), or provide ocp_server and ocp_token together for direct login to any Kubernetes cluster. Cluster Identification ¤ cluster_name ¤ Cluster name for credential lookup — a string matching your cluster name in the provider's system. Required (unless ocp_server and ocp_token are set) Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Combined with cluster_type , automatically retrieves the cluster server URL and login token from the provider API. This is the recommended approach for managed clusters (ROKS, ROSA, Fyre) and requires provider-specific credentials (e.g., ibmcloud_apikey for ROKS, rosa_token for ROSA, fyre_username / fyre_apikey for Fyre). cluster_type ¤ Infrastructure provider type for cluster, which determines which API is used for credential lookup — roks (IBM Cloud Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Service), fyre (IBM DevIT Fyre clusters), or rosa (Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS). Required (unless ocp_server and ocp_token are set) Environment Variable: CLUSTER_TYPE Default: None Each type requires different authentication variables: ibmcloud_apikey for roks , fyre_username / fyre_apikey for fyre , and rosa_token for rosa . The aliases roks-vpc (treated as roks ) and quickburn (treated as fyre ) are also accepted, and in-cluster skips the login entirely. Direct Login ¤ ocp_server ¤ OpenShift server URL for direct login — the full API server URL, for example https://api.cluster.example.com:6443 . Required (unless cluster_name and cluster_type are set) Environment Variable: OCP_SERVER Default: None Used directly for the oc login command, bypassing provider API credential lookup. Both ocp_server and ocp_token must be provided together; this method works with any Kubernetes cluster, including custom or on-premises clusters. ocp_token ¤ Authentication token for direct login — a valid OpenShift authentication token string, such as a service account token or a manually obtained token. Required (unless cluster_name and cluster_type are set) Environment Variable: OCP_TOKEN Default: None Used directly for the oc login --token command, bypassing provider API credential lookup. Both ocp_server and ocp_token must be provided together. ocp_skip_tls_verify ¤ Disable the certificate check when logging in using the ocp_server and ocp_token properties. Optional — only applies to direct login with ocp_server and ocp_token Environment Variable: OCP_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY Default: true IBM Cloud ROKS ¤ ibmcloud_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API key for ROKS authentication, obtained from IBM Cloud IAM. Required (when cluster_type=roks ) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None Used to authenticate with the IBM Cloud API and retrieve the cluster server URL and login token for ROKS clusters. Keep the API key secure and do not commit it to version control. ibmcloud_endpoint ¤ IBM Cloud API endpoint URL used for authentication and cluster lookup. Optional — only applies when cluster_type=roks Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_ENDPOINT Default: https://cloud.ibm.com The default public endpoint works for most deployments; override it only for specific regional or private cloud requirements. IBM DevIT Fyre ¤ fyre_username ¤ IBM DevIT Fyre username. Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_USERNAME Default: None Used with fyre_apikey to authenticate with the Fyre API and retrieve the cluster server URL and login token. Fyre is IBM's internal development and test infrastructure and requires IBM internal credentials. fyre_apikey ¤ IBM DevIT Fyre API key. Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_APIKEY Default: None Used with fyre_username to authenticate with the Fyre API and retrieve the cluster server URL and login token. Keep the API key secure; Fyre is IBM's internal development and test infrastructure. fyre_site ¤ Fyre site location for the cluster — a Fyre site code such as svl or rtp . Optional — only applies when cluster_type=fyre Environment Variable: FYRE_SITE Default: svl Determines which Fyre site API endpoint is used for cluster lookup; use the default ( svl ) for most Fyre clusters and override for clusters provisioned at other sites. AWS ROSA ¤ rosa_token ¤ AWS ROSA authentication token, obtained from the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console. Required (when cluster_type=rosa ) Environment Variable: ROSA_TOKEN Default: None Used to authenticate with the ROSA API and retrieve the cluster server URL and login credentials. Keep the token secure and do not commit it to version control. rosa_cluster_admin_password ¤ ROSA cluster-admin account password, created during cluster provisioning. Required (when cluster_type=rosa ) Environment Variable: ROSA_CLUSTER_ADMIN_PASSWORD Default: None Used to authenticate as the cluster-admin user on ROSA clusters. Keep the password secure and do not commit it to version control. Example Playbook ¤ Direct Login ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: ocp_server: xxxxx ocp_token: xxxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_login IBM Cloud ROKS ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: cluster_name: mycluster cluster_type: roks ibmcloud_apikey: xxxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_login AWS ROSA ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: cluster_name: mycluster cluster_type: rosa rosa_token: xxxxx rosa_cluster_admin_password: xxxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_login IBM DevIT Fyre ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: cluster_name: mycluster cluster_type: fyre fyre_username: xxxxx fyre_apikey: xxxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_login License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_node_config ¤ Configure individual OpenShift nodes with custom labels and taints to control workload placement. This role enables creation of dedicated nodes for specific workloads (e.g., Db2, MongoDB, compute-intensive applications) by applying Kubernetes node selectors and taints. Use labels to direct workloads to specific nodes and taints to prevent unwanted workloads from running on dedicated nodes. This is essential for performance isolation, resource management, and meeting specific hardware requirements. Verification : Use the following command to verify labels and taints: oc get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node-name> Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default ocp_node_name Conditional None ocp_node_index Conditional None ocp_node_label_keys No None ocp_node_label_values No None ocp_node_taint_keys No None ocp_node_taint_values No None ocp_node_taint_effects No None Either ocp_node_name or ocp_node_index must be set to identify the target node. When ocp_node_label_keys or ocp_node_taint_keys are set, the corresponding values/effects variables must provide the same number of entries. Node Selection ¤ ocp_node_name ¤ Node name to configure with labels and/or taints — a valid OpenShift node name, for example worker-0.example.com or 10.172.168.89 . Node names may be hostnames, IP addresses, or cloud provider identifiers; list them with oc get nodes . Optional (but one of ocp_node_name or ocp_node_index is required) Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_NAME Default: None Use when you know the exact node name — the preferred method for production environments where node names are predictable. An incorrect node name will cause the role to fail. Important Specify either ocp_node_name OR ocp_node_index to identify the target node. If both are specified, ocp_node_index takes priority. If neither is specified, the role will fail. ocp_node_index ¤ Zero-based index of the node in the cluster's node list — a non-negative integer, where 0 refers to the first node in the alphabetically sorted list. Optional (but one of ocp_node_name or ocp_node_index is required) Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_INDEX Default: None Useful in automation scenarios where node names are not known in advance, or when configuring nodes sequentially. Takes priority over ocp_node_name if both are set. An index out of range will cause the role to fail; the node order may change if nodes are added or removed, so this is less reliable than node name for production use. Node Labels ¤ ocp_node_label_keys ¤ Comma-separated list of label keys to add to the selected node — valid Kubernetes label keys (alphanumeric plus dash, underscore, or dot; 63 characters or less), for example workload or storage-type,gpu-enabled . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_LABEL_KEYS Default: None Labels are used by pod node selectors ( nodeSelector or nodeAffinity ) to direct workloads to specific nodes. The number of keys must match the number of values in ocp_node_label_values . Common label keys: workload , node-role , storage-type , hardware-type . Labels are additive — existing labels are not removed. ocp_node_label_values ¤ Comma-separated list of label values corresponding to the label keys — valid Kubernetes label values (alphanumeric plus dash, underscore, or dot; 63 characters or less), for example db2 or ssd,true . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_LABEL_VALUES Default: None Required when ocp_node_label_keys is set, providing exactly one value for each key. Order matters — the first value pairs with the first key, and so on. For example, keys= workload,storage with values= db2,ssd creates the labels workload=db2 and storage=ssd . Common label values: db2 , mongodb , compute , storage . Node Taints ¤ ocp_node_taint_keys ¤ Comma-separated list of taint keys to add to the selected node — valid Kubernetes taint keys, for example dedicatedDb2Node or gpu-workload,high-memory . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_TAINT_KEYS Default: None Taints prevent pods without matching tolerations from being scheduled on the node, and are more restrictive than labels. The number of keys must match the number of entries in ocp_node_taint_values and ocp_node_taint_effects . Common taint keys: dedicatedDb2Node , dedicatedMongoNode , gpu-required . ocp_node_taint_values ¤ Comma-separated list of taint values corresponding to the taint keys — for example masinst1 or prod-db,gpu-cluster , typically identifying which workload or instance the node is dedicated to. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_TAINT_VALUES Default: None Required when ocp_node_taint_keys is set, providing exactly one value for each key — the counts must match across keys, values, and effects. For example, key= dedicatedDb2Node with value= masinst1 and effect= NoExecute dedicates the node to masinst1's Db2. ocp_node_taint_effects ¤ Comma-separated list of taint effects defining how each taint impacts pod scheduling — NoSchedule , PreferNoSchedule , or NoExecute . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_TAINT_EFFECTS Default: None Required when ocp_node_taint_keys is set, with one effect per key: NoSchedule : new pods without tolerations will not be scheduled, but existing pods remain — common for gradual migration to dedicated nodes PreferNoSchedule : the scheduler tries to avoid placing pods without tolerations, but it is not guaranteed — least restrictive, useful for soft preferences NoExecute : new pods without tolerations will not be scheduled, and existing pods without tolerations are evicted — the strongest enforcement, and the most disruptive; use it for Db2 dedicated nodes to ensure no other workloads run Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # Turn this worker node into a dedicated Db2 worker node ocp_node_name: "10.172.168.89" # Add the label that will be applied to all dedicated Db2 nodes # this will be used to direct Db2 workloads to these nodes ocp_node_label_keys: workload ocp_node_label_values: db2 # Set a taint preventing anything other than Db2 workloads for masinst1 running # on this node specific Db2 node ocp_node_taint_keys: dedicatedDb2Node ocp_node_taint_values: masinst1 ocp_node_taint_effects: NoExecute roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_node_config License ¤ EPL-2.0
