This role enables creation of dedicated nodes for specific workloads (e.g., Db2, MongoDB, compute-intensive applications) by applying Kubernetes node selectors and taints. Use labels to direct workloads to specific nodes and taints to prevent unwanted workloads from running on dedicated nodes. This is essential for performance isolation, resource management, and meeting specific hardware requirements. Verification : Use the following command to verify labels and taints: oc get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node-name>
docs.title: ocp_node_config

docs.text: Variable Required Default ocp_node_name Conditional None ocp_node_index Conditional None ocp_node_label_keys No None ocp_node_label_values No None ocp_node_taint_keys No None ocp_node_taint_values No None ocp_node_taint_effects No None Either ocp_node_name or ocp_node_index must be set to identify the target node. When ocp_node_label_keys or ocp_node_taint_keys are set, the corresponding values/effects variables must provide the same number of entries.
docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Node name to configure with labels and/or taints — a valid OpenShift node name, for example worker-0.example.com or 10.172.168.89 . Node names may be hostnames, IP addresses, or cloud provider identifiers; list them with oc get nodes . Optional (but one of ocp_node_name or ocp_node_index is required) Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_NAME Default: None Use when you know the exact node name — the preferred method for production environments where node names are predictable. An incorrect node name will cause the role to fail. Important Specify either ocp_node_name OR ocp_node_index to identify the target node. If both are specified, ocp_node_index takes priority. If neither is specified, the role will fail.
docs.title: ocp_node_name

docs.text: Zero-based index of the node in the cluster's node list — a non-negative integer, where 0 refers to the first node in the alphabetically sorted list. Optional (but one of ocp_node_name or ocp_node_index is required) Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_INDEX Default: None Useful in automation scenarios where node names are not known in advance, or when configuring nodes sequentially. Takes priority over ocp_node_name if both are set. An index out of range will cause the role to fail; the node order may change if nodes are added or removed, so this is less reliable than node name for production use.
docs.title: ocp_node_index

docs.text: Comma-separated list of label keys to add to the selected node — valid Kubernetes label keys (alphanumeric plus dash, underscore, or dot; 63 characters or less), for example workload or storage-type,gpu-enabled . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_LABEL_KEYS Default: None Labels are used by pod node selectors ( nodeSelector or nodeAffinity ) to direct workloads to specific nodes. The number of keys must match the number of values in ocp_node_label_values . Common label keys: workload , node-role , storage-type , hardware-type . Labels are additive — existing labels are not removed.
docs.title: ocp_node_label_keys

docs.text: Comma-separated list of label values corresponding to the label keys — valid Kubernetes label values (alphanumeric plus dash, underscore, or dot; 63 characters or less), for example db2 or ssd,true . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_LABEL_VALUES Default: None Required when ocp_node_label_keys is set, providing exactly one value for each key. Order matters — the first value pairs with the first key, and so on. For example, keys= workload,storage with values= db2,ssd creates the labels workload=db2 and storage=ssd . Common label values: db2 , mongodb , compute , storage .
docs.title: ocp_node_label_values

docs.text: Comma-separated list of taint keys to add to the selected node — valid Kubernetes taint keys, for example dedicatedDb2Node or gpu-workload,high-memory . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_TAINT_KEYS Default: None Taints prevent pods without matching tolerations from being scheduled on the node, and are more restrictive than labels. The number of keys must match the number of entries in ocp_node_taint_values and ocp_node_taint_effects . Common taint keys: dedicatedDb2Node , dedicatedMongoNode , gpu-required .
docs.title: ocp_node_taint_keys

docs.text: Comma-separated list of taint values corresponding to the taint keys — for example masinst1 or prod-db,gpu-cluster , typically identifying which workload or instance the node is dedicated to. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_TAINT_VALUES Default: None Required when ocp_node_taint_keys is set, providing exactly one value for each key — the counts must match across keys, values, and effects. For example, key= dedicatedDb2Node with value= masinst1 and effect= NoExecute dedicates the node to masinst1's Db2.
docs.title: ocp_node_taint_values

docs.text: Comma-separated list of taint effects defining how each taint impacts pod scheduling — NoSchedule , PreferNoSchedule , or NoExecute . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_NODE_TAINT_EFFECTS Default: None Required when ocp_node_taint_keys is set, with one effect per key: NoSchedule : new pods without tolerations will not be scheduled, but existing pods remain — common for gradual migration to dedicated nodes PreferNoSchedule : the scheduler tries to avoid placing pods without tolerations, but it is not guaranteed — least restrictive, useful for soft preferences NoExecute : new pods without tolerations will not be scheduled, and existing pods without tolerations are evicted — the strongest enforcement, and the most disruptive; use it for Db2 dedicated nodes to ensure no other workloads run
docs.title: ocp_node_taint_effects

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # Turn this worker node into a dedicated Db2 worker node ocp_node_name: "10.172.168.89" # Add the label that will be applied to all dedicated Db2 nodes # this will be used to direct Db2 workloads to these nodes ocp_node_label_keys: workload ocp_node_label_values: db2 # Set a taint preventing anything other than Db2 workloads for masinst1 running # on this node specific Db2 node ocp_node_taint_keys: dedicatedDb2Node ocp_node_taint_values: masinst1 ocp_node_taint_effects: NoExecute roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_node_config

docs.text: ocp_provision ¤ Provision OCP cluster on IBM Cloud ROKS, ROSA, or DevIT Fyre. Fyre clusters will be automatically reconfigured to enable NFS storage. By default this is made available via the nfs-client storage class and supports both ReadWriteOnce and ReadWriteMany access modes. The image-registry-storage PVC used by the OpenShift image registry component will also be reconfigured to use this storage class. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cluster_type Yes None cluster_name Yes None ocp_version Yes None ocp_fips_enabled No false ocp_storage_provider No None ocp_provision_gpu No false gpu_workerpool_name No gpu gpu_workers No 1 gpu_flavor No gx2.8x64.v100 ibmcloud_apikey Conditional None ibmcloud_endpoint No https://cloud.ibm.com ibmcloud_resourcegroup No Default ibmcloud_region Conditional None roks_zone No dal10 roks_flavor No b3c.16x64.300gb roks_workers No 3 roks_flags No '' roks_vpc_name No cluster_name roks_vpc_id No None roks_subnet_id No None roks_cos_instance_crn No None roks_secondary_storage No '' rosa_token Conditional None rosa_cluster_admin_password No None (auto-generated) rosa_compute_nodes No 3 rosa_compute_machine_type No m5.4xlarge rosa_config_dir No '' fyre_username Conditional None fyre_password Conditional None fyre_quota_type Conditional quick_burn fyre_product_id Conditional None fyre_site No svl cluster_platform No x fyre_cluster_description No No description provided fyre_cluster_size Conditional medium fyre_worker_count Conditional 2 fyre_worker_cpu Conditional 8 fyre_worker_memory Conditional 32 fyre_worker_additional_disks No None fyre_worker_base_disk No None fyre_master_base_disk No None fyre_nfs_image_registry_size No 100Gi ocp_enable_ipv6 No false ipi_platform No aws ipi_region No us-east-1 ipi_base_domain Conditional None ipi_pull_secret_file Conditional None ipi_dir No ~/openshift-install sshKey No '' ipi_controlplane_type No m5.4xlarge ipi_controlplane_replicas No 3 ipi_compute_type No m5.4xlarge ipi_compute_replicas No 3 ipi_rootvolume_size No Platform default (typically 120GB) aws_access_key_id Conditional None aws_secret_access_key Conditional None gcp_service_account_file Conditional None ipi_gcp_projectid Conditional None Most variables are provider-specific: the Conditional entries are only required when provisioning the matching cluster_type (and, for the Fyre sizing variables, the matching fyre_quota_type ) — each entry states its exact condition. Cluster Definition ¤ cluster_type ¤ Infrastructure provider type for cluster provisioning — one of fyre (IBM DevIT Fyre, internal development), roks (IBM Cloud ROKS classic infrastructure), roks-vpc (IBM Cloud ROKS on VPC infrastructure — modern, recommended; requires an existing VPC), roks-vpc-setup (creates a VPC, subnet, and public gateway — run this first, then use the output IDs with roks-vpc ), rosa (Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS), or ipi (Installer-Provisioned Infrastructure, bare metal/on-premises). Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_TYPE Default: None Determines the provisioning workflow and which provider-specific variables are required. Each type has different capabilities — for example GPU support is only available on roks and roks-vpc . cluster_name ¤ Name for the new cluster, used as the cluster identifier in the provider's system — must be unique within the provider's account/region and follow provider naming conventions (typically lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens; some providers impose length limits or character restrictions). Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Used for DNS, resource naming, and cluster identification. ocp_version ¤ OpenShift version to install — a specific version (e.g. 4.22 , 4.22.2 ), the alias default (newest MAS-supported version), or the alias rotate (predetermined version by day of week, for testing only). Required Environment Variable: OCP_VERSION Default: None The version must be compatible with MAS and available from the provider. Warning For ROKS ( cluster_type=roks ), the version must append the _openshift suffix — for example 4.22_openshift or 4.22.13_openshift . ocp_fips_enabled ¤ Whether to provision the cluster with FIPS (Federal Information Processing Standards) 140-2 cryptographic mode enabled — set to true for government or regulated environments that require FIPS 140-2 compliance. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_FIPS_ENABLED Default: false Applies to fyre and ipi cluster types. FIPS mode may impact performance and cannot be changed after cluster creation — only enable it if required for compliance. ocp_storage_provider ¤ Storage provider configuration for Fyre clusters — set to nfs to enable NFS storage; only applies when cluster_type=fyre , leave unset for other cluster types (ROKS, ROSA, IPI). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_STORAGE_PROVIDER Default: None When set to nfs , an nfs-client storage class supporting both ReadWriteOnce (RWO) and ReadWriteMany (RWX) access modes is created connected to the Fyre infrastructure node, and the existing image registry PVC is deleted and recreated with NFS storage. See also fyre_nfs_image_registry_size . GPU Node Support ¤ GPU worker pools are supported on roks (classic) and roks-vpc (VPC) cluster types only. ocp_provision_gpu ¤ Whether to provision GPU-enabled worker nodes with the cluster — required for GPU-intensive workloads such as MAS Visual Inspection (MVI). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_PROVISION_GPU Default: false When true , a GPU worker pool is provisioned with gpu_workers nodes. On classic ROKS ( roks ) the GPU flavor is hardcoded to mg4c.32x384.2xp100 ; on VPC ROKS ( roks-vpc ) set gpu_flavor explicitly. gpu_workerpool_name ¤ Name for the GPU worker pool — use the default ( gpu ) for new GPU deployments, or set to an existing pool name to modify that pool rather than create a duplicate. Optional Environment Variable: GPU_WORKERPOOL_NAME Default: gpu Only applies when ocp_provision_gpu is true . If a GPU worker pool already exists with this name, it will be modified rather than a second pool created. gpu_workers ¤ Number of GPU-enabled worker nodes to provision in the GPU worker pool — a positive integer (e.g. 1 , 2 , 3 ). Optional Environment Variable: GPU_WORKERS Default: 1 Use the default (1) for minimal GPU deployments or testing; increase for production MAS Visual Inspection deployments. GPU nodes use expensive hardware — only provision what you need. gpu_flavor ¤ GPU-enabled machine type for the GPU worker pool when using cluster_type=roks-vpc — for example gx2.8x64.v100 (8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 1x V100 GPU, default) or gx2.16x128.2v100 (16 vCPU, 128 GB RAM, 2x V100 GPUs). Optional Environment Variable: GPU_FLAVOR Default: gx2.8x64.v100 Only applies when ocp_provision_gpu is true and cluster_type=roks-vpc ; on classic ROKS ( roks ) the GPU flavor is hardcoded to mg4c.32x384.2xp100 and this variable is ignored. Tip GPU flavor availability varies by zone — verify availability before deploying with ibmcloud oc flavors --zone <zone> --provider vpc-gen2 | grep gpu . ROKS ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type is roks , roks-vpc , or roks-vpc-setup (unless noted otherwise). ibmcloud_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API key for authentication, used by the ibmcloud CLI for all cluster operations — obtain it from IBM Cloud IAM (Identity and Access Management). Required (when cluster_type is roks , roks-vpc , or roks-vpc-setup ) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None The key must have cluster creation permissions in the target resource group ( ibmcloud_resourcegroup ). Keep API keys secure — use environment variables or secure vaults rather than hardcoding them in playbooks. ibmcloud_endpoint ¤ IBM Cloud API endpoint URL for authentication and cluster operations — override the default only for IBM Cloud dedicated or private environments, or for testing against staging environments. Optional Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_ENDPOINT Default: https://cloud.ibm.com Determines which IBM Cloud environment is targeted for cluster provisioning. Used together with ibmcloud_apikey . ibmcloud_resourcegroup ¤ IBM Cloud resource group in which the ROKS cluster will be created — the group must exist before provisioning and ibmcloud_apikey must have permissions in it. Optional Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Default Use the default for simple deployments; specify a different existing resource group for organizational separation. ibmcloud_region ¤ IBM Cloud region targeted when running VPC Infrastructure Service ( ibmcloud is ) commands — a valid region identifier such as us-south , eu-de , eu-gb , jp-tok , or au-syd . Required (when cluster_type=roks-vpc-setup ) Optional (when cluster_type=roks-vpc — auto-derived from the VPC CRN or from roks_zone ) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_REGION Default: None For roks-vpc-setup this must be provided explicitly, as it determines where all resources are created. For roks-vpc the region is resolved automatically in this order: roks_zone stripped of its zone suffix (e.g. eu-gb-1 → eu-gb ), then the VPC's CRN extracted during the VPC name lookup (which overrides the zone-derived value if different) — an explicitly set ibmcloud_region always wins. roks_zone ¤ IBM Cloud availability zone where the ROKS cluster will be provisioned — classic format for roks ( dal10 , lon02 , fra02 , tok02 ) or VPC format for roks-vpc ( us-south-1 , eu-de-2 , eu-gb-3 , jp-tok-1 — always <region>-<n> ). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_ZONE Default: dal10 The zone determines cluster location, which affects latency, data residency, and available services. For roks-vpc the zone must be within ibmcloud_region (e.g. region us-south → zone us-south-1 ), and not all roks_flavor values are available in all zones — verify availability in your target zone. roks_flavor ¤ Worker node machine type (flavor) for the ROKS cluster — classic flavors for roks (e.g. b3c.4x16 , b3c.16x64.300gb , b3c.32x128 ) or VPC flavors for roks-vpc (e.g. bx2.4x16 , bx2.16x64 , bx2.48x192 ). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_FLAVOR Default: b3c.16x64.300gb The default (16 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 300 GB storage) suits standard MAS deployments on classic ROKS. Larger flavors cost more but provide more resources. Warning The default is a classic flavor and will fail if used with roks-vpc . Always set an appropriate bx2.* VPC flavor when using cluster_type=roks-vpc — check availability with ibmcloud oc flavors --zone <zone> --provider vpc-gen2 . roks_workers ¤ Number of worker nodes to provision in the ROKS cluster — a positive integer (minimum 1; 3 or more recommended for production high availability). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_WORKERS Default: 3 Total cluster capacity = worker count x roks_flavor resources. More workers provide more capacity and better high availability but increase costs; GPU workers can be added separately via ocp_provision_gpu . roks_flags ¤ Additional command-line flags passed to the ibmcloud ks cluster create command — for example --disable-public-service-endpoint , --pod-subnet , or --service-subnet . Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_FLAGS Default: '' Use for advanced configurations not covered by the other ROKS variables; consult the IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service documentation for available flags. Warning Use with caution — incorrect flags can cause provisioning failures. ROKS VPC Setup ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = roks-vpc-setup . Run this provider first to create the VPC infrastructure, then pass the output IDs to cluster_type=roks-vpc . Also uses ibmcloud_apikey , ibmcloud_endpoint , ibmcloud_resourcegroup , and ibmcloud_region . Note : Does not require ocp_version or roks_zone . Subnets are always created in all three zones of ibmcloud_region ( <region>-1 , <region>-2 , <region>-3 ), matching the default IBM Cloud UI layout. Resources created (all idempotent — existing resources with the same name are reused): VPC: <roks_vpc_name> Public gateways: <roks_vpc_name>-pgw-<region>-1/2/3 Subnets: <roks_vpc_name>-subnet-<region>-1/2/3 (256 IPs each, gateway attached inline) COS instance: <roks_vpc_name>-cos (Standard plan, premium-global-deployment ) Outputs printed at completion for use with cluster_type=roks-vpc : ROKS_VPC_ID ROKS_SUBNET_ID (one per zone) ROKS_COS_INSTANCE_CRN roks_vpc_name ¤ Base name applied to the new VPC and all of its associated resources: VPC ( <name> ), subnets ( <name>-subnet-<region>-<n> ), public gateways ( <name>-pgw-<region>-<n> ), and COS instance ( <name>-cos ). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_VPC_NAME Default: cluster_name All resources are created idempotently — existing resources with the same name are reused. With cluster_type=roks-vpc , set this to the name used during roks-vpc-setup and the provider automatically resolves roks_vpc_id , roks_subnet_id , and roks_cos_instance_crn by name (see ROKS VPC ); providing any of those directly overrides the lookup. ROKS VPC ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = roks-vpc . Also uses ibmcloud_apikey , ibmcloud_endpoint , ibmcloud_resourcegroup , ibmcloud_region , roks_zone , roks_flavor , roks_workers , and roks_flags . Note : roks_zone must use VPC zone format (e.g. us-south-1 , eu-de-2 ). roks_vpc_name (see ROKS VPC Setup ) is used as the basis for the name-based lookups described below. roks_vpc_id ¤ IBM Cloud VPC ID — overrides the name-based lookup when provided, for example r006-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx . Optional (if roks_vpc_name is provided) Environment Variable: ROKS_VPC_ID Default: None Use when the VPC was not created by roks-vpc-setup or when the name-based lookup is not suitable; otherwise the VPC is looked up by roks_vpc_name . roks_subnet_id ¤ ID of the VPC subnet to place worker nodes into — for example 0717-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx . Optional (resolved automatically from roks_vpc_id + roks_zone if not provided) Environment Variable: ROKS_SUBNET_ID Default: None When not provided, the subnet is resolved automatically by finding the subnet in the VPC whose zone matches roks_zone . This works correctly when the VPC was created by roks-vpc-setup , which creates exactly one subnet per zone; provide directly to override. roks_cos_instance_crn ¤ CRN of the IBM Cloud Object Storage instance — for example crn:v1:bluemix:public:cloud-object-storage:global:a/...:: — used because VPC-based ROKS clusters store the internal OpenShift image registry in COS. Optional (resolved automatically from <roks_vpc_name>-cos if not provided) Environment Variable: ROKS_COS_INSTANCE_CRN Default: None When not provided, the CRN is looked up from the COS instance named <roks_vpc_name>-cos in the resource group; provide directly to override. roks_secondary_storage ¤ Optional secondary block storage for VPC worker nodes — for example 300gb.5iops-tier — attached to each worker node at provision time, providing additional ephemeral storage capacity beyond the 100GB boot disk. Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_SECONDARY_STORAGE Default: '' Run ibmcloud ks flavor get --provider vpc-gen2 --zone <zone> --flavor <flavor> to list the available secondary storage configurations for your flavor. ROSA ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = rosa . rosa_token ¤ Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) authentication token, obtained from OpenShift Cluster Manager — required for all ROSA cluster operations. Required (when cluster_type=rosa ) Environment Variable: ROSA_TOKEN Default: None The token must be valid and have permissions to create clusters; without it ROSA cluster provisioning will fail. Tokens expire periodically — obtain a fresh token before provisioning and keep it secure. rosa_cluster_admin_password ¤ Password for the cluster-admin user account on the ROSA cluster — a string meeting OpenShift password requirements (typically 8+ characters). Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_CLUSTER_ADMIN_PASSWORD Default: None (auto-generated) When unset, a secure password is auto-generated and saved to the rosa config file in rosa_config_dir . Consider using auto-generation for better security. rosa_compute_nodes ¤ Number of compute (worker) nodes in the ROSA cluster — a positive integer (minimum 2; 3 or more recommended for production high availability). Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_COMPUTE_NODES Default: 3 Total cluster capacity = node count x rosa_compute_machine_type resources. More nodes provide more capacity and better high availability but increase AWS costs. rosa_compute_machine_type ¤ AWS EC2 instance type for ROSA worker nodes — for example m5.2xlarge (development/testing), m5.4xlarge (default, 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM, suitable for most MAS deployments), m5.8xlarge , or m5.12xlarge (larger workloads). Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_COMPUTE_MACHINE_TYPE Default: m5.4xlarge Verify instance type availability in your AWS region. rosa_config_dir ¤ Directory for storing ROSA cluster configuration files — an absolute filesystem path such as /tmp/rosa-config or ~/rosa-clusters . Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_CONFIG_DIR Default: '' When set, cluster details (API endpoint, credentials) are saved to rosa-{{cluster_name}}-details.yaml in this directory, including the auto-generated rosa_cluster_admin_password if one was not specified; when unset, configuration files are not saved and details must be retrieved manually. Warning The config file contains sensitive information (the cluster-admin password). Ensure the directory has appropriate permissions. Fyre ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = fyre . Fyre is an internal IBM development platform — access requires IBM credentials and appropriate permissions. fyre_username ¤ Fyre username for authentication with the IBM DevIT Fyre API — a valid Fyre username (IBM intranet ID). Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_USERNAME Default: None Paired with fyre_password ; without valid credentials Fyre cluster provisioning will fail. fyre_password ¤ Fyre API key for authentication with the Fyre API, paired with fyre_username — obtained from the Fyre portal. Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_APIKEY Default: None Without a valid API key Fyre cluster provisioning will fail. Keys may expire and need renewal — keep them secure and rotate regularly. fyre_quota_type ¤ Type of Fyre quota to use for cluster provisioning, which determines the billing method and required sizing variables — quick_burn (pre-defined cluster sizes, faster and simpler; requires fyre_cluster_size ) or product_group (custom sizing with more control; requires fyre_worker_count , fyre_worker_cpu , and fyre_worker_memory ). Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_QUOTA_TYPE Default: quick_burn fyre_product_id ¤ Product ID for internal IBM accounting and cost tracking — cluster costs are charged to this product ID, so an incorrect ID may cause provisioning to fail or incorrect billing. Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_PRODUCT_ID Default: None Required for both quota types; obtain the correct ID for your project from your IBM product team or manager. fyre_site ¤ Fyre datacenter site to provision the cluster in — a valid Fyre site code such as svl (San Jose/Silicon Valley, default and most commonly used), rtp , or raleigh . Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_SITE Default: svl The site determines cluster location, which affects network latency and available resources — not all sites support all features (see ocp_enable_ipv6 ). cluster_platform ¤ Fyre platform type for the cluster, passed as the platform field in the Fyre API request. Optional Environment Variable: CLUSTER_PLATFORM Default: x fyre_cluster_description ¤ Human-readable description for the Fyre cluster, shown in the Fyre portal — any descriptive string (e.g. "MAS 9.0 testing", "Development cluster"). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_CLUSTER_DESCRIPTION Default: No description provided No functional impact on the cluster; useful for tracking and managing multiple clusters (include purpose, owner, or project information). fyre_cluster_size ¤ Pre-defined Fyre cluster size to use when provisioning with quick_burn quota — for example small (minimal testing), medium (standard development/testing), or large (more intensive workloads). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=quick_burn ) Environment Variable: FYRE_CLUSTER_SIZE Default: medium Quick burn sizes are pre-defined by Fyre and individual resources cannot be customized — for custom sizing use fyre_quota_type=product_group instead. fyre_worker_count ¤ Number of worker nodes to provision when using product_group quota with custom sizing — a positive integer (typically 2-10; use 2+ for development/testing and 3+ for high availability testing). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=product_group ) Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_COUNT Default: 2 More workers provide more resources but consume more quota; total cluster capacity = worker count x per-worker resources. fyre_worker_cpu ¤ CPU cores to assign to each worker node when using product_group quota — a positive integer, maximum 16 (Fyre limit). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=product_group ) Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_CPU Default: 8 Total cluster CPUs = fyre_worker_count x CPU per worker. fyre_worker_memory ¤ Memory in GB to assign to each worker node when using product_group quota — a positive integer, maximum 64 (Fyre limit). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=product_group ) Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_MEMORY Default: 32 Total cluster memory = fyre_worker_count x memory per worker. fyre_worker_additional_disks ¤ Additional disks to attach to every worker node — a comma-separated list of disk sizes in GB (e.g. 400 , 400,400 , 200,300,400 ). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_ADDITIONAL_DISKS Default: None For example 400,400 adds two 400GB disks to each worker; total additional storage = disk sizes x fyre_worker_count . Useful for testing storage configurations or providing extra capacity. fyre_worker_base_disk ¤ Base disk size in GB for each worker node when using product_group quota — an integer between 40 and 500 (Fyre API limits). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_BASE_DISK Default: None When unset, the Fyre API default (250 GB per worker) applies. Reducing this can significantly save disk quota on development and test clusters — for example a 4-worker cluster defaults to at least 1000 GB of worker base disks. fyre_master_base_disk ¤ Base disk size in GB for each master node when using product_group quota — an integer between 40 and 500 (Fyre API limits). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_MASTER_BASE_DISK Default: None When unset, the Fyre API default (100 GB per master) applies. As with fyre_worker_base_disk , reducing this saves disk quota on development and test clusters. fyre_nfs_image_registry_size ¤ Size of NFS storage allocated for the OpenShift image registry when NFS storage is configured on Fyre clusters — a Kubernetes storage size such as 50Gi , 100Gi , or 200Gi . Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_NFS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_SIZE Default: 100Gi Only applies when ocp_storage_provider is nfs . The size is limited by available storage on the Fyre infrastructure node; the image registry stores all container images used in the cluster, so increase for clusters with many container images. ocp_enable_ipv6 ¤ Whether to enable IPv6 networking for the Fyre cluster — set to true for IPv6 testing. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ENABLE_IPV6 Default: false Warning IPv6 is only supported at the RTP (Raleigh) Fyre site ( fyre_site must be rtp ) — it will fail at other sites. IPI ¤ These variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi . Note IPI stands for Installer Provisioned Infrastructure . OpenShift offers two possible deployment methods: IPI and UPI (User Provisioned Infrastructure). The difference is the degree of automation and customization. IPI will not only deploy OpenShift but also all infrastructure components and configurations. ipi_platform ¤ Cloud platform for the IPI deployment — aws (default, tested and supported) or gcp ; other platforms supported by openshift-install may work but are untested. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_PLATFORM Default: aws Determines which cloud provider is used and which provider-specific variables are required: aws requires aws_access_key_id / aws_secret_access_key ; gcp requires gcp_service_account_file and ipi_gcp_projectid . ipi_region ¤ Cloud platform region where the IPI cluster will be deployed — a region valid for the selected platform, such as us-east-1 , us-west-2 , or eu-west-1 for AWS. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_REGION Default: us-east-1 The region determines cluster location, which affects latency, data residency, and service availability — verify that your target region supports the required instance types. ipi_base_domain ¤ Base DNS domain for the OpenShift cluster — a domain you control, such as example.com or ocp.mycompany.com . Required (when cluster_type=ipi ) Environment Variable: IPI_BASE_DOMAIN Default: None Cluster URLs will be subdomains of this base domain (e.g. api.clustername.example.com ). The openshift-install process creates DNS records in this domain, so you must have control over it and the ability to configure DNS. ipi_pull_secret_file ¤ Path to the file containing your Red Hat OpenShift pull secret (required to pull OpenShift container images during installation) — an absolute path to the pull secret JSON file, downloaded from the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console . Required (when cluster_type=ipi ) Environment Variable: IPI_PULL_SECRET_FILE Default: None Must be a valid, non-expired pull secret; without one cluster installation fails when attempting to pull container images. Keep the file secure — it contains authentication credentials. ipi_dir ¤ Working directory for the IPI installation process — an absolute filesystem path containing the openshift-install executable, configuration files, and generated logs. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_DIR Default: ~/openshift-install cluster_name is used in the subdirectory structure beneath this directory. The directory contains sensitive information (kubeconfig, credentials) — ensure appropriate permissions and preserve it for cluster management and troubleshooting. sshKey ¤ Public SSH key to install on all cluster nodes, enabling SSH access via bastion host for troubleshooting — a valid SSH public key string such as ssh-rsa AAAAB3... . Optional Environment Variable: SSH_PUB_KEY Default: '' SSH access to nodes is typically not needed for normal operations of managed clusters; only set this if you need direct node access for debugging or advanced cluster management. ipi_controlplane_type ¤ Machine type for control plane (master) nodes — a machine type valid for the selected platform, such as m5.2xlarge , m5.4xlarge (default, 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM), or m5.8xlarge for AWS. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_CONTROLPLANE_TYPE Default: m5.4xlarge Control plane nodes run cluster management services — an undersized control plane can impact cluster stability, so do not undersize for production. See also ipi_controlplane_replicas . ipi_controlplane_replicas ¤ Number of control plane (master) nodes to provision — an odd positive integer (1, 3, 5, 7) as required for etcd quorum; 3 is recommended for production. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_CONTROLPLANE_REPLICAS Default: 3 Warning Must be an odd number for etcd quorum. Using 1 provides no high availability — use 3 for production. ipi_compute_type ¤ Machine type for compute (worker) nodes — a machine type valid for the selected platform, such as m5.2xlarge (development/testing), m5.4xlarge (default, 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM, suitable for most MAS deployments), m5.8xlarge , or m5.12xlarge (larger workloads) for AWS. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_COMPUTE_TYPE Default: m5.4xlarge Consider total cluster capacity (type x ipi_compute_replicas ) when choosing. ipi_compute_replicas ¤ Number of compute (worker) nodes to provision — a positive integer (minimum 2; 3 or more recommended for production high availability). Optional Environment Variable: IPI_COMPUTE_REPLICAS Default: 3 Total cluster capacity = worker count x ipi_compute_type resources. ipi_rootvolume_size ¤ Root volume size in GiB for cluster nodes — a positive integer such as 120 , 200 , or 500 , covering the OS, container images, and ephemeral storage. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_ROOTVOLUME_SIZE Default: Platform default (typically 120GB) Platform defaults are typically sufficient — only increase for clusters with many container images or workloads with high ephemeral storage needs. Insufficient space can cause node issues. AWS ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi and ipi_platform = aws . aws_access_key_id ¤ AWS access key ID for authentication — a string of typically 20 characters starting with AKIA , associated with an IAM user or role. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=aws ) Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None The IAM user/role must have extensive permissions (VPC, EC2, ELB, Route53, IAM, etc.) to create the cluster infrastructure — consider using a dedicated IAM user for cluster provisioning. aws_secret_access_key ¤ AWS secret access key for authentication, paired with aws_access_key_id — a string of typically 40 characters. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=aws ) Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Warning Keep secret keys secure. Never commit them to version control — use environment variables or secure vaults, and rotate keys regularly. GCP ¤ The following variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi and ipi_platform = gcp . gcp_service_account_file ¤ Path to the GCP service account credentials file — an absolute path to a service account JSON key file, downloaded from GCP IAM. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=gcp ) Environment Variable: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS Default: None The service account must have extensive permissions (Compute, Networking, IAM, etc.) to create instances and networking resources; keep the file secure. ipi_gcp_projectid ¤ GCP project where the IPI cluster will be deployed — a valid, existing GCP project ID. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=gcp ) Environment Variable: GOOGLE_PROJECTID Default: None All cluster resources are created in, and costs billed to, this project. The project must exist before provisioning and gcp_service_account_file must have permissions in it. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: cluster_type: roks cluster_name: mycluster ocp_version: 4.10 ibmcloud_apikey: xxxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_provision License ¤ EPL-2.0
docs.title: ocp_provision

docs.text: Provision OCP cluster on IBM Cloud ROKS, ROSA, or DevIT Fyre. Fyre clusters will be automatically reconfigured to enable NFS storage. By default this is made available via the nfs-client storage class and supports both ReadWriteOnce and ReadWriteMany access modes. The image-registry-storage PVC used by the OpenShift image registry component will also be reconfigured to use this storage class.
docs.title: ocp_provision

docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Infrastructure provider type for cluster provisioning — one of fyre (IBM DevIT Fyre, internal development), roks (IBM Cloud ROKS classic infrastructure), roks-vpc (IBM Cloud ROKS on VPC infrastructure — modern, recommended; requires an existing VPC), roks-vpc-setup (creates a VPC, subnet, and public gateway — run this first, then use the output IDs with roks-vpc ), rosa (Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS), or ipi (Installer-Provisioned Infrastructure, bare metal/on-premises). Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_TYPE Default: None Determines the provisioning workflow and which provider-specific variables are required. Each type has different capabilities — for example GPU support is only available on roks and roks-vpc .
docs.title: cluster_type

docs.text: Name for the new cluster, used as the cluster identifier in the provider's system — must be unique within the provider's account/region and follow provider naming conventions (typically lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens; some providers impose length limits or character restrictions). Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Used for DNS, resource naming, and cluster identification.
docs.title: cluster_name

docs.text: OpenShift version to install — a specific version (e.g. 4.22 , 4.22.2 ), the alias default (newest MAS-supported version), or the alias rotate (predetermined version by day of week, for testing only). Required Environment Variable: OCP_VERSION Default: None The version must be compatible with MAS and available from the provider. Warning For ROKS ( cluster_type=roks ), the version must append the _openshift suffix — for example 4.22_openshift or 4.22.13_openshift .
docs.title: ocp_version

docs.text: Whether to provision the cluster with FIPS (Federal Information Processing Standards) 140-2 cryptographic mode enabled — set to true for government or regulated environments that require FIPS 140-2 compliance. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_FIPS_ENABLED Default: false Applies to fyre and ipi cluster types. FIPS mode may impact performance and cannot be changed after cluster creation — only enable it if required for compliance.
docs.title: ocp_fips_enabled

docs.text: Storage provider configuration for Fyre clusters — set to nfs to enable NFS storage; only applies when cluster_type=fyre , leave unset for other cluster types (ROKS, ROSA, IPI). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_STORAGE_PROVIDER Default: None When set to nfs , an nfs-client storage class supporting both ReadWriteOnce (RWO) and ReadWriteMany (RWX) access modes is created connected to the Fyre infrastructure node, and the existing image registry PVC is deleted and recreated with NFS storage. See also fyre_nfs_image_registry_size .
docs.title: ocp_storage_provider

docs.text: GPU worker pools are supported on roks (classic) and roks-vpc (VPC) cluster types only.
docs.title: GPU Node Support

docs.text: Whether to provision GPU-enabled worker nodes with the cluster — required for GPU-intensive workloads such as MAS Visual Inspection (MVI). Optional Environment Variable: OCP_PROVISION_GPU Default: false When true , a GPU worker pool is provisioned with gpu_workers nodes. On classic ROKS ( roks ) the GPU flavor is hardcoded to mg4c.32x384.2xp100 ; on VPC ROKS ( roks-vpc ) set gpu_flavor explicitly.
docs.title: ocp_provision_gpu

docs.text: Name for the GPU worker pool — use the default ( gpu ) for new GPU deployments, or set to an existing pool name to modify that pool rather than create a duplicate. Optional Environment Variable: GPU_WORKERPOOL_NAME Default: gpu Only applies when ocp_provision_gpu is true . If a GPU worker pool already exists with this name, it will be modified rather than a second pool created.
docs.title: gpu_workerpool_name

docs.text: Number of GPU-enabled worker nodes to provision in the GPU worker pool — a positive integer (e.g. 1 , 2 , 3 ). Optional Environment Variable: GPU_WORKERS Default: 1 Use the default (1) for minimal GPU deployments or testing; increase for production MAS Visual Inspection deployments. GPU nodes use expensive hardware — only provision what you need.
docs.title: gpu_workers

docs.text: GPU-enabled machine type for the GPU worker pool when using cluster_type=roks-vpc — for example gx2.8x64.v100 (8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 1x V100 GPU, default) or gx2.16x128.2v100 (16 vCPU, 128 GB RAM, 2x V100 GPUs). Optional Environment Variable: GPU_FLAVOR Default: gx2.8x64.v100 Only applies when ocp_provision_gpu is true and cluster_type=roks-vpc ; on classic ROKS ( roks ) the GPU flavor is hardcoded to mg4c.32x384.2xp100 and this variable is ignored. Tip GPU flavor availability varies by zone — verify availability before deploying with ibmcloud oc flavors --zone <zone> --provider vpc-gen2 | grep gpu .
docs.title: gpu_flavor

docs.text: The following variables are only used when cluster_type is roks , roks-vpc , or roks-vpc-setup (unless noted otherwise).
docs.title: ROKS

docs.text: IBM Cloud API key for authentication, used by the ibmcloud CLI for all cluster operations — obtain it from IBM Cloud IAM (Identity and Access Management). Required (when cluster_type is roks , roks-vpc , or roks-vpc-setup ) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None The key must have cluster creation permissions in the target resource group ( ibmcloud_resourcegroup ). Keep API keys secure — use environment variables or secure vaults rather than hardcoding them in playbooks.
docs.title: ibmcloud_apikey

docs.text: IBM Cloud API endpoint URL for authentication and cluster operations — override the default only for IBM Cloud dedicated or private environments, or for testing against staging environments. Optional Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_ENDPOINT Default: https://cloud.ibm.com Determines which IBM Cloud environment is targeted for cluster provisioning. Used together with ibmcloud_apikey .
docs.title: ibmcloud_endpoint

docs.text: IBM Cloud resource group in which the ROKS cluster will be created — the group must exist before provisioning and ibmcloud_apikey must have permissions in it. Optional Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_RESOURCEGROUP Default: Default Use the default for simple deployments; specify a different existing resource group for organizational separation.
docs.title: ibmcloud_resourcegroup

docs.text: IBM Cloud region targeted when running VPC Infrastructure Service ( ibmcloud is ) commands — a valid region identifier such as us-south , eu-de , eu-gb , jp-tok , or au-syd . Required (when cluster_type=roks-vpc-setup ) Optional (when cluster_type=roks-vpc — auto-derived from the VPC CRN or from roks_zone ) Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_REGION Default: None For roks-vpc-setup this must be provided explicitly, as it determines where all resources are created. For roks-vpc the region is resolved automatically in this order: roks_zone stripped of its zone suffix (e.g. eu-gb-1 → eu-gb ), then the VPC's CRN extracted during the VPC name lookup (which overrides the zone-derived value if different) — an explicitly set ibmcloud_region always wins.
docs.title: ibmcloud_region

docs.text: IBM Cloud availability zone where the ROKS cluster will be provisioned — classic format for roks ( dal10 , lon02 , fra02 , tok02 ) or VPC format for roks-vpc ( us-south-1 , eu-de-2 , eu-gb-3 , jp-tok-1 — always <region>-<n> ). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_ZONE Default: dal10 The zone determines cluster location, which affects latency, data residency, and available services. For roks-vpc the zone must be within ibmcloud_region (e.g. region us-south → zone us-south-1 ), and not all roks_flavor values are available in all zones — verify availability in your target zone.
docs.title: roks_zone

docs.text: Worker node machine type (flavor) for the ROKS cluster — classic flavors for roks (e.g. b3c.4x16 , b3c.16x64.300gb , b3c.32x128 ) or VPC flavors for roks-vpc (e.g. bx2.4x16 , bx2.16x64 , bx2.48x192 ). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_FLAVOR Default: b3c.16x64.300gb The default (16 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 300 GB storage) suits standard MAS deployments on classic ROKS. Larger flavors cost more but provide more resources. Warning The default is a classic flavor and will fail if used with roks-vpc . Always set an appropriate bx2.* VPC flavor when using cluster_type=roks-vpc — check availability with ibmcloud oc flavors --zone <zone> --provider vpc-gen2 .
docs.title: roks_flavor

docs.text: Number of worker nodes to provision in the ROKS cluster — a positive integer (minimum 1; 3 or more recommended for production high availability). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_WORKERS Default: 3 Total cluster capacity = worker count x roks_flavor resources. More workers provide more capacity and better high availability but increase costs; GPU workers can be added separately via ocp_provision_gpu .
docs.title: roks_workers

docs.text: Additional command-line flags passed to the ibmcloud ks cluster create command — for example --disable-public-service-endpoint , --pod-subnet , or --service-subnet . Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_FLAGS Default: '' Use for advanced configurations not covered by the other ROKS variables; consult the IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service documentation for available flags. Warning Use with caution — incorrect flags can cause provisioning failures.
docs.title: roks_flags

docs.text: The following variables are only used when cluster_type = roks-vpc-setup . Run this provider first to create the VPC infrastructure, then pass the output IDs to cluster_type=roks-vpc . Also uses ibmcloud_apikey , ibmcloud_endpoint , ibmcloud_resourcegroup , and ibmcloud_region . Note : Does not require ocp_version or roks_zone . Subnets are always created in all three zones of ibmcloud_region ( <region>-1 , <region>-2 , <region>-3 ), matching the default IBM Cloud UI layout. Resources created (all idempotent — existing resources with the same name are reused): VPC: <roks_vpc_name> Public gateways: <roks_vpc_name>-pgw-<region>-1/2/3 Subnets: <roks_vpc_name>-subnet-<region>-1/2/3 (256 IPs each, gateway attached inline) COS instance: <roks_vpc_name>-cos (Standard plan, premium-global-deployment ) Outputs printed at completion for use with cluster_type=roks-vpc : ROKS_VPC_ID ROKS_SUBNET_ID (one per zone) ROKS_COS_INSTANCE_CRN
docs.title: ROKS VPC Setup

docs.text: Base name applied to the new VPC and all of its associated resources: VPC ( <name> ), subnets ( <name>-subnet-<region>-<n> ), public gateways ( <name>-pgw-<region>-<n> ), and COS instance ( <name>-cos ). Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_VPC_NAME Default: cluster_name All resources are created idempotently — existing resources with the same name are reused. With cluster_type=roks-vpc , set this to the name used during roks-vpc-setup and the provider automatically resolves roks_vpc_id , roks_subnet_id , and roks_cos_instance_crn by name (see ROKS VPC ); providing any of those directly overrides the lookup.
docs.title: roks_vpc_name

docs.text: The following variables are only used when cluster_type = roks-vpc . Also uses ibmcloud_apikey , ibmcloud_endpoint , ibmcloud_resourcegroup , ibmcloud_region , roks_zone , roks_flavor , roks_workers , and roks_flags . Note : roks_zone must use VPC zone format (e.g. us-south-1 , eu-de-2 ). roks_vpc_name (see ROKS VPC Setup ) is used as the basis for the name-based lookups described below.
docs.title: ROKS VPC

docs.text: IBM Cloud VPC ID — overrides the name-based lookup when provided, for example r006-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx . Optional (if roks_vpc_name is provided) Environment Variable: ROKS_VPC_ID Default: None Use when the VPC was not created by roks-vpc-setup or when the name-based lookup is not suitable; otherwise the VPC is looked up by roks_vpc_name .
docs.title: roks_vpc_id

docs.text: ID of the VPC subnet to place worker nodes into — for example 0717-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx . Optional (resolved automatically from roks_vpc_id + roks_zone if not provided) Environment Variable: ROKS_SUBNET_ID Default: None When not provided, the subnet is resolved automatically by finding the subnet in the VPC whose zone matches roks_zone . This works correctly when the VPC was created by roks-vpc-setup , which creates exactly one subnet per zone; provide directly to override.
docs.title: roks_subnet_id

docs.text: CRN of the IBM Cloud Object Storage instance — for example crn:v1:bluemix:public:cloud-object-storage:global:a/...:: — used because VPC-based ROKS clusters store the internal OpenShift image registry in COS. Optional (resolved automatically from <roks_vpc_name>-cos if not provided) Environment Variable: ROKS_COS_INSTANCE_CRN Default: None When not provided, the CRN is looked up from the COS instance named <roks_vpc_name>-cos in the resource group; provide directly to override.
docs.title: roks_cos_instance_crn

docs.text: Optional secondary block storage for VPC worker nodes — for example 300gb.5iops-tier — attached to each worker node at provision time, providing additional ephemeral storage capacity beyond the 100GB boot disk. Optional Environment Variable: ROKS_SECONDARY_STORAGE Default: '' Run ibmcloud ks flavor get --provider vpc-gen2 --zone <zone> --flavor <flavor> to list the available secondary storage configurations for your flavor.
docs.title: roks_secondary_storage

docs.text: The following variables are only used when cluster_type = rosa .
docs.title: ROSA

docs.text: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) authentication token, obtained from OpenShift Cluster Manager — required for all ROSA cluster operations. Required (when cluster_type=rosa ) Environment Variable: ROSA_TOKEN Default: None The token must be valid and have permissions to create clusters; without it ROSA cluster provisioning will fail. Tokens expire periodically — obtain a fresh token before provisioning and keep it secure.
docs.title: rosa_token

docs.text: Password for the cluster-admin user account on the ROSA cluster — a string meeting OpenShift password requirements (typically 8+ characters). Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_CLUSTER_ADMIN_PASSWORD Default: None (auto-generated) When unset, a secure password is auto-generated and saved to the rosa config file in rosa_config_dir . Consider using auto-generation for better security.
docs.title: rosa_cluster_admin_password

docs.text: Number of compute (worker) nodes in the ROSA cluster — a positive integer (minimum 2; 3 or more recommended for production high availability). Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_COMPUTE_NODES Default: 3 Total cluster capacity = node count x rosa_compute_machine_type resources. More nodes provide more capacity and better high availability but increase AWS costs.
docs.title: rosa_compute_nodes

docs.text: AWS EC2 instance type for ROSA worker nodes — for example m5.2xlarge (development/testing), m5.4xlarge (default, 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM, suitable for most MAS deployments), m5.8xlarge , or m5.12xlarge (larger workloads). Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_COMPUTE_MACHINE_TYPE Default: m5.4xlarge Verify instance type availability in your AWS region.
docs.title: rosa_compute_machine_type

docs.text: Directory for storing ROSA cluster configuration files — an absolute filesystem path such as /tmp/rosa-config or ~/rosa-clusters . Optional Environment Variable: ROSA_CONFIG_DIR Default: '' When set, cluster details (API endpoint, credentials) are saved to rosa-{{cluster_name}}-details.yaml in this directory, including the auto-generated rosa_cluster_admin_password if one was not specified; when unset, configuration files are not saved and details must be retrieved manually. Warning The config file contains sensitive information (the cluster-admin password). Ensure the directory has appropriate permissions.
docs.title: rosa_config_dir

docs.text: The following variables are only used when cluster_type = fyre . Fyre is an internal IBM development platform — access requires IBM credentials and appropriate permissions.
docs.title: Fyre

docs.text: Fyre username for authentication with the IBM DevIT Fyre API — a valid Fyre username (IBM intranet ID). Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_USERNAME Default: None Paired with fyre_password ; without valid credentials Fyre cluster provisioning will fail.
docs.title: fyre_username

docs.text: Fyre API key for authentication with the Fyre API, paired with fyre_username — obtained from the Fyre portal. Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_APIKEY Default: None Without a valid API key Fyre cluster provisioning will fail. Keys may expire and need renewal — keep them secure and rotate regularly.
docs.title: fyre_password

docs.text: Type of Fyre quota to use for cluster provisioning, which determines the billing method and required sizing variables — quick_burn (pre-defined cluster sizes, faster and simpler; requires fyre_cluster_size ) or product_group (custom sizing with more control; requires fyre_worker_count , fyre_worker_cpu , and fyre_worker_memory ). Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_QUOTA_TYPE Default: quick_burn
docs.title: fyre_quota_type

docs.text: Product ID for internal IBM accounting and cost tracking — cluster costs are charged to this product ID, so an incorrect ID may cause provisioning to fail or incorrect billing. Required (when cluster_type=fyre ) Environment Variable: FYRE_PRODUCT_ID Default: None Required for both quota types; obtain the correct ID for your project from your IBM product team or manager.
docs.title: fyre_product_id

docs.text: Fyre datacenter site to provision the cluster in — a valid Fyre site code such as svl (San Jose/Silicon Valley, default and most commonly used), rtp , or raleigh . Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_SITE Default: svl The site determines cluster location, which affects network latency and available resources — not all sites support all features (see ocp_enable_ipv6 ).
docs.title: fyre_site

docs.text: Fyre platform type for the cluster, passed as the platform field in the Fyre API request. Optional Environment Variable: CLUSTER_PLATFORM Default: x
docs.title: cluster_platform

docs.text: Human-readable description for the Fyre cluster, shown in the Fyre portal — any descriptive string (e.g. "MAS 9.0 testing", "Development cluster"). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_CLUSTER_DESCRIPTION Default: No description provided No functional impact on the cluster; useful for tracking and managing multiple clusters (include purpose, owner, or project information).
docs.title: fyre_cluster_description

docs.text: Pre-defined Fyre cluster size to use when provisioning with quick_burn quota — for example small (minimal testing), medium (standard development/testing), or large (more intensive workloads). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=quick_burn ) Environment Variable: FYRE_CLUSTER_SIZE Default: medium Quick burn sizes are pre-defined by Fyre and individual resources cannot be customized — for custom sizing use fyre_quota_type=product_group instead.
docs.title: fyre_cluster_size

docs.text: Number of worker nodes to provision when using product_group quota with custom sizing — a positive integer (typically 2-10; use 2+ for development/testing and 3+ for high availability testing). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=product_group ) Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_COUNT Default: 2 More workers provide more resources but consume more quota; total cluster capacity = worker count x per-worker resources.
docs.title: fyre_worker_count

docs.text: CPU cores to assign to each worker node when using product_group quota — a positive integer, maximum 16 (Fyre limit). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=product_group ) Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_CPU Default: 8 Total cluster CPUs = fyre_worker_count x CPU per worker.
docs.title: fyre_worker_cpu

docs.text: Memory in GB to assign to each worker node when using product_group quota — a positive integer, maximum 64 (Fyre limit). Required (when cluster_type=fyre and fyre_quota_type=product_group ) Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_MEMORY Default: 32 Total cluster memory = fyre_worker_count x memory per worker.
docs.title: fyre_worker_memory

docs.text: Additional disks to attach to every worker node — a comma-separated list of disk sizes in GB (e.g. 400 , 400,400 , 200,300,400 ). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_ADDITIONAL_DISKS Default: None For example 400,400 adds two 400GB disks to each worker; total additional storage = disk sizes x fyre_worker_count . Useful for testing storage configurations or providing extra capacity.
docs.title: fyre_worker_additional_disks

docs.text: Base disk size in GB for each worker node when using product_group quota — an integer between 40 and 500 (Fyre API limits). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_WORKER_BASE_DISK Default: None When unset, the Fyre API default (250 GB per worker) applies. Reducing this can significantly save disk quota on development and test clusters — for example a 4-worker cluster defaults to at least 1000 GB of worker base disks.
docs.title: fyre_worker_base_disk

docs.text: Base disk size in GB for each master node when using product_group quota — an integer between 40 and 500 (Fyre API limits). Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_MASTER_BASE_DISK Default: None When unset, the Fyre API default (100 GB per master) applies. As with fyre_worker_base_disk , reducing this saves disk quota on development and test clusters.
docs.title: fyre_master_base_disk

docs.text: Size of NFS storage allocated for the OpenShift image registry when NFS storage is configured on Fyre clusters — a Kubernetes storage size such as 50Gi , 100Gi , or 200Gi . Optional Environment Variable: FYRE_NFS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_SIZE Default: 100Gi Only applies when ocp_storage_provider is nfs . The size is limited by available storage on the Fyre infrastructure node; the image registry stores all container images used in the cluster, so increase for clusters with many container images.
docs.title: fyre_nfs_image_registry_size

docs.text: Whether to enable IPv6 networking for the Fyre cluster — set to true for IPv6 testing. Optional Environment Variable: OCP_ENABLE_IPV6 Default: false Warning IPv6 is only supported at the RTP (Raleigh) Fyre site ( fyre_site must be rtp ) — it will fail at other sites.
docs.title: ocp_enable_ipv6

docs.text: These variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi . Note IPI stands for Installer Provisioned Infrastructure . OpenShift offers two possible deployment methods: IPI and UPI (User Provisioned Infrastructure). The difference is the degree of automation and customization. IPI will not only deploy OpenShift but also all infrastructure components and configurations.
docs.title: IPI

docs.text: Cloud platform for the IPI deployment — aws (default, tested and supported) or gcp ; other platforms supported by openshift-install may work but are untested. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_PLATFORM Default: aws Determines which cloud provider is used and which provider-specific variables are required: aws requires aws_access_key_id / aws_secret_access_key ; gcp requires gcp_service_account_file and ipi_gcp_projectid .
docs.title: ipi_platform

docs.text: Cloud platform region where the IPI cluster will be deployed — a region valid for the selected platform, such as us-east-1 , us-west-2 , or eu-west-1 for AWS. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_REGION Default: us-east-1 The region determines cluster location, which affects latency, data residency, and service availability — verify that your target region supports the required instance types.
docs.title: ipi_region

docs.text: Base DNS domain for the OpenShift cluster — a domain you control, such as example.com or ocp.mycompany.com . Required (when cluster_type=ipi ) Environment Variable: IPI_BASE_DOMAIN Default: None Cluster URLs will be subdomains of this base domain (e.g. api.clustername.example.com ). The openshift-install process creates DNS records in this domain, so you must have control over it and the ability to configure DNS.
docs.title: ipi_base_domain

docs.text: Path to the file containing your Red Hat OpenShift pull secret (required to pull OpenShift container images during installation) — an absolute path to the pull secret JSON file, downloaded from the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console . Required (when cluster_type=ipi ) Environment Variable: IPI_PULL_SECRET_FILE Default: None Must be a valid, non-expired pull secret; without one cluster installation fails when attempting to pull container images. Keep the file secure — it contains authentication credentials.
docs.title: ipi_pull_secret_file

docs.text: Working directory for the IPI installation process — an absolute filesystem path containing the openshift-install executable, configuration files, and generated logs. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_DIR Default: ~/openshift-install cluster_name is used in the subdirectory structure beneath this directory. The directory contains sensitive information (kubeconfig, credentials) — ensure appropriate permissions and preserve it for cluster management and troubleshooting.
docs.title: ipi_dir

docs.text: Public SSH key to install on all cluster nodes, enabling SSH access via bastion host for troubleshooting — a valid SSH public key string such as ssh-rsa AAAAB3... . Optional Environment Variable: SSH_PUB_KEY Default: '' SSH access to nodes is typically not needed for normal operations of managed clusters; only set this if you need direct node access for debugging or advanced cluster management.
docs.title: sshKey

docs.text: Machine type for control plane (master) nodes — a machine type valid for the selected platform, such as m5.2xlarge , m5.4xlarge (default, 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM), or m5.8xlarge for AWS. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_CONTROLPLANE_TYPE Default: m5.4xlarge Control plane nodes run cluster management services — an undersized control plane can impact cluster stability, so do not undersize for production. See also ipi_controlplane_replicas .
docs.title: ipi_controlplane_type

docs.text: Number of control plane (master) nodes to provision — an odd positive integer (1, 3, 5, 7) as required for etcd quorum; 3 is recommended for production. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_CONTROLPLANE_REPLICAS Default: 3 Warning Must be an odd number for etcd quorum. Using 1 provides no high availability — use 3 for production.
docs.title: ipi_controlplane_replicas

docs.text: Machine type for compute (worker) nodes — a machine type valid for the selected platform, such as m5.2xlarge (development/testing), m5.4xlarge (default, 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM, suitable for most MAS deployments), m5.8xlarge , or m5.12xlarge (larger workloads) for AWS. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_COMPUTE_TYPE Default: m5.4xlarge Consider total cluster capacity (type x ipi_compute_replicas ) when choosing.
docs.title: ipi_compute_type

docs.text: Number of compute (worker) nodes to provision — a positive integer (minimum 2; 3 or more recommended for production high availability). Optional Environment Variable: IPI_COMPUTE_REPLICAS Default: 3 Total cluster capacity = worker count x ipi_compute_type resources.
docs.title: ipi_compute_replicas

docs.text: Root volume size in GiB for cluster nodes — a positive integer such as 120 , 200 , or 500 , covering the OS, container images, and ephemeral storage. Optional Environment Variable: IPI_ROOTVOLUME_SIZE Default: Platform default (typically 120GB) Platform defaults are typically sufficient — only increase for clusters with many container images or workloads with high ephemeral storage needs. Insufficient space can cause node issues.
docs.title: ipi_rootvolume_size

docs.text: The following variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi and ipi_platform = aws .
docs.title: AWS

docs.text: AWS access key ID for authentication — a string of typically 20 characters starting with AKIA , associated with an IAM user or role. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=aws ) Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None The IAM user/role must have extensive permissions (VPC, EC2, ELB, Route53, IAM, etc.) to create the cluster infrastructure — consider using a dedicated IAM user for cluster provisioning.
docs.title: aws_access_key_id

docs.text: AWS secret access key for authentication, paired with aws_access_key_id — a string of typically 40 characters. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=aws ) Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None Warning Keep secret keys secure. Never commit them to version control — use environment variables or secure vaults, and rotate keys regularly.
docs.title: aws_secret_access_key

docs.text: The following variables are only used when cluster_type = ipi and ipi_platform = gcp .
docs.title: GCP

docs.text: Path to the GCP service account credentials file — an absolute path to a service account JSON key file, downloaded from GCP IAM. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=gcp ) Environment Variable: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS Default: None The service account must have extensive permissions (Compute, Networking, IAM, etc.) to create instances and networking resources; keep the file secure.
docs.title: gcp_service_account_file

docs.text: GCP project where the IPI cluster will be deployed — a valid, existing GCP project ID. Required (when cluster_type=ipi and ipi_platform=gcp ) Environment Variable: GOOGLE_PROJECTID Default: None All cluster resources are created in, and costs billed to, this project. The project must exist before provisioning and gcp_service_account_file must have permissions in it.
docs.title: ipi_gcp_projectid

docs.text: ocp_roks_upgrade_registry_storage ¤ Upgrade the storage capacity of the OpenShift image registry for IBM Cloud Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Service (ROKS) clusters. This role uses IBM Cloud APIs to expand the persistent volume backing the internal image registry from the default 100GB to 400GB. The default 100GB registry storage is insufficient for comprehensive Cloud Pak for Data installations or environments with many container images; this role prevents the registry storage exhaustion that would block image pulls and deployments. Important This operation is specific to ROKS clusters on IBM Cloud and requires cluster downtime for the registry during the resize operation (typically 5-15 minutes). Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default ibmcloud_apikey Yes None image_registry_size No 400 IBM Cloud Access ¤ ibmcloud_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API key for authentication and volume management. Required Environment Variable: IBMCLOUD_APIKEY Default: None The key must have IAM permissions for Block Storage and Kubernetes Service, and access to the cluster's resource group. A service ID API key is recommended over a user API key; keys can be created in the IBM Cloud console under Manage > Access (IAM) > API keys. Registry Storage ¤ image_registry_size ¤ Target size for the image registry storage volume, in GB. Optional Environment Variable: None (hardcoded in defaults) Default: 400 Common values are 200 (minimal CP4D installation), 400 (default, suitable for full CP4D with multiple services), 600 (large deployments with many custom images), and 1000 (very large environments with extensive image catalogs). The volume can only be expanded, not shrunk; IBM Cloud charges based on provisioned capacity. Usage can be monitored with oc get pvc -n openshift-image-registry . Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_roks_tuning License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_simulate_disconnected_network ¤ Simulate an air-gapped/disconnected network environment for testing purposes by modifying DNS resolution on OpenShift cluster nodes. This role adds bogus entries to the /etc/hosts file on all nodes (workers and masters) to break DNS resolution for external container registries, forcing the cluster to use mirrored registries. Purpose : Enable testing of disconnected/air-gapped MAS installations without physically isolating the cluster from the network. The cluster can still access other network resources, but cannot reach the specified container registries. Important Notes : Primarily designed and tested for Fyre clusters May require modifications for other cluster providers Uses MachineConfig to modify node host files Changes persist across node reboots Verification : Check node hosts file: oc debug node/<node-name> sh-4.4# cat /host/etc/hosts Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default airgap_network_exclusions No 9 default registries (see below) registry_private_ca_file Conditional None registry_private_ca_crt No None machine_config_multiupdate No false registry_private_ca_file is only required when the private/mirrored registry uses self-signed or custom CA certificates. Network Isolation ¤ airgap_network_exclusions ¤ Space-separated list of container registry hostnames whose DNS resolution will be blocked to simulate disconnected network access. The default list covers the common registries used by MAS and OpenShift; customize it to add or remove registries based on your testing requirements. Optional Environment Variable: None (hardcoded in defaults) Default: quay.io registry.redhat.io registry.connect.redhat.com gcr.io nvcr.io icr.io cp.icr.io docker-na-public.artifactory.swg-devops.com docker-na-proxy-svl.artifactory.swg-devops.com docker-na-proxy-rtp.artifactory.swg-devops.com The default registries are quay.io (Red Hat Quay registry), registry.redhat.io (Red Hat Container Catalog), registry.connect.redhat.com (Red Hat Partner registry), gcr.io (Google Container Registry), nvcr.io (NVIDIA Container Registry), icr.io (IBM Cloud Container Registry, public), cp.icr.io (IBM Cloud Container Registry, entitled), and docker-na-public.artifactory.swg-devops.com , docker-na-proxy-svl.artifactory.swg-devops.com , docker-na-proxy-rtp.artifactory.swg-devops.com (IBM internal Artifactory and proxies). DNS resolution is blocked by adding bogus IP addresses to /etc/hosts ; the internal OpenShift image registry is not affected, and image pulls from the listed registries will fail unless mirrored registries are configured before blocking them. Private Registry Trust ¤ registry_private_ca_file ¤ Local file path to the private/mirrored registry CA certificate — an absolute or relative path to a valid PEM-encoded CA certificate file (e.g. /tmp/registry-ca.pem , ./certs/mirror-registry-ca.crt ). Required when using a private registry with self-signed or custom CA certificates Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PRIVATE_CA_FILE Default: None The file must be accessible from the Ansible controller. The certificate is added to the cluster's trusted certificate bundle, enabling nodes to trust the private registry; it is not needed if the registry uses publicly trusted certificates. registry_private_ca_crt ¤ Content of the private registry CA certificate, automatically loaded from registry_private_ca_file and used internally by the role — do not set it manually. Optional (derived from registry_private_ca_file ) Environment Variable: None (loaded from file) Default: None The PEM-encoded certificate content is embedded in a MachineConfig and distributed to all cluster nodes to configure node trust. MachineConfig Updates ¤ machine_config_multiupdate ¤ Whether multiple MachineConfig changes are applied together in a single operation or separately — true (apply together) or false (apply separately, the default). Optional Environment Variable: MACHINE_CONFIG_MULTIUPDATE Default: false MachineConfig changes trigger node reboots, which are required to apply host file changes. true reduces the number of node reboots, saving time in development environments, but increases risk if the configuration is incorrect; false causes more reboots but is safer for rollback and production-like testing. Monitor progress with oc get mcp . Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: # Add required variables here roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_simulate_disconnected_network License ¤ EPL-2.0
docs.title: ocp_simulate_disconnected_network

docs.text: ocp_upgrade ¤ This role supports the upgrade of the Openshift Cluster version for master and worker nodes in IBM Cloud provider. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default cluster_type Yes None cluster_name Yes None ocp_version_upgrade Yes None Upgrade Target ¤ cluster_type ¤ Cluster type for the upgrade operation. Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_TYPE Default: None The only supported value is roks (IBM Cloud Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Service); the role will fail for any other cluster type — use provider-specific upgrade procedures instead. cluster_name ¤ Name of the cluster to upgrade. Required Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Must exactly match an existing ROKS cluster name in your IBM Cloud account; verify the name before running the upgrade to avoid targeting the wrong cluster. ocp_version_upgrade ¤ Target OpenShift version for the upgrade, in ROKS version format with the _openshift suffix (e.g. 4.10_openshift , 4.11_openshift , 4.12_openshift ). Required Environment Variable: OCP_VERSION_UPGRADE Default: None Warning The version must be a supported upgrade path from the current version (check IBM Cloud documentation for available versions). Upgrades cannot be rolled back and cause temporary service disruption — plan for a maintenance window. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: cluster_name: my-ocp-cluster cluster_type: roks ocp_version_upgrade: 4.10_openshift roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_upgrade License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: ocp_verify ¤ This role will verify that the target OCP cluster is ready to be setup for MAS. For example, in IBMCloud ROKS we have seen delays of over an hour before the Red Hat Operator catalog is ready to use. This will cause attempts to install anything from that CatalogSource to fail as the timeouts built into the roles in this collection are designed to catch problems with an install, rather than a half-provisioned cluster that is not properly ready to use yet. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default verify_cluster No true verify_catalogsources No true verify_subscriptions No true verify_workloads No true verify_ingress No true cluster_name Conditional None ocp_ingress_tls_secret_name No router-certs-default cluster_name is only used when verify_ingress is true , and is only needed in specific cluster configurations. Verification Checks ¤ verify_cluster ¤ Enable cluster health verification — true to verify the cluster is healthy and ready by checking the ClusterVersion resource Ready condition, false to skip (default true ). Optional Environment Variable: VERIFY_CLUSTER Default: true Fails if the cluster is not ready within 1 hour. This check ensures the cluster is fully provisioned and ready; in some environments (e.g., IBMCloud ROKS), clusters may take time to become fully ready, and the 1-hour timeout accommodates typical provisioning delays. Recommended to keep enabled for production deployments. verify_catalogsources ¤ Enable catalog source health verification — true to verify that all installed OCP catalog sources are healthy and ready to provide operators, false to skip (default true ). Optional Environment Variable: VERIFY_CATALOGSOURCES Default: true Verifies that all CatalogSources report lastObservedState as READY , failing if not ready within 30 minutes. Catalog sources must be ready before operators can be installed — this check prevents operator installation failures due to unavailable catalogs, and the 30-minute timeout accommodates typical sync delays (e.g., on IBMCloud ROKS). verify_subscriptions ¤ Enable operator subscription verification — true to verify that all operator subscriptions are up to date and at their latest known version, false to skip (default true ). Optional Environment Variable: VERIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS Default: true Verifies that all Subscriptions report state as AtLatestKnown , failing if not ready within 2 hours — the timeout accommodates operator installation and upgrade processes, ensuring operators are properly installed and ready to manage resources. verify_workloads ¤ Enable workload deployment verification — true to verify that all deployments and statefulsets are fully rolled out, false to skip (default true ). Optional Environment Variable: VERIFY_WORKLOADS Default: true Verifies that all Deployments and StatefulSets have updatedReplicas and availableReplicas equal to replicas , failing if not ready within 3 hours. Workloads must be fully deployed before the cluster is ready for MAS installation; the timeout accommodates large-scale deployments and rolling updates. verify_ingress ¤ Enable ingress TLS certificate verification — true to verify that the cluster ingress TLS certificate can be obtained, false to skip (default true ). Optional Environment Variable: VERIFY_INGRESS Default: true Many roles in this collection require the cluster ingress certificate; this check ensures the certificate is accessible before proceeding with MAS installation. Ingress Certificate Lookup ¤ cluster_name ¤ Cluster name used to determine the default router certificate name in certain cluster configurations — a string matching your cluster name. Optional (only used when verify_ingress=true ) Environment Variable: CLUSTER_NAME Default: None Used to construct the ingress TLS secret name in cluster configurations where the secret name includes the cluster name. Only needed in specific configurations — most clusters use the default secret name and don't require this variable. ocp_ingress_tls_secret_name ¤ Name of the Kubernetes secret in the openshift-ingress namespace containing the cluster's default router certificate. Optional (only used when verify_ingress=true ) Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS_TLS_SECRET_NAME Default: router-certs-default The default router-certs-default works for most OCP clusters — only override it if your cluster uses a custom ingress certificate secret name; an incorrect name will cause verification to fail. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: verify_cluster: True verify_catalogsources: True verify_subscriptions: True verify_workloads: True verify_ingress: True roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocp_verify License ¤ EPL-2.0
