docs.text: ocs ¤ Install and configure OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) Operator, formerly known as OpenShift Container Storage (OCS), along with the Local Storage Operator (LSO) for persistent storage in OpenShift clusters. This role provides automated installation and upgrade of ODF/OCS with local storage backend. The role automatically detects the OpenShift version and installs the appropriate operator version. Version Detection ¤ OCP 4.10 and earlier : Installs OCS operator OCP 4.11 and later : Installs ODF operator Platform Limitations ¤ IBM Cloud ROKS Limitation Starting from OCP 4.8, IBM/Red Hat no longer support OCS/ODF installation via OperatorHub on IBM Cloud ROKS clusters. ROKS clusters are automatically provisioned with their own storage plugin. If you attempt to install ODF on ROKS via OperatorHub, you will encounter this error: "Failed to apply object: admission webhook 'validate.managed.openshift.io' denied the request: Installing OpenShift Data Foundation on IBM Cloud by using OperatorHub is not supported. You can install OpenShift Data Foundation by using the IBM Cloud add-on." For ROKS deployments, use the IBM Cloud add-on instead. Features ¤ Automatic Version Detection : Installs OCS or ODF based on OpenShift version Local Storage Integration : Configures Local Storage Operator for block storage Storage Cluster Setup : Creates and configures ODF/OCS storage cluster Upgrade Support : Can upgrade existing ODF/OCS installations Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default lso_device_path Yes /dev/vdb ocs_action No install Local Storage ¤ lso_device_path ¤ Local disk device path for block storage, used by the Local Storage Operator (e.g. /dev/vdb on virtual machines, /dev/sdc on physical servers, /dev/nvme0n1 for NVMe drives — verify with lsblk on the worker nodes). Required Environment Variable: LSO_DEVICE_PATH Default: /dev/vdb Danger The disk must be unformatted, not in use, available on all worker nodes designated for storage, and have sufficient capacity — all data on the specified disk will be permanently erased during storage cluster setup. Installation ¤ ocs_action ¤ Action to perform on the ODF/OCS installation. Optional Environment Variable: OCS_ACTION Default: install install performs a fresh installation of the Local Storage Operator, ODF/OCS operator, and storage cluster; upgrade updates the operator subscriptions and storage cluster configuration to versions compatible with the current OpenShift version — run it after OpenShift cluster upgrades to keep storage in sync, and always back up data first. Example Playbook ¤ Fresh Installation ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: lso_device_path: /dev/vdb ocs_action: install roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocs Upgrade Existing Installation ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: lso_device_path: /dev/vdb ocs_action: upgrade roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocs Custom Disk Path ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: lso_device_path: /dev/nvme0n1 ocs_action: install roles: - ibm.mas_devops.ocs License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: registry ¤ Create a Docker Registry running on RedHat OpenShift cluster. The registry will be backed by persistant storage, and accessible via either a clusterIP or loadbalancer service. This role can also be used to delete a docker registry on a cluster for a clean start. See usage below for more information. Usage ¤ If you set up the registry with a loadbalancer service you will be able to push to the registry via the cluster's hostname, but before you can use the registry you will need to install the registry's CA certificate and restart the Docker daemon so that your client trusts the new registry: CACERT=$(oc -n airgap-registry get secret airgap-registry-certificate -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d) DOMAIN=$(oc get ingress.config cluster -o jsonpath='{.spec.domain}') sudo mkdir -p /etc/docker/certs.d/$DOMAIN\:32500/ sudo echo "$CACERT" > /etc/docker/certs.d/$DOMAIN\:32500/ca.crt sudo service docker restart You can now use the registry as normal: DOMAIN=$(oc get ingress.config cluster -o jsonpath='{.spec.domain}') docker pull registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal docker tag registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal $DOMAIN:32500/ubi8/ubi-minimal docker push $DOMAIN:32500/ubi8/ubi-minimal If you set up the registry with a clusterip service you will only be able to push to the registry after using port forwarding: oc -n airgap-registry port-forward deployment/airgap-registry 9000:5000 docker pull registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal docker tag registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi-minimal localhost:9000/ubi8/ubi-minimal docker push localhost:9000/ubi8/ubi-minimal However, you will still need to set up Docker trust for the "local" registry: CACERT=$(oc -n airgap-registry get secret airgap-registry-certificate -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d) sudo mkdir -p /etc/docker/certs.d/$DOMAIN\:32500/ sudo mkdir /etc/docker/certs.d/localhost\:9000 sudo echo "$CACERT" > /etc/docker/certs.d/localhost\:9000/ca.crt sudo service docker restart Usage for tear-down action This role can also be used to permanently delete a mirror registry from a given cluster by setting the registry_action to tear-down and specifying the corresponding registry_namespace , if not using the default value. Note that the tear-down action deletes the registry completely including the PVC storage and the registry namespace. To start up the registry again, the role needs to be run again with the registry_action on default or setup . Images previously stored in the registry before the tear-down will no longer be available and will need to be mirrored again once the registry setup has completed. Take precaution when using this function and expect that images can no longer be accessed from the registry that has been torn down. Note: Recreating the registry will also create a new ca cert for the new registry. An appropriate time to use this tear-down function is when the registry has too many images that are not being used or when there has been a shift to support newer versions but images of older versions are clogging the registry. The tear-down function frees the disk space and allows for a new registry to be setup. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default registry_action No setup registry_namespace No airgap-registry registry_username Conditional None registry_password Conditional None registry_storage_class Conditional None registry_storage_capacity No 2000Gi registry_service_type No loadbalancer registry_username and registry_password are required for the setup action. registry_storage_class is required on all clusters except IBM Cloud ROKS, where it defaults to ibmc-block-gold . Registry Deployment ¤ registry_action ¤ Action to perform with the registry deployment — setup to install and configure the registry (default), or tear-down to permanently delete the registry, namespace, and all stored images. Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_ACTION Default: setup Warning The tear-down action is destructive and irreversible. All images stored in the registry will be lost, the PVC storage will be deleted, and a new CA certificate will be generated if the registry is recreated — Docker clients will need to trust the new CA certificate after recreation, and you must re-mirror all required images. Use tear-down when the registry contains too many unused images or when migrating to newer versions; see the Usage section above for more details. registry_namespace ¤ Namespace where the Docker registry will be deployed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_NAMESPACE Default: airgap-registry All registry resources (deployment, service, PVC, secrets) are created in this namespace, which is deleted during tear-down operations. Override the default if you have namespace naming conventions or need multiple registries in the same cluster, and ensure the name doesn't conflict with existing namespaces in your cluster. Registry Authentication ¤ registry_username ¤ Username for authenticating pushes to the registry, used to generate the htpasswd authentication file. Required for the setup action Environment Variable: REGISTRY_USERNAME Default: None registry_password ¤ Password for authenticating pushes to the registry, used together with registry_username to generate the htpasswd authentication file. Required for the setup action Environment Variable: REGISTRY_PASSWORD Default: None Storage ¤ registry_storage_class ¤ Storage class for the registry's persistent volume — any storage class name available in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Common examples: IBM Cloud ROKS ibmc-block-gold , ibmc-block-silver , ibmc-block-bronze ; AWS gp2 , gp3 , io1 ; Azure managed-premium , managed-standard ; on-premises depends on your storage provider. Required (except on IBM Cloud ROKS where it defaults to ibmc-block-gold ) Environment Variable: REGISTRY_STORAGE_CLASS Default: None (IBM Cloud ROKS: ibmc-block-gold ) Must be specified for all non-ROKS clusters; on ROKS the default is usually appropriate unless you have specific performance requirements. Verify the storage class exists before deployment with oc get storageclass — it cannot be changed after initial deployment without recreating the registry. registry_storage_capacity ¤ Size of the persistent volume claim for registry storage — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti ) supported by your storage class. Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_STORAGE_CAPACITY Default: 2000Gi Determines how many images can be stored before the registry runs out of space; insufficient capacity will cause push operations to fail. Plan for growth — container images can be large (1-5GB each) — monitor usage with oc get pvc -n <registry_namespace> , and note that expanding the PVC after deployment depends on your storage class capabilities. For airgap environments, calculate the total size of all images to be mirrored plus a 20% buffer. Service Exposure ¤ registry_service_type ¤ Service type for exposing the registry — loadbalancer to expose the registry externally via the cluster domain on port 32500 (default), or clusterip for internal cluster access only (requires port-forwarding for external access). Optional Environment Variable: REGISTRY_SERVICE_TYPE Default: loadbalancer loadbalancer enables direct external access via <cluster-domain>:32500 ; clusterip is more secure (no external exposure) but requires oc port-forward for each push operation. With either service type you must configure Docker trust for the registry's CA certificate on your client (see the Usage section). Warning The loadbalancer port (32500) cannot be customized. If port 32500 is already in use by another service, you must use clusterip mode. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: registry_storage_class: ibmc-block-gold registry_storage_capacity: 500Gb registry_service_type: loadbalancer roles: - ibm.mas_devops.registry License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: sls ¤ Install IBM Suite License Service and generate a configuration that can be directly applied to IBM Maximo Application Suite. The role assumes that you have already installed the Certificate Manager in the target cluster. This action is performed by the cert_manager role if you want to use this collection to install the cert-manager operator. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default sls_action No install artifactory_username Conditional None artifactory_token Conditional None sls_catalog_source No ibm-operator-catalog sls_channel No 3.x sls_namespace No ibm-sls sls_icr_cpopen No icr.io/cpopen sls_instance_name No sls sls_icr_cp No cp.icr.io/cp ibm_entitlement_key Conditional None sls_entitlement_username No cp sls_entitlement_key No ibm_entitlement_key sls_domain No None sls_auth_enforce No True sls_mongo_retrywrites No true sls_compliance_enforce No True sls_registration_open No True sls_mongodb_cfg_file Conditional None sls_mongodb.hosts Conditional None sls_mongodb.certificates Conditional None sls_mongodb.username Conditional None sls_mongodb.password Conditional None mas_pod_templates_dir No None entitlement_file No '' bootstrap.license_file No '' bootstrap.license_id Conditional '' bootstrap.registration_key No '' mas_instance_id No None mas_config_dir No None sls_url No None mas_license_sync_frequency No */30 * * * * sls_tls_crt No None sls_tls_crt_local_file_path No None sls_registration_key No None custom_labels No None mas_backup_dir Conditional None sls_backup_version Conditional Auto-generated ( YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS ) Variables marked as Conditional are only required in specific circumstances: the Artifactory credentials when using the development catalog, ibm_entitlement_key for SLS 3.7.0 and earlier (unless sls_url is set), sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object to install SLS, bootstrap.license_id when bootstrap.license_file is set, and the backup variables for the backup and restore actions. Actions ¤ sls_action ¤ Operation to perform on the Suite License Service (SLS) instance — install , gencfg , backup , restore , or uninstall . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ACTION Default: install What each action does: install — deploys or updates the SLS operator and instance gencfg — only generates the SLSCfg resource for MAS integration, without installing SLS; requires sls_url to point to an existing SLS instance. Useful when SLS is shared across multiple MAS instances backup — creates a backup of all SLS resources, secrets, and registration data; requires mas_backup_dir and optionally sls_backup_version restore — restores SLS from a previously created backup; requires mas_backup_dir and sls_backup_version uninstall — removes the SLS instance and operator (destructive operation) Always back up license data before using uninstall . Installation ¤ If sls_url is set then the role will skip the installation of an SLS instance and simply generate the SLSCfg resource for the SLS instance defined. artifactory_username ¤ Username for authenticating to IBM Artifactory to access development builds of SLS — typically your IBM w3Id. Required when sls_catalog_source is set to ibm-sls-operators (development catalog) Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None Not needed for production installations using ibm-operator-catalog , which use ibm_entitlement_key instead (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier). Must be set together with artifactory_token — without valid credentials, development catalog subscriptions will fail to pull operator images. artifactory_token ¤ API token for authenticating to IBM Artifactory to access development builds of SLS. Required when sls_catalog_source is set to ibm-sls-operators (development catalog) Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None Must be set together with artifactory_username ; ignored when using production catalogs. Keep this token secure and do not commit it to source control. sls_catalog_source ¤ OpenShift operator catalog source containing the SLS operator subscription — any valid CatalogSource name present in the openshift-marketplace namespace (typically ibm-operator-catalog or ibm-sls-operators ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_CATALOG_SOURCE Default: ibm-operator-catalog Use the default for production installations with official IBM releases; use ibm-sls-operators for development builds from Artifactory, which also requires artifactory_username and artifactory_token . Works with sls_channel to determine the specific operator version installed — an invalid catalog source will cause the subscription to fail. sls_channel ¤ SLS operator subscription channel, which determines the version stream you'll receive updates from — 3.x (check the IBM Operator Catalog for currently available channels). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_CHANNEL Default: 3.x The default 3.x provides the latest SLS 3.x releases (recommended for most deployments); use specific older channels only if required for compatibility with older MAS versions — consult the MAS compatibility matrix before selecting. Changing channels after installation will trigger an upgrade to the latest version in the new channel. SLS 3.8.0+ no longer requires IBM entitlement keys, as images moved to the public registry. sls_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the SLS operator and instance will be deployed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_NAMESPACE Default: ibm-sls All SLS resources (operator, pods, secrets, services, ConfigMaps) are created in this namespace, and it is also used in SLSCfg generation to reference SLS service endpoints. The namespace is created if it doesn't exist — ensure you have permissions to create namespaces in the cluster. Changing it after deployment requires reinstallation. sls_icr_cpopen ¤ Container registry source for SLS operator and component images — any valid container registry URL (e.g. icr.io/cpopen , my-registry.com/sls ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ICR_CPOPEN Default: icr.io/cpopen From SLS 3.8.0 onwards this is the primary registry variable, as images moved to the public IBM Container Registry — the default requires no entitlement key. Override only for development images or airgap/mirror scenarios; an incorrect or inaccessible registry will cause image pull failures. sls_instance_name ¤ Unique identifier for this SLS installation within the cluster — a lowercase alphanumeric string (e.g. sls , sls-prod , sls-dev ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_INSTANCE_NAME Default: sls Distinguishes this SLS installation from others in the same cluster (must be unique if running multiple SLS instances) and is embedded in many SLS resource names. It cannot be changed after installation without reinstalling, so most deployments use the default. sls_icr_cp ¤ Container registry source for SLS images (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only) — any valid container registry URL (e.g. cp.icr.io/cp , my-registry.com/sls ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ICR_CP Default: cp.icr.io/cp Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — SLS images moved to the public registry ( icr.io/cpopen ); for SLS 3.8.0+ use sls_icr_cpopen instead (no entitlement key needed). For SLS 3.7.0 and earlier, all SLS images are pulled from this registry and it requires ibm_entitlement_key for authentication. ibm_entitlement_key ¤ IBM entitlement key for accessing IBM Container Registry images (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only) — obtain it from the IBM Container Library . Required for SLS 3.7.0 and earlier, unless sls_url is provided Environment Variable: IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — SLS images moved to the public registry ( icr.io/cpopen ) and no entitlement key is needed. The key is tied to your IBM Cloud account and product entitlements, and is stored in a Kubernetes secret in the SLS namespace; invalid or expired keys will cause image pull failures. sls_entitlement_username ¤ Username for authenticating to IBM Container Registry (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only) — cp for production installations with an IBM entitlement key. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME Default: cp Used together with ibm_entitlement_key to create image pull secrets for the SLS namespace; an incorrect username will cause image pull authentication failures. Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — SLS images moved to the public registry and no authentication is needed. sls_entitlement_key ¤ SLS-specific IBM entitlement key override (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: Value of ibm_entitlement_key When set, this key is used instead of ibm_entitlement_key for SLS image authentication — primarily used in development scenarios where different keys are needed for different components. Invalid keys will cause image pull failures. Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — no entitlement key is needed. Configuration ¤ sls_domain ¤ Custom domain name for external access to SLS via OpenShift routes — any valid DNS domain name (e.g. sls.mycompany.com , license.example.org ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_DOMAIN Default: None (SLS is only accessible within the cluster) Required when SLS serves MAS instances deployed in separate OpenShift clusters (multi-cluster SLS deployments); leave unset for single-cluster deployments where SLS and MAS are in the same cluster. When set, SLS creates an external route at the specified domain — ensure DNS is properly configured to resolve the domain to your cluster, with appropriate SSL certificates and network security controls. sls_auth_enforce ¤ Whether SLS enforces client authentication via mutual TLS (mTLS) — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_AUTH_ENFORCE Default: True When True , clients must register with SLS and use mTLS certificates for API calls (secure). Setting to False removes authentication requirements, allowing unauthenticated API access — use only in development/testing environments; production deployments should always enforce authentication. Works with sls_registration_open to control client registration and access. sls_mongo_retrywrites ¤ Whether SLS uses the MongoDB retryable writes feature — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_MONGO_RETRYWRITES Default: true When true , failed write operations are automatically retried (improves reliability with MongoDB Community Edition or IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB). Set to false when using AWS DocumentDB or any MongoDB-compatible database that doesn't support retryable writes — DocumentDB does not support them, and leaving this enabled causes connection errors. Must align with the capabilities of the MongoDB provider configured via sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object. sls_compliance_enforce ¤ Whether SLS enforces license token compliance — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_COMPLIANCE_ENFORCE Default: True When True , license checkout requests are denied when insufficient tokens are available (enforces compliance and prevents over-consumption). When False , checkout requests succeed even without available tokens (tracks but doesn't enforce) — this allows operation beyond licensed capacity and may result in license compliance issues; use only in non-production environments or with explicit approval. sls_registration_open ¤ Whether SLS allows new client self-registration — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_REGISTRATION_OPEN Default: True When True , clients such as MAS instances can register themselves and obtain mTLS certificates for SLS API access. For production environments, consider setting to False after all legitimate clients are registered to prevent unauthorized registrations — only pre-registered clients can then access SLS. Works with sls_auth_enforce to control the authentication and registration flow. sls_mongodb_cfg_file ¤ Local file path to a MongoCfg YAML file for SLS MongoDB configuration (e.g. /home/user/masconfig/mongocfg-mongoce-system.yaml ). Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: SLS_MONGODB_CFG_FILE Default: None Preferred method when you've deployed MongoDB using the mongodb role (which generates this file, in mas_config_dir ), as it ensures consistency with the MongoDB deployment. The role extracts the MongoDB connection details (hosts, certificates, credentials) from this file; an invalid or missing file will cause installation to fail. sls_mongodb.hosts ¤ List of MongoDB host:port pairs for the SLS database connection (e.g. ["mongo-0.mongo:27017", "mongo-1.mongo:27017", "mongo-2.mongo:27017"] ). Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Specifies the MongoDB replica set members SLS connects to for license data storage — provide all replica set members for high availability and automatic failover. Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file . sls_mongodb.certificates ¤ List of TLS/SSL certificates for secure MongoDB connections, as an array of certificate strings in PEM format. Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Obtain the CA or server certificate from your MongoDB deployment; the certificates must match the deployment's TLS configuration. Without valid certificates, SLS cannot establish secure connections to MongoDB. Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file . sls_mongodb.username ¤ MongoDB username for SLS database authentication — must correspond to a valid MongoDB user with permission to read and write the SLS database. Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file . sls_mongodb.password ¤ MongoDB password for SLS database authentication — must correspond to the specified MongoDB username. Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Keep this password secure and do not commit it to source control. Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file . mas_pod_templates_dir ¤ Local directory path containing pod template customization files for SLS workloads, enabling control over resource limits, node affinity, tolerations, and other Kubernetes pod settings. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None The role looks for the following files in the named directory; the file content should be the YAML block to insert under a podTemplates: {object} element: ibm-sls-licenseservice.yml — applied to the LicenseService custom resource under spec.podTemplates during installation. See the BestEfforts reference configuration and Customizing Pod Templates ibm-mas-slscfg.yml — inserted into the SlsCfg spec under a top-level podTemplates element during SLSCfg generation. See the BestEfforts reference configuration and Customizing Pod Templates Invalid templates can cause pod scheduling failures. Bootstrap Variables (SLS 3.7.0 and higher) ¤ entitlement_file ¤ Local file path to the IBM license entitlement file for bootstrapping SLS (e.g. /home/user/licenses/entitlement.dat ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ENTITLEMENT_FILE Default: '' When provided, SLS is automatically configured with the license entitlements from this file during installation; without it, you must manually upload license entitlements through the SLS UI or API after installation. Supported in SLS 3.7.0 and higher — this is the new mechanism replacing the old bootstrap. The license file is obtained from IBM and contains your MAS product entitlements; keep it secure as it represents your license rights. Bootstrap [Partly deprecated in SLS 3.7.0] ¤ bootstrap.license_file ¤ Local path to the License File to be used to bootstrap SLS — deprecated in SLS 3.7.0; use only for versions up to 3.6.0. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_LICENSE_FILE Default: '' Don't set if you wish to set up entitlement later on. This variable used to be called bootstrap.entitlement_file and defaulted to {{ mas_config_dir }}/entitlement.lic — this is no longer the case, and SLS_LICENSE_FILE has to be set in order to bootstrap. For SLS 3.7.0 and higher, use entitlement_file instead. bootstrap.license_id ¤ License Id to be used to bootstrap SLS — deprecated in SLS 3.7.0; use only for versions up to 3.6.0. Required when bootstrap.license_file is set (should match the licenseId from the license file) Environment Variable: SLS_LICENSE_ID Default: '' Don't set if you wish to set up entitlement later on. bootstrap.registration_key ¤ Registration Key to be used to bootstrap SLS. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_REGISTRATION_KEY Default: '' Don't set if you wish to set up entitlement later on. SLSCfg Variables ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ The instance ID of Maximo Application Suite that the SlsCfg configuration will target. Optional (if neither this nor mas_config_dir are set then the role will not generate a SlsCfg template) Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory to save the generated SlsCfg resource definition. Optional (if neither this nor mas_instance_id are set then the role will not generate a SlsCfg template) Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None Can be used to manually configure a MAS instance to connect to the SLS instance, or used as an input to the suite_config role. sls_url ¤ The URL of the LicenseService to be called when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. Optional (used to instruct the role to set up MAS for an existing SLS instance) Environment Variable: SLS_URL Default: None mas_license_sync_frequency ¤ The sync frequency of the user license sync cronjob between Maximo Application Suite and SLS. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_LICENSE_SYNC_FREQUENCY Default: */30 * * * * sls_tls_crt ¤ The TLS CA certificate of the LicenseService to be used when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. Takes precedence over sls_tls_crt_local_file_path . Optional (used to instruct the role to set up MAS for an existing SLS instance) Environment Variable: SLS_TLS_CERT Default: None sls_tls_crt_local_file_path ¤ The path on the local system to a file containing the TLS CA certificate of the LicenseService to be used when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. This variable is only used if sls_tls_crt has not been set. Optional (used to instruct the role to set up MAS for an existing SLS instance) Environment Variable: SLS_TLS_CERT_LOCAL_FILE_PATH Default: None sls_registration_key ¤ The Registration key of the LicenseService instance to be used when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_REGISTRATION_KEY Default: None custom_labels ¤ List of comma-separated key=value pairs for setting custom labels on instance-specific resources. Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Backup and Restore Variables ¤ mas_backup_dir ¤ Directory path where SLS backup files will be stored (e.g. /backup/mas , /home/user/sls-backups ). Required for backup and restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None Required when sls_action is set to backup or restore . Backups are written to (for backup) or read from (for restore) a timestamped directory structure under this path: {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-sls/ . Use a persistent location with sufficient storage space and appropriate permissions, and back it up to external storage for disaster recovery. Works with sls_backup_version to create unique backup directories. sls_backup_version ¤ Version identifier for the backup, used to create unique backup directories — any string suitable for directory names (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores). Optional for backup (auto-generated if not provided), Required for restore Environment Variable: SLS_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Auto-generated timestamp in YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS format (e.g. 20260122-131500 ) For backup, creates directory {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-sls/ ; for restore, looks for the backup in {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-sls/ — when restoring, you must know the exact backup version identifier (list the contents of mas_backup_dir to see available backups). Backup and Restore Operations ¤ The SLS role supports backup and restore operations to protect your license service configuration and data. This is essential for disaster recovery, migration, and upgrade scenarios. What Gets Backed Up ¤ The SLS backup operation captures all critical resources needed to restore a complete SLS instance: Kubernetes Resources: Project/Namespace : The SLS namespace configuration Secrets : IBM entitlement credentials ( ibm-entitlement ) MongoDB connection credentials ( ibm-sls-mongo-credentials ) Bootstrap configuration ( {instance-name}-bootstrap ) License entitlement data ( ibm-sls-{instance-name}-entitlement ) All referenced secrets (auto-discovered) ConfigMaps : Suite registration configuration Operator Resources : Subscription ( ibm-sls ) OperatorGroup SLS Custom Resources : LicenseService CR (the main SLS instance) Certificate Manager Resources : Issuers (self-signed and CA issuers) Certificates (CA certificate) Registration Data: License ID Registration key Suite registration information Backup Process ¤ The backup operation performs the following steps: Validation : Verifies required variables ( mas_backup_dir , sls_namespace , sls_instance_name ) Version Generation : Creates or uses provided backup version identifier Resource Discovery : Identifies all SLS resources and auto-discovers referenced secrets Backup Execution : Exports all resources to YAML files in the backup directory Registration Capture : Saves SLS registration details for restore Verification : Reports backup statistics and any failures Backup Directory Structure: {mas_backup_dir}/ └── backup-{version}-sls/ ├── resources/ │ ├── projects/ │ ├── secrets/ │ ├── configmaps/ │ ├── subscriptions/ │ ├── operatorgroups/ │ ├── licenseservices/ │ ├── issuers/ │ └── certificates/ └── sls-registration.yaml Restore Process ¤ The restore operation performs the following steps: Validation : Verifies required variables and backup existence Backup Verification : Checks for valid backup structure and required files Certificate Manager Check : Ensures cert-manager is installed in the cluster Sequential Restoration : Projects/Namespaces Secrets and ConfigMaps OperatorGroups Subscriptions (triggers operator installation) Certificate Manager resources Bootstrap secret (recreated from registration data) LicenseService CR (with optional domain override) Verification : Waits for SLS to become ready and reports restore statistics Important Restore Considerations: The target cluster must have Certificate Manager installed MongoDB must be available and accessible (not restored by this role) The restore can optionally override the sls_domain if deploying to a different cluster All secrets and credentials are restored exactly as backed up Backup Example ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: sls_action: backup mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas sls_namespace: ibm-sls sls_instance_name: sls # Optional: specify custom backup version # sls_backup_version: "pre-upgrade-backup" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Using environment variables: export SLS_ACTION=backup export MAS_BACKUP_DIR=/backup/mas export SLS_NAMESPACE=ibm-sls export SLS_INSTANCE_NAME=sls # Optional: export SLS_BACKUP_VERSION=pre-upgrade-backup ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Restore Example ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: sls_action: restore mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas sls_backup_version: "20260122-131500" # Optional: override domain for different cluster # sls_domain: sls.newcluster.example.com roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Using environment variables: export SLS_ACTION=restore export MAS_BACKUP_DIR=/backup/mas export SLS_BACKUP_VERSION=20260122-131500 # Optional: export SLS_DOMAIN=sls.newcluster.example.com ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Best Practices ¤ Regular Backups : Schedule regular backups before: SLS upgrades License entitlement changes Cluster maintenance MAS upgrades Backup Storage : Store backups in a location separate from the cluster Implement backup retention policies Test restore procedures regularly MongoDB Backup : SLS backup does NOT include MongoDB data Ensure MongoDB is backed up separately using the mongodb role backup functionality Coordinate SLS and MongoDB backups for consistency Pre-Restore Checklist : Verify Certificate Manager is installed Ensure MongoDB is available and accessible Confirm backup version exists and is complete Review and adjust sls_domain if restoring to different cluster Disaster Recovery : Document backup locations and procedures Test restore process in non-production environment Keep backup version identifiers in a safe location Maintain MongoDB connection details separately Migration Scenarios : When migrating to a new cluster, restore MongoDB first Update sls_domain if cluster ingress domain changed Verify network connectivity between restored SLS and MAS instances Troubleshooting ¤ Backup Issues: "Required variables not provided" : Ensure mas_backup_dir , sls_namespace , and sls_instance_name are set "Resource not found" : Some resources may not exist in your deployment (this is normal) Permission errors : Ensure write access to mas_backup_dir Restore Issues: "Backup archive not found" : Verify sls_backup_version matches an existing backup directory "Certificate Manager not found" : Install cert-manager before restoring SLS "LicenseService not ready" : Check operator logs and ensure MongoDB is accessible Domain mismatch : Use sls_domain variable to override domain for new cluster For more information on backup and restore, refer to the IBM Documentation on Backing up and Restoring SLS . Example Playbook ¤ Install and generate a configuration [up to SLS 3.6.0] ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: ibm_entitlement_key: xxxx mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_config_dir: /home/me/masconfig sls_mongodb_cfg_file: "/etc/mas/mongodb.yml" bootstrap: license_id: "aa78dd65ef10" license_file: "/etc/mas/entitlement.lic" registration_key: xxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Install and upload license file [SLS 3.7.0] ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: ibm_entitlement_key: xxxx mas_instance_id: inst1 sls_mongodb_cfg_file: "/etc/mas/mongodb.yml" entitlement_file: "/etc/mas/entitlement.lic" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Install and upload license file [from SLS 3.8.0] ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 sls_mongodb_cfg_file: "/etc/mas/mongodb.yml" entitlement_file: "/etc/mas/entitlement.lic" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Generate a configuration for an existing installation ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_config_dir: /home/me/masconfig sls_action: gencfg sls_tls_crt_local_file_path: "/home/me/sls.crt" slscfg_url: "https://xxx" slscfg_registration_key: "xxx" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Run Role Playbook ¤ export SLS_MONGODB_CFG_FILE=/etc/mas/mongodb.yml export SLS_ENTITLEMENT_FILE=/etc/mas/entitlement.lic export MAS_INSTANCE_ID=inst1 ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: Install IBM Suite License Service and generate a configuration that can be directly applied to IBM Maximo Application Suite. The role assumes that you have already installed the Certificate Manager in the target cluster. This action is performed by the cert_manager role if you want to use this collection to install the cert-manager operator.

docs.text: Operation to perform on the Suite License Service (SLS) instance — install , gencfg , backup , restore , or uninstall . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ACTION Default: install What each action does: install — deploys or updates the SLS operator and instance gencfg — only generates the SLSCfg resource for MAS integration, without installing SLS; requires sls_url to point to an existing SLS instance. docs.text: Container registry source for SLS images (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only) — any valid container registry URL (e.g. cp.icr.io/cp , my-registry.com/sls ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ICR_CP Default: cp.icr.io/cp Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — SLS images moved to the public registry ( icr.io/cpopen ); for SLS 3.8.0+ use sls_icr_cpopen instead (no entitlement key needed). For SLS 3.7.0 and earlier, all SLS images are pulled from this registry and it requires ibm_entitlement_key for authentication.
docs.title: sls_icr_cp

docs.text: IBM entitlement key for accessing IBM Container Registry images (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only) — obtain it from the IBM Container Library . Required for SLS 3.7.0 and earlier, unless sls_url is provided Environment Variable: IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — SLS images moved to the public registry ( icr.io/cpopen ) and no entitlement key is needed. The key is tied to your IBM Cloud account and product entitlements, and is stored in a Kubernetes secret in the SLS namespace; invalid or expired keys will cause image pull failures.
docs.title: ibm_entitlement_key

docs.text: Username for authenticating to IBM Container Registry (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only) — cp for production installations with an IBM entitlement key. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME Default: cp Used together with ibm_entitlement_key to create image pull secrets for the SLS namespace; an incorrect username will cause image pull authentication failures. Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — SLS images moved to the public registry and no authentication is needed.
docs.title: sls_entitlement_username

docs.text: SLS-specific IBM entitlement key override (SLS 3.7.0 and earlier only). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: Value of ibm_entitlement_key When set, this key is used instead of ibm_entitlement_key for SLS image authentication — primarily used in development scenarios where different keys are needed for different components. Invalid keys will cause image pull failures. Deprecated in SLS 3.8.0 — no entitlement key is needed.
docs.title: sls_entitlement_key

docs.text: Custom domain name for external access to SLS via OpenShift routes — any valid DNS domain name (e.g. sls.mycompany.com , license.example.org ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_DOMAIN Default: None (SLS is only accessible within the cluster) Required when SLS serves MAS instances deployed in separate OpenShift clusters (multi-cluster SLS deployments); leave unset for single-cluster deployments where SLS and MAS are in the same cluster. When set, SLS creates an external route at the specified domain — ensure DNS is properly configured to resolve the domain to your cluster, with appropriate SSL certificates and network security controls.
docs.title: sls_domain

docs.text: Whether SLS enforces client authentication via mutual TLS (mTLS) — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_AUTH_ENFORCE Default: True When True , clients must register with SLS and use mTLS certificates for API calls (secure). Setting to False removes authentication requirements, allowing unauthenticated API access — use only in development/testing environments; production deployments should always enforce authentication. Works with sls_registration_open to control client registration and access.
docs.title: sls_auth_enforce

docs.text: Whether SLS uses the MongoDB retryable writes feature — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_MONGO_RETRYWRITES Default: true When true , failed write operations are automatically retried (improves reliability with MongoDB Community Edition or IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB). Set to false when using AWS DocumentDB or any MongoDB-compatible database that doesn't support retryable writes — DocumentDB does not support them, and leaving this enabled causes connection errors. Must align with the capabilities of the MongoDB provider configured via sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object.
docs.title: sls_mongo_retrywrites

docs.text: Whether SLS enforces license token compliance — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_COMPLIANCE_ENFORCE Default: True When True , license checkout requests are denied when insufficient tokens are available (enforces compliance and prevents over-consumption). When False , checkout requests succeed even without available tokens (tracks but doesn't enforce) — this allows operation beyond licensed capacity and may result in license compliance issues; use only in non-production environments or with explicit approval.
docs.title: sls_compliance_enforce

docs.text: Whether SLS allows new client self-registration — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_REGISTRATION_OPEN Default: True When True , clients such as MAS instances can register themselves and obtain mTLS certificates for SLS API access. For production environments, consider setting to False after all legitimate clients are registered to prevent unauthorized registrations — only pre-registered clients can then access SLS. Works with sls_auth_enforce to control the authentication and registration flow.
docs.title: sls_registration_open

docs.text: Local file path to a MongoCfg YAML file for SLS MongoDB configuration (e.g. /home/user/masconfig/mongocfg-mongoce-system.yaml ). Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: SLS_MONGODB_CFG_FILE Default: None Preferred method when you've deployed MongoDB using the mongodb role (which generates this file, in mas_config_dir ), as it ensures consistency with the MongoDB deployment. The role extracts the MongoDB connection details (hosts, certificates, credentials) from this file; an invalid or missing file will cause installation to fail.
docs.title: sls_mongodb_cfg_file

docs.text: List of MongoDB host:port pairs for the SLS database connection (e.g. ["mongo-0.mongo:27017", "mongo-1.mongo:27017", "mongo-2.mongo:27017"] ). Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Specifies the MongoDB replica set members SLS connects to for license data storage — provide all replica set members for high availability and automatic failover. Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file .
docs.title: sls_mongodb.hosts

docs.text: List of TLS/SSL certificates for secure MongoDB connections, as an array of certificate strings in PEM format. Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Obtain the CA or server certificate from your MongoDB deployment; the certificates must match the deployment's TLS configuration. Without valid certificates, SLS cannot establish secure connections to MongoDB. Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file .
docs.title: sls_mongodb.certificates

docs.text: MongoDB username for SLS database authentication — must correspond to a valid MongoDB user with permission to read and write the SLS database. Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file .
docs.title: sls_mongodb.username

docs.text: MongoDB password for SLS database authentication — must correspond to the specified MongoDB username. Required (either sls_mongodb_cfg_file or the sls_mongodb object are required to install SLS) Environment Variable: None Default: None Keep this password secure and do not commit it to source control. Part of the sls_mongodb object; all sls_mongodb.* variables must be provided together when not using sls_mongodb_cfg_file .
docs.title: sls_mongodb.password

docs.text: Local directory path containing pod template customization files for SLS workloads, enabling control over resource limits, node affinity, tolerations, and other Kubernetes pod settings. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None The role looks for the following files in the named directory; the file content should be the YAML block to insert under a podTemplates: {object} element: ibm-sls-licenseservice.yml — applied to the LicenseService custom resource under spec.podTemplates during installation. See the BestEfforts reference configuration and Customizing Pod Templates ibm-mas-slscfg.yml — inserted into the SlsCfg spec under a top-level podTemplates element during SLSCfg generation. See the BestEfforts reference configuration and Customizing Pod Templates Invalid templates can cause pod scheduling failures.
docs.title: mas_pod_templates_dir

docs.text: Local file path to the IBM license entitlement file for bootstrapping SLS (e.g. /home/user/licenses/entitlement.dat ). Optional Environment Variable: SLS_ENTITLEMENT_FILE Default: '' When provided, SLS is automatically configured with the license entitlements from this file during installation; without it, you must manually upload license entitlements through the SLS UI or API after installation. Supported in SLS 3.7.0 and higher — this is the new mechanism replacing the old bootstrap. The license file is obtained from IBM and contains your MAS product entitlements; keep it secure as it represents your license rights.
docs.title: entitlement_file

docs.text: Local path to the License File to be used to bootstrap SLS — deprecated in SLS 3.7.0; use only for versions up to 3.6.0. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_LICENSE_FILE Default: '' Don't set if you wish to set up entitlement later on. This variable used to be called bootstrap.entitlement_file and defaulted to {{ mas_config_dir }}/entitlement.lic — this is no longer the case, and SLS_LICENSE_FILE has to be set in order to bootstrap. For SLS 3.7.0 and higher, use entitlement_file instead.
docs.title: bootstrap.license_file

docs.text: License Id to be used to bootstrap SLS — deprecated in SLS 3.7.0; use only for versions up to 3.6.0. Required when bootstrap.license_file is set (should match the licenseId from the license file) Environment Variable: SLS_LICENSE_ID Default: '' Don't set if you wish to set up entitlement later on.
docs.title: bootstrap.license_id

docs.text: Registration Key to be used to bootstrap SLS. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_REGISTRATION_KEY Default: '' Don't set if you wish to set up entitlement later on.
docs.title: bootstrap.registration_key

docs.text: The instance ID of Maximo Application Suite that the SlsCfg configuration will target. Optional (if neither this nor mas_config_dir are set then the role will not generate a SlsCfg template) Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: Local directory to save the generated SlsCfg resource definition. Optional (if neither this nor mas_instance_id are set then the role will not generate a SlsCfg template) Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None Can be used to manually configure a MAS instance to connect to the SLS instance, or used as an input to the suite_config role.
docs.title: mas_config_dir

docs.text: The URL of the LicenseService to be called when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. Optional (used to instruct the role to set up MAS for an existing SLS instance) Environment Variable: SLS_URL Default: None
docs.title: sls_url

docs.text: The sync frequency of the user license sync cronjob between Maximo Application Suite and SLS. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_LICENSE_SYNC_FREQUENCY Default: */30 * * * *
docs.title: mas_license_sync_frequency

docs.text: The TLS CA certificate of the LicenseService to be used when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. Takes precedence over sls_tls_crt_local_file_path . Optional (used to instruct the role to set up MAS for an existing SLS instance) Environment Variable: SLS_TLS_CERT Default: None
docs.title: sls_tls_crt

docs.text: The path on the local system to a file containing the TLS CA certificate of the LicenseService to be used when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. This variable is only used if sls_tls_crt has not been set. Optional (used to instruct the role to set up MAS for an existing SLS instance) Environment Variable: SLS_TLS_CERT_LOCAL_FILE_PATH Default: None
docs.title: sls_tls_crt_local_file_path

docs.text: The Registration key of the LicenseService instance to be used when the Maximo Application Suite is registered with SLS. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_REGISTRATION_KEY Default: None
docs.title: sls_registration_key

docs.text: List of comma-separated key=value pairs for setting custom labels on instance-specific resources. Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None
docs.title: custom_labels

docs.text: Directory path where SLS backup files will be stored (e.g. /backup/mas , /home/user/sls-backups ). Required for backup and restore operations Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None Required when sls_action is set to backup or restore . Backups are written to (for backup) or read from (for restore) a timestamped directory structure under this path: {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-sls/ . Use a persistent location with sufficient storage space and appropriate permissions, and back it up to external storage for disaster recovery. Works with sls_backup_version to create unique backup directories.
docs.title: mas_backup_dir

docs.text: Version identifier for the backup, used to create unique backup directories — any string suitable for directory names (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores). Optional for backup (auto-generated if not provided), Required for restore Environment Variable: SLS_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Auto-generated timestamp in YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS format (e.g. 20260122-131500 ) For backup, creates directory {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-sls/ ; for restore, looks for the backup in {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-sls/ — when restoring, you must know the exact backup version identifier (list the contents of mas_backup_dir to see available backups).
docs.title: sls_backup_version

docs.text: The SLS role supports backup and restore operations to protect your license service configuration and data. This is essential for disaster recovery, migration, and upgrade scenarios.
docs.title: Backup and Restore Operations

docs.text: The SLS backup operation captures all critical resources needed to restore a complete SLS instance: Kubernetes Resources: Project/Namespace : The SLS namespace configuration Secrets : IBM entitlement credentials ( ibm-entitlement ) MongoDB connection credentials ( ibm-sls-mongo-credentials ) Bootstrap configuration ( {instance-name}-bootstrap ) License entitlement data ( ibm-sls-{instance-name}-entitlement ) All referenced secrets (auto-discovered) ConfigMaps : Suite registration configuration Operator Resources : Subscription ( ibm-sls ) OperatorGroup SLS Custom Resources : LicenseService CR (the main SLS instance) Certificate Manager Resources : Issuers (self-signed and CA issuers) Certificates (CA certificate) Registration Data: License ID Registration key Suite registration information
docs.title: What Gets Backed Up

docs.text: The backup operation performs the following steps: Validation : Verifies required variables ( mas_backup_dir , sls_namespace , sls_instance_name ) Version Generation : Creates or uses provided backup version identifier Resource Discovery : Identifies all SLS resources and auto-discovers referenced secrets Backup Execution : Exports all resources to YAML files in the backup directory Registration Capture : Saves SLS registration details for restore Verification : Reports backup statistics and any failures Backup Directory Structure: {mas_backup_dir}/ └── backup-{version}-sls/ ├── resources/ │ ├── projects/ │ ├── secrets/ │ ├── configmaps/ │ ├── subscriptions/ │ ├── operatorgroups/ │ ├── licenseservices/ │ ├── issuers/ │ └── certificates/ └── sls-registration.yaml
docs.title: Backup Process

docs.text: The restore operation performs the following steps: Validation : Verifies required variables and backup existence Backup Verification : Checks for valid backup structure and required files Certificate Manager Check : Ensures cert-manager is installed in the cluster Sequential Restoration : Projects/Namespaces Secrets and ConfigMaps OperatorGroups Subscriptions (triggers operator installation) Certificate Manager resources Bootstrap secret (recreated from registration data) LicenseService CR (with optional domain override) Verification : Waits for SLS to become ready and reports restore statistics Important Restore Considerations: The target cluster must have Certificate Manager installed MongoDB must be available and accessible (not restored by this role) The restore can optionally override the sls_domain if deploying to a different cluster All secrets and credentials are restored exactly as backed up
docs.title: Restore Process

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: sls_action: backup mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas sls_namespace: ibm-sls sls_instance_name: sls # Optional: specify custom backup version # sls_backup_version: "pre-upgrade-backup" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Using environment variables: export SLS_ACTION=backup export MAS_BACKUP_DIR=/backup/mas export SLS_NAMESPACE=ibm-sls export SLS_INSTANCE_NAME=sls # Optional: export SLS_BACKUP_VERSION=pre-upgrade-backup ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role
docs.title: Backup Example

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: sls_action: restore mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas sls_backup_version: "20260122-131500" # Optional: override domain for different cluster # sls_domain: sls.newcluster.example.com roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls Using environment variables: export SLS_ACTION=restore export MAS_BACKUP_DIR=/backup/mas export SLS_BACKUP_VERSION=20260122-131500 # Optional: export SLS_DOMAIN=sls.newcluster.example.com ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role
docs.title: Restore Example

docs.text: Regular Backups : Schedule regular backups before: SLS upgrades License entitlement changes Cluster maintenance MAS upgrades Backup Storage : Store backups in a location separate from the cluster Implement backup retention policies Test restore procedures regularly MongoDB Backup : SLS backup does NOT include MongoDB data Ensure MongoDB is backed up separately using the mongodb role backup functionality Coordinate SLS and MongoDB backups for consistency Pre-Restore Checklist : Verify Certificate Manager is installed Ensure MongoDB is available and accessible Confirm backup version exists and is complete Review and adjust sls_domain if restoring to different cluster Disaster Recovery : Document backup locations and procedures Test restore process in non-production environment Keep backup version identifiers in a safe location Maintain MongoDB connection details separately Migration Scenarios : When migrating to a new cluster, restore MongoDB first Update sls_domain if cluster ingress domain changed Verify network connectivity between restored SLS and MAS instances
docs.title: Best Practices

docs.text: Backup Issues: "Required variables not provided" : Ensure mas_backup_dir , sls_namespace , and sls_instance_name are set "Resource not found" : Some resources may not exist in your deployment (this is normal) Permission errors : Ensure write access to mas_backup_dir Restore Issues: "Backup archive not found" : Verify sls_backup_version matches an existing backup directory "Certificate Manager not found" : Install cert-manager before restoring SLS "LicenseService not ready" : Check operator logs and ensure MongoDB is accessible Domain mismatch : Use sls_domain variable to override domain for new cluster For more information on backup and restore, refer to the IBM Documentation on Backing up and Restoring SLS .
docs.title: Troubleshooting

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: ibm_entitlement_key: xxxx mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_config_dir: /home/me/masconfig sls_mongodb_cfg_file: "/etc/mas/mongodb.yml" bootstrap: license_id: "aa78dd65ef10" license_file: "/etc/mas/entitlement.lic" registration_key: xxxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls
docs.title: Install and generate a configuration [up to SLS 3.6.0]

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: ibm_entitlement_key: xxxx mas_instance_id: inst1 sls_mongodb_cfg_file: "/etc/mas/mongodb.yml" entitlement_file: "/etc/mas/entitlement.lic" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls
docs.title: Install and upload license file [SLS 3.7.0]

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 sls_mongodb_cfg_file: "/etc/mas/mongodb.yml" entitlement_file: "/etc/mas/entitlement.lic" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls
docs.title: Install and upload license file [from SLS 3.8.0]

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_config_dir: /home/me/masconfig sls_action: gencfg sls_tls_crt_local_file_path: "/home/me/sls.crt" slscfg_url: "https://xxx" slscfg_registration_key: "xxx" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.sls

docs.text: smtp ¤ Generate an SMTP configuration that can be directly applied to IBM Maximo Application Suite. The role supports the Twilio SendGrid email provider. Prior to running this role, you must create an account with SendGrid. The SendGrid account needs to support creating subusers. Tip The role will generate a yaml file containing the definition of a Secret and SmtpCfg resource that can be used to configure the smtp email provider for MAS. This file can be directly applied using oc apply -f $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/smtp-$MAS_INSTANCE_ID.yml" or used in conjunction with the suite_config role. This role will create a subuser that must be validated. An email with a validation link will be sent to the primary email address. You need to validate the subuser using this link. If validation fails, you can resend the email using the SendGrid admin UI. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default smtp_type Yes None mas_instance_id Yes None mas_config_dir Yes None mas_pod_templates_dir No None custom_labels No None sendgrid_primary_username Yes None sendgrid_primary_email Yes None sendgrid_primary_apikey Yes None sendgrid_ips Yes None sendgrid_subuser_username No ibm-mas_{mas_instance_id} sendgrid_subuser_email Yes None sendgrid_defaultrecipientemail Yes None sendgrid_defaultsendername No Empty string sendgrid_defaultshouldemailpasswords No false sendgrid_configscope No system sendgrid_hostname No smtp.sendgrid.net sendgrid_port No 465 sendgrid_security No SSL sendgrid_authentication No true sendgrid_api_url No api.sendgrid.com sendgrid_debug No False SMTP Provider ¤ smtp_type ¤ SMTP email provider type for MAS email notifications — sendgrid is currently the only supported provider. Required Environment Variable: SMTP_TYPE Default: None Determines which SMTP provider configuration is created and which API endpoints are used. Requires an active SendGrid account with subuser support; future versions may support additional SMTP providers. MAS Configuration ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier the SMTP configuration applies to — a valid MAS instance ID (e.g. prod , dev , masinst1 ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Must match the instance ID used during MAS installation. Used to name the generated SmtpCfg resource and in the default subuser username ibm-mas_{mas_instance_id} . mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory where the generated SMTP configuration files are saved — any valid local filesystem path (e.g. ~/masconfig , /opt/mas/config ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The SmtpCfg YAML file (containing the Secret and SmtpCfg resources) is created as smtp-{mas_instance_id}.yml in this directory. Apply it manually with oc apply -f $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/smtp-$MAS_INSTANCE_ID.yml or use it with the suite_config role for automated configuration. Use a consistent directory across all MAS DevOps roles. mas_pod_templates_dir ¤ Directory containing pod template customizations for the SMTP service pods — must contain a file named ibm-mas-smtpcfg.yml . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None The pod template configuration is inserted into the SmtpCfg spec under the podTemplates element. See the BestEfforts reference and the Customizing Pod Templates documentation. custom_labels ¤ Custom key-value labels applied to the generated SMTP resources — comma-separated key=value pairs (e.g. environment=production,team=platform,cost-center=engineering ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Useful for resource organization, cost tracking, environment identification, and automation-driven resource discovery. Follow Kubernetes label naming conventions. SendGrid Primary Account ¤ sendgrid_primary_username ¤ Username of the primary SendGrid account used to create the subuser for MAS email operations. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PRIMARY_USERNAME Default: None The account must have permissions to create subusers. Primary account credentials are only used during setup and are not stored in MAS. sendgrid_primary_email ¤ Email address registered with the primary SendGrid account. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PRIMARY_EMAIL Default: None Subuser validation emails are sent to this address — you must validate the subuser using the link in the email before it can send emails. The validation email can be resent from the SendGrid admin UI if needed. sendgrid_primary_apikey ¤ API key for the primary SendGrid account, with subuser creation and IP management permissions. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PRIMARY_APIKEY Default: None Generate the key from the SendGrid console (Settings > API Keys). Store it securely and never commit it to version control; it is only used during setup for subuser creation and IP assignment, not stored in MAS configuration. sendgrid_ips ¤ SendGrid IP addresses to assign to the subuser — a JSON array string such as '["192.0.2.1", "192.0.2.2"]' . Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_IPS Default: None The IPs must already be allocated to the primary account (find them in the SendGrid console: Settings > IP Addresses). The subuser sends emails from these addresses, so their reputation affects email deliverability. SendGrid Subuser ¤ sendgrid_subuser_username ¤ Username for the SendGrid subuser created for MAS — alphanumeric, with hyphens and underscores allowed. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_SUBUSER_USERNAME Default: ibm-mas_{mas_instance_id} Must be unique within the SendGrid account. Override the default if you need a specific naming convention or share one SendGrid account across multiple MAS instances. See the SendGrid subusers documentation . sendgrid_subuser_email ¤ Email address for the SendGrid subuser dedicated to sending MAS notifications — can be the same as or different from the primary account email. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_SUBUSER_EMAIL Default: None The subuser provides isolation from the primary account. See the SendGrid subusers documentation . Email Defaults ¤ sendgrid_defaultrecipientemail ¤ Default recipient email address for MAS notifications when no specific recipient is configured — typically an admin or operations team email. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEFAULTRECIPIENTEMAIL Default: None Acts as the fallback for unconfigured notifications and can be overridden per notification type in MAS. sendgrid_defaultsendername ¤ Display name shown as the sender in email clients when MAS sends notifications — any string, e.g. MAS Notifications or Maximo Production . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEFAULTSENDERNAME Default: Empty string Improves email recognition and trust; recommended for production deployments and can be left empty for default behavior. sendgrid_defaultshouldemailpasswords ¤ Controls whether MAS sends user passwords via email when creating or resetting accounts — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEFAULTSHOULDEMAILPASSWORDS Default: false Warning Sending passwords via email is generally not recommended — the default false follows security best practices. Only set to true if your security policy allows password transmission via email, and consider alternative password delivery methods. sendgrid_configscope ¤ Configuration scope for the SMTP settings — system is currently the only supported value. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_CONFIGSCOPE Default: system System scope makes the SMTP configuration available to all MAS components; workspace or application scopes may be supported in future versions. SMTP Connection ¤ sendgrid_hostname ¤ SendGrid SMTP server hostname that MAS connects to for sending emails. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_HOSTNAME Default: smtp.sendgrid.net This is SendGrid's standard SMTP endpoint and rarely needs to be changed — verify with the SendGrid documentation if unsure. sendgrid_port ¤ SendGrid SMTP server port: 465 (SMTP with SSL/TLS, recommended default), 587 (SMTP with STARTTLS), or 25 (unencrypted, not recommended — often blocked by ISPs). Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PORT Default: 465 Must match sendgrid_security — port 465 pairs with SSL and port 587 with STARTTLS . sendgrid_security ¤ SMTP connection security protocol: SSL (recommended, default), STARTTLS (upgrade to TLS after initial connection), or NONE (no encryption, not recommended). Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_SECURITY Default: SSL SSL on port 465 is recommended and STARTTLS on port 587 is also secure — never use NONE in production. sendgrid_authentication ¤ Enables SMTP authentication for SendGrid connections — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_AUTHENTICATION Default: true Must remain true : authentication is required by SendGrid and uses the subuser credentials — disabling it will cause the connection to fail. sendgrid_api_url ¤ SendGrid REST API endpoint used by the role for subuser creation and management — a valid SendGrid API hostname. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_API_URL Default: api.sendgrid.com This is SendGrid's standard API endpoint and rarely needs to be changed. It is used during role execution only, not by MAS itself. Debugging ¤ sendgrid_debug ¤ Enables display of detailed SendGrid REST API call results in Ansible logs — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEBUG Default: False Warning Use only for troubleshooting and disable it afterwards — when True , detailed API responses are logged, which may include sensitive information. Example Playbook ¤ Generate a configuration ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_config_dir: /home/me/masconfig smtp_type: sendgrid sendgrid_primary_username: myusername sendgrid_primary_email: myemail@mydomain sendgrid_subuser_username: mysubusername sendgrid_subuser_email: mysubuser@mydomain sendgrid_defaultrecipientemail: myemail@mydomain sendgrid_defaultsendername: 'My Name' sendgrid_primary_apikey: xxxx sendgrid_ips: '["XXX.XXX.XXX.XXX"]' roles: - ibm.mas_devops.smtp License ¤ EPL-2.0

Prior to running this role, you must create an account with SendGrid. The SendGrid account needs to support creating subusers. Tip The role will generate a yaml file containing the definition of a Secret and SmtpCfg resource that can be used to configure the smtp email provider for MAS. This file can be directly applied using oc apply -f $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/smtp-$MAS_INSTANCE_ID.yml" or used in conjunction with the suite_config role. This role will create a subuser that must be validated. An email with a validation link will be sent to the primary email address. You need to validate the subuser using this link. If validation fails, you can resend the email using the SendGrid admin UI.

docs.text: SMTP email provider type for MAS email notifications — sendgrid is currently the only supported provider. Required Environment Variable: SMTP_TYPE Default: None Determines which SMTP provider configuration is created and which API endpoints are used. Requires an active SendGrid account with subuser support; future versions may support additional SMTP providers.
docs.title: smtp_type

docs.text: MAS instance identifier the SMTP configuration applies to — a valid MAS instance ID (e.g. prod , dev , masinst1 ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Must match the instance ID used during MAS installation. Used to name the generated SmtpCfg resource and in the default subuser username ibm-mas_{mas_instance_id} .
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: Local directory where the generated SMTP configuration files are saved — any valid local filesystem path (e.g. ~/masconfig , /opt/mas/config ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The SmtpCfg YAML file (containing the Secret and SmtpCfg resources) is created as smtp-{mas_instance_id}.yml in this directory. Apply it manually with oc apply -f $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/smtp-$MAS_INSTANCE_ID.yml or use it with the suite_config role for automated configuration. Use a consistent directory across all MAS DevOps roles.
docs.title: mas_config_dir

docs.text: Directory containing pod template customizations for the SMTP service pods — must contain a file named ibm-mas-smtpcfg.yml . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None The pod template configuration is inserted into the SmtpCfg spec under the podTemplates element. See the BestEfforts reference and the Customizing Pod Templates documentation.
docs.title: mas_pod_templates_dir

docs.text: Custom key-value labels applied to the generated SMTP resources — comma-separated key=value pairs (e.g. environment=production,team=platform,cost-center=engineering ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Useful for resource organization, cost tracking, environment identification, and automation-driven resource discovery. Follow Kubernetes label naming conventions.
docs.title: custom_labels

docs.text: Username of the primary SendGrid account used to create the subuser for MAS email operations. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PRIMARY_USERNAME Default: None The account must have permissions to create subusers. Primary account credentials are only used during setup and are not stored in MAS.
docs.title: sendgrid_primary_username

docs.text: Email address registered with the primary SendGrid account. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PRIMARY_EMAIL Default: None Subuser validation emails are sent to this address — you must validate the subuser using the link in the email before it can send emails. The validation email can be resent from the SendGrid admin UI if needed.
docs.title: sendgrid_primary_email

docs.text: API key for the primary SendGrid account, with subuser creation and IP management permissions. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PRIMARY_APIKEY Default: None Generate the key from the SendGrid console (Settings > API Keys). Store it securely and never commit it to version control; it is only used during setup for subuser creation and IP assignment, not stored in MAS configuration.
docs.title: sendgrid_primary_apikey

docs.text: SendGrid IP addresses to assign to the subuser — a JSON array string such as '["192.0.2.1", "192.0.2.2"]' . Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_IPS Default: None The IPs must already be allocated to the primary account (find them in the SendGrid console: Settings > IP Addresses). The subuser sends emails from these addresses, so their reputation affects email deliverability.
docs.title: sendgrid_ips

docs.text: Username for the SendGrid subuser created for MAS — alphanumeric, with hyphens and underscores allowed. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_SUBUSER_USERNAME Default: ibm-mas_{mas_instance_id} Must be unique within the SendGrid account. Override the default if you need a specific naming convention or share one SendGrid account across multiple MAS instances. See the SendGrid subusers documentation .
docs.title: sendgrid_subuser_username

docs.text: Email address for the SendGrid subuser dedicated to sending MAS notifications — can be the same as or different from the primary account email. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_SUBUSER_EMAIL Default: None The subuser provides isolation from the primary account. See the SendGrid subusers documentation .
docs.title: sendgrid_subuser_email

docs.text: Default recipient email address for MAS notifications when no specific recipient is configured — typically an admin or operations team email. Required Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEFAULTRECIPIENTEMAIL Default: None Acts as the fallback for unconfigured notifications and can be overridden per notification type in MAS.
docs.title: sendgrid_defaultrecipientemail

docs.text: Display name shown as the sender in email clients when MAS sends notifications — any string, e.g. MAS Notifications or Maximo Production . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEFAULTSENDERNAME Default: Empty string Improves email recognition and trust; recommended for production deployments and can be left empty for default behavior.
docs.title: sendgrid_defaultsendername

docs.text: Controls whether MAS sends user passwords via email when creating or resetting accounts — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEFAULTSHOULDEMAILPASSWORDS Default: false Warning Sending passwords via email is generally not recommended — the default false follows security best practices. Only set to true if your security policy allows password transmission via email, and consider alternative password delivery methods.
docs.title: sendgrid_defaultshouldemailpasswords

docs.text: Configuration scope for the SMTP settings — system is currently the only supported value. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_CONFIGSCOPE Default: system System scope makes the SMTP configuration available to all MAS components; workspace or application scopes may be supported in future versions.
docs.title: sendgrid_configscope

docs.text: SendGrid SMTP server hostname that MAS connects to for sending emails. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_HOSTNAME Default: smtp.sendgrid.net This is SendGrid's standard SMTP endpoint and rarely needs to be changed — verify with the SendGrid documentation if unsure.
docs.title: sendgrid_hostname

docs.text: SendGrid SMTP server port: 465 (SMTP with SSL/TLS, recommended default), 587 (SMTP with STARTTLS), or 25 (unencrypted, not recommended — often blocked by ISPs). Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_PORT Default: 465 Must match sendgrid_security — port 465 pairs with SSL and port 587 with STARTTLS .
docs.title: sendgrid_port

docs.text: SMTP connection security protocol: SSL (recommended, default), STARTTLS (upgrade to TLS after initial connection), or NONE (no encryption, not recommended). Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_SECURITY Default: SSL SSL on port 465 is recommended and STARTTLS on port 587 is also secure — never use NONE in production.
docs.title: sendgrid_security

docs.text: Enables SMTP authentication for SendGrid connections — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_AUTHENTICATION Default: true Must remain true : authentication is required by SendGrid and uses the subuser credentials — disabling it will cause the connection to fail.
docs.title: sendgrid_authentication

docs.text: SendGrid REST API endpoint used by the role for subuser creation and management — a valid SendGrid API hostname. Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_API_URL Default: api.sendgrid.com This is SendGrid's standard API endpoint and rarely needs to be changed. It is used during role execution only, not by MAS itself.
docs.title: sendgrid_api_url

docs.text: Enables display of detailed SendGrid REST API call results in Ansible logs — True or False . Optional Environment Variable: SENDGRID_DEBUG Default: False Warning Use only for troubleshooting and disable it afterwards — when True , detailed API responses are logged, which may include sensitive information.
docs.title: sendgrid_debug
