docs.text: suite_app_install ¤ This role is used to install a specified application in Maximo Application Suite. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_app_id Yes None mas_app_catalog_source No ibm-operator-catalog mas_app_channel No 8.x custom_labels No None artifactory_username Conditional None artifactory_token Conditional None mas_entitlement_username No cp mas_entitlement_key Conditional None mas_app_spec No Application-specific defaults mas_app_bindings_jdbc No system mas_app_plan No Application-specific mas_pod_templates_dir No None mas_app_settings_visualinspection_storage_class No Auto-detected (RWX) mas_app_settings_visualinspection_storage_size No 100Gi mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size No small mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_pvc_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected (RWO) mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_router_pvc_size No 100Gi mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_executor_pvc_size No 100Gi mas_app_settings_iot_mqttbroker_pvc_storage_class Conditional Auto-detected (RWO) mas_app_settings_iot_mqttbroker_pvc_size No 100Gi mas_appws_upgrade_type No regularUpgrade mas_app_settings_monitor_deployment_size No dev The Artifactory credentials are only required when mas_app_catalog_source is set to a development catalog, and mas_entitlement_key is only required for production installations using official IBM releases. The IoT storage class variables are only required when auto-detection cannot find a suitable storage class (and always when mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size is not dev ). Core Installation Settings ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ Unique identifier for the MAS instance where the application will be installed — a lowercase alphanumeric string of 3-12 characters (e.g., prod , dev , inst1 ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None This must match the instance ID used when installing MAS core, cannot be changed after application installation, and should use the same value across all application installations for a given MAS instance. The application is installed into the namespace mas-{mas_instance_id}-{mas_app_id} , so an incorrect instance ID will cause the installation to fail or create resources in the wrong namespace. mas_app_id ¤ Specifies which MAS application to install — one of assist , iot , facilities , manage , monitor , predict , visualinspection , optimizer , or arcgis . Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None Each application requires a separate role execution, determines which application operator is installed and which namespace is created ( mas-{mas_instance_id}-{mas_app_id} ), and has its own set of configuration variables (e.g., mas_app_settings_iot_* for IoT). mas_app_channel must be set to a valid channel and mas_app_catalog_source must contain the operator for the selected application. mas_app_catalog_source ¤ OpenShift operator catalog source containing the MAS application operator subscription — any valid CatalogSource name present in the openshift-marketplace namespace. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CATALOG_SOURCE Default: ibm-operator-catalog Use the default ibm-operator-catalog for production installations with official IBM releases, and ibm-mas-{mas_app_id}-operators (e.g., ibm-mas-manage-operators ) for development builds from Artifactory — development catalogs require additional authentication via artifactory_username and artifactory_token . An invalid catalog source will cause the subscription to fail. mas_app_channel ¤ MAS application operator subscription channel, which determines the version stream you will receive updates from — application-specific channels such as 8.6.x , 8.7.x , or 8.8.x for Manage (check the IBM Operator Catalog for currently available channels for your application). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CHANNEL Default: 8.x The channel determines which application version is installed and which automatic updates are applied. Consult the MAS compatibility matrix before selecting a channel to ensure compatibility with your MAS core version, and change channels only during planned upgrade windows — changing channels after installation triggers an upgrade to the latest version in the new channel, which may require reconfiguration and testing. custom_labels ¤ Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to MAS application resources (e.g., env=prod,team=platform,app=manage ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Use for organizational metadata (e.g., cost-center=engineering , environment=production ), resource tracking, cost allocation, and custom automation or monitoring. Labels can be used for filtering with oc get commands, monitoring queries, and automation scripts, but do not affect application functionality. Entitlement and Registry Credentials ¤ artifactory_username ¤ Username for authenticating to IBM Artifactory to access development builds of MAS applications — typically your IBM w3Id. Optional — required when mas_app_catalog_source is set to a development catalog (e.g., ibm-mas-manage-operators ) Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None Without valid credentials, development catalog subscriptions will fail to pull operator images. Not needed for production installations using ibm-operator-catalog , which use mas_entitlement_key instead. Must be set together with artifactory_token . artifactory_token ¤ API token for authenticating to IBM Artifactory to access development builds of MAS applications. Optional — required when mas_app_catalog_source is set to a development catalog (e.g., ibm-mas-manage-operators ) Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None Without a valid token, development catalog subscriptions will fail to pull operator images. Must be set together with artifactory_username ; production installations use mas_entitlement_key instead. Warning Keep this token secure and do not commit it to source control. Use environment variables or secure secret management. mas_entitlement_username ¤ Username for authenticating to IBM Container Registry to pull MAS application images — cp for production installations with an IBM entitlement key, or your IBM w3Id for development builds. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME Default: cp for production installations Used together with mas_entitlement_key to create image pull secrets for the application namespace; an incorrect username will cause image pull authentication failures. mas_entitlement_key ¤ IBM entitlement key for authenticating access to IBM Container Registry to pull MAS application images — a valid, non-expired key with MAS product entitlements, typically starting with eyJ... . Optional — required for production installations using official IBM releases Environment Variable: MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None (falls back to ibm_entitlement_key / IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY ) Obtain the key from the IBM Container Library at https://myibm.ibm.com/products-services/containerlibrary; for development builds, use your Artifactory API key instead. The key is stored in a Kubernetes secret and used to create image pull secrets for all application pods — invalid or expired keys will cause image pull failures during application installation. Warning Keep this key secure and do not commit it to source control. Use environment variables or secure secret management. Application Configuration ¤ mas_app_spec ¤ Custom YAML specification to override default application configuration settings — a valid YAML dictionary matching the application's Custom Resource specification. Optional Environment Variable: None Default: Application-specific defaults in vars/defaultspecs/{{mas_app_id}}.yml Use for advanced customization scenarios not covered by the standard mas_app_settings_* and mas_app_bindings_* variables; leave unset for standard installations. Warning When set, this completely overrides all other application configuration variables ( mas_app_settings_* , mas_app_bindings_* ) — the role uses this specification directly in the application CR. Incorrect specifications can cause installation failures, so this requires deep knowledge of the application's Custom Resource specification. mas_app_bindings_jdbc ¤ Scope for JDBC database configuration binding — either system (shared across all applications) or application (dedicated to this application). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_BINDINGS_JDBC Default: system With system , the application uses the JDBC configuration defined at the MAS instance level (JdbcCfg with scope=system); with application , the application requires its own application-scoped JdbcCfg resource. Most deployments use system for simplified management. Changing this after installation may require reconfiguration of database connections — ensure the appropriate JdbcCfg resource exists at the corresponding scope before changing this value. mas_app_plan ¤ Licensing plan/tier for the application installation — application-specific; for example Optimizer supports full and limited (v8.2+, defaulting to full ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_PLAN Default: Application-specific (varies by application) The plan determines which features are available in the application. Set it according to your license entitlements — using a plan not covered by your license may result in compliance issues, with some features disabled or unavailable. Consult your IBM license agreement or contact IBM if you're unsure which plan to use. mas_pod_templates_dir ¤ Local directory path containing pod template customization files for the application, enabling control over resource limits, node affinity, tolerations, security contexts, and service accounts. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None mas_app_id determines which pod template files are expected — see the IoT and Manage sections below for the file names each application looks for. The files are applied to the application's Custom Resource, affecting how application pods are scheduled and configured; invalid templates can cause pod scheduling failures. For full documentation, see Customizing Pod Templates in the product documentation. Visual Inspection Configuration ¤ mas_app_settings_visualinspection_storage_class ¤ Storage class for Visual Inspection user data persistent volumes (uploaded images, trained models, and inspection results) — any valid storage class name in your cluster that supports ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_VISUALINSPECTION_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-selected from available ReadWriteMany (RWX) storage classes in the cluster Set explicitly when you have multiple RWX storage classes and want to control which is used, or when auto-selection doesn't choose your preferred class. Important ReadWriteMany (RWX) support is required for Visual Inspection to function correctly. Verify your storage class supports RWX with oc get storageclass before deployment — common RWX storage classes include NFS, CephFS, and cloud provider file storage. mas_app_settings_visualinspection_storage_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for Visual Inspection user data — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti , 2Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_VISUALINSPECTION_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with large image datasets, many trained models, or long data retention; use the default for development, testing, or small deployments. Insufficient storage will prevent uploading new images or training models — plan for growth, monitor storage usage, and check whether your storage class supports PVC expansion before deployment. IoT Configuration ¤ mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size ¤ Deployment size profile for MAS IoT, which determines resource allocations and scaling characteristics — dev , small , or large . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_DEPLOYMENT_SIZE Default: small dev allocates minimal resources suitable for development only, small moderate resources suitable for small to medium production deployments, and large maximum resources suitable for large-scale production deployments. Application support: IoT 8.6+. Ensure your cluster has sufficient resources for the selected size — this cannot be easily changed after deployment without reinstallation. mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_pvc_storage_class ¤ Storage class for IoT Function Pipeline (FPL) component persistent volumes, which store transient state for pipeline processing — any valid storage class name in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional — always required when mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size is not dev Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_FPL_PVC_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-selected from available ReadWriteOnce (RWO) storage classes in the cluster Set explicitly when you have multiple RWO storage classes and want to control which is used, or when auto-selection doesn't choose your preferred class. The storage class determines I/O performance for pipeline state operations. Application support: IoT 8.6+ — verify with oc get storageclass before deployment. mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_router_pvc_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for the IoT FPL pipeline router component's transient state storage — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 50Gi , 100Gi , 200Gi , 500Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_FPL_ROUTER_PVC_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with high pipeline throughput, many concurrent pipelines, or complex pipeline logic; use the default for development, testing, or moderate workloads. Application support: IoT 8.6+. Insufficient storage may cause pipeline execution failures — monitor storage usage and check whether your storage class supports PVC expansion. mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_executor_pvc_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for the IoT FPL pipeline executor component's transient state and intermediate data — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 50Gi , 100Gi , 200Gi , 500Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_FPL_EXECUTOR_PVC_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with high data processing volumes or pipelines that process large datasets; use the default for development, testing, or moderate workloads. Application support: IoT 8.6+. Insufficient storage may cause pipeline execution or data processing failures — monitor storage usage and check whether your storage class supports PVC expansion. mas_app_settings_iot_mqttbroker_pvc_storage_class ¤ Storage class for IoT MQTT broker (MessageSight) persistent volumes, which store message queues, broker state, and retained messages — any valid storage class name in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional — always required when mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size is not dev Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_MQTTBROKER_PVC_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-selected from available ReadWriteOnce (RWO) storage classes in the cluster Set explicitly when you have multiple RWO storage classes, when auto-selection doesn't choose your preferred class, or when you need specific performance characteristics for MQTT message handling. Application support: IoT 8.3+ — verify with oc get storageclass before deployment. mas_app_settings_iot_mqttbroker_pvc_size ¤ Size of the persistent volume for the IoT MQTT broker (MessageSight) component — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 50Gi , 100Gi , 200Gi , 500Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_MQTTBROKER_PVC_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with many connected devices, high message volumes, long message retention, or devices that frequently disconnect and require message queuing; use the default for development, testing, or moderate device counts. Application support: IoT 8.3+. Insufficient storage may cause message loss, device connection failures, or broker instability — monitor storage usage to prevent message queue overflow. IoT pod templates : when mas_app_id is iot , mas_pod_templates_dir is used with configuration files named ibm-mas-iot-iot.yml , ibm-mas-iot-actions.yml , ibm-mas-iot-auth.yml , ibm-mas-iot-datapower.yml , ibm-mas-iot-devops.yml , ibm-mas-iot-dm.yml , ibm-mas-iot-dsc.yml , ibm-mas-iot-edgeconfig.yml , ibm-mas-iot-fpl.yml , ibm-mas-iot-guardian.yml , ibm-mas-iot-mbgx.yml , ibm-mas-iot-mfgx.yml , ibm-mas-iot-monitor.yml , ibm-mas-iot-orgmgmt.yml , ibm-mas-iot-provision.yml , ibm-mas-iot-registry.yml , ibm-mas-iot-state.yml , and ibm-mas-iot-webui.yml . The content of each file should be the YAML block you wish to be inserted into the IoT CR: ibm-mas-iot-iot.yml is inserted into the main IoT CR spec -> podTemplates , whereas the component ones (e.g., ibm-mas-iot-actions.yml ) go under spec -> components -> {componentName} -> podTemplates . The ibm-mas-iot operator then passes this on to the corresponding component CR when available. See the BestEfforts reference configuration in the MAS CLI for an example of one of the components (actions), and Customizing Pod Templates in the product documentation for full documentation of the supported options. Manage Configuration ¤ Manage pod templates : when mas_app_id is manage , mas_pod_templates_dir is used with a configuration file named ibm-mas-manage-manageapp.yml . The content of the file should be the YAML block you wish to be inserted into the ManageApp CR: it is inserted into the ManageApp CR spec -> podTemplates , and the ibm-mas-manage operator then passes this on to the corresponding deployments when available. For full documentation of the supported options refer to Customizing Pod Templates in the product documentation. mas_appws_upgrade_type ¤ Upgrade strategy for Manage workspace database schema updates — regularUpgrade (standard upgrade with full system downtime) or onlineUpgrade (minimized downtime, requires additional resources and time). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APPWS_UPGRADE_TYPE Default: regularUpgrade regularUpgrade gives a shorter upgrade time but requires full system downtime; onlineUpgrade takes longer but minimizes downtime and requires additional database resources during the upgrade. Applies to Manage application upgrades only — online upgrades require careful planning. For full documentation of upgrade types and requirements, refer to the Manage Upgrade information in the product documentation. Monitor Configuration ¤ mas_app_settings_monitor_deployment_size ¤ Deployment size profile for MAS Monitor, which determines resource allocations and scaling characteristics — dev , small , or large . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_MONITOR_DEPLOYMENT_SIZE Default: dev dev allocates minimal resources suitable for development only, small moderate resources suitable for small to medium production deployments, and large maximum resources suitable for large-scale production deployments with extensive monitoring. Application support: Monitor 8.6+. Ensure your cluster has sufficient resources for the selected size — this cannot be easily changed after deployment without reinstallation. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # Choose which catalog source to use for the MAS install, default to the IBM operator catalog mas_app_catalog_source: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_CATALOG_SOURCE') | default('ibm-operator-catalog', true) }}" # Which MAS channel to subscribe to mas_app_channel: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_CHANNEL') | default('8.x', true) }}" # MAS configuration mas_instance_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_INSTANCE_ID') }}" # MAS configuration - Entitlement mas_entitlement_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME') | default('cp', true) }}" mas_entitlement_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY') }}" # MAS application configuration mas_app_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_ID') }}" # Application Configuration - Spec mas_app_spec: bindings: jdbc: system mongo: system kafka: system settings: messagesight: storage: class: block1000p size: 100Gi deployment: size: medium # Application Configuration - Install Plan mas_app_plan: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_PLAN') | default('full', true) }}" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_install License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: MAS application operator subscription channel, which determines the version stream you will receive updates from — application-specific channels such as 8.6.x , 8.7.x , or 8.8.x for Manage (check the IBM Operator Catalog for currently available channels for your application). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CHANNEL Default: 8.x The channel determines which application version is installed and which automatic updates are applied. Consult the MAS compatibility matrix before selecting a channel to ensure compatibility with your MAS core version, and change channels only during planned upgrade windows — changing channels after installation triggers an upgrade to the latest version in the new channel, which may require reconfiguration and testing.
docs.title: mas_app_channel

docs.text: Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to MAS application resources (e.g., env=prod,team=platform,app=manage ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Use for organizational metadata (e.g., cost-center=engineering , environment=production ), resource tracking, cost allocation, and custom automation or monitoring. Labels can be used for filtering with oc get commands, monitoring queries, and automation scripts, but do not affect application functionality.
docs.title: custom_labels

docs.text: Username for authenticating to IBM Artifactory to access development builds of MAS applications — typically your IBM w3Id. Optional — required when mas_app_catalog_source is set to a development catalog (e.g., ibm-mas-manage-operators ) Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None Without valid credentials, development catalog subscriptions will fail to pull operator images. Not needed for production installations using ibm-operator-catalog , which use mas_entitlement_key instead. Must be set together with artifactory_token .
docs.title: artifactory_username

docs.text: API token for authenticating to IBM Artifactory to access development builds of MAS applications. Optional — required when mas_app_catalog_source is set to a development catalog (e.g., ibm-mas-manage-operators ) Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None Without a valid token, development catalog subscriptions will fail to pull operator images. Must be set together with artifactory_username ; production installations use mas_entitlement_key instead. Warning Keep this token secure and do not commit it to source control. Use environment variables or secure secret management.
docs.title: artifactory_token

docs.text: Username for authenticating to IBM Container Registry to pull MAS application images — cp for production installations with an IBM entitlement key, or your IBM w3Id for development builds. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME Default: cp for production installations Used together with mas_entitlement_key to create image pull secrets for the application namespace; an incorrect username will cause image pull authentication failures.
docs.title: mas_entitlement_username

docs.text: IBM entitlement key for authenticating access to IBM Container Registry to pull MAS application images — a valid, non-expired key with MAS product entitlements, typically starting with eyJ... . Optional — required for production installations using official IBM releases Environment Variable: MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: None (falls back to ibm_entitlement_key / IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY ) Obtain the key from the IBM Container Library at https://myibm.ibm.com/products-services/containerlibrary; for development builds, use your Artifactory API key instead. The key is stored in a Kubernetes secret and used to create image pull secrets for all application pods — invalid or expired keys will cause image pull failures during application installation. Warning Keep this key secure and do not commit it to source control. Use environment variables or secure secret management.
docs.title: mas_entitlement_key

docs.text: Custom YAML specification to override default application configuration settings — a valid YAML dictionary matching the application's Custom Resource specification. Optional Environment Variable: None Default: Application-specific defaults in vars/defaultspecs/{{mas_app_id}}.yml Use for advanced customization scenarios not covered by the standard mas_app_settings_* and mas_app_bindings_* variables; leave unset for standard installations. Warning When set, this completely overrides all other application configuration variables ( mas_app_settings_* , mas_app_bindings_* ) — the role uses this specification directly in the application CR. Incorrect specifications can cause installation failures, so this requires deep knowledge of the application's Custom Resource specification.
docs.title: mas_app_spec

docs.text: Scope for JDBC database configuration binding — either system (shared across all applications) or application (dedicated to this application). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_BINDINGS_JDBC Default: system With system , the application uses the JDBC configuration defined at the MAS instance level (JdbcCfg with scope=system); with application , the application requires its own application-scoped JdbcCfg resource. Most deployments use system for simplified management. Changing this after installation may require reconfiguration of database connections — ensure the appropriate JdbcCfg resource exists at the corresponding scope before changing this value.
docs.title: mas_app_bindings_jdbc

docs.text: Licensing plan/tier for the application installation — application-specific; for example Optimizer supports full and limited (v8.2+, defaulting to full ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_PLAN Default: Application-specific (varies by application) The plan determines which features are available in the application. Set it according to your license entitlements — using a plan not covered by your license may result in compliance issues, with some features disabled or unavailable. Consult your IBM license agreement or contact IBM if you're unsure which plan to use.
docs.title: mas_app_plan

docs.text: Local directory path containing pod template customization files for the application, enabling control over resource limits, node affinity, tolerations, security contexts, and service accounts. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None mas_app_id determines which pod template files are expected — see the IoT and Manage sections below for the file names each application looks for. The files are applied to the application's Custom Resource, affecting how application pods are scheduled and configured; invalid templates can cause pod scheduling failures. For full documentation, see Customizing Pod Templates in the product documentation.
docs.title: mas_pod_templates_dir

docs.text: Storage class for Visual Inspection user data persistent volumes (uploaded images, trained models, and inspection results) — any valid storage class name in your cluster that supports ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_VISUALINSPECTION_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-selected from available ReadWriteMany (RWX) storage classes in the cluster Set explicitly when you have multiple RWX storage classes and want to control which is used, or when auto-selection doesn't choose your preferred class. Important ReadWriteMany (RWX) support is required for Visual Inspection to function correctly. Verify your storage class supports RWX with oc get storageclass before deployment — common RWX storage classes include NFS, CephFS, and cloud provider file storage.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_visualinspection_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the persistent volume for Visual Inspection user data — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 100Gi , 500Gi , 1Ti , 2Ti ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_VISUALINSPECTION_STORAGE_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with large image datasets, many trained models, or long data retention; use the default for development, testing, or small deployments. Insufficient storage will prevent uploading new images or training models — plan for growth, monitor storage usage, and check whether your storage class supports PVC expansion before deployment.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_visualinspection_storage_size

docs.text: Deployment size profile for MAS IoT, which determines resource allocations and scaling characteristics — dev , small , or large . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_DEPLOYMENT_SIZE Default: small dev allocates minimal resources suitable for development only, small moderate resources suitable for small to medium production deployments, and large maximum resources suitable for large-scale production deployments. Application support: IoT 8.6+. Ensure your cluster has sufficient resources for the selected size — this cannot be easily changed after deployment without reinstallation.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size

docs.text: Storage class for IoT Function Pipeline (FPL) component persistent volumes, which store transient state for pipeline processing — any valid storage class name in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional — always required when mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size is not dev Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_FPL_PVC_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-selected from available ReadWriteOnce (RWO) storage classes in the cluster Set explicitly when you have multiple RWO storage classes and want to control which is used, or when auto-selection doesn't choose your preferred class. The storage class determines I/O performance for pipeline state operations. Application support: IoT 8.6+ — verify with oc get storageclass before deployment.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_pvc_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the persistent volume for the IoT FPL pipeline router component's transient state storage — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 50Gi , 100Gi , 200Gi , 500Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_FPL_ROUTER_PVC_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with high pipeline throughput, many concurrent pipelines, or complex pipeline logic; use the default for development, testing, or moderate workloads. Application support: IoT 8.6+. Insufficient storage may cause pipeline execution failures — monitor storage usage and check whether your storage class supports PVC expansion.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_router_pvc_size

docs.text: Size of the persistent volume for the IoT FPL pipeline executor component's transient state and intermediate data — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 50Gi , 100Gi , 200Gi , 500Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_FPL_EXECUTOR_PVC_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with high data processing volumes or pipelines that process large datasets; use the default for development, testing, or moderate workloads. Application support: IoT 8.6+. Insufficient storage may cause pipeline execution or data processing failures — monitor storage usage and check whether your storage class supports PVC expansion.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_iot_fpl_executor_pvc_size

docs.text: Storage class for IoT MQTT broker (MessageSight) persistent volumes, which store message queues, broker state, and retained messages — any valid storage class name in your cluster that supports ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode. Optional — always required when mas_app_settings_iot_deployment_size is not dev Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_MQTTBROKER_PVC_STORAGE_CLASS Default: Auto-selected from available ReadWriteOnce (RWO) storage classes in the cluster Set explicitly when you have multiple RWO storage classes, when auto-selection doesn't choose your preferred class, or when you need specific performance characteristics for MQTT message handling. Application support: IoT 8.3+ — verify with oc get storageclass before deployment.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_iot_mqttbroker_pvc_storage_class

docs.text: Size of the persistent volume for the IoT MQTT broker (MessageSight) component — any valid Kubernetes storage size (e.g., 50Gi , 100Gi , 200Gi , 500Gi ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_IOT_MQTTBROKER_PVC_SIZE Default: 100Gi Increase for production environments with many connected devices, high message volumes, long message retention, or devices that frequently disconnect and require message queuing; use the default for development, testing, or moderate device counts. Application support: IoT 8.3+. Insufficient storage may cause message loss, device connection failures, or broker instability — monitor storage usage to prevent message queue overflow. IoT pod templates : when mas_app_id is iot , mas_pod_templates_dir is used with configuration files named ibm-mas-iot-iot.yml , ibm-mas-iot-actions.yml , ibm-mas-iot-auth.yml , ibm-mas-iot-datapower.yml , ibm-mas-iot-devops.yml , ibm-mas-iot-dm.yml , ibm-mas-iot-dsc.yml , ibm-mas-iot-edgeconfig.yml , ibm-mas-iot-fpl.yml , ibm-mas-iot-guardian.yml , ibm-mas-iot-mbgx.yml , ibm-mas-iot-mfgx.yml , ibm-mas-iot-monitor.yml , ibm-mas-iot-orgmgmt.yml , ibm-mas-iot-provision.yml , ibm-mas-iot-registry.yml , ibm-mas-iot-state.yml , and ibm-mas-iot-webui.yml . The content of each file should be the YAML block you wish to be inserted into the IoT CR: ibm-mas-iot-iot.yml is inserted into the main IoT CR spec -> podTemplates , whereas the component ones (e.g., ibm-mas-iot-actions.yml ) go under spec -> components -> {componentName} -> podTemplates . The ibm-mas-iot operator then passes this on to the corresponding component CR when available. See the BestEfforts reference configuration in the MAS CLI for an example of one of the components (actions), and Customizing Pod Templates in the product documentation for full documentation of the supported options.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_iot_mqttbroker_pvc_size

docs.text: Manage pod templates : when mas_app_id is manage , mas_pod_templates_dir is used with a configuration file named ibm-mas-manage-manageapp.yml . The content of the file should be the YAML block you wish to be inserted into the ManageApp CR: it is inserted into the ManageApp CR spec -> podTemplates , and the ibm-mas-manage operator then passes this on to the corresponding deployments when available. For full documentation of the supported options refer to Customizing Pod Templates in the product documentation.
docs.title: Manage Configuration

docs.text: Upgrade strategy for Manage workspace database schema updates — regularUpgrade (standard upgrade with full system downtime) or onlineUpgrade (minimized downtime, requires additional resources and time). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APPWS_UPGRADE_TYPE Default: regularUpgrade regularUpgrade gives a shorter upgrade time but requires full system downtime; onlineUpgrade takes longer but minimizes downtime and requires additional database resources during the upgrade. Applies to Manage application upgrades only — online upgrades require careful planning. For full documentation of upgrade types and requirements, refer to the Manage Upgrade information in the product documentation.
docs.title: mas_appws_upgrade_type

docs.text: Deployment size profile for MAS Monitor, which determines resource allocations and scaling characteristics — dev , small , or large . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_SETTINGS_MONITOR_DEPLOYMENT_SIZE Default: dev dev allocates minimal resources suitable for development only, small moderate resources suitable for small to medium production deployments, and large maximum resources suitable for large-scale production deployments with extensive monitoring. Application support: Monitor 8.6+. Ensure your cluster has sufficient resources for the selected size — this cannot be easily changed after deployment without reinstallation.
docs.title: mas_app_settings_monitor_deployment_size

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # Choose which catalog source to use for the MAS install, default to the IBM operator catalog mas_app_catalog_source: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_CATALOG_SOURCE') | default('ibm-operator-catalog', true) }}" # Which MAS channel to subscribe to mas_app_channel: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_CHANNEL') | default('8.x', true) }}" # MAS configuration mas_instance_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_INSTANCE_ID') }}" # MAS configuration - Entitlement mas_entitlement_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_USERNAME') | default('cp', true) }}" mas_entitlement_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY') }}" # MAS application configuration mas_app_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_ID') }}" # Application Configuration - Spec mas_app_spec: bindings: jdbc: system mongo: system kafka: system settings: messagesight: storage: class: block1000p size: 100Gi deployment: size: medium # Application Configuration - Install Plan mas_app_plan: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_PLAN') | default('full', true) }}" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_install

docs.text: suite_app_restore ¤ Restore MAS Applications Important Supported only for MAS 9.1.x. Restore can only be made to an instance with the same MAS instance ID as the backup. Overview ¤ This role supports restoring MAS application resources and data from backups created by the suite_app_backup role. Currently supported applications: manage : Restores Manage namespace resources (CRs, secrets, subscriptions) and persistent volume data facilities : Restores Facilities namespace resources (CRs, secrets, subscriptions) and persistent volume data Future support planned for: iot , monitor , health , optimizer , visualinspection The restore process follows these phases: Phase 1 : Restore Kubernetes resources like Project, Secrets, Configmaps, Subscription, Certificates and ManageApp CR (not ManageWorkspace CR) Phase 2 : Check if ManageWorkspace CR is already available Phase 3 : Restore persistent volume data If ManageWorkspace exists: Scale it down, restore data, then continue If ManageWorkspace doesn't exist: Create PVCs, create dummy pod, restore data, delete dummy pod Phase 4 : Restore ManageWorkspace CR Phase 5 : Wait for Manage deployment to be activated Important An application backup can only be restored to an instance with the same MAS instance ID This role restores application resources and PV data only. Database restores must be performed separately using the appropriate database restore role For Manage, see the db2 role for database restore The restore process is designed to be idempotent and can handle both fresh installations and existing deployments Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_app_id Yes None mas_instance_id Yes None mas_backup_dir Yes None mas_app_backup_version Yes None mas_workspace_id No Auto-discovered mas_app_restore_include_pvc No true mas_app_restore_wait_retries No 180 mas_app_restore_wait_delay No 360 override_storageclass No false mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwx No None mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwo No None helper_pod_image No registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi:latest The two custom storage class variables only take effect when override_storageclass is enabled. Restore Target ¤ mas_app_id ¤ MAS application to restore — manage or facilities are the currently supported applications. Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None Future support is planned for iot , monitor , health , optimizer , and visualinspection . mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance ID of the restore target — must match the instance ID used when the backup was created. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None An application backup can only be restored to an instance with the same MAS instance ID as the backup. mas_backup_dir ¤ Directory where backups are stored — for example /backup/mas . The role looks for the backup version subdirectory within this location. Required Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None mas_app_backup_version ¤ Backup version to restore, matching the version identifier used during backup — for example 20240315-143022 or v1.0-prod . Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_BACKUP_VERSION Default: None mas_workspace_id ¤ MAS workspace ID for the restore action. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: Auto-discovered from the mas.ibm.com/workspaceId label on the workspace backup CR Only set it explicitly if you want to override the value discovered from the backup. Restore Behavior ¤ mas_app_restore_include_pvc ¤ Controls whether persistent volume data is restored — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_RESTORE_INCLUDE_PVC Default: true When false , only namespace resources (CRs, secrets, subscriptions) are restored and the PVC data restore is skipped. mas_app_restore_wait_retries ¤ Number of retries when waiting for the workspace to become ready after the restore. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_RESTORE_WAIT_RETRIES Default: 180 Together with mas_app_restore_wait_delay this defines the total wait time — increase both for large or slow deployments. mas_app_restore_wait_delay ¤ Delay in seconds between status checks when waiting for the workspace to become ready. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_RESTORE_WAIT_DELAY Default: 360 for Manage, 180 for Facilities The default differs by application: with the default retries (180), Manage waits up to 18 hours (180 × 360 seconds) and Facilities up to 9 hours (180 × 180 seconds). Storage Class Override ¤ override_storageclass ¤ Enables storage class override during restore — true or false . When enabled, the restore process uses custom storage classes instead of the storage classes from the backup. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_STORAGECLASS Default: false Useful when restoring to a different cluster with different storage classes. PVCs are mapped to storage classes based on their access mode: ReadWriteMany (RWX) uses mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwx and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) uses mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwo ; if a custom class is not specified, the cluster's default storage class is used automatically. mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwx ¤ Custom storage class for PVCs with ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode when override_storageclass is enabled — for example ocs-storagecluster-cephfs . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWX Default: None (uses the cluster's default storage class) mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwo ¤ Custom storage class for PVCs with ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode when override_storageclass is enabled — for example ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWO Default: None (uses the cluster's default storage class) Helper Pod ¤ helper_pod_image ¤ Image used by the PVC-restore helper pod, which is deployed in the application's namespace to mount PVC volumes and extract the PVC backup to the mounted path. Optional Environment Variable: HELPER_POD_IMAGE Default: registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi:latest The image must have tar installed for oc cp to work. What Gets Restored ¤ Manage Application ¤ When restoring the Manage application, the following resources are restored: Namespace Resources (Phase 1 & 4): Project (namespace) Encryption secrets Certificates with mas.ibm.com/instanceId label IBM entitlement secret All referenced secrets Subscription and OperatorGroup ManageApp CR (Phase 1) ManageWorkspace CR (Phase 4) Persistent Volume Data (Phase 3): All persistent volumes defined in spec.settings.deployment.persistentVolumes Data is restored from compressed tar.gz archives Each PVC's mount path is restored separately Archives are read from the data subdirectory NOT Restored (must be restored separately): Manage database (Db2) - use the db2 role Suite-level resources - use the suite_restore role Facilities Application ¤ When restoring the Facilities application, the following resources are restored: Namespace Resources (Phase 1 & 4): Project (namespace) Encryption secrets Certificates with mas.ibm.com/instanceId label IBM entitlement secret All referenced secrets Subscription and OperatorGroup FacilitiesApp CR (Phase 1) FacilitiesWorkspace CR (Phase 4) Persistent Volume Data (Phase 3): All persistent volumes defined in spec.settings.deployment.persistentVolumes Data is restored from compressed tar.gz archives Each PVC is restored with special handling for extracted data: Extracts tar.gz to temporary location Moves config files to appropriate config directory Moves userfiles to userfiles directory Preserves original file ownership Archives are read from the data subdirectory NOT Restored (must be restored separately): Facilities database (Db2) - use the db2 role Suite-level resources - use the suite_restore role How Persistent Volume Restore Works ¤ The role intelligently handles PV restoration based on whether ManageWorkspace CR is already deployed: Scenario 1: ManageWorkspace CR Does Not Exist (Fresh Restore) ¤ Read Configuration : Extracts PVC configuration from ManageWorkspace CR backup Create PVCs : Creates all PVCs defined in the backup Create Dummy Pod : Creates a temporary pod that mounts all PVCs Restore Data : Copies tar.gz archives to the pod and extracts them to mount paths Cleanup : Deletes the dummy pod Deploy CR : Restores the ManageWorkspace CR Wait : Waits for Manage deployment to be activated Scenario 2: ManageWorkspace CR Already Exists (Re-restore/Update) ¤ Scale Down : Sets ManageWorkspace spec.settings.deployment.mode to down Wait : Waits for workspace to scale down Find Pod : Locates UI, ALL, or maxinst pod for data access Restore Data : Copies tar.gz archives to the pod and extracts them to mount paths Update CR : Restores the ManageWorkspace CR (which will scale back up) Wait : Waits for Manage deployment to be activated Dummy Pod Specification ¤ When a dummy pod is created for restoration, it uses: Image : helper_pod_image (default registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi:latest ) Command : sleep infinity (keeps pod running) Volumes : All PVCs from ManageWorkspace CR configuration Labels : Tagged with instance ID and workspace ID for easy identification Manage Restore Process Phases ¤ Phase 1: Restore Resources Until ManageApp CR ¤ Restores all namespace resources except ManageWorkspace CR Includes: ManageApp, secrets, certificates, subscriptions, operator groups Waits for ManageApp CR to become ready Auto-discovers and restores referenced secrets Phase 2: Check ManageWorkspace Status ¤ Checks if ManageWorkspace CR already exists If exists: Sets spec.settings.deployment.mode to down and waits for scale down If not exists: Proceeds to create PVCs and dummy pod Phase 3: Restore Persistent Volume Data ¤ Reads PVC configuration from ManageWorkspace CR backup Creates PVCs if needed (when ManageWorkspace doesn't exist) Creates dummy pod or uses existing server bundle pod Restores data from tar.gz archives to each PVC Cleans up dummy pod if created Phase 4: Restore ManageWorkspace CR ¤ Restores the ManageWorkspace CR This triggers the Manage deployment to start/restart Phase 5: Wait for Deployment Activation ¤ Monitors ManageWorkspace CR status Waits for Ready condition to be True Configurable timeout and delay between checks Facilities Restore Process Phases ¤ Phase 1: Restore Resources Until FacilitiesApp CR ¤ Restores all namespace resources except FacilitiesWorkspace CR Includes: FacilitiesApp, secrets, certificates, subscriptions, operator groups Waits for FacilitiesApp CR to become ready Auto-discovers and restores referenced secrets Phase 2: Check FacilitiesWorkspace Status ¤ Checks if FacilitiesWorkspace CR already exists If exists: Proceeds to scale down deployments and statefulsets using pod templates If not exists: Deploys FacilitiesWorkspace CR and waits for CR to be ready and proceeds to scale down deployments and statefulsets replicas using pod templates Phase 3: Restore Persistent Volume Data ¤ PVC backup tar.gz are named after the pvc names PVCs are created by the workspace operator when CR was deployed Create dummy pods to mount to each of the PVCs Restore data from tar.gz archives to each PVC Clean up dummy pods Phase 4: Restore FacilitiesWorkspace CR ¤ Revert the podtemplates changes done in phase 2 Wait for deployments and statefulsets to be ready Expected Backup Directory Structure ¤ The role expects the backup directory to have the following structure: <mas_backup_dir>/ ├── backup-<version>-app-manage/ │ ├── resources/ │ │ ├── projects │ │ │ └── mas-<instance_id>-manage.yaml │ | ├── secrets │ │ │ └── <secret1_name>.yaml │ │ │ └── <secret2_name>.yaml │ | ├── configmaps │ │ │ └── <configmap1_name>.yaml │ │ │ └── <configmap2_name>.yaml │ ├── subscriptions │ │ │ └── <subscription_name>.yaml │ │ └── ... (other resources) │ └── data/ │ ├── <pvc-name-1>.tar.gz │ └── <pvc-name-2>.tar.gz └── backup-<version>-app-facilities/ ├── resources/ │ ├── projects │ │ └── mas-<instance_id>-facilities.yaml │ ├── secrets │ │ └── <secret1_name>.yaml │ │ └── <secret2_name>.yaml │ ├── configmaps │ │ └── <configmap1_name>.yaml │ │ └── <configmap2_name>.yaml │ ├── subscriptions │ │ └── <subscription_name>.yaml │ └── ... (other resources) └── data/ ├── <pvc-name-1>.tar.gz └── <pvc-name-2>.tar.gz Example Playbooks ¤ Basic Restore ¤ Restore Manage namespace resources and persistent volumes from a backup. The workspace ID is automatically derived from the backup CR: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_app_id: manage mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas mas_app_backup_version: "20240315-143022" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_restore Restore with Custom Timeout ¤ Restore with a custom wait timeout for large deployments: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_app_id: manage mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas mas_app_backup_version: "prod-backup-20240315" mas_app_restore_wait_retries: 180 mas_app_restore_wait_delay: 360 # Check 6 minutes roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_restore Restore Facilities Application ¤ Restore Facilities namespace resources and persistent volumes from a backup: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_app_id: facilities mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas mas_app_backup_version: "20240315-143022" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_restore Complete Restore Workflow - Manage ¤ Complete workflow including database restore: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas backup_version: "20240315-143022" tasks: # 1. Restore Db2 database first - name: "Restore Manage database" include_role: name: ibm.mas_devops.db2 vars: db2_action: restore db2_backup_version: "{{ backup_version }}" # 2. Restore Manage application - name: "Restore Manage application" include_role: name: ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_restore vars: mas_app_id: manage mas_app_backup_version: "{{ backup_version }}" Complete Restore Workflow - Facilities ¤ Complete workflow including database restore: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas backup_version: "20240315-143022" tasks: # 1. Restore Db2 database first - name: "Restore Facilities database" include_role: name: ibm.mas_devops.db2 vars: db2_action: restore db2_backup_version: "{{ backup_version }}" # 2. Restore Facilities application - name: "Restore Facilities application" include_role: name: ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_restore vars: mas_app_id: facilities mas_app_backup_version: "{{ backup_version }}" Restore with Storage Class Override ¤ Restore to a different cluster with different storage classes: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_app_id: manage mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas mas_app_backup_version: "20240315-143022" # Enable storage class override override_storageclass: true # Specify custom storage classes mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwo: "ocs-storagecluster-cephfs" mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwx: "ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_restore Restore with Storage Class Override Using Default Classes ¤ Restore with override enabled but using cluster's default storage classes: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_app_id: manage mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas mas_app_backup_version: "20240315-143022" # Enable storage class override without specifying custom classes # Will automatically use the cluster's default storage class override_storageclass: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_restore Troubleshooting ¤ Restore Fails at Phase 1 ¤ Issue : Resources fail to restore in Phase 1 Solution : Check that the backup directory exists and contains the expected files Verify namespace exists: oc get namespace mas-<instance_id>-manage Check for conflicting resources: oc get manageapp,subscription -n mas-<instance_id>-manage Dummy Pod Fails to Start ¤ Issue : Dummy pod remains in Pending state Solution : Check PVC status: oc get pvc -n mas-<instance_id>-manage Verify storage class exists and can provision volumes Check pod events: oc describe pod <pod-name> -n mas-<instance_id>-manage PV Data Restore Fails ¤ Issue : Data extraction fails in the pod Solution : Verify tar.gz archives are not corrupted Check pod has sufficient disk space Verify mount paths are accessible in the pod ManageWorkspace Never Becomes Ready ¤ Issue : Phase 5 times out waiting for ManageWorkspace Solution : Check ManageWorkspace status: oc describe manageworkspace -n mas-<instance_id>-manage Verify database is accessible and restored Check pod logs: oc logs -l mas.ibm.com/appType=serverBundle -n mas-<instance_id>-manage Increase mas_app_restore_wait_retries and mas_app_restore_wait_delay values if deployment is slow Notes ¤ Workspace ID Auto-Discovery : mas_workspace_id is automatically derived from the mas.ibm.com/workspaceId label on the workspace backup CR. You only need to set MAS_WORKSPACE_ID explicitly if you want to override the value from the backup Database Restore : This role does NOT restore application databases. Use the db2 role to restore Db2 databases separately, and do this BEFORE running the application restore Suite Resources : This role restores application-specific resources only. For suite-level resources (Suite CR, workspace CRs, etc.), use the suite_restore role Instance ID Match : The restore must be performed on a cluster with the same MAS instance ID as the backup Idempotent : The restore process is idempotent and can be run multiple times Dummy Pod : When workspace CR doesn't exist, a temporary pod is created for data restoration and automatically cleaned up Scale Down : When workspace CR exists, it's automatically scaled down before data restoration Automatic Detection : Persistent volumes are automatically detected from the workspace CR backup Compression : All PV data is stored as compressed tar.gz archives Wait Time : Default wait timeout varies by application (Manage: 18 hours, Facilities: 9 hours), but can be adjusted based on deployment size Prerequisites : Ensure the MAS operator and application operator are installed before running restore Storage Class Override : When restoring to a different cluster with different storage classes, enable override_storageclass to automatically map PVCs to appropriate storage classes based on access modes (RWX/RWO) Default Storage Classes : If override_storageclass is enabled but custom storage classes are not specified, the cluster's default storage class will be used automatically Access Mode Mapping : The role intelligently assigns storage classes based on PVC access modes - RWX (ReadWriteMany) uses mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwx and RWO (ReadWriteOnce) uses mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwo License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: This role supports restoring MAS application resources and data from backups created by the suite_app_backup role. Currently supported applications: manage : Restores Manage namespace resources (CRs, secrets, subscriptions) and persistent volume data facilities : Restores Facilities namespace resources (CRs, secrets, subscriptions) and persistent volume data Future support planned for: iot , monitor , health , optimizer , visualinspection The restore process follows these phases: Phase 1 : Restore Kubernetes resources like Project, Secrets, Configmaps, Subscription, Certificates and ManageApp CR (not ManageWorkspace CR) Phase 2 : Check if ManageWorkspace CR is already available Phase 3 : Restore persistent volume data If ManageWorkspace exists: Scale it down, restore data, then continue If ManageWorkspace doesn't exist: Create PVCs, create dummy pod, restore data, delete dummy pod Phase 4 : Restore ManageWorkspace CR Phase 5 : Wait for Manage deployment to be activated Important An application backup can only be restored to an instance with the same MAS instance ID This role restores application resources and PV data only. Database restores must be performed separately using the appropriate database restore role For Manage, see the db2 role for database restore The restore process is designed to be idempotent and can handle both fresh installations and existing deployments
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: MAS application to restore — manage or facilities are the currently supported applications. Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None Future support is planned for iot , monitor , health , optimizer , and visualinspection .
docs.title: mas_app_id

docs.text: MAS instance ID of the restore target — must match the instance ID used when the backup was created. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None An application backup can only be restored to an instance with the same MAS instance ID as the backup.
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: Directory where backups are stored — for example /backup/mas . The role looks for the backup version subdirectory within this location. Required Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None
docs.title: mas_backup_dir

docs.text: Backup version to restore, matching the version identifier used during backup — for example 20240315-143022 or v1.0-prod . Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_BACKUP_VERSION Default: None
docs.title: mas_app_backup_version

docs.text: MAS workspace ID for the restore action. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: Auto-discovered from the mas.ibm.com/workspaceId label on the workspace backup CR Only set it explicitly if you want to override the value discovered from the backup.
docs.title: mas_workspace_id

docs.text: Controls whether persistent volume data is restored — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_RESTORE_INCLUDE_PVC Default: true When false , only namespace resources (CRs, secrets, subscriptions) are restored and the PVC data restore is skipped.
docs.title: mas_app_restore_include_pvc

docs.text: Number of retries when waiting for the workspace to become ready after the restore. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_RESTORE_WAIT_RETRIES Default: 180 Together with mas_app_restore_wait_delay this defines the total wait time — increase both for large or slow deployments.
docs.title: mas_app_restore_wait_retries

docs.text: Delay in seconds between status checks when waiting for the workspace to become ready. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_RESTORE_WAIT_DELAY Default: 360 for Manage, 180 for Facilities The default differs by application: with the default retries (180), Manage waits up to 18 hours (180 × 360 seconds) and Facilities up to 9 hours (180 × 180 seconds).
docs.title: mas_app_restore_wait_delay

docs.text: Enables storage class override during restore — true or false . When enabled, the restore process uses custom storage classes instead of the storage classes from the backup. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_STORAGECLASS Default: false Useful when restoring to a different cluster with different storage classes. PVCs are mapped to storage classes based on their access mode: ReadWriteMany (RWX) uses mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwx and ReadWriteOnce (RWO) uses mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwo ; if a custom class is not specified, the cluster's default storage class is used automatically.
docs.title: override_storageclass

docs.text: Custom storage class for PVCs with ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode when override_storageclass is enabled — for example ocs-storagecluster-cephfs . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWX Default: None (uses the cluster's default storage class)
docs.title: mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwx

docs.text: Custom storage class for PVCs with ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode when override_storageclass is enabled — for example ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CUSTOM_STORAGE_CLASS_RWO Default: None (uses the cluster's default storage class)
docs.title: mas_app_custom_storage_class_rwo

docs.text: Image used by the PVC-restore helper pod, which is deployed in the application's namespace to mount PVC volumes and extract the PVC backup to the mounted path. Optional Environment Variable: HELPER_POD_IMAGE Default: registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi:latest The image must have tar installed for oc cp to work.
docs.title: helper_pod_image

docs.text: When restoring the Manage application, the following resources are restored: Namespace Resources (Phase 1 & 4): Project (namespace) Encryption secrets Certificates with mas.ibm.com/instanceId label IBM entitlement secret All referenced secrets Subscription and OperatorGroup ManageApp CR (Phase 1) ManageWorkspace CR (Phase 4) Persistent Volume Data (Phase 3): All persistent volumes defined in spec.settings.deployment.persistentVolumes Data is restored from compressed tar.gz archives Each PVC's mount path is restored separately Archives are read from the data subdirectory NOT Restored (must be restored separately): Manage database (Db2) - use the db2 role Suite-level resources - use the suite_restore role
docs.title: Manage Application

docs.text: When restoring the Facilities application, the following resources are restored: Namespace Resources (Phase 1 & 4): Project (namespace) Encryption secrets Certificates with mas.ibm.com/instanceId label IBM entitlement secret All referenced secrets Subscription and OperatorGroup FacilitiesApp CR (Phase 1) FacilitiesWorkspace CR (Phase 4) Persistent Volume Data (Phase 3): All persistent volumes defined in spec.settings.deployment.persistentVolumes Data is restored from compressed tar.gz archives Each PVC is restored with special handling for extracted data: Extracts tar.gz to temporary location Moves config files to appropriate config directory Moves userfiles to userfiles directory Preserves original file ownership Archives are read from the data subdirectory NOT Restored (must be restored separately): Facilities database (Db2) - use the db2 role Suite-level resources - use the suite_restore role
docs.title: Facilities Application

docs.text: The role intelligently handles PV restoration based on whether ManageWorkspace CR is already deployed:
docs.title: How Persistent Volume Restore Works

docs.text: Read Configuration : Extracts PVC configuration from ManageWorkspace CR backup Create PVCs : Creates all PVCs defined in the backup Create Dummy Pod : Creates a temporary pod that mounts all PVCs Restore Data : Copies tar.gz archives to the pod and extracts them to mount paths Cleanup : Deletes the dummy pod Deploy CR : Restores the ManageWorkspace CR Wait : Waits for Manage deployment to be activated
docs.title: Scenario 1: ManageWorkspace CR Does Not Exist (Fresh Restore)

docs.text: Scale Down : Sets ManageWorkspace spec.settings.deployment.mode to down Wait : Waits for workspace to scale down Find Pod : Locates UI, ALL, or maxinst pod for data access Restore Data : Copies tar.gz archives to the pod and extracts them to mount paths Update CR : Restores the ManageWorkspace CR (which will scale back up) Wait : Waits for Manage deployment to be activated
docs.title: Scenario 2: ManageWorkspace CR Already Exists (Re-restore/Update)

docs.text: When a dummy pod is created for restoration, it uses: Image : helper_pod_image (default registry.redhat.io/ubi9/ubi:latest ) Command : sleep infinity (keeps pod running) Volumes : All PVCs from ManageWorkspace CR configuration Labels : Tagged with instance ID and workspace ID for easy identification
docs.title: Dummy Pod Specification

docs.text: Checks if ManageWorkspace CR already exists If exists: Sets spec.settings.deployment.mode to down and waits for scale down If not exists: Proceeds to create PVCs and dummy pod

docs.text: Reads PVC configuration from ManageWorkspace CR backup Creates PVCs if needed (when ManageWorkspace doesn't exist) Creates dummy pod or uses existing server bundle pod Restores data from tar.gz archives to each PVC Cleans up dummy pod if created

docs.text: Restores the ManageWorkspace CR This triggers the Manage deployment to start/restart

docs.text: Monitors ManageWorkspace CR status Waits for Ready condition to be True Configurable timeout and delay between checks
docs.title: Phase 5: Wait for Deployment Activation

docs.text: suite_app_rollback ¤ Roll back Maximo Application Suite applications to earlier versions when issues are encountered after upgrades. This role provides a safe rollback mechanism with built-in compatibility validation to ensure the target version is supported for rollback from the current version and compatible with the running MAS core platform. Important : Currently designed for Manage application only. Rollback capability is available in MAS 8.7 and later versions. Each version defines a set of supported rollback targets (e.g., from 8.7.x to 8.7.0). The role performs comprehensive validation before rollback and monitors the reconciliation process to ensure successful completion at the target version. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_app_id Yes None mas_app_version Conditional None rollback_mas_app No true verify_app_version No false mas_rollback_dryrun No false skip_compatibility_check No false mas_app_version is only required when rollback_mas_app or verify_app_version is true . Instance and Application ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier where the application rollback will be performed — typically 3-12 lowercase alphanumeric characters matching an existing MAS instance with the application installed. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The rollback operation targets the application in the mas-<instance-id>-<app-id> namespace; the value is case-sensitive and must match the instance ID used during MAS installation. mas_app_id ¤ MAS application identifier to roll back. Currently only manage (Maximo Manage) is supported; future versions may support additional applications. Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None Determines which application namespace and resources are targeted for rollback. The application must be installed and running before rollback, and rollback capability requires MAS 8.7 or later. mas_app_version ¤ Target version to roll back to — for example 8.7.0 , 8.7.1 , or 8.8.0 . Required when rollback_mas_app or verify_app_version is true Environment Variable: MAS_APP_VERSION Default: None The version must be a supported rollback target from the current version (each MAS version defines its own set), compatible with the running MAS core platform version, and available in the configured catalog source. Built-in validation prevents unsupported rollback paths — in most cases you cannot roll back across major version boundaries. Consider database schema compatibility when rolling back, and verify rollback compatibility in IBM documentation before proceeding. Warning Always back up your data before performing rollback operations. Rollback Behavior ¤ rollback_mas_app ¤ Controls whether the role performs the actual rollback or only validation checks — true to perform the rollback (default), false for validation only with no changes made. Optional Environment Variable: ROLLBACK_MAS_APP Default: true Set to false for a dry-run check of rollback feasibility before execution; validation includes compatibility checks and version availability. Combine with verify_app_version for post-rollback verification. verify_app_version ¤ Verify that the current application version matches the specified target version — true to check, false to skip (default). No changes are made to the application. Optional Environment Variable: VERIFY_APP_VERSION Default: false Useful for post-rollback verification in automation pipelines, and can be used independently of the rollback operation: set rollback_mas_app=false and verify_app_version=true for verification-only mode. mas_rollback_dryrun ¤ Dry-run mode for rollback operations — true to run all validation checks without executing the rollback, false for normal operation (default). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ROLLBACK_DRYRUN Default: false Recommended before an actual rollback: all compatibility checks and validations are performed and any errors reported, with no changes made to the application or cluster. skip_compatibility_check ¤ Bypass the built-in compatibility validation between the target rollback version and the current MAS core platform version — true to skip the checks, false to perform them (default, recommended). Optional Environment Variable: SKIP_COMPATIBILITY_CHECK Default: false Warning Skipping compatibility checks can allow unsupported rollback operations that may cause system instability, application failures, or data corruption. Only use this when you have verified compatibility through other means or are following IBM support guidance. Example Playbook ¤ Automatic Target Selection ¤ Running this playbook will rollback Manage Application to the 8.7.1 version. If you run this playbook when you are already on the same version it will take no action. - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: instance1 mas_app_id: manage mas_app_version: 8.7.1 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_rollback Verify Manage App Version ¤ Running this playbook will attempt to verify the current version of Manage Application matches with the specified version. - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: instance1 mas_app_id: manage mas_app_version: 8.7.1 rollback_mas_app: False verify_app_version: True roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_rollback License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: Target version to roll back to — for example 8.7.0 , 8.7.1 , or 8.8.0 . docs.text: suite_app_uninstall ¤ Uninstall Maximo Application Suite applications from a MAS instance. This role provides a clean removal process for MAS applications, removing all application-specific resources, configurations, and namespaces while preserving the MAS core platform and other applications. The role supports uninstallation of all MAS applications including Assist, Health, IoT, Manage, Monitor, Optimizer, Predict, Visual Inspection, and Facilities (TRIRIGA). Warning Application uninstallation is permanent and cannot be undone. Back up any critical data before proceeding — data in external databases (for example the Manage database) is not removed by this role, but everything in the application namespace is. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_app_id Yes None Application Selection ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier from which the application will be uninstalled (typically 3-12 lowercase alphanumeric characters). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Must match the instance ID used during MAS installation; the value is case-sensitive. The uninstall targets the application in the mas-<instance-id>-<app-id> namespace — all resources in that namespace are removed. Other applications in the same instance are not affected. mas_app_id ¤ MAS application identifier to be uninstalled. Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None Valid values: assist (Maximo Assist), health (Maximo Health, formerly Predict), iot (Maximo IoT), manage (Maximo Manage), monitor (Maximo Monitor), optimizer (Maximo Optimizer), predict (Maximo Predict), visualinspection (Maximo Visual Inspection), facilities (Maximo Facilities, TRIRIGA). Uninstalling removes the application namespace and all contained resources, application custom resources (e.g. ManageApp, IoTApp), application-specific configurations, and workspaces. If you may need to reinstall later, consider deactivating the application instead. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # MAS configuration mas_instance_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_INSTANCE_ID') }}" # MAS application configuration mas_app_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_APP_ID') }}" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_uninstall License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: suite_app_upgrade ¤ This role will upgrade the subscription channel for an installed MAS application after validating: That the application is installed and in a healthy state That the new version of the application can be upgraded to from the existing version That the new version of the application is compatible with the running MAS core platform Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_app_id Yes None mas_app_channel Yes None mas_upgrade_dryrun No false skip_compatibility_check No false Upgrade Target ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier containing the application to upgrade — a lowercase alphanumeric string, 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , inst1 ), matching the instance ID from the MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The role uses this to locate the application installation and validate that the application is installed and healthy in the instance before proceeding with the upgrade; an incorrect instance ID will cause the upgrade to fail. mas_app_id ¤ MAS application identifier to upgrade — a valid MAS application ID such as iot , manage , monitor , predict , health , assist , visualinspection , or optimizer . Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_ID Default: None Must match an installed application in the instance, in a healthy state. The role performs comprehensive validation — application health, upgrade path compatibility, and MAS core platform compatibility — before upgrading the application's subscription channel. mas_app_channel ¤ Target subscription channel for the application upgrade — a valid channel for the application representing a newer version than currently installed (e.g. 8.5.x , 8.6.x , 8.7.x for IoT; 8.4.x , 8.5.x , 8.6.x for Manage). Required Environment Variable: MAS_APP_CHANNEL Default: None Before upgrading, the role validates that a supported upgrade path exists from the current version and that the target version is compatible with the running MAS core platform. The role will fail if the upgrade path is not supported or the target version is incompatible. Upgrade Validation ¤ mas_upgrade_dryrun ¤ Dry-run mode, which performs all validation checks (health check, compatibility check, upgrade path validation) without making any changes to the installation — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_UPGRADE_DRYRUN Default: false When false , validation runs and the upgrade is executed if validation passes. Dry-run mode is highly recommended before production upgrades to identify potential issues while testing and planning upgrade paths. skip_compatibility_check ¤ Whether to skip the compatibility validation that checks the target channel against the current MAS and application versions — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: SKIP_COMPATIBILITY_CHECK Default: false Warning Skipping compatibility checks can lead to failed upgrades or unstable installations. Only set this to true in exceptional cases where you have manually verified that the upgrade path is supported — the default validation protects against incompatible upgrades. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: instance1 mas_app_id: iot mas_app_channel: 8.5.x roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_app_upgrade License ¤ EPL-2.0
