docs.text: suite_backup ¤ Backup MAS Core Overview ¤ This role supports backing up MAS Core namespace resources and supporting resources in other namespaces; supports creating on-demand full backups. Important Supported only for MAS 9.1.x. Backup can only be restored to an instance with the same MAS instance ID. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_backup_dir Yes None suite_backup_version No YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS timestamp include_sls No true include_dro No true Backup Target and Version ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ The instance ID of the Maximo Application Suite installation to backup. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None mas_backup_dir ¤ The local directory path where backup files will be stored, for example /tmp/mas_backups . Required Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None suite_backup_version ¤ Set a version to override the default YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS timestamp version used in the name of the backup file, for example 20260116-130937 . Optional Environment Variable: SUITE_BACKUP_VERSION Default: YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS timestamp Backup Content ¤ include_sls ¤ Controls whether to include the Suite SLS (Suite License Service) configuration in the backup archive. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_SLS Default: true If you plan to install a new SLS in any recovery action then you should set this to false . include_dro ¤ Controls whether to include the Suite DRO configuration in the backup archive. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_DRO Default: true If you plan to install a new DRO in any recovery action then you should set this to false . Backup Operations ¤ This section provides comprehensive information about MAS Core backup operations. Overview ¤ The MAS Core backup operation creates a comprehensive backup of your MAS Core installation, including all namespace resources and supporting resources in other namespaces. This backup can be restored using the suite_restore role. Important : Backup can only be restored to an instance with the same MAS instance ID. What Gets Backed Up ¤ The MAS Core backup operation captures all critical resources needed to restore a complete MAS Core instance: Core Namespace Resources ( mas-{instance-id}-core ): Projects/Namespaces : The MAS Core namespace Secrets : Superuser credentials ( {instance-id}-credentials-superuser ) IBM entitlement key ( ibm-entitlement ) Public certificates ( {instance-id}-cert-public ) All auto-discovered secrets referenced by other resources Operator Resources : Subscription ( ibm-mas ) OperatorGroup Certificate Manager Resources : Certificates (with label mas.ibm.com/instanceId={instance-id} ) MAS Addon Resources (addons.mas.ibm.com): MVIEdge ReplicaDB GenericAddon MAS Core Resources (core.mas.ibm.com): Suite CR Workspace CRs MAS Internal Resources (internal.mas.ibm.com): CoreIDP MAS Configuration Resources (config.mas.ibm.com): IDPCfg, JdbcCfg, KafkaCfg, McpiCfg, MongoCfg ObjectStorageCfg, PushNotificationCfg, ScimCfg SmtpCfg, WatsonStudioCfg AppCfg (MAS 9.1 and later only) AiCfg (MAS 9.2 and later only) BasCfg (if include_dro is true) SlsCfg (if include_sls is true) The MAS version is auto-detected from the installed ibm-mas operator subscription channel, and version-specific resource kinds (AppCfg, AiCfg) are only included in the backup when the installed MAS version defines them. Certificate Manager Resources: ClusterIssuers : Public cluster issuer (detected automatically) mas-{instance-id}-core-internal-issuer mas-{instance-id}-ca Issuers (in cert-manager namespace): mas-{instance-id}-core-internal-ca-issuer mas-{instance-id}-core-public-ca-issuer Certificates (in cert-manager namespace): {instance-id}-cert-internal-ca {instance-id}-cert-public-ca Backup Process ¤ The MAS Core backup operation performs the following steps: Validation : Verifies required variables ( mas_instance_id , mas_backup_dir ) Version Generation : Creates or uses provided backup version identifier Certificate Manager Detection : Detects the Certificate Manager installation and namespace Cluster Issuer Detection : Identifies the public cluster issuer in use MAS Version Detection : Detects the installed MAS version from the ibm-mas subscription channel Resource Discovery : Identifies all MAS Core resources and auto-discovers referenced secrets Backup Execution : Exports all resources to YAML files in the backup directory Verification : Reports backup statistics and any failures Backup Directory Structure: {mas_backup_dir}/ └── backup-{version}-suite/ └── resources/ ├── projects/ ├── secrets/ ├── configmaps/ ├── subscriptions/ ├── operatorgroups/ ├── clusterissuers/ ├── issuers/ ├── certificates/ ├── mviedges/ ├── replicadbs/ ├── genericaddons/ ├── suites/ ├── workspaces/ ├── coreidps/ ├── appcfgs/ ├── idpcfgs/ ├── jdbccfgs/ ├── kafkacfgs/ ├── mcpicfgs/ ├── mongocfgs/ ├── objectstoragecfgs/ ├── pushnotificationcfgs/ ├── scimcfgs/ ├── smtpcfgs/ ├── watsonstudiocfgs/ ├── bascfgs/ (if include_dro is true) └── slscfgs/ (if include_sls is true) Important Considerations ¤ Instance ID Requirement: Backup can only be restored to an instance with the same MAS instance ID The instance ID is embedded in resource names and cannot be changed during restore Storage Requirements: Ensure sufficient storage in the backup directory Backup directory structure: {mas_backup_dir}/backup-{version}-suite/ Monitor disk space during backup operations Security: Backup files contain sensitive data including credentials and certificates Secure backup directory with appropriate permissions (chmod 700 recommended) Consider encrypting backups for long-term storage Restrict access to backup files to authorized personnel only SLS and DRO Configuration: Use include_sls=false if you plan to install a new SLS during recovery Use include_dro=false if you plan to install a new DRO during recovery Default is true for both, which includes the configuration in the backup Backup Best Practices ¤ Regular Backups : Schedule automated backups at regular intervals, especially before: MAS upgrades Configuration changes Application installations Cluster maintenance Test Restores : Periodically test restore procedures in non-production environments Monitor Operations : Implement monitoring and alerting for backup failures Backup Validation : Verify backup integrity after completion Retention Policy : Implement and document backup retention policies Disaster Recovery : Include MAS Core backup/restore in your DR plan Coordinate Backups : Coordinate MAS Core backups with: Database backups (MongoDB, Db2) SLS backups (if using separate SLS) DRO backups (if using separate DRO) Application-specific backups Example Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - hosts: localhost vars: mas_instance_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_INSTANCE_ID') }}" mas_backup_dir: /tmp/mas_backups suite_backup_version: 20260116-130937 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_backup License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: suite_certs ¤ This role manages TLS certificates for Maximo Application Suite core platform and applications. It processes certificate files organized in a directory structure and creates TLS secrets in the appropriate namespaces. The role supports manual certificate management and optional integration with IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) for DNS management. Certificate Directory Structure Certificates must be organized in subdirectories named after the MAS component ( core , monitor , manage , iot , etc.). Each subdirectory must contain three mandatory files: tls.crt , tls.key , and ca.crt . What This Role Does ¤ Iterates through certificate subdirectories in $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/certs Validates presence of required certificate files ( tls.crt , tls.key , ca.crt ) Creates TLS secrets in appropriate MAS namespaces Optionally manages DNS CNAME records in IBM Cloud Internet Services Supports GitOps mode for generating configurations without applying them Certificate Directory Structure ¤ Required Structure ¤ $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/certs/ ├── core/ │ ├── tls.crt │ ├── tls.key │ └── ca.crt ├── monitor/ │ ├── tls.crt │ ├── tls.key │ └── ca.crt ├── manage/ │ ├── tls.crt │ ├── tls.key │ └── ca.crt └── <app>/ ├── tls.crt ├── tls.key └── ca.crt Supported Applications ¤ core - MAS core platform iot - IoT application monitor - Monitor application manage - Manage application health - Health application predict - Predict application assist - Assist application optimizer - Optimizer application visualinspection - Visual Inspection application facilities - Facilities application add - Add application arcgis - ArcGIS integration Warning All three certificate files ( tls.crt , tls.key , ca.crt ) are mandatory in each subdirectory. The role will fail if a subdirectory is empty or missing any required file. Secret Names TLS secret names for each application are defined in suite_certs/defaults/main.yml . Changes to secret names or adding new applications requires updating this file. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_manual_cert_mgmt No false mas_config_dir Yes None mas_channel No None gitops No false dns_provider No None mas_routing_mode No None mas_workspace_id Conditional None cis_crn Conditional None cis_apikey Conditional None cis_subdomain Conditional None cis_proxy No false The CIS variables ( mas_workspace_id , cis_crn , cis_apikey , and cis_subdomain ) are only required when dns_provider is set to cis . Certificate Management ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier the certificates belong to — a lowercase alphanumeric string of 3-12 characters (for example prod , dev , or masinst1 ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Used to construct both the target namespaces ( mas-{instance_id}-{app} , e.g. mas-prod-core or mas-prod-monitor ) and the TLS secret names, following MAS naming conventions. mas_manual_cert_mgmt ¤ Enable manual certificate management mode, providing your own certificates instead of relying on cert-manager-generated ones — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_MANUAL_CERT_MGMT Default: false When true , the role processes the certificate files under $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/certs . Enable this for custom or purchased certificates, environments without cert-manager, custom domains, or corporate policies requiring a specific certificate authority. mas_config_dir ¤ Root configuration directory containing the certs subdirectory with certificates organized by MAS component — a valid local filesystem path such as /home/user/masconfig or ~/masconfig/inst1 . Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None All certificate processing is relative to this path: certificates are read from $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/certs/{app}/ , and in GitOps mode generated YAML is written to $MAS_CONFIG_DIR/app/certs/{app}/ . The certs subdirectory is appended automatically (see mas_suite_certs_dir in the role defaults). mas_channel ¤ MAS channel (version) of the target instance, for example 9.1.x or 9.2.x — used to select version-appropriate naming conventions. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CHANNEL Default: None When set, the role detects whether the instance is running MAS earlier than 9.2 and adjusts the generated configuration accordingly; when unset, MAS earlier than 9.2 is assumed. gitops ¤ Generate the certificate secret configurations without applying them to the cluster — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: GITOPS Default: false When true , generated YAML files can be committed to Git and applied through your GitOps tooling (ArgoCD, Flux, etc.); when false , resources are created directly on the cluster. CIS DNS Provider ¤ Optional variables for users managing DNS with IBM Cloud Internet Services. When configured, this role automatically creates or updates CNAME records for MAS routes in your CIS instance. dns_provider ¤ DNS provider for automatic DNS record management — cis (IBM Cloud Internet Services) is the only supported value. Optional Environment Variable: DNS_PROVIDER Default: None When set to cis , the role creates or updates CNAME records for MAS routes in your CIS instance. Leave unset when not using automatic DNS management; any value other than cis or empty is not supported. mas_routing_mode ¤ MAS routing mode controlling the shape of the DNS records created in CIS — subdomain (each MAS component gets its own subdomain) or path (components share a single hostname with path-based routing). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ROUTING_MODE Default: None (treated as subdomain ) Only applies when dns_provider is cis . mas_workspace_id ¤ MAS workspace identifier used when constructing DNS CNAME records for workspace-scoped applications — a lowercase alphanumeric string, typically 3-12 characters (for example prod , dev , or masdev ). Required when dns_provider is cis Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None Also used in the TLS secret names for the workspace-scoped applications ( manage , health , facilities ). DNS names for workspace applications take the form {workspace_id}.{subdomain}.{domain} . cis_crn ¤ Cloud Resource Name (CRN) identifying the CIS instance in IBM Cloud where DNS records are managed — format crn:v1:bluemix:public:internet-svcs:... . Required when dns_provider is cis Environment Variable: CIS_CRN Default: None Find it in the IBM Cloud console under your CIS instance details. All CNAME operations target this CIS instance. cis_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API key used to authenticate with CIS — must have IAM permissions to manage DNS in the target CIS instance. Required when dns_provider is cis Environment Variable: CIS_APIKEY Default: None Warning The API key grants access to your IBM Cloud account — keep it secure, obtain it from IBM Cloud IAM, and never commit it to version control. cis_subdomain ¤ Subdomain within your CIS-managed domain where MAS CNAME records are created — for example mas , maximo , or apps . Required when dns_provider is cis Environment Variable: CIS_SUBDOMAIN Default: None The subdomain must already exist in your CIS domain; this role creates CNAME records within it, not the subdomain itself. Full DNS names take the form {component}.{subdomain}.{domain} or {workspace}.{subdomain}.{domain} . cis_proxy ¤ Enable CIS proxy mode for the created CNAME records — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: CIS_PROXY Default: false When true , traffic flows through CIS infrastructure so security features such as WAF rules, DDoS protection, and rate limiting can be applied, at the cost of some added latency; when false , records are DNS-only. Only applies when dns_provider is cis . docs.text: suite_config ¤ This role applies configuration files to a Maximo Application Suite installation. It searches for YAML configuration files in a specified directory and applies them to the cluster using the Kubernetes API. This is typically used after installing MAS to configure various aspects of the suite such as workspace configurations, JDBC configurations, SMTP settings, and other custom resources. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_config_dir Yes None Instance Configuration ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ Unique identifier for the MAS instance to apply configurations to (lowercase alphanumeric, 3-12 characters, e.g. prod , dev , inst1 ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Must match the instance ID used during MAS core installation. Configurations are applied to the mas-{mas_instance_id}-core namespace and related application namespaces; an incorrect instance ID will apply configurations to the wrong instance or fail if it doesn't exist. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory path containing MAS configuration YAML files to apply to the cluster. Required Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None The role recursively searches this directory for all *.yaml and *.yml files and applies them to the cluster. Use the same directory where dependency roles (mongodb, db2, sls) generate their configuration files — typically a consistent location across all MAS setup roles such as ~/masconfig . Files matching jdbc-aiservice*.yml / jdbc-aiservice*.yaml are automatically excluded, as AI Service JDBC configurations require special handling. Ensure the directory contains only Kubernetes resources intended for this MAS instance. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: "inst1" mas_config_dir: "/home/user/masconfig" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_config License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: suite_db2_setup_for_facilities ¤ This role performs initial Db2 database setup required for Maximo Facilities (Real Estate and Facilities Management) application. It configures database parameters, creates tablespaces, and applies performance optimizations that the Facilities operator cannot yet handle automatically. Temporary Role This role exists as a workaround until the Facilities operator can perform these setup tasks automatically. It handles Facilities-specific database requirements. What This Role Does ¤ Installs Db2 with required properties for Facilities Copies setup scripts into Db2 pod Executes database configuration changes inside container Creates and configures tablespaces for Facilities Applies enhanced Db2 performance parameters Optionally restarts Db2 instance to apply configuration Downtime Risk Setting enforce_db2_config=true will restart the Db2 instance, causing downtime. Schedule during maintenance windows or use with newly created instances. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default db2_instance_name Yes None db2_namespace No db2u db2_dbname No BLUDB db2_schema No TRIDATA db2_username No tridata db2_tablespace_data_size No 5000 M db2_tablespace_index_size No 5000 M db2_config_version No 1.0.0 enforce_db2_config No true db2_facilities_timezone No UTC Db2 Connection ¤ db2_instance_name ¤ Db2 instance name for the Facilities setup — for example db2w-facilities or db2u-db01 . Required Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None Identifies the Db2 Warehouse instance that receives the Facilities-specific configuration and tablespace setup; the role uses it to locate the correct Db2 pod. To find the instance name, go to the Db2 namespace and look for pods with label=engine , then describe the pod and find the app label value. db2_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the Db2 instance is deployed. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_NAMESPACE Default: db2u Override if Db2 is deployed in a custom namespace; the default db2u is used by most Db2 Warehouse deployments. db2_dbname ¤ Database name within the Db2 instance where the Facilities setup is performed; the database must exist before running this role. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DBNAME Default: BLUDB BLUDB is the default database name for Facilities deployments. db2_schema ¤ Schema where the Facilities (TRIRIGA) tables and objects are created. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_SCHEMA Default: TRIDATA TRIDATA is standard for Facilities/TRIRIGA deployments — this differs from Manage, which uses the maximo schema. Ensure this matches your Facilities database configuration. db2_username ¤ Username for connecting to the Db2 database during the Facilities setup script execution. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_USERNAME Default: tridata The default tridata user is specific to Facilities/TRIRIGA; the user must have sufficient privileges to create tablespaces and modify the database configuration. Tablespace Sizing ¤ db2_tablespace_data_size ¤ Size of the data tablespace created for Facilities application data, in Db2 size format — for example 5000 M , 10 G , or 50 G . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TABLESPACE_DATA_SIZE Default: 5000 M Insufficient size will prevent data insertion. Requirements depend on the number of buildings and spaces, historical data retention, document attachments, and custom fields and extensions — start with 5GB and monitor usage; tablespaces can be expanded later if needed. db2_tablespace_index_size ¤ Size of the index tablespace created for Facilities database indexes, in Db2 size format — for example 5000 M , 10 G , or 20 G . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_TABLESPACE_INDEX_SIZE Default: 5000 M A good rule of thumb is to allocate 20-30% of the data tablespace size for indexes; insufficient size will prevent index creation and impact performance. Monitor usage and adjust as needed. Db2 Configuration ¤ db2_config_version ¤ Version of the enhanced Db2 performance parameters to apply — 1.0.0 is the currently supported version. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CONFIG_VERSION Default: 1.0.0 The parameter set includes optimizations for Facilities' specific database access patterns; future versions may include additional optimizations. enforce_db2_config ¤ Whether the enhanced Db2 parameters are applied together with a database restart — true or false . The restart is required for the parameters to take effect. Optional Environment Variable: ENFORCE_DB2_CONFIG Default: true Warning Setting this to true will restart the Db2 instance, causing downtime for all applications using the database. Schedule during maintenance windows and coordinate with stakeholders for production systems; for newly created instances it is safe as no applications are using the database yet. Setting it to false skips the enhanced parameter application, resulting in suboptimal performance. db2_facilities_timezone ¤ Timezone used by the Db2 server for timestamp operations and scheduling — for example GMT , EST , PST , CET , or UTC . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_FACILITIES_TIMEZONE Default: UTC Use UTC for globally distributed systems, or the local timezone when all users are in the same timezone. Must match the MAS Facilities Server timezone. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: # Configuration for the Db2 cluster db2_namespace: db2u db2_instance_name: db2u-db01 db2_dbname: BLUDB roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_db2_setup_for_facilities License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: suite_db2_setup_for_manage ¤ This role performs initial setup on Db2 instances for use with the Maximo Manage application. It supports both CP4D version 3.5 and 4.0, and now supports both Db2uCluster (deprecated) and Db2uInstance (current) custom resources . The role will copy a bash script (setupdb.sh) into the Db2 pod and execute it inside the container, performing configuration changes to the database and configuring tablespaces for Maximo Manage. It configures database parameters, creates tablespaces, and applies performance optimizations that the Manage operator cannot yet handle automatically. Supported Db2 Custom Resources ¤ Db2uCluster (deprecated, maintained for backward compatibility) Db2uInstance (current, recommended for new deployments) The role automatically detects which CR type is deployed and applies the appropriate configuration. No changes to your playbooks are required. Downtime Risk Setting enforce_db2_config=true will restart the Db2 instance, causing downtime. Schedule during maintenance windows or use with newly created instances. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default db2_instance_name Yes None db2_namespace No db2u db2_dbname No BLUDB db2_config_version No 1.0.0 enforce_db2_config No true db2_helm_operator_mode No false Db2 Connection ¤ db2_instance_name ¤ Db2 Warehouse instance name where the Manage database setup will be performed — a valid Db2 instance name (e.g. db2w-manage , db2u-manage ). Required Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None Used to locate the correct Db2 pod. To find the instance name, go to the Db2 namespace and look for pods with label=engine ; describe the pod and find the app label value. db2_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the Db2 instance is deployed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_NAMESPACE Default: db2u The default db2u namespace is used by most Db2 Warehouse deployments; override it if Db2 is deployed in a custom namespace. db2_dbname ¤ Database name within the Db2 instance where the Manage setup will be performed — a valid Db2 database name that must exist before running this role. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DBNAME Default: BLUDB BLUDB is the default database name for Manage deployments. Db2 Configuration ¤ db2_config_version ¤ Version of the enhanced Db2 performance parameter set to apply during setup — 1.0.0 is the currently supported version. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CONFIG_VERSION Default: 1.0.0 The parameter set includes optimizations for Manage's specific database access patterns; different versions may have different parameter sets, and future versions may include additional optimizations. enforce_db2_config ¤ Apply the enhanced Db2 parameters with a database restart — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ENFORCE_DB2_CONFIG Default: true A restart is required for the parameters to take effect. Setting to false skips the enhanced parameter application, which is not recommended (suboptimal performance). Warning Setting this to true will restart the Db2 instance, causing downtime for all applications using the database. Schedule during maintenance windows and, for production systems, coordinate with stakeholders. For new instances this is safe, as no applications are using the database yet. db2_helm_operator_mode ¤ Set to true when using the new helm-based Db2 operator, which has the archive logs PVC pre-configured — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_HELM_OPERATOR_MODE Default: false CR Type Detection ¤ The role automatically: Queries for both Db2uCluster and Db2uInstance resources Validates that exactly one CR type exists Applies configuration appropriate for the detected CR type Fails with clear error messages if: No CR is found Both CR types exist (invalid state) CR is not in Ready state Example Playbook ¤ Example 1: With Db2uCluster (Legacy) ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: db2_instance_name: mydb2-cluster db2_namespace: db2u db2_config_version: "1.0.0" enforce_db2_config: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_db2_setup_for_manage Example 2: With Db2uInstance (Current) ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: db2_instance_name: mydb2-instance db2_namespace: db2u db2_config_version: "1.0.0" enforce_db2_config: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_db2_setup_for_manage The playbook syntax is identical for both CR types — the role handles the differences automatically. Troubleshooting ¤ Error: "Both Db2uCluster and Db2uInstance resources exist" ¤ This indicates an invalid state. Ensure only one CR type exists: oc get db2ucluster -n <namespace> oc get db2uinstance -n <namespace> Delete the unwanted CR (Db2uInstance is recommended for new deployments). Error: "No Db2 instance found" ¤ Verify the instance name and namespace: oc get db2ucluster,db2uinstance -n <namespace> Configuration Not Applied ¤ Check the ConfigMap to see if configuration was already applied: oc get configmap <instance-name>-enforce-config -n <namespace> -o yaml License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: This role performs initial setup on Db2 instances for use with the Maximo Manage application. It supports both CP4D version 3.5 and 4.0, and now supports both Db2uCluster (deprecated) and Db2uInstance (current) custom resources . The role will copy a bash script (setupdb.sh) into the Db2 pod and execute it inside the container, performing configuration changes to the database and configuring tablespaces for Maximo Manage. It configures database parameters, creates tablespaces, and applies performance optimizations that the Manage operator cannot yet handle automatically.
docs.title: suite_db2_setup_for_manage

docs.text: Db2uCluster (deprecated, maintained for backward compatibility) Db2uInstance (current, recommended for new deployments) The role automatically detects which CR type is deployed and applies the appropriate configuration. No changes to your playbooks are required. Downtime Risk Setting enforce_db2_config=true will restart the Db2 instance, causing downtime. Schedule during maintenance windows or use with newly created instances.
docs.title: Supported Db2 Custom Resources

docs.text: Variable Required Default db2_instance_name Yes None db2_namespace No db2u db2_dbname No BLUDB db2_config_version No 1.0.0 enforce_db2_config No true db2_helm_operator_mode No false
docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Db2 Warehouse instance name where the Manage database setup will be performed — a valid Db2 instance name (e.g. db2w-manage , db2u-manage ). Required Environment Variable: DB2_INSTANCE_NAME Default: None Used to locate the correct Db2 pod. To find the instance name, go to the Db2 namespace and look for pods with label=engine ; describe the pod and find the app label value.
docs.title: db2_instance_name

docs.text: OpenShift namespace where the Db2 instance is deployed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_NAMESPACE Default: db2u The default db2u namespace is used by most Db2 Warehouse deployments; override it if Db2 is deployed in a custom namespace.
docs.title: db2_namespace

docs.text: Database name within the Db2 instance where the Manage setup will be performed — a valid Db2 database name that must exist before running this role. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_DBNAME Default: BLUDB BLUDB is the default database name for Manage deployments.
docs.title: db2_dbname

docs.text: Version of the enhanced Db2 performance parameter set to apply during setup — 1.0.0 is the currently supported version. Optional Environment Variable: DB2_CONFIG_VERSION Default: 1.0.0 The parameter set includes optimizations for Manage's specific database access patterns; different versions may have different parameter sets, and future versions may include additional optimizations.
docs.title: db2_config_version

docs.text: Apply the enhanced Db2 parameters with a database restart — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: ENFORCE_DB2_CONFIG Default: true A restart is required for the parameters to take effect. Setting to false skips the enhanced parameter application, which is not recommended (suboptimal performance). Warning Setting this to true will restart the Db2 instance, causing downtime for all applications using the database. Schedule during maintenance windows and, for production systems, coordinate with stakeholders. For new instances this is safe, as no applications are using the database yet.
docs.title: enforce_db2_config

docs.text: Set to true when using the new helm-based Db2 operator, which has the archive logs PVC pre-configured — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: DB2_HELM_OPERATOR_MODE Default: false
docs.title: db2_helm_operator_mode

docs.text: The role automatically: Queries for both Db2uCluster and Db2uInstance resources Validates that exactly one CR type exists Applies configuration appropriate for the detected CR type Fails with clear error messages if: No CR is found Both CR types exist (invalid state) CR is not in Ready state
docs.title: CR Type Detection

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: db2_instance_name: mydb2-cluster db2_namespace: db2u db2_config_version: "1.0.0" enforce_db2_config: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_db2_setup_for_manage
docs.title: Example 1: With Db2uCluster (Legacy)

docs.text: - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: db2_instance_name: mydb2-instance db2_namespace: db2u db2_config_version: "1.0.0" enforce_db2_config: true roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_db2_setup_for_manage The playbook syntax is identical for both CR types — the role handles the differences automatically.
