docs.text: suite_dns ¤ This role manages DNS provider integration for both IBM Maximo Application Suite (MAS) and AI Service. IBM Cloud Internet Services, Cloudflare, and AWS Route 53 are the supported DNS providers. It will also create a secure route (https://cp4d. ) to the CP4D web client using the custom domain used in this role. Note : this role will take no action when mas_manual_cert_mgmt is set to True MAS vs AI Service Mode ¤ This role automatically detects whether it's being used for MAS or AI Service based on the presence of AISERVICE_INSTANCE_ID : MAS Mode : Uses ClusterIssuer (cluster-wide certificate issuer) and supports multiple workspaces AI Service Mode : Uses namespace-scoped Issuer within the AI Service namespace ( aiservice-{instance_id} ) The key difference is that AI Service creates the certificate Issuer within its own namespace rather than using a shared ClusterIssuer. DNS Management ¤ There are two different ways this role controls DNS entries in the provider: Top Level DNS Entries ¤ This mode will create the entries directly under your DNS zone. Use this when the DNS zone matches the MAS domain exactly. If your MAS installation will be using the domain mymas.mycompany.com and you have a DNS zone for mymas.mycompany.com then you will be creating top-level DNS entries for MAS, e.g. admin , home , & api . Subdomain DNS Entries ¤ This mode will create DNS entries in the zone under a subdomain. Use this when your DNS zone will be used for more than just one MAS instance. If your MAS installation will be using the domain mymas.mycompany.com and you have a DNS zone for mycompany.com then you will be creating subdomain DNS entries for MAS, e.g. admin.mymas , home.mymas , & api.mymas . CIS and Cloudflare integrations support both modes of DNS management. A single optional variable is required to enable subdomain DNS management, in the examples above you would set these to mymas : cis_subdomain cloudflare_subdomain Let's Encrypt Integration ¤ Both the CIS and Cloudflare options also enable integration with Let's Encrypt for automatic certificate management via IBM Certificate Manager. Each will create a new ClusterIssuer which can be used when installing Maximo Application Suite: Cloudflare Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer: {{ mas_instance_id }}-cloudflare-le-prod IBM Cloud Internet Services Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer: {{ mas_instance_id }}-cis-le-prod If you want to use Let's Encrypt certificates in your MAS installation you will need to configure the mas_cluster_issuer variable in the suite_install role, setting it to the name of the ClusterIssuer as documented above. Note There are issues with how cert-manager works with LetsEncrypt staging servers. It creates a secret for the certificate that doesn't contain the LetsEncrypt CA, but the staging service does not use a well known cert so we end up with MAS unable to trust the certificates generated by LetsEncrypt staging. At present there is no workaround for this, so do not use the LetsEncrypt staging certificate issuer. HTTP-01 (path-based routing extension) ¤ When mas_routing_mode is path and mas_le_email is set, this role additionally creates a Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 issuer. This is an opt-in extension — existing DNS-01 behaviour is unchanged when mas_le_email is not set. The issuer kind is controlled by mas_issuer_kind ( ClusterIssuer or Issuer ) and the issuer name defaults to {{ mas_instance_id }}-http01-le-prod (override via MAS_CLUSTER_ISSUER ). Note HTTP-01 requires the cluster to be publicly reachable from the internet. It cannot be used in private network environments. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default aiservice_instance_id Conditional None aiservice_domain No None dns_provider Yes None mas_manual_cert_mgmt No false cert_manager_namespace No Auto-detected mas_instance_id Conditional None mas_workspace_id Conditional None mas_domain Conditional None ocp_ingress No Auto-detected mas_le_email No None mas_issuer_kind No ClusterIssuer mas_ingress_controller_name No default custom_labels No None output_dir No . cloudflare_email Conditional None cloudflare_apitoken Conditional None cloudflare_zone Conditional None cloudflare_subdomain No None cis_email Conditional None cis_apikey Conditional None cis_crn Conditional None cis_subdomain No None cis_enhanced_security No false cis_service_name No {ClusterName}-cis-{mas_instance_id} cis_waf No true cis_proxy No false cis_allowed_ips No None update_dns No true delete_wildcards No false override_edge_certs No true cis_entries_to_add No all route53_hosted_zone_name Conditional None route53_hosted_zone_region No AWS_REGION , else us-east-2 route53_subdomain No None route53_email No None aws_access_key_id Conditional None aws_secret_access_key Conditional None cpd_instance_namespace No None cpd_prod_issuer_name No {mas_instance_id}-{dns_provider}-le-prod cpd_custom_domain No mas_domain cpd_public_route_enabled No false Variables marked Conditional are only required in specific circumstances: in MAS mode you must set mas_instance_id , mas_workspace_id , and mas_domain (they are not required in AI Service mode, where aiservice_instance_id is required instead), and each DNS provider requires its own credentials — cloudflare requires cloudflare_email , cloudflare_apitoken , and cloudflare_zone ; cis requires cis_email , cis_apikey , and cis_crn ; route53 requires route53_hosted_zone_name plus the AWS credentials. AI Service Variables ¤ aiservice_instance_id ¤ Unique identifier for the AI Service instance requiring DNS configuration — a lowercase alphanumeric string (e.g. aiservice1 , prod , dev ) that must match the instance ID used during AI Service installation. Required for AI Service mode Environment Variable: AISERVICE_INSTANCE_ID Default: None When set, the role operates in AI Service mode: DNS entries are created for the aiservice-{aiservice_instance_id} namespace, and a namespace-scoped Issuer (not a ClusterIssuer) is created in that namespace with the name format {aiservice_instance_id}-{provider}-le-prod . When this is set, mas_instance_id and mas_workspace_id are not required. aiservice_domain ¤ Custom domain name for accessing AI Service APIs and interfaces — any valid DNS domain name (e.g. aiservice.mycompany.com , ai.example.org ). Optional Environment Variable: AISERVICE_DOMAIN Default: None (uses the cluster's default application domain) All AI Service routes and DNS entries are constructed from this domain, and it must align with your DNS provider zone configuration ( cloudflare_zone , cis_crn , etc.). If not set, the cluster's default application domain is used for AI Service routes. DNS Provider and Certificate Management ¤ dns_provider ¤ Specifies which DNS provider to use for managing MAS domain DNS entries — cis (IBM Cloud Internet Services), cloudflare (Cloudflare DNS), or route53 (AWS Route 53). Required Environment Variable: DNS_PROVIDER Default: None The selected provider determines which additional variables are required and which features are available — for example, Let's Encrypt integration is available for CIS and Cloudflare but not Route 53. This role takes no action when mas_manual_cert_mgmt is set to true . mas_manual_cert_mgmt ¤ Controls whether to disable automatic DNS and certificate management. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_MANUAL_CERT_MGMT Default: false When true , this role takes no action and all other DNS provider variables are ignored — you are responsible for creating all required DNS entries and managing certificates manually (or through alternative methods) before MAS installation. When false (default), the role automatically creates DNS entries and optionally configures Let's Encrypt integration. cert_manager_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where Certificate Manager is installed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name. Optional Environment Variable: CERT_MANAGER_NAMESPACE Default: None (automatically detected) ClusterIssuer resources for Let's Encrypt integration are created referencing this namespace, so an incorrect value will cause ClusterIssuer creation to fail. Automatic detection typically finds Certificate Manager in standard namespaces; only override it when using a custom installation or when detection fails. MAS Domain and Routes ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ Unique identifier for the MAS instance requiring DNS configuration — a lowercase alphanumeric string, 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , inst1 ), that must match the instance ID used during MAS core installation. Required for MAS mode Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None This ID is embedded in DNS record names and ClusterIssuer names (e.g. {mas_instance_id}-cloudflare-le-prod ), so an incorrect ID will create DNS entries for the wrong instance. Works with mas_domain to construct full DNS names for MAS routes. mas_workspace_id ¤ Workspace identifier for the MAS installation requiring DNS configuration — a lowercase alphanumeric string (e.g. masdev , prod , ws1 ) that must match an existing workspace in your MAS instance, typically the primary workspace. Required for MAS mode Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None This ID is used together with mas_instance_id and mas_domain to generate workspace-specific DNS entries and routes; an incorrect workspace ID may result in DNS entries that don't match your MAS workspace configuration. mas_domain ¤ Custom domain name for accessing MAS web interfaces and APIs — any valid DNS domain name (e.g. mas.mycompany.com , prod-mas.example.org ). Required for MAS mode Environment Variable: MAS_DOMAIN Default: None All MAS URLs and DNS entries are constructed from this domain (e.g. admin.{mas_domain} , home.{mas_domain} , api.{mas_domain} ), and it must be the same domain used in MAS core installation and be properly configured in your DNS provider's zone before running this role. Subdomain mode is available via cloudflare_subdomain or cis_subdomain . DNS propagation may take time after entries are created. ocp_ingress ¤ Override for the OpenShift cluster ingress domain used as the target for DNS CNAME records — e.g. apps.cluster-name.domain.com . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS Default: None (automatically detected from the cluster) Leave unset to allow automatic detection (recommended); set only when automatic detection fails, when using a non-default ingress controller, or in airgap or restricted network environments where detection may not work. An incorrect value will cause DNS entries to point to the wrong location. Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 ¤ mas_le_email ¤ Contact email for Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 certificate issuance. Setting this is the sole signal that enables HTTP-01 mode — no separate flag is needed. Optional — only required when using Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 with path-based routing Environment Variable: MAS_LE_EMAIL Default: None Only applies when mas_routing_mode is path ; existing DNS-01 behaviour is unchanged when this is not set. mas_issuer_kind ¤ Kind of cert-manager issuer resource to create for Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 ( ClusterIssuer or Issuer ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ISSUER_KIND Default: ClusterIssuer mas_ingress_controller_name ¤ Name of the OpenShift IngressController used for the HTTP-01 ACME challenge solver. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_INGRESS_CONTROLLER_NAME Default: default Only relevant when mas_le_email is set. Resource Labels and Output ¤ custom_labels ¤ Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to DNS-related resources (e.g. env=prod,team=platform,component=dns ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels are for organization, selection, filtering, resource tracking, cost allocation, and custom automation; they do not affect DNS functionality. output_dir ¤ Local directory path where the edge routes output file will be saved — any valid local filesystem path (e.g. /home/user/mas-output , ~/masconfig , ./output ). Optional Environment Variable: OUTPUT_DIR Default: . (current directory) The edge-routes-{mas_instance_id}.txt file containing information about the DNS entries and routes created by this role is written to this directory; it is useful for verifying DNS configuration and troubleshooting connectivity issues. Ensure the directory exists and is writable. Cloudflare DNS Integration ¤ cloudflare_email ¤ Email address associated with your Cloudflare account, used together with cloudflare_apitoken to authenticate Cloudflare API requests. Required if dns_provider is set to cloudflare Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL Default: None The account must have permissions to create and manage DNS records in the target zone ( cloudflare_zone ); an incorrect email will cause authentication failures. cloudflare_apitoken ¤ API token for authenticating with the Cloudflare API, used together with cloudflare_email . Required if dns_provider is set to cloudflare Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_APITOKEN Default: None Generate the token from the Cloudflare dashboard with DNS edit permissions for the target zone, following the Cloudflare documentation . Keep this token secure and do not commit it to source control. cloudflare_zone ¤ DNS zone name managed by Cloudflare where MAS DNS entries will be created — e.g. mydomain.com , example.org . Required if dns_provider is set to cloudflare Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_ZONE Default: None Must be an active zone configured in your Cloudflare account and the parent domain of mas_domain (or equal to it for top-level entries); the credentials used must have access to this zone. Ensure the zone is active and DNS is properly delegated before running this role. cloudflare_subdomain ¤ Subdomain within the Cloudflare zone for MAS DNS entries (subdomain mode). Optional Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_SUBDOMAIN Default: None (uses top-level DNS entries) Use when your DNS zone will host multiple MAS instances or other services, i.e. when mas_domain is a subdomain of cloudflare_zone . When set, DNS entries are created as admin.{cloudflare_subdomain} , home.{cloudflare_subdomain} , etc.; when unset, entries are created directly in the zone as admin , home , etc. The relationship must be {cloudflare_subdomain}.{cloudflare_zone} = mas_domain — for example, if the zone is mycompany.com and mas_domain is mas.mycompany.com , set the subdomain to mas . IBM Cloud Internet Services DNS Integration ¤ Note When using CIS integration, some resources will be installed in the cluster such as RBACs, API Services and CIS Webhook deployments. In OCP 4.12+, to avoid CIS webhook deployment failure at start up, this role will grant anyuid permission to cert-manager-webhook-ibm-cis service account so it can fully access the cert-manager-webhook-ibm-cis deployment pod as a workaround: oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid -z cert-manager-webhook-ibm-cis -n ibm-common-services cis_email ¤ Email address for Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer registration when using IBM CIS. Required if dns_provider is set to cis Environment Variable: CIS_EMAIL Default: None This email is embedded in the {mas_instance_id}-cis-le-prod ClusterIssuer and registered with Let's Encrypt, which uses it for certificate expiration notifications and account recovery — use a monitored team or service email address rather than a personal one. cis_apikey ¤ IBM Cloud API key for authenticating with IBM Cloud Internet Services. Required if dns_provider is set to cis Environment Variable: CIS_APIKEY Default: None Generate the key from IBM Cloud IAM with permissions for the CIS instance specified by cis_crn ; it authenticates all CIS API operations including DNS record management and ClusterIssuer configuration. Keep this key secure and do not commit it to source control. cis_crn ¤ Cloud Resource Name (CRN) identifying the IBM Cloud Internet Services instance — format crn:v1:bluemix:public:internet-svcs:... . Required if dns_provider is set to cis Environment Variable: CIS_CRN Default: None Obtain the CRN from the IBM Cloud console under your CIS instance details; it must correspond to the instance containing your target DNS zone. All DNS operations target this CIS instance, so an incorrect CRN will cause operations to fail or target the wrong instance. cis_subdomain ¤ Subdomain within the CIS zone for MAS DNS entries (subdomain mode). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_SUBDOMAIN Default: None (uses top-level DNS entries) Use when your CIS zone will host multiple MAS instances or other services, i.e. when mas_domain is a subdomain of your CIS zone domain. When set, DNS entries are created as admin.{cis_subdomain} , home.{cis_subdomain} , etc.; when unset, entries are created directly in the zone as admin , home , etc. The relationship must be {cis_subdomain}.{cis_zone_domain} = mas_domain — for example, if the CIS zone is mycompany.com and mas_domain is mas.mycompany.com , set the subdomain to mas . cis_enhanced_security ¤ Enables enhanced security features for IBM CIS DNS integration. Optional Environment Variable: CIS_ENHANCED_SECURITY Default: false When enabled, this configures a WAF firewall with rules optimized for MAS ( cis_waf ), proxy mode for DNS entries so traffic is routed through CIS ( cis_proxy ), an expanded list of DNS entries for comprehensive coverage, prevention of wildcard DNS entries, and edge certificates in the CIS instance. Recommended for production environments requiring WAF and proxy protection; leave false for development/test environments. See the IBM Cloud CIS security documentation for details — enhanced security may impact performance due to proxy routing. cis_service_name ¤ Custom name for the CIS service resources created in the cluster — a valid Kubernetes resource name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_SERVICE_NAME Default: {ClusterName}-cis-{mas_instance_id} (auto-generated) Leave unset to use the auto-generated name (recommended); set only when you need a specific naming convention or when the auto-generated name conflicts with existing resources. Changing it after initial deployment may cause issues with resource management. Enhanced IBM CIS Security ¤ cis_waf ¤ Controls Web Application Firewall (WAF) configuration for CIS. Optional Environment Variable: CIS_WAF Default: true When true , the WAF is configured with rules specifically tuned to protect MAS while allowing required application functionality; when false , the WAF is not configured (less security protection). Set to false only if WAF causes issues or conflicts with other security tools. Typically used in conjunction with cis_enhanced_security and cis_proxy . cis_proxy ¤ Controls whether DNS entries use CIS proxy mode (traffic routed through CIS). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_PROXY Default: false When true , traffic routes through CIS (orange cloud icon in the CIS console), enabling DDoS protection and CIS security features but adding latency; when false , DNS entries point directly to the OpenShift ingress (grey cloud icon) — lower latency but no CIS protection. Proxy mode is required for WAF and other CIS security features to function, so consider the latency vs. security tradeoff for your use case. cis_allowed_ips ¤ Comma-separated list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges (IPv4 and IPv6) that are permitted to access the MAS instance, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8,192.168.1.0/24,2405:201:d000:9060::/64,49.37.171.108 . Optional Environment Variable: CIS_ALLOWED_IPS Default: None When set, a CIS WAF custom block rule is created with the expression not ip.src in {<ip1> <ip2> ...} and http.host contains "<mas_domain>" , denying all traffic not originating from the specified IPs on the MAS domain. When unset or empty, any existing WAF block rule for this instance is removed, restoring unrestricted access. Supported MAS versions : 9.1.x and above only; ignored when mas_channel is 9.0.x or earlier Requires dns_provider=cis with CIS enhanced security enabled ( cis_enhanced_security and cis_waf ); the rule is scoped to mas_domain and identified in CIS by the description mas-ip-allowlist-<mas_domain> . IP allowlisting requires MAS 9.1.x or above — when mas_channel is 9.0.x or earlier, the WAF allowlist task is automatically skipped regardless of whether this variable is set. Feature status reporting (SaaS) When the allowlist is added, updated or removed, the role records the progress of the change in the SaaS feature status MongoDB by calling mas-devops-feature-status-update . Status is written only when all of the following are true: MAS mode is enabled cis_waf is enabled and mas_channel is 9.1.x or above devops_mongo_uri , account_id , cluster_id and region_id are all set (no status call is made when any of them is empty) The WAF rule in CIS differs from the requested cis_allowed_ips (no status call is made when the allowlist is already in the desired state) Status is only ever written for the MAS instance; in AI Service mode the allowlist rule is still managed, but no status is written. Status Written when REQUESTED An allowlist change is detected, before any other CIS work starts IN_PROGRESS Just before the WAF rule is created, updated or deleted ACTIVE The WAF rule was created or updated successfully DEACTIVATED The WAF rule was deleted successfully ( cis_allowed_ips unset or empty) ERROR A failure occurs after REQUESTED and the allowlist change has not completed successfully, including a failed WAF rule call after its retries. A failure after ACTIVE / DEACTIVATED has been reached does not write ERROR Whether or not status reporting is active, a failed CIS call (including a failed WAF rule create / update / delete after its retries) always fails the job. The call made for each status is: bash mas-devops-feature-status-update status-update \ --region "<region_id>" \ --instance-id "<mas_instance_id>" \ --account "<account_id>" \ --cluster "<cluster_id>" \ --subscription-id "<subscription_id>" \ --type allow-list \ --feature-details '{"ips": ["<ip1>", "<ip2>"]}' \ --deployment-start "<start timestamp>" \ --status <REQUESTED|IN_PROGRESS|ACTIVE|DEACTIVATED|ERROR> \ --status-details '{"message": "<message>", "request_configuration": "<ip1>, <ip2>"}' \ --deployment-end "<end timestamp>" --feature-details carries the requested IPs ( [] when the allowlist is being removed). --subscription-id is optional and is only passed when subscription_id is set. --deployment-start is the time the change was detected (taken when the change is detected, not when the play started) and is passed unchanged on every call. --deployment-end is only passed for ACTIVE , DEACTIVATED and ERROR , and is taken when that status is written. The JSON passed to --status-details and --feature-details is built in Ansible and shell-quoted, so quotes, newlines and backslashes in CIS output are safe. For ERROR , --status-details also includes error_code and an error_source object ( gitops_version , filename , log_file and stacktrace ). The following variables are used when writing the status: Variable Environment variable Default devops_mongo_uri DEVOPS_MONGO_URI None. Status updates are skipped when empty account_id ACCOUNT_ID None. Status updates are skipped when empty cluster_id CLUSTER_ID None. Status updates are skipped when empty region_id REGION_ID None. Status updates are skipped when empty subscription_id SLS_SUBSCRIPTION_ID None. Optional, --subscription-id is omitted when empty account_id , cluster_id , region_id and subscription_id identify the MAS instance the status is recorded for — they are not the account, region or cluster of the CIS instance. Warning Failures while disabling WAF rules ( cis_waf_rule.yml ) or managed ruleset rules ( cis_managed_ruleset.yml ) used to be tolerated and now fail the job in MAS mode, so that they are reported as ERROR and are not silently ignored. IBM CIS DNS Entries and Edge Certificates ¤ update_dns ¤ Whether to update DNS entries if they already exist. Optional Environment Variable: UPDATE_DNS_ENTRIES Default: true Set to false to leave existing DNS entries untouched. delete_wildcards ¤ Whether to force deletion of wildcard DNS entries in CIS. Optional Environment Variable: DELETE_WILDCARDS Default: false override_edge_certs ¤ Whether to override and delete any existing edge certificates in the CIS instance when creating new edge certificates. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_EDGE_CERTS Default: true Set to false to keep existing edge certificates. cis_entries_to_add ¤ Comma separated list of entries to add for edge certificates, broken down into functional areas of MAS: all (include all entries — default), core (MAS Core), health (MAS Health App), iot (MAS IoT app), manage (MAS Manage app), monitor (MAS Monitor app), predict (MAS Predict app), visualinspection (MAS VisualInspection app), optimizer (MAS Optimizer app), assist (MAS Assist app), arcgis (MAS Arcgis), reportdb (MAS ReportDB), facilities (MAS Facilities app), cpd-public (CP4D public route — creates cpd-public.<mas_domain> DNS CNAME and edge certificate for VPN-free CP4D access). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_ENTRIES_TO_ADD Default: all AWS Route 53 ¤ Prerequisites: To run this role successfully you must have already installed the AWS CLI . Also, you need to have AWS user credentials configured via aws configure command or simply export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables with your corresponding AWS username credentials prior running this role. Note In some cases, the Route 53 zone may not resolve the certificate challenges generated by IBM Certificate Manager, which could cause a problem while issuing the public certificates via Let's Encrypt. In this case, a manual workaround might be needed in cert-manager-controller pod to enable recursive nameservers. For more details on how to apply this workaround, refer to this documentation . This workaround is not automated, as most of the times this is not needed, but when it is, it requires the cert-manager-controller pod to be stopped, thus we want to avoid making this behavior as standard approach. route53_hosted_zone_name ¤ AWS Route53 Hosted Zone name. Required if dns_provider is set to route53 Environment Variable: ROUTE53_HOSTED_ZONE_NAME Default: None route53_hosted_zone_region ¤ AWS Route53 Hosted Zone region. Optional Environment Variable: ROUTE53_HOSTED_ZONE_REGION Default: Same value as defined in AWS_REGION , or us-east-2 if none is defined route53_subdomain ¤ Subdomain used to create the corresponding CNAME entries in the targeted Route53 hosted zone. Optional Environment Variable: ROUTE53_SUBDOMAIN Default: None The Route53 subdomain combined with the Route53 hosted zone name must match the chosen MAS domain, otherwise the DNS records won't be able to get resolved — e.g. MAS top level domain my-mas-instance.mycompany.com , AWS Route53 hosted zone name mycompany.com , AWS Route53 subdomain my-mas-instance . route53_email ¤ AWS Route53 contact e-mail. Will be set in the cluster issuer created in order to receive alerts. Optional Environment Variable: ROUTE53_EMAIL Default: None aws_access_key_id ¤ AWS access key ID for authentication. Required if dns_provider is set to route53 Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None aws_secret_access_key ¤ AWS secret access key for authentication. Required if dns_provider is set to route53 Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None CloudPak for Data ¤ cpd_instance_namespace ¤ Namespace where the Cloud Pak for Data is installed and the cpd route exists. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE Default: None If set, then this role will also attempt to configure public certificates to the CPD route using the DNS provider defined. cpd_prod_issuer_name ¤ Certificate issuer responsible for generating the public certificate for your CPD route. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_PROD_ISSUER_NAME Default: {mas_instance_id}-{dns_provider}-le-prod (the same production issuer used to set up the MAS instance) cpd_custom_domain ¤ Custom domain for your CPD route. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_CUSTOM_DOMAIN Default: Value of mas_domain ; the CPD route and certificate are then created for cp4d.{{ cpd_custom_domain }} cpd_public_route_enabled ¤ Whether to create the cpd-public DNS entry and edge certificate providing VPN-free public access to the CP4D route ( cpd-public.<mas_domain> ). Optional Environment Variable: CPD_PUBLIC_ROUTE_ENABLED Default: false Example Playbook ¤ MAS with CIS or Cloudflare ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: dns_provider: cis # or cloudflare mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_workspace_id: masdev mas_domain: mydomain.com cis_crn: xxx cis_apikey: xxx cis_email: xxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_dns MAS with AWS Route 53 ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: dns_provider: route53 mas_instance_id: inst1 mas_workspace_id: masdev mas_domain: inst1.mydomain.com aws_access_key_id: xxx aws_secret_access_key: xxx route53_hosted_zone_name: mydomain.com route53_hosted_zone_region: us-east-2 route53_subdomain: inst1 route53_email: anyemail@test.com roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_dns AI Service with CIS ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: dns_provider: cis aiservice_instance_id: aiservice1 aiservice_domain: aiservice.mydomain.com cis_crn: xxx cis_apikey: xxx cis_email: xxx roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_dns AI Service with AWS Route 53 ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: dns_provider: route53 aiservice_instance_id: aiservice1 aiservice_domain: aiservice.mydomain.com aws_access_key_id: xxx aws_secret_access_key: xxx route53_hosted_zone_name: mydomain.com route53_hosted_zone_region: us-east-2 route53_subdomain: aiservice route53_email: anyemail@test.com roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_dns License ¤ EPL-2.0
docs.title: suite_dns

docs.text: This role manages DNS provider integration for both IBM Maximo Application Suite (MAS) and AI Service. IBM Cloud Internet Services, Cloudflare, and AWS Route 53 are the supported DNS providers. It will also create a secure route (https://cp4d. ) to the CP4D web client using the custom domain used in this role. Note : this role will take no action when mas_manual_cert_mgmt is set to True
docs.title: suite_dns

docs.text: This role automatically detects whether it's being used for MAS or AI Service based on the presence of AISERVICE_INSTANCE_ID : MAS Mode : Uses ClusterIssuer (cluster-wide certificate issuer) and supports multiple workspaces AI Service Mode : Uses namespace-scoped Issuer within the AI Service namespace ( aiservice-{instance_id} ) The key difference is that AI Service creates the certificate Issuer within its own namespace rather than using a shared ClusterIssuer.
docs.title: MAS vs AI Service Mode

docs.text: There are two different ways this role controls DNS entries in the provider:
docs.title: DNS Management

docs.text: This mode will create the entries directly under your DNS zone. Use this when the DNS zone matches the MAS domain exactly. If your MAS installation will be using the domain mymas.mycompany.com and you have a DNS zone for mymas.mycompany.com then you will be creating top-level DNS entries for MAS, e.g. admin , home , & api .
docs.title: Top Level DNS Entries

docs.text: This mode will create DNS entries in the zone under a subdomain. Use this when your DNS zone will be used for more than just one MAS instance. If your MAS installation will be using the domain mymas.mycompany.com and you have a DNS zone for mycompany.com then you will be creating subdomain DNS entries for MAS, e.g. admin.mymas , home.mymas , & api.mymas . CIS and Cloudflare integrations support both modes of DNS management. A single optional variable is required to enable subdomain DNS management, in the examples above you would set these to mymas : cis_subdomain cloudflare_subdomain
docs.title: Subdomain DNS Entries

docs.text: Both the CIS and Cloudflare options also enable integration with Let's Encrypt for automatic certificate management via IBM Certificate Manager. Each will create a new ClusterIssuer which can be used when installing Maximo Application Suite: Cloudflare Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer: {{ mas_instance_id }}-cloudflare-le-prod IBM Cloud Internet Services Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer: {{ mas_instance_id }}-cis-le-prod If you want to use Let's Encrypt certificates in your MAS installation you will need to configure the mas_cluster_issuer variable in the suite_install role, setting it to the name of the ClusterIssuer as documented above. Note There are issues with how cert-manager works with LetsEncrypt staging servers. It creates a secret for the certificate that doesn't contain the LetsEncrypt CA, but the staging service does not use a well known cert so we end up with MAS unable to trust the certificates generated by LetsEncrypt staging. At present there is no workaround for this, so do not use the LetsEncrypt staging certificate issuer.
docs.title: Let's Encrypt Integration

docs.text: When mas_routing_mode is path and mas_le_email is set, this role additionally creates a Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 issuer. This is an opt-in extension — existing DNS-01 behaviour is unchanged when mas_le_email is not set. The issuer kind is controlled by mas_issuer_kind ( ClusterIssuer or Issuer ) and the issuer name defaults to {{ mas_instance_id }}-http01-le-prod (override via MAS_CLUSTER_ISSUER ). Note HTTP-01 requires the cluster to be publicly reachable from the internet. It cannot be used in private network environments.
docs.title: HTTP-01 (path-based routing extension)

docs.text: Variable Required Default aiservice_instance_id Conditional None aiservice_domain No None dns_provider Yes None mas_manual_cert_mgmt No false cert_manager_namespace No Auto-detected mas_instance_id Conditional None mas_workspace_id Conditional None mas_domain Conditional None ocp_ingress No Auto-detected mas_le_email No None mas_issuer_kind No ClusterIssuer mas_ingress_controller_name No default custom_labels No None output_dir No . cloudflare_email Conditional None cloudflare_apitoken Conditional None cloudflare_zone Conditional None cloudflare_subdomain No None cis_email Conditional None cis_apikey Conditional None cis_crn Conditional None cis_subdomain No None cis_enhanced_security No false cis_service_name No {ClusterName}-cis-{mas_instance_id} cis_waf No true cis_proxy No false cis_allowed_ips No None update_dns No true delete_wildcards No false override_edge_certs No true cis_entries_to_add No all route53_hosted_zone_name Conditional None route53_hosted_zone_region No AWS_REGION , else us-east-2 route53_subdomain No None route53_email No None aws_access_key_id Conditional None aws_secret_access_key Conditional None cpd_instance_namespace No None cpd_prod_issuer_name No {mas_instance_id}-{dns_provider}-le-prod cpd_custom_domain No mas_domain cpd_public_route_enabled No false Variables marked Conditional are only required in specific circumstances: in MAS mode you must set mas_instance_id , mas_workspace_id , and mas_domain (they are not required in AI Service mode, where aiservice_instance_id is required instead), and each DNS provider requires its own credentials — cloudflare requires cloudflare_email , cloudflare_apitoken , and cloudflare_zone ; cis requires cis_email , cis_apikey , and cis_crn ; route53 requires route53_hosted_zone_name plus the AWS credentials.
docs.title: Role Variables

docs.text: Unique identifier for the AI Service instance requiring DNS configuration — a lowercase alphanumeric string (e.g. aiservice1 , prod , dev ) that must match the instance ID used during AI Service installation. Required for AI Service mode Environment Variable: AISERVICE_INSTANCE_ID Default: None When set, the role operates in AI Service mode: DNS entries are created for the aiservice-{aiservice_instance_id} namespace, and a namespace-scoped Issuer (not a ClusterIssuer) is created in that namespace with the name format {aiservice_instance_id}-{provider}-le-prod . When this is set, mas_instance_id and mas_workspace_id are not required.
docs.title: aiservice_instance_id

docs.text: Custom domain name for accessing AI Service APIs and interfaces — any valid DNS domain name (e.g. aiservice.mycompany.com , ai.example.org ). Optional Environment Variable: AISERVICE_DOMAIN Default: None (uses the cluster's default application domain) All AI Service routes and DNS entries are constructed from this domain, and it must align with your DNS provider zone configuration ( cloudflare_zone , cis_crn , etc.). If not set, the cluster's default application domain is used for AI Service routes.
docs.title: aiservice_domain

docs.text: Specifies which DNS provider to use for managing MAS domain DNS entries — cis (IBM Cloud Internet Services), cloudflare (Cloudflare DNS), or route53 (AWS Route 53). Required Environment Variable: DNS_PROVIDER Default: None The selected provider determines which additional variables are required and which features are available — for example, Let's Encrypt integration is available for CIS and Cloudflare but not Route 53. This role takes no action when mas_manual_cert_mgmt is set to true .
docs.title: dns_provider

docs.text: Controls whether to disable automatic DNS and certificate management. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_MANUAL_CERT_MGMT Default: false When true , this role takes no action and all other DNS provider variables are ignored — you are responsible for creating all required DNS entries and managing certificates manually (or through alternative methods) before MAS installation. When false (default), the role automatically creates DNS entries and optionally configures Let's Encrypt integration.
docs.title: mas_manual_cert_mgmt

docs.text: OpenShift namespace where Certificate Manager is installed — any valid Kubernetes namespace name. Optional Environment Variable: CERT_MANAGER_NAMESPACE Default: None (automatically detected) ClusterIssuer resources for Let's Encrypt integration are created referencing this namespace, so an incorrect value will cause ClusterIssuer creation to fail. Automatic detection typically finds Certificate Manager in standard namespaces; only override it when using a custom installation or when detection fails.
docs.title: cert_manager_namespace

docs.text: Unique identifier for the MAS instance requiring DNS configuration — a lowercase alphanumeric string, 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , inst1 ), that must match the instance ID used during MAS core installation. Required for MAS mode Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None This ID is embedded in DNS record names and ClusterIssuer names (e.g. {mas_instance_id}-cloudflare-le-prod ), so an incorrect ID will create DNS entries for the wrong instance. Works with mas_domain to construct full DNS names for MAS routes.
docs.title: mas_instance_id

docs.text: Workspace identifier for the MAS installation requiring DNS configuration — a lowercase alphanumeric string (e.g. masdev , prod , ws1 ) that must match an existing workspace in your MAS instance, typically the primary workspace. Required for MAS mode Environment Variable: MAS_WORKSPACE_ID Default: None This ID is used together with mas_instance_id and mas_domain to generate workspace-specific DNS entries and routes; an incorrect workspace ID may result in DNS entries that don't match your MAS workspace configuration.
docs.title: mas_workspace_id

docs.text: Custom domain name for accessing MAS web interfaces and APIs — any valid DNS domain name (e.g. mas.mycompany.com , prod-mas.example.org ). Required for MAS mode Environment Variable: MAS_DOMAIN Default: None All MAS URLs and DNS entries are constructed from this domain (e.g. admin.{mas_domain} , home.{mas_domain} , api.{mas_domain} ), and it must be the same domain used in MAS core installation and be properly configured in your DNS provider's zone before running this role. Subdomain mode is available via cloudflare_subdomain or cis_subdomain . DNS propagation may take time after entries are created.
docs.title: mas_domain

docs.text: Override for the OpenShift cluster ingress domain used as the target for DNS CNAME records — e.g. apps.cluster-name.domain.com . Optional Environment Variable: OCP_INGRESS Default: None (automatically detected from the cluster) Leave unset to allow automatic detection (recommended); set only when automatic detection fails, when using a non-default ingress controller, or in airgap or restricted network environments where detection may not work. An incorrect value will cause DNS entries to point to the wrong location.
docs.title: ocp_ingress

docs.text: Contact email for Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 certificate issuance. Setting this is the sole signal that enables HTTP-01 mode — no separate flag is needed. Optional — only required when using Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 with path-based routing Environment Variable: MAS_LE_EMAIL Default: None Only applies when mas_routing_mode is path ; existing DNS-01 behaviour is unchanged when this is not set.
docs.title: mas_le_email

docs.text: Kind of cert-manager issuer resource to create for Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 ( ClusterIssuer or Issuer ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ISSUER_KIND Default: ClusterIssuer
docs.title: mas_issuer_kind

docs.text: Name of the OpenShift IngressController used for the HTTP-01 ACME challenge solver. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_INGRESS_CONTROLLER_NAME Default: default Only relevant when mas_le_email is set.
docs.title: mas_ingress_controller_name

docs.text: Comma-separated list of key=value labels to apply to DNS-related resources (e.g. env=prod,team=platform,component=dns ). Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels are for organization, selection, filtering, resource tracking, cost allocation, and custom automation; they do not affect DNS functionality.
docs.title: custom_labels

docs.text: Local directory path where the edge routes output file will be saved — any valid local filesystem path (e.g. /home/user/mas-output , ~/masconfig , ./output ). Optional Environment Variable: OUTPUT_DIR Default: . (current directory) The edge-routes-{mas_instance_id}.txt file containing information about the DNS entries and routes created by this role is written to this directory; it is useful for verifying DNS configuration and troubleshooting connectivity issues. Ensure the directory exists and is writable.
docs.title: output_dir

docs.text: Email address associated with your Cloudflare account, used together with cloudflare_apitoken to authenticate Cloudflare API requests. Required if dns_provider is set to cloudflare Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL Default: None The account must have permissions to create and manage DNS records in the target zone ( cloudflare_zone ); an incorrect email will cause authentication failures.
docs.title: cloudflare_email

docs.text: API token for authenticating with the Cloudflare API, used together with cloudflare_email . Required if dns_provider is set to cloudflare Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_APITOKEN Default: None Generate the token from the Cloudflare dashboard with DNS edit permissions for the target zone, following the Cloudflare documentation . Keep this token secure and do not commit it to source control.
docs.title: cloudflare_apitoken

docs.text: DNS zone name managed by Cloudflare where MAS DNS entries will be created — e.g. mydomain.com , example.org . Required if dns_provider is set to cloudflare Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_ZONE Default: None Must be an active zone configured in your Cloudflare account and the parent domain of mas_domain (or equal to it for top-level entries); the credentials used must have access to this zone. Ensure the zone is active and DNS is properly delegated before running this role.
docs.title: cloudflare_zone

docs.text: Subdomain within the Cloudflare zone for MAS DNS entries (subdomain mode). Optional Environment Variable: CLOUDFLARE_SUBDOMAIN Default: None (uses top-level DNS entries) Use when your DNS zone will host multiple MAS instances or other services, i.e. when mas_domain is a subdomain of cloudflare_zone . When set, DNS entries are created as admin.{cloudflare_subdomain} , home.{cloudflare_subdomain} , etc.; when unset, entries are created directly in the zone as admin , home , etc. The relationship must be {cloudflare_subdomain}.{cloudflare_zone} = mas_domain — for example, if the zone is mycompany.com and mas_domain is mas.mycompany.com , set the subdomain to mas .
docs.title: cloudflare_subdomain

docs.text: Note When using CIS integration, some resources will be installed in the cluster such as RBACs, API Services and CIS Webhook deployments. In OCP 4.12+, to avoid CIS webhook deployment failure at start up, this role will grant anyuid permission to cert-manager-webhook-ibm-cis service account so it can fully access the cert-manager-webhook-ibm-cis deployment pod as a workaround: oc adm policy add-scc-to-user anyuid -z cert-manager-webhook-ibm-cis -n ibm-common-services
docs.title: IBM Cloud Internet Services DNS Integration

docs.text: Email address for Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer registration when using IBM CIS. Required if dns_provider is set to cis Environment Variable: CIS_EMAIL Default: None This email is embedded in the {mas_instance_id}-cis-le-prod ClusterIssuer and registered with Let's Encrypt, which uses it for certificate expiration notifications and account recovery — use a monitored team or service email address rather than a personal one.
docs.title: cis_email

docs.text: IBM Cloud API key for authenticating with IBM Cloud Internet Services. Required if dns_provider is set to cis Environment Variable: CIS_APIKEY Default: None Generate the key from IBM Cloud IAM with permissions for the CIS instance specified by cis_crn ; it authenticates all CIS API operations including DNS record management and ClusterIssuer configuration. Keep this key secure and do not commit it to source control.
docs.title: cis_apikey

docs.text: Cloud Resource Name (CRN) identifying the IBM Cloud Internet Services instance — format crn:v1:bluemix:public:internet-svcs:... . Required if dns_provider is set to cis Environment Variable: CIS_CRN Default: None Obtain the CRN from the IBM Cloud console under your CIS instance details; it must correspond to the instance containing your target DNS zone. All DNS operations target this CIS instance, so an incorrect CRN will cause operations to fail or target the wrong instance.
docs.title: cis_crn

docs.text: Subdomain within the CIS zone for MAS DNS entries (subdomain mode). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_SUBDOMAIN Default: None (uses top-level DNS entries) Use when your CIS zone will host multiple MAS instances or other services, i.e. when mas_domain is a subdomain of your CIS zone domain. When set, DNS entries are created as admin.{cis_subdomain} , home.{cis_subdomain} , etc.; when unset, entries are created directly in the zone as admin , home , etc. The relationship must be {cis_subdomain}.{cis_zone_domain} = mas_domain — for example, if the CIS zone is mycompany.com and mas_domain is mas.mycompany.com , set the subdomain to mas .
docs.title: cis_subdomain

docs.text: Enables enhanced security features for IBM CIS DNS integration. Optional Environment Variable: CIS_ENHANCED_SECURITY Default: false When enabled, this configures a WAF firewall with rules optimized for MAS ( cis_waf ), proxy mode for DNS entries so traffic is routed through CIS ( cis_proxy ), an expanded list of DNS entries for comprehensive coverage, prevention of wildcard DNS entries, and edge certificates in the CIS instance. Recommended for production environments requiring WAF and proxy protection; leave false for development/test environments. See the IBM Cloud CIS security documentation for details — enhanced security may impact performance due to proxy routing.
docs.title: cis_enhanced_security

docs.text: Custom name for the CIS service resources created in the cluster — a valid Kubernetes resource name (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_SERVICE_NAME Default: {ClusterName}-cis-{mas_instance_id} (auto-generated) Leave unset to use the auto-generated name (recommended); set only when you need a specific naming convention or when the auto-generated name conflicts with existing resources. Changing it after initial deployment may cause issues with resource management.
docs.title: cis_service_name

docs.text: Controls Web Application Firewall (WAF) configuration for CIS. Optional Environment Variable: CIS_WAF Default: true When true , the WAF is configured with rules specifically tuned to protect MAS while allowing required application functionality; when false , the WAF is not configured (less security protection). Set to false only if WAF causes issues or conflicts with other security tools. Typically used in conjunction with cis_enhanced_security and cis_proxy .
docs.title: cis_waf

docs.text: Controls whether DNS entries use CIS proxy mode (traffic routed through CIS). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_PROXY Default: false When true , traffic routes through CIS (orange cloud icon in the CIS console), enabling DDoS protection and CIS security features but adding latency; when false , DNS entries point directly to the OpenShift ingress (grey cloud icon) — lower latency but no CIS protection. Proxy mode is required for WAF and other CIS security features to function, so consider the latency vs. security tradeoff for your use case.
docs.title: cis_proxy

docs.text: Comma-separated list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges (IPv4 and IPv6) that are permitted to access the MAS instance, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8,192.168.1.0/24,2405:201:d000:9060::/64,49.37.171.108 . Optional Environment Variable: CIS_ALLOWED_IPS Default: None When set, a CIS WAF custom block rule is created with the expression not ip.src in {<ip1> <ip2> ...} and http.host contains "<mas_domain>" , denying all traffic not originating from the specified IPs on the MAS domain. When unset or empty, any existing WAF block rule for this instance is removed, restoring unrestricted access. Supported MAS versions : 9.1.x and above only; ignored when mas_channel is 9.0.x or earlier Requires dns_provider=cis with CIS enhanced security enabled ( cis_enhanced_security and cis_waf ); the rule is scoped to mas_domain and identified in CIS by the description mas-ip-allowlist-<mas_domain> . IP allowlisting requires MAS 9.1.x or above — when mas_channel is 9.0.x or earlier, the WAF allowlist task is automatically skipped regardless of whether this variable is set. Feature status reporting (SaaS) When the allowlist is added, updated or removed, the role records the progress of the change in the SaaS feature status MongoDB by calling mas-devops-feature-status-update . Status is written only when all of the following are true: MAS mode is enabled cis_waf is enabled and mas_channel is 9.1.x or above devops_mongo_uri , account_id , cluster_id and region_id are all set (no status call is made when any of them is empty) The WAF rule in CIS differs from the requested cis_allowed_ips (no status call is made when the allowlist is already in the desired state) Status is only ever written for the MAS instance; in AI Service mode the allowlist rule is still managed, but no status is written. Status Written when REQUESTED An allowlist change is detected, before any other CIS work starts IN_PROGRESS Just before the WAF rule is created, updated or deleted ACTIVE The WAF rule was created or updated successfully DEACTIVATED The WAF rule was deleted successfully ( cis_allowed_ips unset or empty) ERROR A failure occurs after REQUESTED and the allowlist change has not completed successfully, including a failed WAF rule call after its retries. A failure after ACTIVE / DEACTIVATED has been reached does not write ERROR Whether or not status reporting is active, a failed CIS call (including a failed WAF rule create / update / delete after its retries) always fails the job. The call made for each status is: bash mas-devops-feature-status-update status-update \ --region "<region_id>" \ --instance-id "<mas_instance_id>" \ --account "<account_id>" \ --cluster "<cluster_id>" \ --subscription-id "<subscription_id>" \ --type allow-list \ --feature-details '{"ips": ["<ip1>", "<ip2>"]}' \ --deployment-start "<start timestamp>" \ --status <REQUESTED|IN_PROGRESS|ACTIVE|DEACTIVATED|ERROR> \ --status-details '{"message": "<message>", "request_configuration": "<ip1>, <ip2>"}' \ --deployment-end "<end timestamp>" --feature-details carries the requested IPs ( [] when the allowlist is being removed). --subscription-id is optional and is only passed when subscription_id is set. --deployment-start is the time the change was detected (taken when the change is detected, not when the play started) and is passed unchanged on every call. --deployment-end is only passed for ACTIVE , DEACTIVATED and ERROR , and is taken when that status is written. The JSON passed to --status-details and --feature-details is built in Ansible and shell-quoted, so quotes, newlines and backslashes in CIS output are safe. For ERROR , --status-details also includes error_code and an error_source object ( gitops_version , filename , log_file and stacktrace ). The following variables are used when writing the status: Variable Environment variable Default devops_mongo_uri DEVOPS_MONGO_URI None. Status updates are skipped when empty account_id ACCOUNT_ID None. Status updates are skipped when empty cluster_id CLUSTER_ID None. Status updates are skipped when empty region_id REGION_ID None. Status updates are skipped when empty subscription_id SLS_SUBSCRIPTION_ID None. Optional, --subscription-id is omitted when empty account_id , cluster_id , region_id and subscription_id identify the MAS instance the status is recorded for — they are not the account, region or cluster of the CIS instance. Warning Failures while disabling WAF rules ( cis_waf_rule.yml ) or managed ruleset rules ( cis_managed_ruleset.yml ) used to be tolerated and now fail the job in MAS mode, so that they are reported as ERROR and are not silently ignored.
docs.title: cis_allowed_ips
IBM CIS DNS Entries and Edge Certificates

docs.text: Whether to update DNS entries if they already exist. Optional Environment Variable: UPDATE_DNS_ENTRIES Default: true Set to false to leave existing DNS entries untouched.
docs.title: update_dns

docs.text: Whether to force deletion of wildcard DNS entries in CIS. Optional Environment Variable: DELETE_WILDCARDS Default: false
docs.title: delete_wildcards

docs.text: Whether to override and delete any existing edge certificates in the CIS instance when creating new edge certificates. Optional Environment Variable: OVERRIDE_EDGE_CERTS Default: true Set to false to keep existing edge certificates.
docs.title: override_edge_certs

docs.text: Comma separated list of entries to add for edge certificates, broken down into functional areas of MAS: all (include all entries — default), core (MAS Core), health (MAS Health App), iot (MAS IoT app), manage (MAS Manage app), monitor (MAS Monitor app), predict (MAS Predict app), visualinspection (MAS VisualInspection app), optimizer (MAS Optimizer app), assist (MAS Assist app), arcgis (MAS Arcgis), reportdb (MAS ReportDB), facilities (MAS Facilities app), cpd-public (CP4D public route — creates cpd-public.<mas_domain> DNS CNAME and edge certificate for VPN-free CP4D access). Optional Environment Variable: CIS_ENTRIES_TO_ADD Default: all
docs.title: cis_entries_to_add

docs.text: Prerequisites: To run this role successfully you must have already installed the AWS CLI . Also, you need to have AWS user credentials configured via aws configure command or simply export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables with your corresponding AWS username credentials prior running this role. Note In some cases, the Route 53 zone may not resolve the certificate challenges generated by IBM Certificate Manager, which could cause a problem while issuing the public certificates via Let's Encrypt. In this case, a manual workaround might be needed in cert-manager-controller pod to enable recursive nameservers. For more details on how to apply this workaround, refer to this documentation . This workaround is not automated, as most of the times this is not needed, but when it is, it requires the cert-manager-controller pod to be stopped, thus we want to avoid making this behavior as standard approach.
docs.title: AWS Route 53

docs.text: AWS Route53 Hosted Zone name. Required if dns_provider is set to route53 Environment Variable: ROUTE53_HOSTED_ZONE_NAME Default: None
docs.title: route53_hosted_zone_name

docs.text: AWS Route53 Hosted Zone region. Optional Environment Variable: ROUTE53_HOSTED_ZONE_REGION Default: Same value as defined in AWS_REGION , or us-east-2 if none is defined
docs.title: route53_hosted_zone_region

docs.text: Subdomain used to create the corresponding CNAME entries in the targeted Route53 hosted zone. Optional Environment Variable: ROUTE53_SUBDOMAIN Default: None The Route53 subdomain combined with the Route53 hosted zone name must match the chosen MAS domain, otherwise the DNS records won't be able to get resolved — e.g. MAS top level domain my-mas-instance.mycompany.com , AWS Route53 hosted zone name mycompany.com , AWS Route53 subdomain my-mas-instance .
docs.title: route53_subdomain

docs.text: AWS Route53 contact e-mail. Will be set in the cluster issuer created in order to receive alerts. Optional Environment Variable: ROUTE53_EMAIL Default: None
docs.title: route53_email

docs.text: AWS access key ID for authentication. Required if dns_provider is set to route53 Environment Variable: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None
docs.title: aws_access_key_id

docs.text: AWS secret access key for authentication. Required if dns_provider is set to route53 Environment Variable: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None
docs.title: aws_secret_access_key

docs.text: Namespace where the Cloud Pak for Data is installed and the cpd route exists. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE Default: None If set, then this role will also attempt to configure public certificates to the CPD route using the DNS provider defined.
docs.title: cpd_instance_namespace

docs.text: Certificate issuer responsible for generating the public certificate for your CPD route. Optional Environment Variable: CPD_PROD_ISSUER_NAME Default: {mas_instance_id}-{dns_provider}-le-prod (the same production issuer used to set up the MAS instance)
docs.title: cpd_prod_issuer_name

docs.text: suite_install ¤ This role installs Maximo Application Suite. It internally resolves the namespace based on the mas_instance_id as mas-{mas_instance_id}-core . Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_catalog_source No ibm-operator-catalog mas_channel Yes None mas_domain No None mas_instance_id Yes None mas_entitlement_key Yes Value of IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY mas_config_dir No None mas_annotations No None mas_img_pull_policy No None custom_labels No None mas_manual_cert_mgmt No false mas_routing_mode No None mas_manual_route_mgmt No false mas_trust_default_cas No None mas_pod_templates_dir No None mas_cluster_issuer Conditional None mas_issuer_kind No None mas_certificate_duration No 8760h0m0s mas_certificate_renew_before No 720h0m0s mas_superuser_username Conditional None mas_superuser_password Conditional None artifactory_username Conditional None artifactory_token Conditional None mas_cluster_issuer is required when automatic certificate management is enabled ( mas_manual_cert_mgmt is false ). The superuser and Artifactory credentials only apply in the specific scenarios described in their sections. Basic Install ¤ mas_catalog_source ¤ OpenShift operator catalog source containing the MAS operator subscription — any valid CatalogSource name in the openshift-marketplace namespace, typically ibm-operator-catalog . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CATALOG_SOURCE Default: ibm-operator-catalog Controls where OpenShift looks for the MAS operator images and metadata, and works with mas_channel to determine the version installed. Only change it when directed to use a custom catalog for specific testing or airgap scenarios — an invalid catalog source causes the subscription to fail. mas_channel ¤ MAS operator subscription channel, which determines the version stream installed and the updates applied automatically — for example 8.9.x , 8.10.x , 8.11.x , or 9.0.x (check the IBM Operator Catalog for currently available channels). Required Environment Variable: MAS_CHANNEL Default: None The channel corresponds to major.minor version releases and determines the feature set and compatibility level of the installation. Changing channels after installation triggers an upgrade to the latest version in the new channel, which may require application reconfiguration and testing — consult the MAS compatibility matrix and upgrade documentation before changing it. Basic Configuration ¤ mas_domain ¤ Custom domain name used to construct all MAS URLs (for example admin.{mas_domain} , home.{mas_domain} ) — any valid DNS domain such as mas.mycompany.com or prod-mas.example.org . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_DOMAIN Default: None (auto-generated as {mas_instance_id}.{cluster ingress domain} ) Set it for production environments that need branded or corporate domain names, integration with external DNS providers (Cloudflare, Route53, IBM CIS), or custom SSL certificates tied to a specific domain; leave unset for development and testing. DNS must resolve the domain to the cluster, and the value must align with mas_routing_mode . The suite_dns role uses it to configure DNS entries and certificates. mas_instance_id ¤ Unique identifier for this MAS installation within the cluster — a string of 3-12 characters using lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, starting with a lowercase letter and ending with a lowercase letter or number (for example prod , dev01 , mastest ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None This ID becomes the core namespace name ( mas-{mas_instance_id}-core ) and is embedded in resource names and configuration identifiers across all MAS configuration, application, and backup/restore roles. It must be unique within the cluster when running multiple instances and cannot be changed after installation without reinstalling — use consistent naming across environments (for example dev , test , prod ). mas_entitlement_key ¤ IBM entitlement key authenticating image pulls from IBM Container Registry — for development builds on Artifactory, use your Artifactory API key instead. Required Environment Variable: MAS_ENTITLEMENT_KEY Default: Value of IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY if set Obtain the key from the IBM Container Library at https://myibm.ibm.com/products-services/containerlibrary . The key is stored in a Kubernetes secret and used to create image pull secrets for all MAS pods — invalid or expired keys cause image pull failures and the installation cannot proceed. Keep the key secure and do not commit it to source control. mas_config_dir ¤ Local directory containing Kubernetes configuration files that are applied to the cluster during MAS installation. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CONFIG_DIR Default: None All *.yaml and *.yml files in the directory are applied with oc apply in alphabetical order — typically MAS configuration resources (MongoCfg, BASCfg, JdbcCfg, etc.) generated by dependency roles such as mongodb , db2 , and sls , which the suite_config role applies after this role. Files must be valid Kubernetes resources; the role does not validate their contents before applying, and invalid resources cause it to fail. Advanced Configuration ¤ mas_annotations ¤ Comma-separated list of key=value annotations applied to all MAS resources — for example mas.ibm.com/operationalMode=nonproduction or key1=value1,key2=value2 . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ANNOTATIONS Default: None The role validates annotation values and combinations (including the mas.ibm.com/hyperscaler* annotations) and fails the installation on invalid input. Works alongside custom_labels for resource metadata. Warning The mas.ibm.com/operationalMode=nonproduction annotation significantly reduces CPU and memory requirements and must only be used in development and test environments — it reduces resource allocations below production requirements. mas_img_pull_policy ¤ Image pull policy for all MAS container images: Always , IfNotPresent , or Never . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_IMG_PULL_POLICY Default: None (operator default) Always pulls the latest image on every pod restart (useful in development, at the cost of slower starts and higher network usage), IfNotPresent uses cached images for faster starts (typical for production), and Never requires images to be pre-loaded (airgap environments). When unset, imagePullPolicy is omitted from the Suite CR and the operator default (typically IfNotPresent ) applies. custom_labels ¤ Comma-separated list of key=value labels applied to all MAS resources — for example env=prod,team=platform,cost-center=12345 . Optional Environment Variable: CUSTOM_LABELS Default: None Labels enable resource organization, selection, and filtering with standard Kubernetes tooling ( oc get -l , monitoring queries, automation scripts) and support cost allocation and labeling standards. They do not affect MAS functionality. Works alongside mas_annotations for resource metadata. mas_manual_cert_mgmt ¤ Enables manual certificate management, disabling automatic certificate generation by cert-manager. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_MANUAL_CERT_MGMT Default: false When true , you must manually create and manage all certificates required by MAS, including renewal before expiry, and the suite_dns role will not configure automatic certificate issuers. When false (default), cert-manager generates and renews certificates and mas_cluster_issuer must be set. Manual certificate management carries significant operational overhead — use automatic management unless you have specific requirements. mas_routing_mode ¤ URL routing strategy for MAS applications and services: subdomain (for example admin.mas.example.com ) or path (for example mas.example.com/admin ). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ROUTING_MODE Default: None (MAS default: subdomain ) subdomain creates separate DNS entries for each service (requires wildcard DNS or multiple entries) and is recommended for production; path uses a single DNS entry with path-based routing, which is simpler for DNS but produces more complex URLs. The choice affects DNS configuration in the suite_dns role and certificate requirements (wildcard vs single certificate), and must align with mas_domain . It cannot be changed after installation without reinstalling. mas_manual_route_mgmt ¤ Enables manual route management, disabling automatic route creation and management by MAS. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_MANUAL_ROUTE_MGMT Default: false Set to true only when alternative routing is required — you must then manually create and manage all routes required by MAS yourself. mas_trust_default_cas ¤ Controls whether default system Certificate Authorities (such as Let's Encrypt and DigiCert) are included in MAS trust stores. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_TRUST_DEFAULT_CAS Default: None (MAS default: true ) Leave unset for most installations so MAS can connect to services using certificates from well-known public CAs. Set to false only in highly restricted or airgap environments where external connections are not permitted — MAS will then only trust explicitly configured custom CAs, which may break connections to external services. Only available in MAS 8.11 and above; it has no effect in earlier versions. mas_pod_templates_dir ¤ Directory containing pod template customization files for MAS workloads — for example ibm-mas-suite.yml (core suite workloads), ibm-mas-coreidp.yml (identity provider workloads), or ibm-data-dictionary-assetdatadictionary.yml (data dictionary workloads). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_POD_TEMPLATES_DIR Default: None Pod templates customize resource requests and limits, node selectors, tolerations, and QoS classes for MAS workloads — incorrect configurations can cause pods to fail scheduling or perform poorly. See the MAS CLI pod templates for examples and the product documentation for full details. Similar pod template configuration is available in other roles (SLS, applications). Certificate Management ¤ mas_cluster_issuer ¤ Name of the cert-manager ClusterIssuer used for automatic certificate generation — for example {mas_instance_id}-cloudflare-le-prod , as created by the suite_dns role. Required when mas_manual_cert_mgmt is false Environment Variable: MAS_CLUSTER_ISSUER Default: None The ClusterIssuer defines the Certificate Authority and authentication method used for all MAS certificates. Ensure it is created and functional before installing MAS (test certificate generation with a test Certificate resource first) — if it is misconfigured or lacks necessary credentials, certificate generation fails and MAS will not be accessible. mas_issuer_kind ¤ Issuer kind written to spec.settings.issuerKind of the MAS Suite custom resource: Issuer (namespace-scoped) or ClusterIssuer (cluster-scoped). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ISSUER_KIND Default: None (automatically set to ClusterIssuer when installing MAS 9.2 or later) Issuer certificate references remain namespace-scoped and can be used in all permission modes ( cluster , namespaced , and minimal ), while ClusterIssuer references a cluster-scoped issuer and should only be used when MAS is installed in cluster permission mode. mas_certificate_duration ¤ Validity period for MAS certificates, as a duration string in {hours}h{minutes}m{seconds}s format — for example 8760h0m0s (1 year, default), 2160h0m0s (90 days), or 17520h0m0s (2 years). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CERTIFICATE_DURATION Default: 8760h0m0s (1 year) Must be longer than mas_certificate_renew_before and only applies when automatic certificate management is in use. Shorter durations increase security but require more frequent renewals; cert-manager renews certificates automatically before they expire. mas_certificate_renew_before ¤ How far in advance of expiry cert-manager renews certificates, as a duration string in {hours}h{minutes}m{seconds}s format — for example 720h0m0s (30 days, default), 1440h0m0s (60 days), or 168h0m0s (7 days). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CERTIFICATE_RENEW_BEFORE Default: 720h0m0s (30 days) Must be shorter than mas_certificate_duration and only applies when automatic certificate management is in use. Longer renewal windows provide more time to resolve renewal issues but result in more frequent certificate changes. Superuser Account ¤ The MAS Superuser account username and password can be customized during the install by setting both of these variables. mas_superuser_username ¤ Custom username for the MAS superuser administrator account — any valid username string (alphanumeric, may include underscores and hyphens). Optional — must be set together with mas_superuser_password Environment Variable: MAS_SUPERUSER_USERNAME Default: None (uses MAS default superuser) The superuser has full administrative access to all MAS functions and applications. If only one of username/password is set, both are ignored and the default account is used. mas_superuser_password ¤ Custom password for the MAS superuser administrator account — any string meeting MAS password requirements (minimum length, complexity). Optional — must be set together with mas_superuser_username Environment Variable: MAS_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD Default: None (auto-generated) Setting the password in advance lets you know the superuser credentials and comply with organizational password policies. If only one of username/password is set, both are ignored and the default account is used with an auto-generated password. Keep the password secure and do not commit it to source control. Developer Mode ¤ artifactory_username ¤ Username for authenticating to Artifactory for development builds — your IBM w3Id username. Optional — only required when installing development builds from Artifactory Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None Must be set together with artifactory_token ; the credentials are used to create image pull secrets for Artifactory registries when mas_icr_cp and mas_icr_cpopen are pointed at Artifactory. Not needed for production installations using IBM Container Registry with an entitlement key. artifactory_token ¤ API token for authenticating to Artifactory for development builds. Optional — only required when installing development builds from Artifactory Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None Must be set together with artifactory_username and can serve as the mas_entitlement_key equivalent for development builds. Only for internal development and testing — keep tokens secure, and use IBM Container Registry with entitlement keys for production. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: "inst1" mas_config_dir: "/home/david/masconfig" mas_entitlement_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'IBM_ENTITLEMENT_KEY') }}" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_install - ibm.mas_devops.suite_config - ibm.mas_devops.suite_verify License ¤ EPL-2.0
