docs.text: suite_restore ¤ Restore MAS Core Overview ¤ This role supports restoring the MAS Core namespace resources and supporting resources in other namespace when provided the backup archive generated from suite_backup role. Important Supported only for MAS 9.1.x. Restore can only be made to an instance with the same MAS instance ID as the backup. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_backup_dir Yes None suite_backup_version Yes None mas_domain No NO_OVERRIDE include_sls_from_backup No true sls_url No NO_OVERRIDE sls_cfg_file Conditional None include_dro_from_backup No true bas_url No NO_OVERRIDE dro_cfg_file Conditional None sls_cfg_file is required only when include_sls_from_backup is false , and dro_cfg_file only when include_dro_from_backup is false . Backup Source ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ The instance ID of the Maximo Application Suite installation to restore. This must match the instance ID of the backup. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None mas_backup_dir ¤ The local directory path where backup files to restore are stored — for example /tmp/mas_backups . Required Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None suite_backup_version ¤ The version of the backup file located in the MAS_BACKUP_DIR to be used in the restore — for example 20260116-130937 . Required Environment Variable: SUITE_BACKUP_VERSION Default: None Domain Override ¤ mas_domain ¤ The domain to use for the MAS Suite instance — for example mydomain.example.com . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_DOMAIN Default: NO_OVERRIDE (uses value from backup) Use to change the domain when restoring to a different cluster; when not provided, the domain from the backup is used. SLS Configuration ¤ include_sls_from_backup ¤ Controls whether to restore the Suite SLS (Suite License Service) configuration from the backup archive. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_SLS_FROM_BACKUP Default: true Set to true when the registration key stays the same, either because the same SLS service is also being restored or because you are using a centralized SLS service that has not changed. If you plan to install and use a new SLS service, set this to false and use the sls_cfg_file variable to point to the new SLS configuration file. sls_url ¤ The URL for the Suite License Service (SLS) — for example https://sls.example.com . Only applies when include_sls_from_backup is true . Optional Environment Variable: SLS_URL Default: NO_OVERRIDE (uses value from backup) Use when the domain has changed for SLS but SLS was restored from a backup, so the registration key is the same. sls_cfg_file ¤ Path to the file containing an external SLS configuration YAML file to apply — for example /tmp/sls_config/sls.yml . Only applies when include_sls_from_backup is false . Required when include_sls_from_backup is false Environment Variable: SLS_CFG_FILE Default: None Use SLS configuration from outside the backup archive (e.g., from a separate SLS role execution). DRO (BAS) Configuration ¤ include_dro_from_backup ¤ Controls whether to restore the Suite DRO configuration from the backup archive. Optional Environment Variable: INCLUDE_DRO_FROM_BACKUP Default: true Set to true when the DRO details stay the same and you are using a centralized DRO service that has not changed. If you plan to install and use a new DRO service, set this to false and use the dro_cfg_file variable to point to the new DRO configuration file. bas_url ¤ The URL for the Behavior Analytics Service (BAS) — for example https://bas.example.com . Only applies when include_dro_from_backup is true . Optional Environment Variable: BAS_URL Default: NO_OVERRIDE (uses value from backup) Use when the domain has changed for DRO but DRO was restored from a backup, so the API key is the same. dro_cfg_file ¤ Path to the file containing an external DRO (BAS) configuration YAML file to apply — for example /tmp/dro_config/dro.yml . Only applies when include_dro_from_backup is false . Required when include_dro_from_backup is false Environment Variable: DRO_CFG_FILE Default: None Use DRO configuration from outside the backup archive (e.g., from a separate DRO role execution). Restore Operations ¤ This section provides comprehensive information about MAS Core restore operations. Overview ¤ The MAS Core restore operation performs a complete restoration of a MAS Core installation from a backup created by the suite_backup role. The restore process recreates all namespace resources and supporting resources in the correct order. Important : Restore can only be made to an instance with the same MAS instance ID as the backup. Restore Process ¤ The MAS Core restore operation performs the following steps in sequence: Validation : Verifies required variables and backup archive existence Certificate Manager Check : Ensures cert-manager is installed in the cluster Projects Restoration : Restores the MAS Core namespace Secrets and ConfigMaps : Restores all secrets and configuration maps Operator Resources : Restores OperatorGroups and Subscriptions Subscription Wait : Waits for subscriptions to be ready (up to 30 minutes) Certificate Manager Resources : Restores ClusterIssuers, Issuers, and Certificates MAS Addon Resources : Restores MVIEdge, ReplicaDB, and GenericAddon resources MAS Configuration Resources : Restores all config.mas.ibm.com resources with optional overrides: BasCfg (if include_dro_from_backup is true, with optional bas_url override) SlsCfg (if include_sls_from_backup is true, with optional sls_url override) AppCfg, IDPCfg, JdbcCfg, KafkaCfg, MongoCfg, ObjectStorageCfg, etc. MAS Internal Resources : Restores CoreIDP resources Suite Restoration : Restores the Suite CR with optional mas_domain override Suite Wait : Waits for Suite to be ready (up to 60 minutes) Workspace Restoration : Restores all Workspace CRs Workspace Wait : Waits for all Workspaces to be ready (up to 60 minutes) Configuration Override Options ¤ The restore process supports several override options to adapt the backup to a new environment: Domain Override: Use mas_domain to change the domain when restoring to a different cluster Default: Uses the domain from the backup SLS Configuration: If include_sls_from_backup=true : Restores SlsCfg from backup Use sls_url to override the SLS URL if the domain changed If include_sls_from_backup=false : Use sls_cfg_file to provide external SLS configuration DRO Configuration: If include_dro_from_backup=true : Restores BasCfg from backup Use bas_url to override the BAS URL if the domain changed If include_dro_from_backup=false : Use dro_cfg_file to provide external DRO configuration When to Use ¤ Full Restore Scenarios: Disaster recovery after cluster failure Migrating MAS Core to a new cluster Recreating a deleted MAS Core instance Setting up a new environment from backup Testing backup integrity in non-production Partial Configuration Scenarios: Restoring with new SLS service (set include_sls_from_backup=false ) Restoring with new DRO service (set include_dro_from_backup=false ) Restoring to cluster with different domain (use mas_domain override) Important Considerations ¤ Prerequisites: Target cluster must have Certificate Manager installed Target cluster must have the same MAS instance ID as the backup Required dependencies (MongoDB, Db2, etc.) must be available and accessible Sufficient cluster resources (CPU, memory, storage) must be available Instance ID Requirement: Restore can only be made to an instance with the same MAS instance ID The instance ID is embedded in resource names and cannot be changed Storage Requirements: Ensure backup directory is accessible from the restore environment Verify backup archive integrity before starting restore Security: Backup files contain sensitive data including credentials and certificates Ensure secure transfer of backup files to restore environment Verify backup file permissions and access controls Configuration Dependencies: If using external SLS/DRO configuration files, ensure they are valid and accessible Coordinate with database restore operations to ensure data consistency Verify network connectivity to external services (SLS, DRO, databases) Restore Best Practices ¤ Pre-Restore Validation : Verify backup archive exists and is complete Confirm Certificate Manager is installed Ensure target cluster has sufficient resources Verify MAS instance ID matches the backup Dependency Coordination : Restore databases (MongoDB, Db2) before MAS Core Restore SLS before MAS Core if using separate SLS Restore DRO before MAS Core if using separate DRO Ensure all external services are accessible Configuration Planning : Determine if domain override is needed Decide whether to use backup SLS/DRO or new services Prepare external configuration files if needed Document any configuration changes Post-Restore Verification : Verify Suite status is Ready Verify all Workspaces are Ready Test application connectivity Verify database connections Test user authentication Disaster Recovery : Test restore procedures regularly in non-production Document restore procedures and configuration Maintain backup version identifiers Keep external configuration files secure and accessible Example Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - hosts: localhost vars: mas_instance_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'MAS_INSTANCE_ID') }}" mas_backup_dir: /tmp/mas_backups suite_backup_version: 20260116-130937 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_restore License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: suite_rollback ¤ This role rolls back Maximo Application Suite core platform to an earlier version. Rollback capability is available in MAS 8.11 and later versions. Each MAS version includes a list of supported rollback target versions. For example, you can roll back from MAS 8.11.x to 8.11.0. Warning Rollback is a significant operation that should be carefully planned and tested. Always perform a dry run first and ensure you have backups before proceeding with actual rollback. What This Role Does ¤ Validates the specified target version is compatible for rollback from the current version Verifies the core platform is not already at the target version Executes the rollback to the desired version (unless dry run mode is enabled) Validates the core platform successfully reconciles at the rolled back version Note : Does not validate that all core services successfully deploy after reconcile (future enhancement) Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_core_version Conditional None rollback_mas_core No true verify_core_version No false mas_rollback_dryrun No false skip_compatibility_check No false mas_core_version is only required when rollback_mas_core or verify_core_version is true . Instance and Version ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier to rollback — a lowercase alphanumeric string, 3-12 characters (e.g., prod , dev , masinst1 ), matching the instance ID from MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None All validation and rollback operations target this instance. Ensure the instance is in a stable state before initiating rollback, and that applications are stopped or in maintenance mode during rollback. mas_core_version ¤ Target MAS core version for rollback or verification — a valid MAS version string (e.g., 8.11.0 , 8.11.1 , 8.12.0 ) that must be listed in the current version's supported rollback targets. Required when rollback_mas_core=true or verify_core_version=true Environment Variable: MAS_CORE_VERSION Default: None The role validates this version is compatible before proceeding. Check the MAS documentation for supported rollback paths from your current version — not all versions support rollback to all earlier versions. Rollback Behavior ¤ rollback_mas_core ¤ Controls whether the role performs the rollback or only validates/verifies version information — true to execute the rollback to the specified version (default), false to skip rollback execution. Optional Environment Variable: ROLLBACK_MAS_CORE Default: true When false , typically used with verify_core_version=true to check the current version without making changes; combine with mas_rollback_dryrun=true for validation without changes. verify_core_version ¤ Version verification mode — true to verify that the current MAS core version matches mas_core_version (failing on mismatch), false to skip verification (default). No rollback operations are performed. Optional Environment Variable: VERIFY_CORE_VERSION Default: false Useful for post-rollback validation to confirm a successful version change, or for validation in automation pipelines; typically used with rollback_mas_core=false . mas_rollback_dryrun ¤ Dry run mode (validation only) — true to perform all rollback compatibility validation checks without making any changes, false to execute the actual rollback after validation (default). Optional Environment Variable: MAS_ROLLBACK_DRYRUN Default: false Tip Best practice: always run with mas_rollback_dryrun=true first to validate the rollback is possible, then execute the actual rollback with mas_rollback_dryrun=false . Rollback must be enabled ( rollback_mas_core=true ) for a dry run to be meaningful. skip_compatibility_check ¤ Skip the version compatibility validation that confirms the target version is in the list of supported rollback versions — true to skip, false to enforce the check (default). Optional Environment Variable: SKIP_COMPATIBILITY_CHECK Default: false Intended for development and testing scenarios only, allowing rollback between pre-built versions on the same base (e.g., 8.11.0-pre.dev to 8.11.0-pre.stable ). Warning Development purposes only — never use in production. Skipping compatibility checks can result in failed rollbacks, data corruption, or unstable installations; the check exists to prevent unsupported rollback scenarios. Example Playbook ¤ Rollback to Specified Version ¤ Running this playbook will rollback MAS core to the specified version. If you run this playbook when you are already on the same version it will take no action. - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: instance1 mas_core_version: 8.11.0 mas_rollback_dryrun: False roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_rollback Verify MAS Core Version ¤ Running this playbook will attempt to verify the current version of MAS core matches with the specified version. - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: instance1 mas_core_version: 8.11.0 mas_rollback_dryrun: False rollback_mas_core: False verify_core_version: True roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_rollback License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: suite_uninstall ¤ This role removes Maximo Application Suite Core Platform. Note that it does not remove any data from MongoDB by default, and does not remove any applications from the MAS install. Generally it should be used after suite_app_uninstall to remove all installed Maximo Application Suite applications. Warning This role performs destructive operations. Ensure you have backups before proceeding. Use mas_wipe_mongo_data carefully as it permanently deletes all MAS data. Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_wipe_mongo_data No false Uninstall Configuration ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier to uninstall (lowercase alphanumeric, 3-12 characters, e.g. prod , dev , masinst1 ). Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None Must match the instance ID from MAS installation. The role deletes the Suite custom resource and the associated core platform resources; MongoDB data is preserved unless mas_wipe_mongo_data is enabled. Applications must be uninstalled separately with suite_app_uninstall before running this role. mas_wipe_mongo_data ¤ Delete MongoDB databases during uninstall. Optional Environment Variable: MAS_WIPE_MONGO_DATA Default: false Danger Setting this to true permanently deletes all MAS data, including configurations, workspaces, and application data. The operation cannot be undone — always verify you have backups before enabling it. The default false is strongly recommended for production environments. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: "inst1" roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_uninstall License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: suite_upgrade ¤ This role validates if a given MAS installation is ready for the core platform to be upgraded to a specific subscription channel, and (as long as dry run mode is not enabled) will execute the upgrade. It will validate that the current subscription channel is able to be upgraded to the target channel. It will validate that all installed applications have already been upgraded to versions compatible with the new version of the Core Platform. It will upgrade the MAS core platform to the desired channel (as long as dry run is not enabled). It will validate that the core platform has been successfully reconciled at the upgraded version. It will not validate that all core services successfully deploy after the reconcile (but we will be working on this limitation). Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_channel No Auto-selected mas_upgrade_dryrun No false skip_compatibility_check No false Upgrade Target ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ MAS instance identifier whose core platform will be upgraded — a lowercase alphanumeric string, 3-12 characters (e.g. prod , dev , inst1 ), matching the instance ID from the MAS installation. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None The role uses this to locate the installation and validate upgrade readiness and application compatibility; an incorrect instance ID will cause the upgrade to fail. mas_channel ¤ Target subscription channel for the MAS core platform upgrade — a valid MAS subscription channel such as 8.8.x , 8.9.x , 8.10.x , or 8.11.x . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_CHANNEL Default: Auto-selected based on current version (the next appropriate release) When unset, the role automatically selects the next release; if already on the latest release, no action is taken. Set it explicitly when you need a specific target version — the role validates that a supported upgrade path exists from the current version and that all installed applications are compatible with the target MAS version, and no upgrade is performed if validation fails. Upgrade Validation ¤ mas_upgrade_dryrun ¤ Dry-run mode, which performs all validation checks (upgrade path check, application compatibility check) without making any changes to the MAS installation — true or false . Optional Environment Variable: MAS_UPGRADE_DRYRUN Default: false When false , validation runs and the upgrade is executed if validation passes. Optional Environment Variable: SKIP_COMPATIBILITY_CHECK Default: false Warning Skipping compatibility checks can lead to failed upgrades, application incompatibilities, or unstable installations. Only set this to true in exceptional cases where you have manually verified that the upgrade path from the current to the target MAS version is supported and that all installed applications are compatible with the target MAS version — the default validation protects against incompatible upgrades and application version mismatches. Example Playbook ¤ Automatic Target Selection ¤ Running this playbook will upgrade MAS to the next release. If you run this playbook when you are already on the latest release then it will take no action. - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: mas_instance_id: instance1 mas_upgrade_dryrun: False roles: - ibm.mas_devops.suite_upgrade Explicit Upgrade Target ¤ Running this playbook will attempt to upgrade MAS to the specified release. docs.text: This role validates if a given MAS installation is ready for the core platform to be upgraded to a specific subscription channel, and (as long as dry run mode is not enabled) will execute the upgrade. It will validate that the current subscription channel is able to be upgraded to the target channel. It will validate that all installed applications have already been upgraded to versions compatible with the new version of the Core Platform. It will upgrade the MAS core platform to the desired channel (as long as dry run is not enabled). It will validate that the core platform has been successfully reconciled at the upgraded version. It will not validate that all core services successfully deploy after the reconcile (but we will be working on this limitation).

docs.text: turbonomic ¤ Installs and configures kubeturbo to connect your OpenShift cluster to a Turbonomic Application Resource Management (ARM) server. Kubeturbo is an agent that collects cluster resource utilization data and sends it to Turbonomic for analysis and optimization recommendations. Disconnected Installation Not Supported The Turbonomic Kubernetes Operator does not support disconnected/air-gapped installation. The kubeturbo deployment uses image tags rather than digests, preventing the use of ImageContentSourcePolicy to configure a mirror registry. What This Role Does ¤ Installs the Turbonomic Kubernetes Operator from available CatalogSource Deploys kubeturbo agent in the specified namespace Configures kubeturbo to connect to your Turbonomic server Sets up authentication credentials for server communication Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default kubeturbo_namespace No kubeturbo kubeturbo_package_name No kubeturbo-certified turbonomic_target_name Yes None turbonomic_server_url Yes None turbonomic_server_version No None turbonomic_username Yes None turbonomic_password Yes None KubeTurbo Installation ¤ kubeturbo_namespace ¤ OpenShift namespace where the KubeTurbo operator and agent are installed — a valid Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens). All operator and agent components are created in this namespace, which is created if it doesn't exist. Optional Environment Variable: KUBETURBO_NAMESPACE Default: kubeturbo Using the default kubeturbo namespace is recommended for consistency; override it only for multi-tenant or custom namespace requirements. kubeturbo_package_name ¤ Name of the kubeturbo package in the CatalogSource, used to locate the PackageManifest for the operator subscription. Optional Environment Variable: None (hardcoded in defaults) Default: kubeturbo-certified Turbonomic Server ¤ turbonomic_target_name ¤ Name by which this cluster is identified in the Turbonomic ARM server — typically the cluster name or identifier, for example prod-ocp-cluster or dev-cluster-01 . Required Environment Variable: TURBONOMIC_TARGET_NAME Default: None The kubeturbo agent uses this name when registering and sending data to Turbonomic; it determines how the cluster appears in Turbonomic dashboards and reports. Choose a unique, descriptive name that follows your cluster naming conventions and is unique across all clusters managed by the same Turbonomic server. turbonomic_server_url ¤ URL of the Turbonomic ARM server that kubeturbo connects to for sending cluster data and receiving optimization actions — a full URL including the protocol, for example https://turbonomic.example.com or https://turbo-server.company.com:8080 . Required Environment Variable: TURBONOMIC_SERVER_URL Default: None The server must be reachable from the OpenShift cluster network for kubeturbo to function properly — kubeturbo establishes its connection to this endpoint for all communication. turbonomic_server_version ¤ Version of the Turbonomic server being connected to — a Turbonomic version string such as 8.9.4 , 8.10.0 , or 8.11.2 , used for version-specific compatibility and feature enablement. Optional Environment Variable: TURBONOMIC_SERVER_VERSION Default: None If not specified, kubeturbo attempts to detect the server version automatically; specify only to enforce specific version compatibility, which may affect feature availability between the kubeturbo agent and the server. turbonomic_username ¤ Username for authenticating the kubeturbo agent with the Turbonomic server — a valid Turbonomic username with permissions to register targets and send data. Required Environment Variable: TURBONOMIC_USERNAME Default: None Tip Use a dedicated service account rather than a personal user account, and ensure it has the appropriate permissions in Turbonomic for target registration and data submission. turbonomic_password ¤ Password for authenticating the kubeturbo agent with the Turbonomic server — must match the password for turbonomic_username ; authentication must succeed for data transmission. Required Environment Variable: TURBONOMIC_PASSWORD Default: None Warning Keep the password secure and do not commit it to version control. Store it in a secure secret management system and use strong passwords following your organization's security policies. Example Playbook ¤ - hosts: localhost any_errors_fatal: true vars: turbonomic_server_url: https://myturbonomicserver.com turbonomic_server_version: "8.9.4" turbonomic_username: user turbonomic_password: passw0rd turbonomic_target_name: myocp roles: - ibm.mas_devops.turbonomic License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: upload_backup_archive ¤ Creates a compressed archive of MAS backup directories and uploads it to AWS S3 or Artifactory. This role automates the process of packaging MAS backup directories into a single tar.gz archive and uploading it to a remote storage location. It supports multiple backup components (IBM catalogs, cert-manager, SLS, MongoDB, Manage and Facilities applications with their Db2 databases, and the MAS Suite) and allows for component-specific backup versions. The role intelligently detects which backup directories exist and only archives those that are present. Key features: Creates compressed tar.gz archives of MAS backup directories Supports uploading to AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage Supports uploading to Artifactory repositories Handles component-specific backup versions Automatic cleanup of temporary files Configurable upload timeouts for large archives Prerequisites ¤ For S3 Upload ¤ AWS CLI or boto3 Python library must be installed amazon.aws Ansible collection must be installed AWS credentials with S3 write permissions S3 bucket must exist and be accessible For Artifactory Upload ¤ curl command-line tool must be installed Artifactory API token with upload permissions Artifactory repository must exist and be accessible Role Variables ¤ Variable Required Default mas_instance_id Yes None mas_backup_dir Yes None backup_version Yes None ibm_catalogs_backup_version No Value of backup_version certmanager_backup_version No Value of backup_version mongodb_backup_version No Value of backup_version sls_backup_version No Value of backup_version suite_backup_version No Value of backup_version manage_backup_version No Value of backup_version manage_db2_backup_version No Value of backup_version facilities_backup_version No Value of backup_version facilities_db2_backup_version No Value of backup_version aws_access_key_id Conditional None aws_secret_access_key Conditional None s3_bucket_name Conditional None s3_region No us-east-1 s3_endpoint_url No None artifactory_username Conditional None artifactory_token Conditional None artifactory_repository Conditional None artifactory_url No https://na.artifactory.swg-devops.com/artifactory backup_temp_dir No <mas_backup_dir>/mas-<mas_instance_id>-backup-<backup_version> upload_timeout No 10800 The S3 variables are required when uploading to AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage, and the Artifactory variables when uploading to Artifactory. If S3 credentials are provided, the S3 upload takes precedence over Artifactory. Backup Identification ¤ mas_instance_id ¤ Instance ID of the MAS instance. This is used to identify the backup directories. Required Environment Variable: MAS_INSTANCE_ID Default: None mas_backup_dir ¤ Directory containing the MAS backup folders. This is the parent directory where all component backup directories are located. Required Environment Variable: MAS_BACKUP_DIR Default: None backup_version ¤ Version identifier for the backup. This is used as the default version for all component backups unless component-specific versions are provided. Required Environment Variable: BACKUP_VERSION Default: None Component-Specific Backup Versions ¤ These variables allow you to specify different backup versions for individual components. If not provided, they default to the value of backup_version . ibm_catalogs_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the IBM catalogs component. Optional Environment Variable: IBM_CATALOGS_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version certmanager_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the cert-manager component. Optional Environment Variable: CERTMANAGER_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version mongodb_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the MongoDB component. Optional Environment Variable: MONGODB_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version sls_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the SLS (Suite License Service) component. Optional Environment Variable: SLS_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version suite_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the MAS Suite component. Optional Environment Variable: SUITE_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version manage_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the MAS Manage application. Optional Environment Variable: MANAGE_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version manage_db2_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the Manage Db2 database component. Optional Environment Variable: MANAGE_DB2_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version facilities_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the MAS Facilities application. Optional Environment Variable: FACILITIES_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version facilities_db2_backup_version ¤ Backup version for the Facilities Db2 database component. Optional Environment Variable: FACILITIES_DB2_BACKUP_VERSION Default: Value of backup_version S3 Upload Variables ¤ Provide these variables to upload the backup archive to AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage. If S3 credentials are provided, S3 upload takes precedence over Artifactory. aws_access_key_id ¤ AWS access key ID for authentication. Required for S3 upload Environment Variable: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None aws_secret_access_key ¤ AWS secret access key for authentication. Required for S3 upload Environment Variable: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None s3_bucket_name ¤ Name of the S3 bucket where the archive will be uploaded. Required for S3 upload Environment Variable: S3_BUCKET_NAME Default: None s3_region ¤ AWS region where the S3 bucket is located. Optional Environment Variable: S3_REGION Default: us-east-1 s3_endpoint_url ¤ Custom S3 endpoint URL for S3-compatible storage services (e.g., MinIO, Wasabi, IBM Cloud Object Storage). Optional Environment Variable: S3_ENDPOINT_URL Default: None (uses AWS S3 endpoints) Artifactory Upload Variables ¤ Provide these variables to upload the backup archive to Artifactory. Artifactory upload is used only if S3 credentials are not provided. artifactory_username ¤ Artifactory username for authentication. Required for Artifactory upload Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None artifactory_token ¤ Artifactory API token for authentication. Required for Artifactory upload Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None artifactory_repository ¤ Name of the Artifactory repository where the archive will be uploaded. Required for Artifactory upload Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_REPOSITORY Default: None artifactory_url ¤ Base URL of the Artifactory server (e.g., https://artifactory.example.com/artifactory ). Optional Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_URL Default: https://na.artifactory.swg-devops.com/artifactory Archive and Upload Settings ¤ backup_temp_dir ¤ Temporary directory where the archive will be created before upload. The directory is created if it doesn't exist and cleaned up after upload. Optional Environment Variable: None Default: <mas_backup_dir>/mas-<mas_instance_id>-backup-<backup_version> upload_timeout ¤ Maximum time in seconds to wait for the upload to complete. Useful for large archives or slow network connections. Optional Environment Variable: None Default: 10800 (3 hours) Example Playbook ¤ S3 Upload ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - hosts: localhost vars: mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas backup_version: "20260117-191500" aws_access_key_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID') }}" aws_secret_access_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY') }}" s3_bucket_name: my-mas-backups s3_region: us-west-2 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.upload_backup_archive Artifactory Upload ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas backup_version: "20260117-191500" artifactory_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME') }}" artifactory_token: "{{ lookup('env', 'ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN') }}" artifactory_url: https://artifactory.example.com/artifactory artifactory_repository: mas-backups roles: - ibm.mas_devops.upload_backup_archive S3-Compatible Storage (IBMcloud, MinIO, Wasabi, etc.) ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas backup_version: "20260117-191500" aws_access_key_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'S3_ACCESS_KEY') }}" aws_secret_access_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'S3_SECRET_KEY') }}" s3_bucket_name: mas-backups s3_region: us-east-1 s3_endpoint_url: https://s3.example.com roles: - ibm.mas_devops.upload_backup_archive Component-Specific Backup Versions ¤ - hosts: localhost vars: mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas backup_version: "20260117-191500" # Override specific component versions mongodb_backup_version: "20260116-120000" manage_db2_backup_version: "20260115-180000" aws_access_key_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID') }}" aws_secret_access_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY') }}" s3_bucket_name: my-mas-backups roles: - ibm.mas_devops.upload_backup_archive Run Role Playbook ¤ After installing the Ansible Collection you can easily run the role standalone using the run_role playbook provided. S3 Upload ¤ export MAS_BACKUP_DIR=/backup/mas export BACKUP_VERSION=20260117-191500 export S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key export S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key export S3_BUCKET_NAME=my-mas-backups export S3_REGION=us-west-2 ROLE_NAME=upload_backup_archive ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role Artifactory Upload ¤ export MAS_BACKUP_DIR=/backup/mas export BACKUP_VERSION=20260117-191500 export ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME=your_username export ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN=your_token export ARTIFACTORY_URL=https://artifactory.example.com/artifactory export ARTIFACTORY_REPOSITORY=mas-backups ROLE_NAME=upload_backup_archive ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role License ¤ EPL-2.0

docs.text: Provide these variables to upload the backup archive to AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage. If S3 credentials are provided, S3 upload takes precedence over Artifactory.
docs.title: S3 Upload Variables

docs.text: AWS access key ID for authentication. Required for S3 upload Environment Variable: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID Default: None
docs.title: aws_access_key_id

docs.text: AWS secret access key for authentication. Required for S3 upload Environment Variable: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Default: None
docs.title: aws_secret_access_key

docs.text: Name of the S3 bucket where the archive will be uploaded. Required for S3 upload Environment Variable: S3_BUCKET_NAME Default: None
docs.title: s3_bucket_name

docs.text: AWS region where the S3 bucket is located. Optional Environment Variable: S3_REGION Default: us-east-1
docs.title: s3_region

docs.text: Custom S3 endpoint URL for S3-compatible storage services (e.g., MinIO, Wasabi, IBM Cloud Object Storage). Optional Environment Variable: S3_ENDPOINT_URL Default: None (uses AWS S3 endpoints)
docs.title: s3_endpoint_url

docs.text: Provide these variables to upload the backup archive to Artifactory. Artifactory upload is used only if S3 credentials are not provided.
docs.title: Artifactory Upload Variables

docs.text: Artifactory username for authentication. Required for Artifactory upload Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_USERNAME Default: None
docs.title: artifactory_username

docs.text: Artifactory API token for authentication. Required for Artifactory upload Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN Default: None
docs.title: artifactory_token

docs.text: Name of the Artifactory repository where the archive will be uploaded. Required for Artifactory upload Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_REPOSITORY Default: None
docs.title: artifactory_repository

docs.text: Base URL of the Artifactory server (e.g., https://artifactory.example.com/artifactory ). Optional Environment Variable: ARTIFACTORY_URL Default: https://na.artifactory.swg-devops.com/artifactory
docs.title: artifactory_url

docs.text: Temporary directory where the archive will be created before upload. The directory is created if it doesn't exist and cleaned up after upload. Optional Environment Variable: None Default: <mas_backup_dir>/mas-<mas_instance_id>-backup-<backup_version>
docs.title: backup_temp_dir

docs.text: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the upload to complete. Useful for large archives or slow network connections. Optional Environment Variable: None Default: 10800 (3 hours)
docs.title: upload_timeout

docs.text: After installing the Ansible Collection you can include this role in your own custom playbooks. - hosts: localhost vars: mas_backup_dir: /backup/mas backup_version: "20260117-191500" aws_access_key_id: "{{ lookup('env', 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID') }}" aws_secret_access_key: "{{ lookup('env', 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY') }}" s3_bucket_name: my-mas-backups s3_region: us-west-2 roles: - ibm.mas_devops.upload_backup_archive

docs.text: After installing the Ansible Collection you can easily run the role standalone using the run_role playbook provided.
docs.title: Run Role Playbook

docs.text: export MAS_BACKUP_DIR=/backup/mas export BACKUP_VERSION=20260117-191500 export S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key export S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key export S3_BUCKET_NAME=my-mas-backups export S3_REGION=us-west-2 ROLE_NAME=upload_backup_archive ansible-playbook ibm.mas_devops.run_role
docs.title: S3 Upload
